instances.label: Site inspection of a specific parcel for a proposed development or rezoning: planner drives to the site, walks the parcel and its frontage, photographs existing structures, vegetation, topography, driveways and access, notes adjacent land uses and street conditions, and records observations used in a staff report. Private or vacant land, variable terrain, one-off visit, outdoor conditions as found.

Field observation of traffic and circulation: planner stands at or drives an intersection/corridor during peak periods to observe traffic flow, queueing, turning movements, parking occupancy and pedestrian activity, recording counts and qualitative observations for a traffic-impact or corridor study. Public streets and sidewalks.

Neighborhood-scale land use and housing-condition survey: planner covers many blocks on foot or by car, recording per-parcel existing use, occupancy/vacancy, building condition, and infrastructure deficiencies for a comprehensive plan or neighborhood plan inventory. Public rights-of-way and residential streets.

Stakeholder interviews and public surveys: semi-structured interviews with residents, property owners, business operators and agency staff, plus administering questionnaires (door-to-door, intercept at public places, or in a community room / city hall meeting) about housing needs, land use concerns and travel behavior.

Compliance/verification inspection of a built or partially built project: planner visits the site to check conformance with approved plans and conditions - measuring setbacks and building height, counting parking stalls, verifying landscaping, screening, signage and access improvements - and documents findings with photos and measurements.

sources.title: Construction | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped is sold and used for autonomous data capture on construction sites, navigating job-site environments to document progress and as-built conditions with 360-degree imagery and laser scanning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction site progress/as-built documentation. It is the same physical act as a planner's site inspection - traversing an unstructured outdoor/indoor site and systematically recording conditions of structures, surfaces and features - with comparable objects and precision (visual/laser documentation, not manipulation).

instances.label: Ethnographic/participant-observation recording: the anthropologist carries a camera, camcorder and audio recorder through homes, streets, markets, workplaces, ceremonies and community events, negotiating consent on the spot, choosing which moments and material culture to photograph/film, capturing ambient and spoken audio, and logging the media as field data.

Site- and trench-scale archaeological photographic documentation: overhead/plan photos of open excavation areas, standing architecture, profiles and site overviews, increasingly by photogrammetry, at CRM and research excavations taken as found (uneven ground, spoil heaps, vegetation, variable weather).

Close-range in-situ documentation: cleaning the surface, placing a scale bar, north arrow and context/ID board, controlling shadow, and shooting individual features, burials, unit profiles and artifacts in place from prescribed angles, then completing the photo log/metadata - done kneeling in or beside a fragile excavation unit.

Aerial imagery and landscape-scale survey records: UAV overflights of sites and cultural landscapes to produce orthophotos, 3D models and condition-monitoring imagery of ruins, mounds, earthworks and eroding shorelines.

Laboratory/collections imaging: catalog-quality photography and 3D scanning of artifacts, ceramics, lithics, faunal and skeletal material on a copy stand or turntable in a CRM lab or museum, with scale and color reference, multiple views, and image metadata attached to the catalog record.

Recorded interviews and oral histories: setting up camera and microphone and capturing an audio/video record of a seated interview or focus group in an institutional room (university, museum, tribal or agency office, community center), then saving and labeling the file.

instances.label: University archaeological field school: the director/instructor runs a multi-week teaching excavation, explains and demonstrates unit layout, troweling, screening, stratigraphic recognition and paperwork, then circulates among student units giving verbal correction, feedback, and grades. Purpose is instruction and assessment; students perform the digging.

CRM firm on-project training of newly hired field technicians: safety and protocol briefings, walking crews through shovel-test spacing, screening standards, feature recording forms and photo logs, then spot-checking work and correcting errors verbally during the workday.

Public/volunteer dig day or avocational society excavation: short orientation talk to untrained volunteers of mixed ages, repeated one-on-one guidance and explanation at the trench edge, monitoring for safety and artifact-handling errors, answering questions.

Leading the training site as an operation: setting the day's excavation plan, assigning units and crew chiefs, scheduling rotations through survey/excavation/lab stations, reviewing forms and level records for quality, and holding end-of-day debriefs.

instances.label: Phase I pedestrian survey of a rural or undeveloped parcel for CRM compliance: walking transects across plowed fields, pasture and brush, spotting and identifying surface lithics/ceramics/historic debris, excavating and screening shovel test probes at fixed intervals, backfilling, recording finds and negative tests with GPS, and judging whether an archaeological site is present.

Hand excavation and assessment at an identified site: laying out and digging test units or trenches with trowel and shovel by natural or arbitrary levels, recognizing soil changes and cultural features in profile and plan, deciding what to sample, piece-plotting and photographing in situ, drawing profiles; includes standing by an excavator during mechanical stripping/construction monitoring and calling stops when features appear.

Metric documentation and condition assessment of an exposed site, ruin, rock-art panel or standing feature: capturing georeferenced 3D models, orthophotos or laser scans of the visible surface and structures, and comparing them over time to assess extent, layout and deterioration.

Subsurface geophysical prospection of a field or known site: laying out grids and collecting magnetometer, GPR or resistivity data over several hectares, processing into anomaly maps, and flagging targets for ground-truthing.

Laboratory/curation assessment of the recovered assemblage to answer the project's research questions: washing, sorting and cataloging mixed bags of sherds, lithics, faunal bone and historic material, identifying and quantifying types, selecting samples for dating or analysis, and integrating results into the site interpretation.

Survey and assessment of a submerged or otherwise physically inaccessible site: locating and characterizing a shipwreck or drowned landscape on the seabed, mapping its extent and content with acoustic and optical imaging.

instances.label: CRM Phase I survey: pedestrian transects and shovel test pits across farm fields, woodlots, roadside corridors or vacant lots. Worker spots surface finds or screens fill, judges what is an artifact, records the findspot with handheld GNSS/compass-and-tape, notes artifact type and condition on field forms, and photographs representative finds and settings.

Phase III data recovery or research excavation unit: in-situ artifacts and features exposed in a trench are piece-plotted with a total station or RTK GNSS, depth/level and matrix recorded, condition (burned, eroded, refit potential, fragility) described, plan and profile drawings made on graph paper or tablet, and scaled photographs with north arrow and scale board taken before removal.

Photogrammetric surface documentation at an open-air excavation: at the end of a level or when a feature/artifact cluster is exposed, the excavated surface is captured (drone or pole camera imagery, or laser scan) and processed into a georeferenced orthophoto/3D model that serves as the plan record of the surface and the artifacts lying in place on it.

Post-field lab documentation in a CRM or university archaeology lab: recovered artifacts are laid out at a bench or copy stand, provenience transferred from bag tags to the catalog, condition assessed (breakage, wear, burning, corrosion), and each diagnostic piece photographed or 3D-scanned with scale, plus ink or digital illustrations produced for the report.

Difficult or special contexts: monitoring mechanical stripping on an active urban construction site, recording burials and human remains, confined or unstable exposures, or submerged/underwater finds; recording done under time pressure, weather, machinery traffic, or restricted access.

tasks.label: Assess archeological sites for resource management, development, or conservation purposes and recommend methods for site protection.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: CRM Phase I identification survey of a project parcel or corridor (pipeline, transmission line, solar farm, subdivision) on rural undeveloped land: walk pedestrian transects through brush/plowed field/forest, hand-dig and screen shovel test pits at 15-30 m intervals, log soil profiles, collect and bag artifacts, GPS-map finds and site boundaries, then evaluate significance and recommend avoidance, buffering or further work.

Condition assessment / monitoring visit to a previously recorded site on federal, state or tribal land (BLM, USFS, NPS): travel off-road or hike in, inspect for erosion gullies, looting pits, vandalism, livestock/OHV and vegetation impacts, photograph and measure features and artifact scatters, update the site condition form, and recommend stabilization, fencing, signage, backfilling or patrol frequency.

Assessment in a developed/urban setting for a construction or redevelopment project: archaeological monitoring and deep testing at an active construction site or historic property, inspecting machine-cut trench walls and backdirt for intact strata, features and artifacts amid heavy equipment, then assessing integrity and recommending protection/mitigation (avoidance, capping, data recovery).

Non-invasive remote-sensing/geophysical assessment of a site or study area: autonomous UAV photogrammetry or LiDAR mapping and repeat change-detection flights, and/or towed GPR/magnetometer survey over open ground or fields, to delineate site extent and buried features and quantify condition change, delivering maps used to set protective buffers and monitoring intervals.

Condition assessment at an institutionally managed heritage property (state/national park unit, museum-run ruins, historic site with gates, staff and maintained visitor routes): inspect masonry, structural and surface condition, visitor-caused wear, drainage and unauthorized tunnels/digging; document with photography and 3D scanning; recommend barriers, shelters, drainage works or route changes.

tasks.label: Gather and analyze artifacts and skeletal remains to increase knowledge of ancient cultures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: CRM or research excavation at an open-air site: hand-excavating shovel tests and 1x1 m units with trowel and shovel, screening sediment through 1/4-inch mesh, spotting and recovering lithics, sherds, faunal bone and charcoal, bagging by provenience, drawing/photographing profiles and features, in weather, on uneven ground, occasionally including delicate exposure and lifting of human burials.

Laboratory processing of a recovered assemblage: washing and drying finds, sorting by material class, counting and weighing, labeling individual specimens, rebagging and boxing to curation standard, and entering catalog records into a database in a university/CRM lab.

Reconstruction and documentation work in the lab: refitting and mending fragmented pottery vessels, frescoes or plaster, and producing metric photographic/3D records of finds for the report and archive, on a bench in an institutional lab or museum workroom.

Specialist artifact analysis: caliper and microscope work on lithics (attribute, raw material, use-wear) or ceramics (paste, temper, typology), comparing specimens to type collections, illustrating diagnostics, and interpreting the assemblage in a lab or museum collections room.

Osteological/bioarchaeological analysis of human skeletal remains in a lab: inventorying and siding fragmentary elements, laying out the skeleton, taking osteometric measurements, estimating age, sex, stature and ancestry, scoring pathology and trauma, and recording to standard while handling fragile remains under curation and NAGPRA-type protocols.

Biomolecular/geochemical analysis of samples: subsampling bone, teeth, ceramics or sediment, running or commissioning ZooMS, aDNA, stable isotope, pXRF or radiocarbon workflows in a controlled lab, and turning the instrument output into species, date or provenance determinations.

sources.developer: University of Bonn, Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Italian Institute of Technology (EU Horizon RePAIR)
sources.title: Robotics Reconstructs History: Bonn Research Team Develops AI-Supported "Robo-Puzzler" for Pompeii
sources.claim: The EU RePAIR project's bimanual robot with soft grippers autonomously picks up fragile Pompeii fresco fragments and places them ... millimetre-accurate positions computed by an AI puzzle solver; tested on heavily fragmented ceiling paintings at the Archaeological Park of Pompeii.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: refitting/reassembling fragmented archaeological finds, a standard part of artifact study. Transfers because the objects (fragile plaster/ceramic fragments), the precision required (millimetre placement without damage), and the bench-top lab setting match the refit-and-reconstruct portion of artifact analysis.

sources.system: RASCAL and RePAIR manipulator robots (as surveyed)
sources.title: Survey on the Application of Robotics in Archaeology (Sensors 2025)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed survey of robotics in archaeology reports that manipulator robots such as RASCAL and RePAIR perform automated handling, classification and reassembly ... using computer vision and AI matching, with repeatable precision on fragile objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and reconstruction of excavated finds. Used only as corroborating context for the RePAIR demonstration; autonomy is not established in this source, so it does not carry a positive judgment by itself.

sources.title: Fraunhofer IGD develops new and improved CultArm3D archival scanner
sources.claim: CultArm3D-P is a robot-arm, colour-calibrated autonomous scanner that automates the entire 3D digitization of artifacts placed on its turntable; it was trialled by the J. Paul Getty Trust in 2022 and is commercialized via the Verus Digital spin-off.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: metric 3D documentation of artifacts for study and archiving. Transfers to the documentation half of lab artifact work: same object class (museum/excavated finds), same record quality expected, performed in a purpose-built scanning cell.

sources.developer: University of Manchester (Manchester Institute of Biotechnology, Buckley lab)
sources.title: AutoZooMS: Integrating robotics into high-throughput ZooMS for the species identification of palaeontological remains at Grotte Mandrin, France
sources.claim: AutoZooMS used liquid-handling robots to run collagen-peptide (ZooMS) species identification on fragmentary bone from Grotte Mandrin, processing 1026 morphologically indeterminate specimens and yielding new taxa including Ursidae, Mammuthus and further hominin remains, with little human intervention.

sources.title: Stanford's humanoid robotic diver recovers treasures from King Louis XIV's wrecked flagship
sources.claim: Underwater artifact recovery by the leading archaeological diving robot remains continuously human-piloted: OceanOne lifted a vase from the La Lune wreck under haptic joystick control from the surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recovery of an artifact from an archaeological deposit. Shows the flagship field-recovery robot is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous artifact gathering.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Archaeological Park of Pompeii
sources.title: Meet Spot, the Dog-Like Robot Roaming the Ruins of Pompeii
sources.claim: At the Archaeological Park of Pompeii a Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped autonomously patrols the ruins collecting structural and safety data; its role is inspection and documentation, not excavation, artifact recovery, or artifact analysis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous data collection on an archaeological site. Cited to characterise field robotics in archaeology as mapping/monitoring only, supporting the negative judgment on autonomous excavation and recovery.

tasks.label: Compare findings from one site with archeological data from other sites to find similarities or differences.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Describe artifacts' physical properties or attributes, such as the materials from which artifacts are made and their size, shape, function, and decoration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: CRM or university archaeology lab: bulk processing of an excavated assemblage — washing/sorted bags of non-diagnostic sherds, lithic debitage, faunal fragments, nails and glass are sorted by material class, counted, weighed, size-graded, and coded on standard attribute forms/databases at a bench.

Museum, repository or lab collections room: documentation of an individual catalogued or diagnostic artifact — caliper measurements, weight, condition, photography or 3D scan, and a database record of form, dimensions, surface treatment and decoration.

Interpretive/scholarly description for a site report, catalog entry or publication: determining manufacturing technique, probable function/use, typological and cultural attribution, and describing decorative motifs, using hand lens and comparative collections.

Field description at an excavation or pedestrian survey: describing artifacts as recovered in the trench, screen, or on the ground surface (material, size, form, apparent function) in field notes/forms, outdoors in variable light, weather and terrain.

Ethnographic/material-culture description in community settings: recording objects in homes, workshops or markets — materials, dimensions, construction, decoration and use — while working with their owners/makers.

sources.developer: Fraunhofer Institute for Computer Graphics Research IGD
sources.title: CultArm3D, an Automated Robotic Arm That Can Scan Cultural Objects in 3D - 3Dnatives
sources.claim: CultArm3D is a robotic-arm 3D scanning system that autonomously plans views and captures colour-faithful, high-resolution 3D models of museum objects placed on its turntable; reported in use at several museums and archives and commercialized with Phase One.
sources.transferJustification: Directly captures artifact size, shape, surface and decoration as a metric digital record — the documentation core of describing an artifact's physical attributes — with the object presented on a scanner turntable.

sources.developer: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (Centre for Cultural Heritage Technology, Venice; Industrial Robotics Facility, Genova)
sources.title: Hands-Free Heritage: Automated 3D Scanning for Cultural Heritage Digitization (arXiv:2510.04781)
sources.claim: An automated two-robot cell (one robot scans, a second robot re-orients a transparent tray of ...) performs full-coverage high-resolution 3D scanning of cultural heritage artefacts without handheld or semi-automatic human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Shows autonomous robotic handling and repositioning of fragile artefacts inside a purpose-built cell, the manipulation step required to measure and image an artifact from all sides.

sources.title: Forabot: Automated Planktic Foraminifera Isolation and Imaging (Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems)
sources.claim: Forabot autonomously isolates individual microfossil specimens from a bulk sample, images each one, and classifies it with a CNN (79% validation accuracy), processing about 27 specimens per hour on a lab bench apparatus.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk sorting, imaging and morphological identification of small fragile specimens from an excavated sample — the same physical operation as bench-top sorting and attribute recording of sherds and debitage.

sources.title: Artificial intelligence for recycling: AMP Robotics — Ellen MacArthur Foundation
sources.claim: AMP Robotics' Cortex sorting robots autonomously identify heterogeneous items by material type (plastics, metals, paper) from shape, colour and texture on conveyor lines in commercial recycling facilities, at up to 99% accuracy and 80 picks per minute.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine identification of the material class and gross form of mixed small objects presented on a purpose-built conveyor, the same physical/perceptual operation as sorting a bulk artifact lot into material categories.

sources.developer: FEI/Thermo Fisher (QEMSCAN); applied by archaeometry labs
sources.title: Automated SEM Mineralogy and Archaeological Ceramics: Applications in Formative Period Pottery From the Atacama Desert (Frontiers in Earth Science)
sources.claim: Automated SEM-EDS (QEMSCAN) instruments produce quantitative mineralogical and compositional characterization of archaeological ceramics, identifying and quantifying the minerals and inclusions from which the pottery was made.
sources.transferJustification: Directly delivers the 'materials from which artifacts are made' component of the description, for samples loaded into an instrument chamber.

sources.date: 2024 (product page, technique in museum use since ~2013)
sources.title: M6 JETSTREAM | Bruker
sources.claim: The Bruker M6 JETSTREAM is a motorized macro-XRF scanner that automatically rasters a measuring head over cultural heritage objects and paintings to map their elemental composition, including topographic 3D objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated, non-destructive determination of the materials (pigments, alloys) of heritage objects positioned in front of the scanner, supplying the material-identification part of an artifact description.

sources.title: AI DIAMOND GRADING BEYOND THE 4Cs / The 2nd Generation of Automated Diamond Color Grading (Sarine)
sources.claim: Sarine's machine-vision grading devices automatically map inclusions and grade colour of polished diamonds to lab standards, replacing subjective human graders; the systems are commercially deployed in manufacturing and grading facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a machine produces the accepted attribute description (dimensions, shape, colour, internal features) of small objects loaded into it, in place of a trained human describer — the same output type as a catalog attribute record.

tasks.label: Collect artifacts made of stone, bone, metal, and other materials, placing them in bags and marking them to show where they were found.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hand-excavating a 1x1 m unit at an open-air terrestrial site (CRM or research dig): troweling through soil, spotting lithic flakes, ceramic sherds, bone fragments and metal in situ, recording unit/level/depth (and often point-provenience), then bagging finds and marking the bag/tag. Uneven ground, variable light, weather, roots and rodent disturbance.

Working the screen station beside the excavation: dumping buckets of matrix onto 1/4-inch mesh, shaking, and picking artifacts (small flakes, sherds, bone, nails, glass, beads) out of gravel, clods and roots, then placing them in the pre-labeled bag for that unit and level.

Pedestrian survey and shovel testing on CRM projects: walking transects over plowed fields, pasture, desert or wooded terrain, spotting surface artifacts, and screening shovel-test fill; collecting diagnostics into bags marked with transect/STP number and GPS coordinates.

Recovering fragile or complex finds: crumbling bone or a human burial, waterlogged wood, corroded iron, articulated features. Requires pedestaling, dental-pick and brush work, consolidation or block-lifting, in-place photography and mapping before the object is lifted into a padded, labeled container.

Construction monitoring / salvage recovery: an archaeologist watching mechanical excavation in a utility trench or building footprint, quickly recovering artifacts from backdirt and trench walls amid running machinery, and bagging them with the best available provenience.

Underwater/maritime recovery: a diver on a shipwreck or submerged site removing sediment, tagging an artifact in situ, and placing it in a mesh or rigid container marked with grid square and depth for controlled ascent.

sources.developer: Ca' Foscari University of Venice / Archaeological Park of Pompeii (EU RePAIR consortium)
sources.title: THE RePAIR PROJECT COMES ONLINE ROBOTICS AND DIGITALISATION AT THE SERVICE OF ARCHAEOLOGY - Pompeii Sites
sources.claim: EU RePAIR project robotic arms at Pompeii scan, recognize and manipulate fragile fresco fragments held in the park's storerooms and reassemble them; the fragments are already-collected material presented to the machine in a purpose-built rig, not recovered in situ with provenience.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of fragile archaeological fragments. It is the closest demonstration of a robot manipulating real artifacts, but it works on fragments already collected, cleaned and presented in a lab rig; it performs no in-ground detection, selective recovery, bagging or provenience marking.

sources.system: ROGO robotic soil sampler (Kubota UTV platform)
sources.title: Inside an Autonomous Soil Sampling Robot | Central Valley Ag
sources.claim: ROGO's autonomous soil-sampling robots drive themselves to georeferenced points in farm fields, pull cores, ensure each core reaches the correct sample bag and track samples with QR codes and GPS - autonomous ground sampling with recorded provenience, but no discrimination of artifacts from matrix.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: collecting material from the ground at recorded locations and bagging it with a location label. Transfer is limited: the robot extracts a fixed-volume core at a pre-planned point; it never has to recognise which items in the matrix are artifacts, extract them without damage, or tie them to excavated levels.

sources.date: 2024-02 (4.0 launch); deployed in sorting facilities since 2015
sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker robots autonomously identify and pick stone, brick, wood, metal and other categories out of mixed bulky construction and demolition waste on conveyors in sorting plants, dropping picks into bins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking heterogeneous rubble-like objects (stone, metal, wood) from a presented stream into containers - the E1 analogue of a screen station. It does not substantiate archaeological completion: categories are coarse material classes, purity targets tolerate misses, and no deployment distinguishes a worked flake, small sherd or bone splinter from natural gravel.

sources.developer: North Carolina State University (Lobaton, Richmond et al.)
sources.title: Forabot robot searches through tiny shells from prehistoric times | New Atlas
sources.claim: Forabot autonomously isolates individual sub-millimetre fossils from prepared sediment samples and sorts them by AI classification in the laboratory, at 79% identification accuracy and about 27 specimens per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic picking of small objects out of sediment residue and sorting them by identity, the closest analogue to sorting screened matrix. Throughput (tens of items per hour) and accuracy (79-89% on six trained classes) fall far below the recovery standard a field crew must meet.

sources.title: Stanford team develops humanoid robot for virtual deep-sea exploration - CBS San Francisco
sources.claim: OceanOneK, the humanoid submersible used to recover artifacts from Mediterranean shipwrecks, is driven by a human pilot at the surface through haptic controls rather than operating autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (underwater artifact recovery), but continuously teleoperated, so under the rules it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / EU SeaClear consortium
sources.title: Autonomous gripper robot hauls heavy trash from Marseille seafloor | New Atlas
sources.claim: The SeaClear 2 underwater robot autonomously detected, gripped and retrieved sunken waste from the seabed in the Port of Marseille, placing it in a collection basket.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous underwater detection and retrieval of objects from sediment. Targets are robust litter collected in bulk with a heavy claw; no fragile-artifact handling, in-situ tagging or per-item provenience recording is demonstrated.

sources.title: Autonomous rubbish robot wins Galileo Masters 2020 - GPS World
sources.claim: Angsa's autonomous outdoor cleaning robot detects and picks individual small items such as bottle caps and cigarette butts out of grass and gravel in parks and event grounds without external infrastructure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous detection and pickup of small objects from unstructured outdoor ground, the analogue of surface collection. It recognises a few trained litter classes and dumps everything into one hopper; it cannot distinguish artifacts from natural stone or bag items individually with georeferenced provenience.

sources.system: state-of-the-art review (RASCAL, RePAIR, ROVs, UGVs, UAVs)
sources.title: Survey on the Application of Robotics in Archaeology (Sensors 25:4836)
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed survey of robotics in archaeology reports manipulator robots used for conservation-lab handling, classification and reassembly of fragments, and field robots used for sensing, mapping and access to inaccessible areas; no autonomous system for recovering and bagging finds during excavation is described.
sources.transferJustification: Survey evidence on the state of the art rather than a single system; used to confirm that demonstrated robotic manipulation in archaeology is confined to post-excavation laboratory handling of already-recovered fragments.

tasks.label: Study objects and structures recovered by excavation to identify, date, and authenticate them and to interpret their significance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-excavation lab at a university, museum, or CRM firm: washing, sorting, weighing, measuring and typologically identifying bulk assemblages of potsherds, lithics, faunal bone and building material; assigning ware/type and date ranges; entering the catalog record that anchors later interpretation.

Close study of diagnostic or unique finds in the lab: binocular/SEM examination of manufacturing traces, use-wear and residues, comparison against reference collections and published typologies, judging genuineness versus modern intrusion or forgery, and writing the interpretation of the object's significance.

Archaeometric work: selecting stratigraphically secure samples (charcoal, bone, seeds), pretreating and submitting them for AMS radiocarbon dating, preparing thin sections, running pXRF/ICP-MS or aDNA sampling, then evaluating quality flags and integrating results into dates and provenance conclusions.

On-site study of excavated structures and features in an open trench: reading wall bonding, floors, hearths and stratigraphic sections, phasing construction, sampling mortar or plaster, recording and interpreting the architecture in weather, dust and uneven footing.

Re-study of curated legacy collections in a museum or repository: retrieving boxed material from shelving, re-examining and re-identifying artifacts against new comparanda, correcting old attributions and reinterpreting the assemblage for publication.

sources.title: Fraunhofer IGD develops automated robotic arm to scan cultural objects in 3D, now cooperating with Phase One
sources.claim: CultArm3D is a commercially available robotic arm scanner that autonomously produces high-resolution colour-accurate 3D records of museum objects; it automates artifact documentation but performs no identification, dating, authentication, or interpretation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: 3D digitization of excavated/curated artifacts in museum studios. It shows robots can safely handle and image the same objects, but digitization is a sub-step of studying an object; the identification, dating, authentication and interpretive output of this task is not produced.

sources.developer: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (Centre for Cultural Heritage Technology, Venice; Industrial Robotics Facility, Genova)
sources.title: Hands-Free Heritage: Automated 3D Scanning for Cultural Heritage Digitization (arXiv:2510.04781)
sources.claim: A two-robot laboratory system coordinates a scanner arm and a tray-handling arm to scan heritage artefacts without handheld operation; a research demonstration of automated artefact documentation only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation and geometric capture of fragile heritage objects in a purpose-built lab rig. Transfers only to the handling/recording sub-step; no analytical identification, dating or authentication of the artefact is produced.

sources.developer: North Carolina State University with University of Colorado Boulder
sources.title: Fossil-sorting robot to make it easier to study oceans, climate
sources.claim: Forabot is a proof-of-concept robot that isolates individual microfossils from a bulk sample, images them, and classifies them, reaching 79% accuracy across six species at about 27 specimens per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated isolation and taxonomic identification of small excavated/recovered specimens in a purpose-built bench rig. Scope is six foraminifera species at 79% accuracy in a proof of concept, far short of the open-ended typological identification, dating and authentication of archaeological assemblages.

sources.date: 2009-10 (system introduced; AGE-3 in routine lab use through 2024)
sources.title: A revolutionary graphitisation system: Fully automated, compact and simple
sources.claim: Automated graphitization systems coupled to an elemental analyser prepare samples for AMS radiocarbon measurement under machine control, automating one chemical step of the dating chain.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated preparation of samples for radiocarbon dating. It covers only the benchtop chemistry sub-step; stratigraphic sample selection, pretreatment decisions, quality evaluation and interpretation of the resulting date remain with the specialist.

tasks.label: Consult site reports, existing artifacts, and topographic maps to identify archeological sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Clean, restore, and preserve artifacts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk post-excavation finds processing in a CRM/university field lab or wash station: emptying provenience bags of ceramics, lithics, brick and bone, deciding which materials may be wet-washed and which must only be dry-brushed (friable, painted, metal, residue-bearing), brushing under water with soft brushes, drying on labeled screens, keeping bag/provenience association intact.

Fine mechanical cleaning of delicate or diagnostic objects in a conservation lab under magnification: removing concretion and corrosion from metal, soil from fragile bone, glass or plaster with scalpel, dental picks, air-abrasive or solvent swabs, judging pass-by-pass when to stop at the original surface.

Matching and physically re-assembling large sets of like fragments (fresco plaster, coarseware sherds) into laid-out, correctly grouped and positioned assemblies on a work table in a lab or collections storeroom, before a restorer fixes them.

Mending and stabilizing an individual object in the lab: cleaning break edges, joining sherds with reversible adhesive, supporting the vessel in a sandbox while curing, consolidating friable surfaces with dilute Paraloid B-72, filling and toning losses.

Preventive preservation and rehousing in a lab or collections facility: applying catalog numbers to artifacts (barrier coat, ink, sealant), bagging by provenience with tags, cutting padding and packing objects into archival boxes, shelving and recording storage location.

In-field stabilization and lifting of a fragile find in an open excavation trench: brushing loose soil in situ, applying consolidant or facing, undercutting and pedestalling, block-lifting with plaster/foam/bandage jacket, transporting intact to the lab, under weather and uneven ground.

sources.system: RePAIR robotic platform (IIT dual-arm system with SoftHands)
sources.developer: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia / Ca' Foscari University of Venice / Archaeological Park of Pompeii
sources.title: The research project for the reassembly of fragmented frescoes using an "intelligent robot" comes to an end
sources.claim: RePAIR's dual-arm robotic platform (IIT/Ca' Foscari, at the Archaeological Park of Pompeii) autonomously places fresco fragments in the positions computed by an AI reassembly solver, on a purpose-built workbench with a linear guide inside the Casina Rustica building; the project ended in Dec 2025 as a validated prototype, with testing phases performed on artificial replicas of the digitized fragments.

sources.developer: University of Bonn (motion planning) within the EU RePAIR consortium
sources.title: EU Project: Bonn Robot Unjumbles Ancient Jigsaw
sources.claim: University of Bonn description of the same RePAIR platform confirms the robot physically grasped mural fragments with soft gripper hands and set them down at the positions computed by the AI jigsaw solver.

sources.system: Survey of manipulative robots in archaeological conservation (RePAIR, RASCAL)
sources.developer: ICCS / National Technical University of Athens (review authors)
sources.title: Survey on the Application of Robotics in Archaeology (Sensors 25:4836)
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed survey of robotics in archaeology characterizes the state of the art in conservation as robotic arms that scan, classify and propose fragment matches in a hybrid human-machine workflow; it reports no robotic system that cleans, consolidates or rehouses excavated artifacts.

sources.system: RASCAL (Robotic Arm for Sherds and Ceramics Automated Locomotion)
sources.developer: Temple University Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory with University of Hong Kong
sources.title: RASCAL: Robotic Arm for Sherds and Ceramics Automated Locomotion (ICRA 2021)
sources.claim: RASCAL is the only named robotic system aimed at handling bulk excavated sherds (pick up, transport between weighing/photography stations, store); the published system was validated in simulation rather than by autonomous physical processing of real excavated assemblages.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cataloging/handling of excavated sherds. It would be the closest analogue to robotic bulk-finds processing, but validation is in simulation only, so it cannot substantiate physical completion of washing or rehousing.

sources.system: Hands-Free Heritage automated two-robot scanning system
sources.title: Hands-Free Heritage: Automated 3D Scanning for Cultural Heritage Digitization
sources.claim: An automated two-robot cell (scanner robot plus tray-handling robot) autonomously digitizes cultural-heritage artefacts in a laboratory without handheld operation, showing autonomous, delicate positioning of heritage objects but no cleaning, consolidation or packing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: digital documentation of artifacts. It shows autonomous robotic manipulation of artefact trays in a fixtured lab cell, but involves no material removal or treatment, so it does not carry over to cleaning, mending or rehousing.

sources.system: Cultural relics protection robot (Dunhuang Academy / Chinese Academy of Sciences)
sources.developer: Dunhuang Academy with Chinese Academy of Sciences institutes
sources.title: China Develops Robot for Cultural Relics Protection
sources.claim: The most advanced heritage-conservation field robot reported, developed for the Dunhuang Academy for on-site protection of tomb murals, is remotely operated rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ conservation intervention on fragile painted surfaces. Being remotely operated, it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous cleaning or stabilization of artifacts.

sources.system: Robot-assisted femtosecond laser ablation cleaning system
sources.title: Robot-assisted laser ablation for 3D surfaces. Application for paint removal with ultrashort pulse laser
sources.claim: Robot-mounted laser cleaning can automatically process three-dimensional industrial parts of arbitrary geometry to remove paint layers, operating in fenced industrial cells with pre-known part geometry.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated coating removal. It does not transfer to artifact cleaning: heritage cleaning must stop at an unknown, irreplaceable original surface judged spot by spot on unique objects, and no cited deployment applies this system to excavated artifacts.

tasks.label: Participate in forensic activities, such as tooth and bone structure identification, in conjunction with police departments and pathologists.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Forensic anthropology lab case at a medical examiner's/coroner's office or university lab: unpack and inventory skeletonized or decomposed remains submitted by police, remove residual soft tissue (maceration), lay out the skeleton anatomically, refit fragments, take osteometric measurements with calipers/osteometric board, score morphological traits (pubic symphysis, auricular surface, cranial/pelvic traits, dental development), estimate age/sex/ancestry/stature, and issue a signed report to the ME and investigating agency.

Trauma consultation with a forensic pathologist at the morgue: examine fractured, cut, burned or gunshot-damaged bone at autopsy or after excision, clean and reconstruct the fragmented element with adhesive, distinguish perimortem trauma from postmortem damage and taphonomic artifacts, document with photos/radiographs, and provide an opinion to the pathologist and detectives.

Dental/odontological identification work in the morgue: expose and examine the dentition of a decomposed, burned or fragmentary decedent (sometimes resecting the jaws), position fragile jaws for postmortem radiographs, chart restorations and morphology, and compare against antemortem dental records/radiographs supplied by police for a positive identification.

Outdoor scene recovery with law enforcement: locate and recover remains from a clandestine grave, surface scatter, burned structure or water-margin site; map with total station/GPS, remove overburden and hand-trowel and screen sediment, discriminate bone fragments from rock, roots and debris, recover teeth and small bones, and package with chain of custody in variable weather, vegetation and terrain.

Mass fatality / commingled assemblage work in a temporary or permanent DVI morgue: triage and sort thousands of fragmented, burned or commingled remains, segregate human from nonhuman, re-associate elements, establish minimum number of individuals, sample bone for DNA, and track everything through the DVI case management system.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Bern / University of Zurich (with ARC Seibersdorf)
sources.date: 2010 (paper); Virtobot 2.0 installed Zurich 2012, routine use reported thereafter
sources.title: Virtobot--a multi-functional robotic system for 3D surface scanning and automatic post mortem biopsy - PubMed
sources.claim: Virtobot is a robotic system installed in a forensic medicine institute that performs automated 3D surface scanning of bodies and CT-guided needle placement for postmortem biopsy; its role is documentation and sampling, not osteological examination, handling or interpretation of skeletal elements.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic system operating in the forensic morgue where instances 0-2 and 4 occur. It substantiates only automated imaging/needle sampling of a body on a table; it does not manipulate, measure, refit or diagnostically assess bones or teeth, so it does not substantiate completion of any listed instance.

sources.date: January 2023 (product release announcement); earlier CultArm3D-P from 2019
sources.title: Fraunhofer IGD develops automated robotic arm to scan cultural objects in 3D, now cooperating with Phase One
sources.claim: CultArm3D is a commercially available autonomous robot-arm scanner that produces high-resolution 3D models of fragile cultural objects placed on its turntable in museum settings; it delivers digital documentation only, with no analysis, sorting or physical processing of the object.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic documentation of fragile, irregular heritage objects presented on a fixture, comparable in delicacy to a bone element. It supports only the imaging sub-step; it does not perform maceration, layout, caliper measurement, morphological scoring, trauma interpretation or report issuance, so it cannot complete a forensic identification instance even at E1.

sources.developer: Ca' Foscari University of Venice with EU partners and the Archaeological Park of Pompeii
sources.title: RePAIR: Results and Future Prospects of the Project Integrating Robotics and Artificial Intelligence in the Reassembly of Frescoes at Pompeii
sources.claim: RePAIR built a prototype two-arm robotic system with soft grippers that scans, matches and physically repositions fragile fresco fragments in a laboratory setup at Pompeii, with archaeologists reviewing and correcting the AI's proposed solutions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sorting and re-association of fragile fragments, nearest analogue to commingled/fragmented remains sorting (instance 4). It remains a research prototype requiring expert-in-the-loop correction, works on flat painted plaster in a dedicated rig, and has not been shown on bone or to forensic evidentiary standards, so it cannot substantiate completion.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot (archaeological site documentation deployments) as surveyed
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics; deployed by archaeological teams/ephorates
sources.title: Survey on the Application of Robotics in Archaeology (Sensors, 2025)
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of robotics in archaeology finds robots are used for exploration, mapping and documentation (e.g., Spot at excavation sites for data collection and monitoring), while excavation itself continues to be performed manually by specialized workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work at outdoor/subterranean excavation sites, the setting of instance 3. The surveyed deployments are sensing and documentation platforms; the same review notes 'manual excavation techniques by specialized workers' remain standard, so no cited system substantiates delicate recovery of buried remains.

emergingTasks.label: Write, present, and publish research findings for a variety of specialized and general audiences.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

instances.label: Aerial survey mission over a specified study area (rural/natural or mixed terrain — a watershed, coastline, floodplain, quarry, land-cover mosaic): fly a mapping drone on a planned grid to capture photogrammetric/LiDAR/multispectral data for a DEM, orthomosaic and land-cover map; open airspace, variable wind and light.

Ground topographic/geomorphic survey at an accessible site (graded or excavated ground, quarry, gravel bar, farm field, mine working): collect georeferenced points or terrestrial laser scans along a route with GNSS rover, total station or scanner, walking over mud, rubble and uneven ground.

Ground plot work in wildland or rugged terrain reached on foot: vegetation composition, cover, canopy and tree measurements in forest/rangeland plots, plus hand-instrument readings (soil moisture, slope, aspect, quadrat counts) on steep, brushy, wet or trackless ground away from roads.

Soil/regolith sampling and in-situ soil measurement at prescribed georeferenced points across a field-scale area (agricultural landscape, grassland, tilled or bare ground): extract cores to a set depth, bag and label them by location, record depth-consistent georeferenced data.

Meteorological/atmospheric data collection across a study area: run instrumented transects, take vertical profiles of temperature, humidity and wind, or gather metocean data over water for a specified period; outdoor, weather-exposed, sometimes severe conditions.

Install, service and download fixed field instrumentation at remote sites: carry a tripod weather station, rain gauge, stream gauge or soil-moisture loggers over rough ground, level and anchor the mast, wire sensors, swap batteries/desiccant and retrieve logger data.

sources.title: Mapping floodplains with a high-accuracy survey drone (Septentrio customer story)
sources.claim: WingtraOne VTOL survey drone flies fully autonomous mapping missions, including take-off and landing, producing centimetre-accurate geotagged imagery; used commercially for topographic mapping of natural terrain such as floodplains.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: instrument-based collection of topographic data over a natural study area; floodplain mapping is the geographer's aerial survey at survey-grade accuracy.

sources.title: The Inside Story on Chevron's Autonomous Drone Inspections with Percepto
sources.claim: Percepto operates automated drone-in-a-box systems flying autonomous beyond-visual-line-of-sight missions at mining, utility and energy sites under a nationwide FAA waiver, coordinated remotely; deployed with customers including Chevron.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (unattended autonomous aerial data capture over outdoor sites): the same flight autonomy and imaging payloads generate the terrain models a geographer collects.

sources.title: The drone future is autonomous: Percepto says its ready - DroneDJ
sources.claim: Percepto's autonomous drone flights over mine sites capture imagery that is converted into 3D maps and volumetric measurements ... — terrain-surface measurement with no on-site pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (stockpile/terrain volumetrics) uses the identical measurement chain — photogrammetric survey of ground-surface form over an outdoor area.

sources.system: Spot with Trimble X7 laser scanner
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot legged robots live on construction sites running programmed Autowalk missions that autonomously traverse obstacles and standing water while capturing laser scans (e.g. Trimble X7) for as-built and progress documentation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (survey-grade reality capture on a jobsite) uses the same surveying instruments and route-based scan collection over uneven outdoor ground as a ground geomorphic survey.

sources.title: Leica adds to functionality of Spot the robot dog
sources.claim: Leica's BLK ARC scanning payload on Spot lets users launch an autonomous laser-scanning walk that executes without human intervention, producing survey-grade 3D capture of site conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous terrestrial laser scanning) is precisely surveying-equipment data collection; cited environments include plants, warehouses and enclosed structures ... sites.

sources.title: Emesent - CSIRO
sources.claim: Emesent's Hovermap autonomy/LiDAR payload flies drones autonomously beyond visual line of sight in GPS-denied underground mine workings, automating 3D mapping of stopes and ore passes people cannot safely survey.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous LiDAR mapping of rock excavations) matches collecting data on geological formations: same instrument class, same 3D-form output, harsher unstructured terrain.

sources.title: Autonomous soil sampling: Robo sampling improves accuracy - Top Crop Manager
sources.claim: Rogo's SmartCore robot autonomously drives a field, pulls soil cores at RTK-GPS locations to consistent depth and bags them, returning to the same cores each season.

sources.title: Soil Sampling Goes Robotic – DTN (AgFax)
sources.claim: Rogo has run SmartCore as a commercial soil-sampling service at large scale across Midwest fields, sampling hundreds of thousands of acres per season for dealers and farmers.

sources.developer: EarthSense, Inc. / Corteva / University of Illinois
sources.title: Breaking the field phenotyping bottleneck in maize with autonomous robots (DeBruin et al.)
sources.claim: TerraSentia autonomous under-canopy ground robots collected sensor data from nearly 200,000 experimental plots across 142 research fields in the USA ... over five years, yielding ground-truth-validated plant height, ear height, stem diameter and leaf area index.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (in-field vegetation trait measurement) covers the vegetation-data portion of this task, but the fields are institutionally managed, standard-row research plots, not trackless wildland.

sources.title: NOAA Sends Autonomous Surface Vehicles Into Hurricanes to Study Rapid Intensification - DroneLife
sources.claim: NOAA and Saildrone deploy fleets of wind- and solar-powered uncrewed surface vehicles that sail into hurricanes for months, collecting and transmitting data; the partnership has run every season since 2021, with 10 USVs planned for 2026.

sources.title: Saildrone Partners With NOAA to Study Hurricanes for 5th Year in a Row - Carrier Management

instances.label: Aerial/topographic survey campaign at an outdoor study site: plan and fly a gridded UAS mission over tens to hundreds of hectares (rangeland, dunes, floodplain, burn scar, urban fringe), capture RGB/multispectral/lidar with PPK/RTK georeferencing, and deliver an orthomosaic, point cloud or DEM; includes repeat flights of the same site for change monitoring.

Ground-truth / field verification traverse: drive and walk a study region, reach predetermined sample points across roadsides, farms, woodlots and built-up edges, judge and record land cover/land use class, crop type, disturbance or feature presence, take georeferenced photos and field notes, and negotiate access across property lines and fences.

Georeferenced physical sampling on accessible open ground or water: soil cores collected on a grid or transect across a drivable field or rangeland with samples bagged and labeled by point, or water-quality sampling and bathymetric/hydrographic profiling along planned lines on a lake, reservoir, river reach or nearshore area.

In-situ measurement and description in rough or vegetated terrain: dig and describe a soil pit or streambank exposure, collect sediment, run vegetation quadrats with species identification and cover estimates, survey a stream cross-section and measure discharge with a flow meter, on steep, wooded, wet or trail-less ground.

Installing, servicing and retrieving field instrumentation: site and erect a weather station or camera trap, level and anchor tripods/stakes, wire sensors, deploy water-level and soil-moisture loggers, swap batteries and desiccant, download data on site, and repair storm or vandalism damage.

Human-geography community fieldwork at outdoor sites: walk neighborhoods, markets or informal settlements doing land-use and streetscape inventory, conduct intercept interviews and short surveys with residents and vendors, do participant observation, and walk sites with local officials or landowners.

sources.title: Extensive easy-to-use drone features | Wingtra

sources.title: B-Roll: Field and drone remote sensing operations near Moab, Utah – May 2025 | U.S. Geological Survey
sources.claim: The USGS National Uncrewed Systems Office routinely collects drone data for geographic science field campaigns, e.g. a May 2025 dryland vegetation campaign near Moab with the Western Geographic Science Center; human personnel collected field measurements alongside the drone data.

sources.claim: NOAA's Office of Coast Survey ... Seafloor Systems EchoBoat autonomous surface vehicle to collect hydrographic/bathymetric data in shallow Great Lakes areas; the EchoBoat line navigates survey lines by autonomous wayfinding.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot (with 360 camera / Trimble X7)

sources.system: UAS imagery in rangeland monitoring programs

sources.title: Integrating drone imagery with existing rangeland monitoring programs

instances.label: Archives/historical-society processing room: rehousing an accession of loose manuscripts, letters, clippings and typescripts — removing rusted staples, paper clips and rubber bands, unfolding and interleaving brittle sheets, transferring them in original order into acid-free folders and record cartons, and labeling folders and boxes.

Institutional digitization lab: creating preservation surrogates of bound material (ledgers, minute books, bound newspapers, rare printed volumes) on a cradle scanner so the fragile originals need less handling; includes page-by-page capture, quality control and safe reshelving.

Imaging lab / copy stand: photographing or scanning loose flat items — single-sheet documents, maps, prints and photographic prints and negatives — to make preservation-quality digital surrogates, placing each item, capturing, and returning it to its enclosure.

Conservation bench in a lab or workroom: minor stabilization of items — dry surface cleaning, humidifying and flattening rolled or folded documents, mending tears with Japanese tissue and wheat-starch paste, polyester encapsulation, plus condition surveys and temperature/humidity and mold/pest inspection rounds in the stacks.

Climate-controlled stacks or high-density vault: moving boxed collections into and out of proper storage — shelving new boxes in call-number order, retrieving requested boxes for the reading room, and reshelving them without crushing, mis-filing or exposing them to light and heat.

Objects and off-site work: caring for three-dimensional artifacts in a historic house, gallery or a donor's premises — dusting and condition-checking objects on open display, padding and packing items for transport, and picking up or salvaging records and artifacts from attics, basements, storage units or water-damaged sites.

sources.title: Automatic Book Scanner | Treventus
sources.claim: The Treventus ScanRobot 2.0 MDS is a commercial automatic book scanner that turns pages by air flow and captures images without human page handling, at up to 2,500 pages/hour, in an enclosed purpose-built cradle unit.

sources.title: McFarlin's new ScanRobot protects rare books while increasing access for students, scholars
sources.claim: A US special-collections library (McFarlin Library, University of Tulsa) installed the ScanRobot in 2024-25 explicitly to reduce mechanical handling of fragile rare books; the machine turns pages with air and detects mis-seated books or double page turns, with a certified operator supervising at the control panel.

sources.title: ScanRobot | Image Access GmbH
sources.claim: The ScanRobot has been installed in libraries and archives in more than 60 countries, including national libraries, showing routine institutional deployment rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.system: Smithsonian digitization conveyor (Rapid Capture mass digitization line)
sources.developer: Smithsonian Digitization Program Office / NMNH Botany
sources.title: The digitization conveyor project hits 2 million scans
sources.claim: The Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History ran a purpose-built digitization conveyor line that transported flat archival sheets under a fixed high-speed camera and imaged 3,000-4,000 sheets per day for seven years, completing 3.8 million sheets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mass imaging of mounted herbarium sheets. Transfers to preservation imaging of loose archival sheets — same flat, fragile paper objects, same fixed-camera capture geometry and image-quality requirements, in the same kind of institutional imaging line.

sources.system: Smithsonian Rapid Capture digitization line (National Numismatic Collection)
sources.title: Museums Are Now Able to Digitize Thousands of Artifacts in Just Hours
sources.claim: The same Smithsonian rapid-capture conveyor pipeline was used on paper archival documents from the National Numismatic Collection, with bank note proof sheets carried down the conveyor belt to ....
sources.transferJustification: Confirms the conveyor imaging line handles archival paper documents (bank note proof sheets), not only botanical mounts, so transfer to manuscript/photograph imaging is direct.

sources.title: The Robot - UMKC Libraries
sources.claim: Miller Nichols Library's automated storage and retrieval system (in service since 2010) uses a robotic crane to place and retrieve collection material in bins inside a temperature- and humidity-controlled, light-tight steel rack vault, and the library describes this as a preservation benefit.

sources.title: The Giant Robots That Serve the World's Largest Library Archives
sources.claim: Large library archive facilities use multi-crane automated storage and retrieval systems that store and retrieve bins holding books and historical artifacts.

sources.system: Archive access robot for smart archive repositories
sources.developer: Chinese National Archives Bureau research programme (Industrial Robot, 2022)
sources.title: Archive access robot for smart archive repositories
sources.claim: A mobile archive access robot with a bionic manipulator was built to navigate an existing (unmodified) archive storage room and retrieve archive files from shelves; it was tested in one real archive storage room in Jiangsu, China.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous retrieval/return of archive files in conventional human archive stacks. Bears on whether storage handling could be done at E2, but it is a single pilot covering retrieval only, not condition-aware preservation storage.

sources.title: An Electroadhesive Paper Gripper With Application to a Document-Sorting Robot
sources.claim: A laboratory robot gripper using electroadhesion was developed to pick up single sheets of paper non-destructively for a document-sorting robot; this is component-level paper handling, not an archival processing workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of office paper. It shows only that single clean sheets can be lifted and sorted in a lab; it does not cover fastener removal, unfolding brittle sheets, order preservation or foldering, so it cannot substantiate the rehousing instance.

sources.system: Vision-based cobot system for reconstruction of fragmented documents
sources.title: A Vision Based System for Guided and Collaborative Reconstruction of Fragmented Documents
sources.claim: A cobot with a custom vacuum gripper and machine vision was demonstrated for guided, human-collaborative physical reconstruction of fragmented paper documents in a laboratory workspace, with users assisting in positioning fragments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation of damaged paper for conservation-style reconstruction. It is explicitly guided/collaborative with a human in the loop, so it cannot support autonomous completion of bench conservation work.

roles.description: Work with agricultural scientists in plant, fiber, and animal research, or assist with animal breeding and nutrition. tasks.label: Prepare land for cultivated crops, orchards, or vineyards by plowing, discing, leveling, or contouring.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Primary tillage of a research-station or cooperator field ahead of a trial or crop: chisel plowing, moldboard plowing or discing a mapped 10-80 acre field with a full-size tractor and implement, in fall or spring, with residue, variable soil moisture and known field boundaries.

Secondary tillage and seedbed finishing for small research plots: field cultivating, harrowing, packing and leveling a plot block to a uniform seedbed, working around alleys, borders, flagged corners, irrigation lines and previous-year plot stakes so plots can be laid out and planted on RTK guidance.

Ground preparation in an established orchard or vineyard block: discing or cultivating row middles, ripping and berming planting rows, between trellis posts, drip lines and trunks with narrow tractor clearance.

Land leveling, grading and contouring: laser/GPS leveling a field for flood or furrow irrigation, forming contour beds, borders or terraces, and smoothing rough or newly broken ground with a scraper, land plane or bed former.
Small outdoor areas: preparing nursery beds, high-tunnel beds and garden-scale trial plots with a compact tractor, two-wheel tractor or walk-behind rotary tiller, then raking level.

Indoor greenhouse ground beds and bench/container media preparation in tight quarters: tilling or turning bed soil with a small tiller and hand tools, mixing and leveling media around benches, posts and doorways.

tasks.label: Operate farm machinery, including tractors, plows, mowers, combines, balers, sprayers, earthmoving equipment, or trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tillage and seedbed preparation on a research-station or cooperator production field: technician hitches a field cultivator, disk or chisel plow to a mid-to-large tractor and works the ground to a set depth across a mapped field, working around headlands, waterways and plot stakes, in fall or pre-plant spring windows with variable soil moisture.

Pesticide, herbicide or fertilizer application: technician runs a tractor-drawn boom sprayer, airblast/orchard sprayer or spreader over trial blocks, seed-increase fields, pastures, orchards or vineyards, following prescribed rates, buffers and row spacing, in variable wind and terrain.

Mowing and slashing: rotary/batwing or flail mowing of plot alleys, field borders, pastures, turf/sod blocks, cover crops and fallow ground with a tractor-mounted mower, navigating between fields and around trees, fences and irrigation risers.

Research-plot planting and harvest with specialized plot machinery: cone or belt plot planter loaded packet-by-packet with numbered seed lots, and a self-propelled plot combine that must start/stop per plot, weigh and moisture-test each plot, take and bag a labeled sample, and clean out between plots to avoid seed mixing.

Whole-field harvest with conventional machinery: running a full-size combine through seed-increase or production fields (with header height and loss adjustment for lodged or uneven crop) and running the tractor/grain cart alongside to receive and transfer grain.

Hauling and utility equipment: driving farm trucks or a tractor-trailer with grain, samples, feed or equipment over farm lanes and public rural roads, and running a loader/skid steer/backhoe for material handling, drainage, gravel and earthmoving jobs around the research farm.

tasks.label: Maintain or repair agricultural facilities, equipment, or tools to ensure operational readiness, safety, and cleanliness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-trial bulk sanitation of reusable containers and small gear at a research greenhouse headhouse / lab wash room: hundreds of pots, flats, seedling trays, media pans, plus sample containers, probes and glassware — washed, rinsed, disinfected/autoclaved, dried and returned to stock.

Cleaning and servicing benchtop instruments and work surfaces in an agricultural research lab: wiping benches and fume hoods, cleaning drying ovens, sample grinders/mills and sieves between sample sets, checking and calibrating balances, pH and moisture meters, replacing tubing, filters and worn parts, troubleshooting an instrument that has drifted or stopped.

Servicing and repairing field and plot machinery at a research farm shop: tractors, plot planters and cone seeders, sprayers, plot combines, mowers and ATVs — greasing zerks, oil and filter changes, replacing belts, chains, bearings, nozzles and shear bolts, tire repair, blade sharpening, seed-hopper and threshing cleanout between entries, and wash-down before storage.

Maintaining and repairing facility infrastructure at field stations, greenhouses and barns: irrigation mainlines, drip tape and plugged emitters, growth-chamber lamps, sensors and fans, fences, gates and doors, hoop-house covers, drainage, and minor plumbing and electrical fixes; sweeping and washing floors and walkways.

Daily cleanliness of animal housing at a research dairy, swine or poultry unit: scraping or collecting manure from alleys, slats and pens, keeping floors and bedded areas clean and dry while animals are present.

Between-group washdown and disinfection of animal housing and its equipment: pressure-washing pens, walls and slats, washing removable caging, feeders, waterers and bottles, then applying disinfectant before the next group arrives.

tasks.label: Perform crop production duties, such as tilling, hoeing, pruning, weeding, or harvesting crops.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tractor ground work on research-farm field plots: tilling, discing, bed preparation and between-row cultivation of experimental fields before planting and during the season, on an institution-run research farm with mapped, laid-out plot areas.

Weed control in field research plots: hoeing, hand-pulling and mechanical cultivation of weeds within and between plot rows and alleys on a research farm, without damaging tagged experimental plants, borders or plot stakes.

Harvest of field research plots: running a plot combine or hand-cutting/hand-picking sample rows, keeping each plot's material separate, weighing, bagging and labeling sub-samples, and cleaning out between plots to avoid seed contamination.
Research greenhouse plant establishment: transplanting seedlings/plugs from flats into labeled pots, potting up, and moving/spacing containers on benches for experimental blocks.

Research greenhouse/growth-chamber hand crop work on standing experimental plants: pruning, pinching, deleafing, training/tying, thinning and hand-weeding pots across heterogeneous genotypes and species, plus a minority of uniform high-wire row trials.
Research orchard/vineyard trial blocks: dormant pruning, canopy management, tying and thinning of trees or vines in trellised experimental blocks managed by the station.

tasks.label: Collect animal or crop samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outdoor field research plots (row crops, forage, orchard/vineyard): technician walks staked plots and hand-collects crop samples — leaf tissue/punches, whole plants, ears, heads, pods, stalk sections, tiller counts — into per-plot labeled bags, keeping plot identity and chain of custody, in mud, heat, wind and canopy clutter, often on a tight phenological window.

Greenhouse, headhouse, growth chamber or nursery: technician takes tissue samples from potted or tray-grown plants — leaf punches into 96-well plates for genotyping, cuttings, root or explant tissue, nutrient-analysis leaf sets — matching each sample to a plant ID on a bench of hundreds of plants.

Harvested-commodity sampling at a research farm, seed conditioning plant or elevator: probe or stream sampling of grain from trucks, bins, combine hoppers and seed lots; forage core sampling of bales/silage; subdividing to labeled sample envelopes for moisture, quality and composition testing.

Livestock biological sampling requiring animal handling: blood draws (jugular/coccygeal) from cattle in a chute or headlock, pigs, sheep or poultry; nasal/oral/rectal swabs; fecal grabs; hair, wool, ear-notch or biopsy tissue; semen collection at a stud — done in barns, chutes and pens with animals that move and resist.

Dairy milk sampling: per-cow milk samples taken at milking for herd testing (DHI/milk recording), component analysis, somatic cell counts or mastitis culture, in a parlor or robotic-milking barn, each vial matched to cow ID.

sources.title: Automated plant manipulation system speeds up bioscience research | ORNL
sources.claim: ORNL's SMART Plant 1.0 robotic system autonomously scans a plant presented to it with computer vision, selects a leaf, and excises a uniform live tissue sample with a punch-like tool, depositing it into a petri dish — i.e., machine collection of plant tissue samples at a fixed workstation.

sources.date: 2019-01 (article); technology in production use since late 2000s
sources.title: Seed Chipper lets breeders take a peek at a seed's DNA - Top Crop Manager
sources.claim: Automated seed chipping machines cut a small tissue chip from each individual seed at about one seed per second, with chips tracked to individual seeds for genotyping — high-throughput automated collection of crop tissue samples on presented material in a breeding pipeline.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is single-seed tissue sampling for genotyping; it is the same act as a technician chipping/subsampling seed for a lab, with the seed presented to the machine, and it preserves per-sample identity.

sources.title: Rogo's Self-Driving, Fully Autonomous Soil Sampler Covers 100k Acres in 2019 | AgriTechTomorrow
sources.claim: Rogo's SmartCore robot autonomously navigates commercial row-crop fields, extracts georeferenced cores and delivers identified samples for lab analysis at commercial scale (100,000+ acres/season).
sources.transferJustification: Related task is georeferenced soil-core sampling in open fields: it shows autonomous field navigation, sample extraction and identified sample handling, but the sampled medium is soil, not plant tissue or animal material, so the plant-manipulation part of crop sampling is not covered.

tasks.label: Examine animals or crop specimens to determine the presence of diseases or other problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scouting a commercial row-crop field (corn, soybean, wheat, cotton): walking or driving transects, examining leaves, stems and stands for lesions, insect feeding, nutrient deficiency and stand loss, and reporting which problems are present and at what threshold. Open field, variable weather, mud, weeds and volunteer plants.

Inspecting plants in a greenhouse, nursery, growth chamber or headhouse: walking benches or gutter rows, scoring disease severity and pest incidence on individual plants, checking sticky cards and undersides of leaves, and recording ratings for a trial or production block. Fixed layout, controlled access, standard benches/rails.

Examining collected specimens in a diagnostic or research laboratory: preparing leaf/tissue/fecal/milk/blood samples, microscopy of slides, plating and reading cultures, running immunoassay or PCR panels, and reporting presence or absence of the pathogen or parasite. Institution-controlled bench lab with standard equipment.

Checking dairy cows in a research or commercial barn for health problems: observing individual cows, checking udders/milk for mastitis, flagging off-feed, lame or sick animals and recording findings for the herd health record. Freestall barn with alleys, headlocks and a milking area.

Walking a poultry house (broiler or layer flock) to assess flock health: spotting sick, lame or dead birds, checking litter condition, droppings and bird distribution, and reporting mortality and disease signs. Enclosed house, standard equipment lines, controlled biosecure access.

Examining swine in confinement pens or beef cattle in feedlot pens/pasture: moving through pens observing gait, breathing, appetite and lesions, pulling and restraining suspect animals for closer inspection, and recording suspected disease. Dusty, crowded pens or open pasture with loose, unrestrained animals.
