tasks.label: Conduct chemical or physical laboratory tests to assist scientists in making qualitative or quantitative analyses of solids, liquids, or gaseous materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pharma/chemical/petrochemical QC lab: routine assay, purity or composition testing of liquid or readily dissolved samples. Technician logs the sample, weighs a portion, dissolves/dilutes in volumetric glassware, filters into 2 mL vials, loads the HPLC/GC/ICP autosampler, runs the validated method, checks system suitability and reports the result to LIMS.

Contract environmental, food or waste testing lab: heterogeneous field samples (soil, sludge, filter cartridges, foodstuffs, wastewater) arriving in assorted jars and bottles. Technician homogenizes, weighs, digests or solvent-extracts, cleans up with classical glassware, then analyzes by ICP-MS/GC-MS against EPA/AOAC methods, with matrix spikes and duplicates.

Instrumented benchtop determinations in a QC lab: acid-base or Karl Fischer titration, pH/conductivity, moisture/loss-on-drying, ash in a muffle furnace, colorimetric/UV-Vis assay. Sample containers sit on the bench; the technician weighs aliquots, prepares reagents, runs the benchtop instrument and records results.

Physical/mechanical/rheological property testing of solids and viscous products in a materials or polymer lab: tensile and flexure tests, hardness, melt flow index, viscosity, density, particle size, on specimens and pellets that must be conditioned, measured and mounted.

R&D lab support: running a screening or characterization campaign for scientists — preparing a series of samples or formulations, executing the treatment/reaction step, then characterizing by LC-MS, NMR, XRD or thermal analysis and tabulating results; occasionally assembling a non-standard apparatus for a one-off test.

Plant/process at-line lab (refinery, cement, steel, chemical plant): rapid-turnaround tests on process samples delivered from the line, using a fixed set of methods (XRF/OES, distillation, flash point, fineness), with results fed back to production within minutes.

tasks.label: Maintain, clean, or sterilize laboratory instruments or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Washing a batch of dirty labware at the end of a run: beakers, volumetric flasks, vials, sample cups, sieves and stir bars are solvent-rinsed or scraped, either hand-scrubbed at the lab sink or racked into a lab glassware washer, then dried, inspected for residue/cracks, and returned to storage.

Running the instrument's own cleaning/flush operations: flushing HPLC/UHPLC lines and autosampler needles with solvent, washing sample probes and cuvettes on an analyzer, purging/conditioning columns, cleaning an MS ion source, rinsing an ICP nebulizer/spray chamber between sample sets.

Preventive maintenance requiring disassembly and part replacement on analytical instruments: swapping GC inlet liners, septa and ferrules, trimming/replacing chromatography columns, changing HPLC pump seals, frits and in-line filters, replacing pH/conductivity electrodes, pulling and hand-cleaning an MS source or a torch, then leak-checking and verifying performance.

Sterilizing and decontaminating: loading glassware, media bottles, tools and biohazard/chemical waste into an autoclave or washer-disinfector, selecting and running the cycle, verifying indicators, and unloading hot items.

Cleaning and decontaminating fixed work areas and small shared equipment: wiping down benches and fume-hood/biosafety-cabinet interiors, cleaning balance pans and hot plates, mopping up chemical spills, wiping sample-prep tools and spatulas, in a lab where instruments, reagents and glassware are sitting out.

Cleaning process-scale or pilot-plant equipment served by the QC lab: reactor and tank interiors, transfer piping, sampling lines and probes, mills and sieves, between batches, followed by rinse-sample verification.

tasks.label: Monitor product quality to ensure compliance with standards and specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: QC lab batch / finished-product testing: technician weighs and preps a sample (dilution, filtration, vialing), runs a bench or instrument method (titration, HPLC/GC, moisture, viscosity, spectroscopy) in a lab built for people, integrates the result, compares it to the product specification, and records pass/fail or flags an OOS. Standard glassware, balances, human-scale instruments.

In-process monitoring: technician walks onto the production floor, draws a grab sample from a reactor port/valve/hopper into a labelled container, carries it to the at-line or QC lab, runs a quick conformance test (pH, density, particle size, assay), and reports back so operators can adjust the process. Plant floor with PPE, valves, ladders, hot/hazardous streams.

Routine monitoring round: technician tours the plant/lab checking local gauges, panel readouts, online analyzer values and sample-point conditions against expected ranges, logs readings, verifies instrument status/calibration due dates, and flags out-of-range trends for follow-up.

Physical/visual conformance inspection of finished product and packaging: appearance, color, clarity/particulates, fill level or net weight, seal and label correctness on units pulled from the line or presented in trays; defective units rejected and results logged against the spec.

Incoming raw material / bulk shipment verification: sampling a tank truck, railcar, drum or bulk-solids load at the receiving bay, then running identity and purity tests (NIR/Raman ID, moisture, assay) and releasing or rejecting the lot against the material spec.

Field / environmental compliance sampling: driving to an outfall, well, pond, stack or client site taken as found, collecting samples with the correct preservation and chain-of-custody, then analyzing them and reporting against permit limits.

sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A mobile robot autonomously operated analytical instrument stations in an ordinary wet-chemistry laboratory, running 688 experiments over eight days including dispensing, sample handling and instrument-based measurement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous photocatalyst optimization. Transfer to QC testing rests on the same objects and precision (vials, solid/liquid dispensing, sonication, loading and reading an analytical instrument) in the same kind of human-built laboratory, which is what a routine conformance test requires.

tasks.label: Set up and conduct chemical experiments, tests, and analyses, using techniques such as chromatography, spectroscopy, physical or chemical separation techniques, or microscopy.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine QC assay in a pharma, food or consumer-products quality-control lab: weigh solid or liquid sample, dissolve/sonicate, dilute, filter into autosampler vials, prepare calibration standards and controls, run an HPLC/GC/UV sequence with system suitability, integrate peaks and report against specification.

Environmental or contract testing lab: acid digestion of soil/dust or liquid-liquid/solid-phase extraction of water samples, spiking of QC and matrix spikes, dilution series, then ICP-MS or GC-MS analysis with calibration curve and reporting of results.

Plant/production support lab (cement, mining, steel, polymers, fuels): process samples received or grabbed at-line, prepared by crushing, milling, pressing, fusion or dilution, then analyzed by XRF, OES, titration or moisture/density methods with results returned quickly to production.

R&D support: run a screening or formulation campaign for a scientist — set up a series of reactions or mixtures on a bench/automated platform and characterize the products by chromatography (LC-MS/GC) and spectroscopy (NMR, UV-vis, XRD), then summarize which conditions worked.

Non-routine setup work: assemble bespoke apparatus (reflux/distillation rig, extraction train, glovebox or electrochemical cell), adapt a method to a new matrix, or change over an instrument — install and equilibrate a new HPLC column, prepare and degas mobile phase, replace GC liner/septum, calibrate and troubleshoot before running samples.

Microscopy and physical characterization: mount, section, grind/polish, stain or sputter-coat a specimen, then examine it under optical or electron microscope, capture images and make measurements (grain size, particle count, inclusions, defects) for a report.

tasks.label: Prepare chemical solutions for products or processes, following standardized formulas, or create experimental formulas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine reagent/standard solution prep in a QC or analytical lab: read the SOP formula, weigh a solid reagent or primary standard on an analytical balance, dissolve in a beaker, transfer quantitatively to a 250 mL-2 L volumetric flask, dilute to the mark, mix, label and log the solution (sometimes standardize by titration).

Preparing calibration standards, spiking solutions and serial dilutions from liquid stock solutions for instrument analysis (HPLC/GC/ICP): pipetting microliter-to-milliliter volumes into vials, tubes or flasks, diluting with solvent, capping and mixing.

Bulk/production-scale solution or batch preparation in a plant or pilot area: charging water/solvent to a mixing tank or drum, dosing acids, caustics, colorants or additives to a standardized batch formula, adding bagged powders, agitating, sampling and adjusting to spec, in PPE.

R&D formulation development in an industrial lab (coatings, adhesives, personal care, lubricants): building multi-component experimental formulas from powders, pastes and viscous liquids in 50-500 mL vessels, heating and stirring, checking pH/viscosity and iterating toward target properties.

Creating arrays of experimental solution formulas in a research lab to explore a composition space: dispensing small quantities of solids and stock solutions into vials at chemist- or algorithm-specified concentrations, capping, sonicating/mixing, and passing them on for testing.

Preparing hazardous, air-sensitive or specialty solutions: concentrated acids/bases or volatile solvents in a fume hood, or moisture-sensitive reagents and electrolytes weighed and dissolved inside an inert-atmosphere glovebox.

tasks.label: Provide and maintain a safe work environment by participating in safety programs, committees, or teams and by conducting laboratory or plant safety audits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Safety program/committee participation inside the employer's facility: attending EHS or chemical-hygiene committee meetings, reviewing incident and near-miss reports, updating SOPs/JHAs and chemical hygiene plans, giving toolbox talks, and tracking corrective-action items to closure. Office/conference-room work with facility-controlled access.

Scheduled laboratory safety audit walkthrough of an R&D or QC lab against a checklist: verifying eyewash/shower access and inspection tags, extinguisher tags, chemical storage segregation and labeling, secondary containment, fume hood sash and flow indicator, satellite waste accumulation, aisle/egress clearance and PPE stocks; photographing and writing up deficiencies with owners and due dates.

Routine plant or pilot-plant safety round through process areas, tank farms and utility rooms: walking a fixed route to look, listen and smell for leaks, spills, hot spots, corrosion, abnormal gauge/level readings and noisy pumps, logging readings, and flagging anomalies to operations and EHS. Indoor/outdoor industrial site under company control, often classified (Ex) areas.

On-the-spot hazard correction and staff engagement during an audit: clearing a blocked eyewash or exit, re-labeling or re-segregating incompatible containers, wiping a small spill, restocking spill kit and PPE, tagging out defective equipment, and questioning lab or plant staff about practices before recording the finding as closed.

Functional testing of emergency and safety equipment on a schedule: activating and flushing eyewash stations and safety showers and verifying flow/temperature, checking extinguisher pressure/pin/seal and signing tags, measuring fume hood face velocity with an anemometer, bump-testing portable and fixed gas detectors, and testing alarms; results signed onto tags and logs.

tasks.label: Provide technical support or assistance to chemists or engineers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine analytical support in an R&D or QC lab: a chemist or engineer submits samples with a requested method; the technician logs them in, preps them (weighing, dissolution, dilution, filtration, aliquoting into vials/plates), runs the standard instrument method (HPLC/GC-MS/ICP/UV-Vis/titration/XRD), checks QC standards, processes the chromatograms/spectra and reports results back to the requester.

Preparing the materials a chemist's or engineer's experiment needs: making up reagents, buffers, calibration standards and stock solutions from bottled chemicals; weighing solids, diluting to volume, labelling and storing; laying out and assembling the labware/glassware and racks for the run; restocking consumables and handling the resulting waste.

Equipment support at a scientist's request: setting up and calibrating instruments (balances, pH meters, detectors), swapping HPLC columns, septa, tubing and fittings, chasing down leaks and baseline problems, running system-suitability checks, installing or modifying a piece of apparatus, and troubleshooting an instrument that failed mid-run.

Routine plant or pilot-plant rounds performed for process engineers: walking a fixed route through the unit, reading gauges and local panels, checking for leaks, noise and hot spots, and logging the readings/observations into the engineer's data sheet.

Hands-on pilot-plant/production support during an engineer's trial: drawing samples from sample points and reactors into bottles, connecting hoses and lines, changing filters or feed drums, adjusting valves and set points on instruction, and carrying samples back to the lab for analysis.

Ad hoc bench assistance on a scientist's non-routine project: building a one-off reaction or test rig, running an unfamiliar procedure alongside the chemist, adapting a method when something behaves unexpectedly, fetching and handling odd materials, and recording observations for the scientist.

tasks.label: Develop or conduct programs of sampling and analysis to maintain quality standards of raw materials, chemical intermediates, or products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine instrumental analysis of incoming raw-material, intermediate or finished-product samples in a plant or contract QC lab: log the sample, weigh/dissolve/dilute an aliquot, filter and vial it, run HPLC/GC/ICP/XRF/FTIR, check the result against spec and record it in LIMS.

Drawing the samples out in the plant or warehouse: reactor and pipeline sample ports, tank trucks and rail cars at the receiving dock, drums/totes/bags in the raw-material warehouse; PPE and purge procedures, sample thief or bomb, filling, capping, labelling and carrying the sample to the lab.

Routine wet-chemistry and physical-property QC tests on in-process and finished product at the lab bench: potentiometric titration, Karl Fischer moisture, pH, density, viscosity, loss-on-drying, sieve/particle size; multiple lots per shift, retains kept and results logged against spec.

Keeping the analytical program running: preparing calibration standards and control samples, calibrating/standardizing balances, titrators and instruments, running system-suitability and check standards, and charting control data.

Developing the sampling and analysis program itself: setting sampling points, frequencies and plans for a new material or process, developing and validating a test method, writing the SOP, and investigating out-of-spec or drifting results with production and QA.

tasks.label: Train new employees on topics such as the proper operation of laboratory equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench-side, one-on-one orientation of a newly hired technician on a routine analytical instrument (HPLC, GC, ICP, titrator, balance) in a QC or R&D lab: explaining startup/shutdown, sample introduction, calibration and sequence setup, then talking the trainee through their first runs and answering questions.

Classroom or desk-side instruction on written procedures: SOPs, chemical hygiene and safety plans, PPE and waste-handling rules, LIMS data entry and GLP/GMP documentation practices, delivered with manuals, slides, and a computer.
Observing a trainee perform a method independently, critiquing technique and troubleshooting habits, then completing competency assessment and training-record sign-off for the quality system.
Small-group training session for several technicians on a newly installed instrument or revised method, coordinating with the vendor applications specialist and fielding questions.
Training in a pilot plant, production area, or field setting: process analyzers, on-line samplers, environmental sampling gear and grab-sample protocols, taught while walking the unit or site.

tasks.label: Order and inventory materials to maintain supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine stock check of the lab bench areas and stockroom: walk the shelves for reagents, solvents, standards, columns, glassware and consumables, note which items are low or near expiry, record levels in a spreadsheet/inventory system, and enter a requisition or purchase order with the usual vendors.

Periodic (annual/semiannual) full chemical inventory audit required by EHS: open flammables/acid cabinets, refrigerators, freezers and fume hoods, handle and read the label/barcode of every container, estimate remaining volume, check expiry, reconcile each container against the chemical inventory database.

Receiving a shipment: unpack cartons of reagent bottles, kits and consumables, verify contents and lot numbers against the packing slip, barcode/log items into inventory, then transport and shelve each item in its correct storage location (flammables cabinet, corrosive cabinet, fridge, freezer, general shelf).
Replenishment run: fetch requested consumables (tip racks, gloves, vials, PPE, wipes, solvent bottles) from the central stockroom or receiving dock and transport them to the lab that needs them.
Point-of-use stocking: place the fetched consumables into their designated bench, drawer, cart and cabinet locations, rotate older stock forward, and top up par levels at each workstation.

Bulk and hazardous supply management: track and swap compressed gas cylinders for GC/AA instruments, move solvent drums and carboys, refill/exchange liquid nitrogen dewars, and stage empties for vendor pickup while keeping the cylinder/bulk log current.

sources.title: Automated handling of heavy gas cylinders - Photoneo
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile manipulator with 3D vision picks and places heavy gas cylinders into baskets for order preparation in an industrial gas facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cylinder picking and staging. Same objects and weights as lab cylinder management, demonstrated in a controlled industrial cylinder yard with cylinders presented in standard baskets.

tasks.label: Operate experimental pilot plants, assisting with experimental design.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Continuous experimental unit campaign in an R&D pilot hall (e.g., fixed-bed catalyst test unit, hydroprocessing skid, or continuous flow/crystallization train): technician lines up the unit, starts feeds, sets flows/temperatures/pressures per the run matrix, watches the DCS, pulls periodic liquid/gas samples for online or offline GC, trims conditions as the engineer's matrix directs, then shuts down and hands over the data package.

Batch/semi-batch pilot reactor campaign (roughly 100-1,000 L glass-lined or stainless reactor): charge solvents by pump and solids from bags/drums/totes through a manway or charge chute, run heat/cool and addition profiles, take in-process samples, quench, transfer to filter/centrifuge and dryer, drum off product, then wash out and prepare for the next batch.

Rounds during a running experiment: walk the unit, line up manual valves, read gauges and sight glasses, draw process samples into bottles at sample taps, carry them to the lab and run in-process analyses (GC, HPLC, titration, moisture), log results on the run sheet/ELN, and flag deviations to the engineer.

Between-campaign changeover, maintenance and troubleshooting in the pilot plant: reconfigure tubing/piping and swap fittings, load or dump a catalyst bed, replace filters, gaskets and pump seals, pressure- and leak-test, calibrate transmitters and mass-flow controllers, and clear plugged or fouled lines.

Assisting with experimental design and executing the revised plan: review prior run data with the process engineer, propose condition ranges and a DOE/run matrix, write run sheets and take part in the safety review, then execute the modified condition set on the unit and report results.

sources.title: AlphaFlow: autonomous discovery and optimization of multi-step chemistry using a self-driven fluidic lab guided by reinforcement learning
sources.claim: AlphaFlow is a self-driven fluidic platform that autonomously runs multi-step chemistry in a purpose-built modular flow reactor, with in-situ monitoring and reinforcement learning selecting the next experimental conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation of a small continuous chemistry unit with online analysis and algorithmic selection of the next run conditions. This is the core of operating an experimental continuous unit while assisting experimental design; fluids, pumps, valves and inline analytics are the same class of hardware, though at far smaller scale than a pilot plant.

sources.system: Automated continuous crystallization platform with self-optimization
sources.developer: Pfizer Worldwide Research and Development (Chemical R&D, Groton)
sources.title: Automated self-optimization of continuous crystallization of nirmatrelvir API
sources.claim: Pfizer process R&D built a custom automated continuous crystallization platform coupled to self-optimization algorithms that automatically optimized the continuous crystallization of the nirmatrelvir API.
sources.transferJustification: Continuous crystallization is a standard pilot-plant unit operation; the cited platform runs the unit, measures product attributes and chooses the next conditions, which is exactly 'operate an experimental unit while assisting experimental design' in a purpose-built, plumbed setting.

sources.title: Autonomous optimisation of a nanoparticle catalysed reduction reaction in continuous flow
sources.claim: An autonomous continuous-flow platform pumped reagents into a tubular reactor and analysed the reactor outlet inline, closing the loop to optimize a nanoparticle-catalysed reaction without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sampling/analysis of a running reactor stream and automatic adjustment of conditions, i.e. the sampling-and-analysis and condition-trimming steps of pilot unit operation, executed with the analytics plumbed to the unit.

sources.system: FKDPP reinforcement learning AI plant control
sources.title: In a World First, Yokogawa and JSR Use AI to Autonomously Control a Chemical Plant for 35 Consecutive Days
sources.claim: Reinforcement-learning AI autonomously controlled distillation columns at an operating JSR chemical plant for 35 consecutive days, manipulating real control valves under conditions conventional PID/APC could not handle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous supervisory control of a distillation unit. It substantiates the monitoring-and-setpoint-control portion of running an experimental unit, but only where the plant's valves are already actuated and plumbed; it performs no sampling, charging or hands-on work.

sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Ceder/Zeng) with Google DeepMind
sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of novel materials
sources.claim: The A-Lab performed autonomous solid-state synthesis campaigns for 17 continuous days in an enclosed robotic cell, dosing powders, heating, characterizing by XRD and using ML to plan and interpret the next experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous end-to-end powder synthesis campaigns (dose solids, thermally process, characterize, decide next experiment) inside a purpose-built cell. It shows solids handling can be automated, but only at gram scale with fixtured crucibles, not at pilot batch scale; some of its phase-identification claims were later contested.

sources.title: Autonomous continuous flow reactor synthesis for scalable atom-precision (review citing the Liverpool mobile robotic chemist)
sources.claim: A mobile robotic chemist working in a laboratory built for humans autonomously ran 688 photocatalysis experiments over eight days, choosing its own experiments with a Bayesian optimization algorithm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running an experimental campaign and selecting the next experiments in a human-built lab. It substantiates autonomous experiment-design assistance, but at vial/flask scale with lab instruments, not the kilogram-scale vessels, hoses and drums of a pilot plant.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry
sources.title: AI-driven mobile robots team up to tackle chemical synthesis
sources.claim: Two AI-driven mobile robots carried out exploratory synthetic chemistry in a standard human chemistry laboratory, running reactions, analysing products and deciding what to ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile-robot execution of a chemistry campaign in a facility laid out for people. It shows E2-style lab work is feasible at bench scale, but the objects handled are vials and standard benchtop instruments, not pilot-plant valves, hoses, drums or reactors.

sources.title: ANYmal X Tested for Autonomous Robot Inspections in Ex-zones at BASF
sources.claim: ANYmal X, an Ex-certified legged robot, autonomously performs inspection rounds through multi-level explosion-hazard zones of BASF's Ludwigshafen steamcracker and Oxo plant, collecting trend and anomaly data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operator rounds in a chemical process facility. It covers navigation and gauge/anomaly reading in an E2 plant, but the robot has no manipulator and does not draw samples, line up valves or run analyses.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot Arm turns valves, flips levers and opens doors only semi-autonomously, with an operator pointing the robot at the target or pressing a button, or by direct telemanipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulation of plant hardware by a mobile robot. The vendor's own description shows the manipulation is operator-initiated, so it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous valve line-ups, sampling or maintenance in a pilot plant.

sources.title: Modular, multi-robot integration of laboratories: an autonomous workflow for solid-state chemistry
sources.claim: A fully autonomous modular workflow linked a Chemspeed FLEX liquid-handling platform with mobile robots to prepare crystalline materials and collect their powder diffraction data across a 12-step, multi-instrument sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sample preparation plus automated analysis and data capture. It substantiates the sample-to-result and logging loop when the analytics are integrated with the synthesis platform, at lab (gram) scale.

tasks.label: Design or fabricate experimental apparatus to develop new products or processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench-scale reaction/test rig in an R&D chemistry lab: technician lays out and assembles a custom apparatus in a fume hood for trialing a new formulation or process — reactor or round-bottom flask, condenser, stirrer/heater, thermocouple and septa, gas and coolant lines, clamped to a lattice or stand — then leak-checks and shakes it down before first run.

Custom part fabrication: technician designs a bracket, sample holder, flow cell, window fixture or adapter in CAD or a sketch and produces it — 3D print, mill/lathe, drill and tap, cut to size — then deburrs, checks fit and dimensions, and hands off a finished one-off part for the experimental setup.

Plumbed flow / gas-handling rig for process development: cut and bend tubing, make up compression and threaded fittings, install valves, regulators, pumps, mass-flow controllers and pressure transducers on a board or frame, then pressure/leak test the assembled circuit.

Larger structural fabrication for pilot-scale or field apparatus: cut and weld a steel stand, cart, skid frame or enclosure, bolt up mounts for pumps, vessels and heaters, so a scale-up unit can be built on it in the shop or pilot plant bay.

In-situ retrofit/modification of existing equipment: add a custom port, bracket, sampling line or sensor to an installed analyzer, oven, hood or reactor already in service — drill and mount, route and terminate wiring to a DAQ, seal penetrations, and verify signals — working around the machine in place.

sources.system: OptoMate (UFACTORY xArm7 + LLM design agent + fine-alignment tool)
sources.title: AI-Driven Robotics for Free-Space Optics (arXiv:2505.17985)
sources.claim: OptoMate (MIT) generates a benchtop optical experiment design with a fine-tuned LLM, then autonomously assembles the setup with a 7-DoF xArm7 and fine-aligns it with a robot-deployable motorized Allen-key tool before running measurements; components are pre-housed in custom 3D-printed casings with ArUco markers on magnetic bases, with external stereo cameras around the workspace.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: designing and building a benchtop experimental apparatus (free-space optics rather than chemistry). Transfer holds for the assembly step — bench-scale rigid lab components placed to sub-mm accuracy on a table, then adjusted by turning fine-adjustment knobs, then used to take data — which is the same class of manipulation as erecting a bench reaction/test rig; note the components had to be re-housed in robot-specific fixtures with fiducials.

sources.system: Robotic flow-synthesis platform (modular reactor/separator units + robotic arm)
sources.developer: MIT (Coley, Jensen, Jamison et al.), published in Science
sources.title: A robotic platform for flow synthesis of organic compounds informed by AI planning | Science
sources.claim: An MIT robotic flow-chemistry platform autonomously reconfigures its own apparatus: a robotic arm plugs modular reactor and separator units into a rack to build a continuous flow path matching a computer-generated route, which was then used to make many different target compounds.
sources.transferJustification: This is the task itself in a purpose-built form: the robot builds (reconfigures) the experimental reaction apparatus — reactors, separators and fluid path — required to develop a new synthesis process, with connections made robotically and the resulting rig then run under pressure and flow.

sources.system: Path Robotics AF-1 and AW-3 robotic welding cells
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding – The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics sells autonomous welding cells that scan incoming parts, generate weld paths without programming, and in the AF-1 configuration pick, fit up and weld parts with no human intervention; the cells are installed in fabrication shops in the US and Canada.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix, low-volume steel fabrication in job shops. Transfer holds for fabricating one-off stands, carts, skids and enclosures for experimental apparatus — same steel parts, same fit-up-and-weld operations, and the system handles new part geometries by scanning rather than by per-part programming.

sources.system: Hadrian autonomous machining factory / factory-as-a-service production cell
sources.title: Report: Hadrian Business Breakdown & Founding Story | Contrary Research
sources.claim: Hadrian operates highly automated machining factories combining CNC machines and robotics with its own software; the machining fleet runs unattended overnight and is set up the same way whether producing one part or a hundred, and a Hadrian machining-and-inspection cell is being embedded in a Lockheed Martin plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: one-off and small-batch precision machining of metal parts to aerospace tolerances. Transfer holds for machining a custom bracket, holder, flow cell or adapter for lab apparatus — same materials, tighter tolerances than lab hardware requires, and the same CAD-to-part workflow with robotic loading in a fenced cell.

sources.title: Formlabs Automation Ecosystem | Formlabs
sources.claim: Formlabs sells Form Auto, a hardware extension that automatically removes finished parts ... and starts the next print, enabling unattended 24/7 production of custom parts from digital designs on a printer fleet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended additive manufacture of one-off custom parts. Transfer holds directly — chemical technicians routinely 3D print holders, adapters and fixtures for experimental apparatus, and the machine produces the designed part and clears the build platform without an operator.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA KMR iiwa mobile manipulator)
sources.title: Self-driving labs are changing how chemists work – C&EN
sources.claim: The Liverpool mobile robotic chemist, a KUKA mobile manipulator, worked inside an ordinary chemistry laboratory, moving between workstations to pick up vials, operate instruments and dispense liquids and solids for days at a time — experiment execution, not construction of apparatus.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E2 case: this is the leading example of a robot working in a standard human chemistry lab, and its demonstrated repertoire is sample handling and instrument operation, not designing, building or plumbing new apparatus.

tasks.label: Develop new chemical engineering processes or production techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench-scale process development in an industrial/R&D chemistry lab: technician runs reaction-condition screens (catalyst, solvent, temperature, stoichiometry, time) in standard glassware or a jacketed lab reactor in a fume hood, quenches, works up (filtration/extraction), samples for HPLC/GC/NMR, records data and iterates toward an improved route for a candidate process.

Formulation / product-technique development trials in a lab: weigh powders and liquids, disperse/blend/homogenize multi-component mixtures, test performance and properties (activity, viscosity, particle size, stability), and iterate the recipe toward a producible formulation.

Pilot-plant scale-up runs (roughly 10–1000 L): charge solids and drums, connect hoses and nitrogen lines, operate valves, pumps, filters, centrifuges and dryers, draw samples from sample ports during the run, adjust conditions, troubleshoot upsets, and clean down between trials of a new process.

Plant-floor trial of a new production technique on an operating manufacturing line: set up trial conditions on existing production equipment with operators, pull in-process samples, adjust settings between batches/lots, troubleshoot deviations, and verify trial product meets specification.

Building or modifying bench apparatus for a new process: assemble tubing, fittings, pumps, sensors and reactor modules into a custom rig, leak-test and pressure-check, calibrate instruments, and integrate inline analytics before development runs begin.

Continuous-flow process development on a bench flow rig: prime pumps and reagent lines, vary flow rate, residence time, temperature and stoichiometry with inline/online analysis, and converge on an optimized continuous production recipe.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA KMR iiwa based)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A free-roaming mobile robot autonomously ran 688 photocatalyst-mixture experiments over eight days in a wet chemistry laboratory, choosing its own next experiments with Bayesian optimization and using human-designed lab instruments, improving formulation activity six-fold.
sources.transferJustification: The demonstrated work is formulation/condition development (multi-component photocatalyst mixtures, ten variables) with autonomous decision-making — the same activity as lab-scale development of a new chemical recipe, using the same dosing, mixing and analysis operations.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robotic chemists (exploratory synthesis workflow)
sources.title: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry | Nature
sources.claim: Two mobile robots integrated a conventional synthesis laboratory into an autonomous laboratory, operating shared human lab instruments (LC-MS, benchtop NMR, Chemspeed synthesizer) and making experiment decisions across exploratory synthetic chemistry campaigns.

sources.developer: University of Liverpool (Brass, Ward, Cooper et al.)
sources.title: A mobile robotic process chemist | Digital Discovery | Royal Society of Chemistry
sources.claim: A mobile robot working in a standard fume hood ran late-stage process chemistry unattended: process-scale synthesis in an automated reactor, filtration work-up, transport of vials across the lab to a UHPLC-MS, and reactor cleaning between runs, at human-level reaction performance.

sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of novel materials (abstract)
sources.claim: The A-Lab, an enclosed robotic solid-state synthesis facility (robotic arms, powder dosing, furnaces, automated XRD), autonomously proposed, executed and revised synthesis recipes, realizing 41 novel compounds from 58 targets in 17 days of continuous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Developing and iterating a solid-state synthesis recipe (dosing, milling, heating profile, product verification) is process/production-technique development for a material, using the same class of unit operations and analytical acceptance as lab process development.

sources.title: Automated Formulation Development - FORMAX from CHEMSPEED
sources.claim: Commercially sold robotic formulation workstations perform gravimetric dispensing of solids, powders, liquids ... into formulation vessels and carry out development, optimization and characterization of ... without manual intervention.

sources.system: Robotic flow synthesis platform (AI route planning + reconfigurable modules)
sources.title: A robotic platform for flow synthesis of organic compounds informed by AI planning | Science
sources.claim: A robotic flow-chemistry platform used a robotic arm to automatically reconfigure modular fluidic unit operations into the rig required for each AI-planned synthetic route, then executed the reaction.

sources.system: Self-optimising flow reactor with online HPLC
sources.title: Enhanced process development using automated continuous reactors by self-optimisation algorithms and statistical empirical modelling
sources.claim: A self-optimising continuous flow reactor with online HPLC autonomously searched reaction conditions and optimized the yield of a Claisen-Schmidt condensation directly at mesoscale, producing 0.24 kg/day of product.

roles.description: Perform laboratory and field tests to monitor the environment and investigate sources of pollution, including those that affect health, under the direction of an environmental scientist, engineer, or other specialist. May collect samples of gases, soil, water, and other materials for testing.

tasks.label: Collect samples of gases, soils, water, industrial wastewater, or asbestos products to conduct tests on pollutant levels or identify sources of pollution.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Surface-water sampling: grab and depth-integrated samples from streams, rivers, ponds, lakes/reservoirs and stormwater outfalls, taken by wading, from banks/bridges or a small boat; multiple preserved bottles, field parameters, chain of custody; access, weather and bank conditions taken as found.

Routine compliance sampling of municipal and industrial wastewater inside a treatment plant or permitted facility: influent, effluent and pretreatment points, 24-hour flow-paced composites and grabs collected at fixed, plumbed sampling stations on plant premises.

Groundwater monitoring-well sampling at remediation, landfill and UST sites: locate and open flush-mount/stickup wells, gauge water level, purge with a low-flow pump while watching field parameters, then fill preserved bottles; wells sit in yards, gravel lots, roadsides and fields.

Soil and sediment sampling at contaminated or built-up sites: surface grabs and shallow hand-auger/direct-push cores on industrial and urban parcels, stockpiles and landfill cover, plus stream sediment; pavement, fill, debris, utilities and variable depth requirements.

Air and gas sampling: filters, canisters and sorbent tubes at ambient monitoring stations; 8-24 hour indoor-air canisters set in occupied buildings; landfill gas probes; stack/duct and fenceline sampling at industrial plants.

Bulk sampling of suspect asbestos-containing materials (and lead paint chips) during building surveys: cutting or scraping small plugs from wall board, pipe and boiler insulation, floor tile, mastic and roofing in occupied homes, schools and commercial buildings, wetting and patching the sample point.

sources.system: OceanAlpha ESM30 autonomous water sampling and monitoring USV
sources.title: Autonomous Reservoir Water Quality Monitoring with USVs | UST
sources.claim: OceanAlpha ESM30 autonomous water sampling and monitoring ... have been procured and operated since 2017 by Hong Kong's Water Supplies Department to collect water samples and water-quality data on an open impounding reservoir, navigating with GPS and obstacle avoidance.

sources.date: product page, accessed 2026-07 (product line marketed since ~2018)
sources.title: Oceanalpha ESM30 Autonomous Water Sampling & Monitoring Boat
sources.claim: The commercially sold ESM30 collects discrete bottled water samples autonomously from multiple locations at a set depth, with separate tubing channels to avoid cross-contamination — the same physical output as a technician's grab sample set.

sources.developer: U.S. Geological Survey with MBARI and Smith-Root
sources.title: READI-Net: Providing Tools for the Early Detection and Management of Aquatic Invasive Species | U.S. Geological Survey
sources.claim: USGS's READI-Net program uses autonomous robotic autosamplers (developed with MBARI and Smith-Root) placed at creek and stream sites, which pump, filter and preserve water samples on a programmed schedule for later laboratory analysis; one is shown deployed at a Montana creek.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous eDNA water sampling rather than pollutant sampling, but the physical act is identical to the technician's: intake stream water at an unimproved creek site, meter a known volume, filter and preserve the sample, and hold it for laboratory analysis under an unattended schedule.

sources.title: MBARI’s new robotic sampler aims to transform monitoring of aquatic ecosystems
sources.claim: MBARI's Environmental Sample Processor is a fielded robot that autonomously collects, processes and preserves water samples in marine and freshwater settings, including for water-quality and toxin assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Analyte is biological rather than chemical, but the collection step — autonomous in-situ acquisition, filtration and preservation of discrete water samples for later lab analysis in open water — is the same physical work as pollutant grab sampling.

sources.date: product line long-established; pages accessed 2026-07 (3710 listing 2018)
sources.title: Automatic Water Samplers | Teledyne ISCO
sources.claim: Teledyne ISCO automatic water/wastewater samplers are the standard commercial machines used at municipal treatment plants and industrial discharge points to collect timed and flow-paced discrete and composite samples unattended, chilled in an ice base, for regulatory compliance analysis.

sources.system: Teledyne ISCO and YSI WS-Series automated water samplers
sources.developer: Teledyne ISCO / YSI (as described by Universidad Católica Boliviana / QMUL authors)

sources.system: Solar-powered autonomous surface vehicle with syringe sampling array
sources.developer: Universidad Católica Boliviana / Queen Mary University of London
sources.title: High-Resolution Water Sampling via a Solar-Powered Autonomous Surface Vehicle (arXiv:2512.09798)
sources.claim: A fully autonomous solar-powered USV with a syringe-based sampler collected 72 discrete, contamination-minimised water samples per mission during field trials on a natural lagoon, navigating unstructured water with RTK-GPS, LiDAR and stereo vision.

sources.system: Rogo SmartCore autonomous soil sampling robot
sources.title: New Soil Sampling Autonomous Robot Aims to Boost Farm Production
sources.claim: Rogo's SmartCore robots autonomously drive open fields, extract soil cores at a controlled depth with a hydraulic auger, and package and label each sample for shipment to a third-party laboratory; the company ran them as a commercial sampling service across Indiana, Ohio and Illinois.
sources.transferJustification: Agronomic rather than environmental soil sampling, but the medium (soil), the deliverable (depth-controlled core, bagged and labelled for third-party lab analysis) and the georeferenced point-location requirement are the same as environmental surface-soil sampling.

sources.title: Soil Sampling Robot – ROGO
sources.claim: Rogo continues to operate its robotic soil sampling service, driving autonomously to georeferenced points with RTK GPS and hitting specified depth repeatably, with recorded path, point and depth for every core.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: autonomous positioning plus depth-controlled coring, packaging and labelling of soil samples destined for laboratory analysis.

sources.system: Thermo Scientific Partisol 2025i Sequential Air Sampler
sources.title: Partisol™ 2025i Sequential Air Sampler
sources.claim: The Partisol 2025i sequential air sampler mechanically exchanges 47 mm filter cassettes from an onboard magazine on a programmed schedule, collecting up to two weeks of daily particulate samples unattended, and is a US EPA-designated equivalent sampler.

sources.developer: Rupprecht & Patashnick / Thermo, operated by Washington State Department of Ecology
sources.title: PM2.5 & PM10 2025 Sequential Sampler Standard Operating Procedure
sources.claim: A state environmental agency operates Partisol sequential samplers at its ambient air monitoring stations under a written SOP to collect regulatory 24-hour PM2.5/PM10 filter samples.

tasks.label: Investigate hazardous conditions or spills or outbreaks of disease or food poisoning, collecting samples for analysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land-based hazmat/spill response: technician responds to a reported release (tanker rollover on a highway, derailment, leaking drums in a yard, tank-farm overflow), dons PPE, screens the scene with PID/4-gas meters, determines the extent, collects discrete soil, liquid, wipe and air samples with decontamination between points, and documents the scene with chain-of-custody paperwork. Site layout, weather and hazards are taken as found.

Foodborne-illness or disease-outbreak investigation at a food establishment or institutional facility: walkthrough of a restaurant kitchen, cafeteria, or a building's water system after illness reports; check temperatures, observe practices, interview staff, and aseptically collect suspect food, ice, water and surface-swab samples for laboratory analysis.

Open-water contamination or spill investigation from a vessel: oil sheen, algal bloom, or discharge reported on a river, lake, reservoir, harbor or coastal water; survey the affected water body, locate the plume, and collect surface/subsurface water samples in clean bottles for lab analysis.

Complaint-driven water sampling at fixed but scattered points: storm-drain and outfall grab samples during an illicit-discharge trace, tap samples in a residence after a lead or bacterial complaint, or private-well samples after a spill; requires access to the point, purge/field measurements, preservation, labeling and chain of custody.

Indoor hazardous-condition investigation in an occupied building or home: mold/moisture, lead dust, asbestos, or an unexplained odor/indoor-air complaint at a school, office, apartment or house; visual investigation of the space, then collection of spore-trap air cassettes, wipe samples, bulk material samples or sorbent-tube air samples amid furniture, occupants and varied layouts.

Hazardous-atmosphere or leak investigation inside an industrial or utility facility (refinery, midstream gas plant, chemical plant, wastewater treatment plant): respond to an alarm or odor report, walk the process area with gas monitors, localize and characterize the release, and take air measurements/samples for analysis and reporting.

sources.system: Midwater Oil Sampler on REMUS 600 AUV
sources.developer: NOAA-supported research team (DiPinto et al., JMSE)
sources.title: Autonomous Water Sampler for Oil Spill Response
sources.claim: A Midwater Oil Sampler carried by a REMUS 600 AUV autonomously detected an underwater oil plume with an onboard fluorometer and triggered collection of clean 1-L water samples that were capped and shipped to a laboratory, during a multi-agency exercise simulating rapid spill response over natural oil seeps offshore Santa ....
sources.transferJustification: Same task: investigating a spill and collecting samples for laboratory analysis; the vehicle detects the plume in situ and fills contamination-controlled bottles that go to a lab, as a technician's grab samples would.

sources.title: Autonomous Reservoir Water Quality Monitoring with USVs
sources.claim: Hong Kong's Water Supplies Department operates five OceanAlpha ESM30 autonomous water sampling and monitoring ... that navigate an impounding reservoir with GPS and obstacle avoidance to monitor water quality and collect samples, including deployment during water-quality emergencies.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: agency water-quality investigation and sample collection on an open water body, including response to unexpected incidents such as algal events.

sources.title: High-Resolution Water Sampling via a Solar-Powered Autonomous Surface Vehicle
sources.claim: A solar-powered fully autonomous surface vessel with a syringe-based sampler collected dozens of discrete, contamination-minimized water samples per ... in field tests on a lagoon.
sources.transferJustification: Same act: unattended collection of discrete water samples for later laboratory analysis on an open water body.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with FLIR MUVE C360 and Enhanced Autonomy Payload
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / MFE Inspection Solutions / Teledyne FLIR
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: During an autonomous inspection round at a midstream gas plant, a Spot quadruped carrying a FLIR MUVE C360 gas monitor and thermal/visual payloads detected and reported a combustible-gas plume from a pinhole leak and shut itself down at the LEL threshold.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: investigating a hazardous condition (gas release) inside a facility, with the MUVE C360 drawing and analyzing air on the spot in place of grab air samples, and logging the data for the report.

sources.title: Rogo's Self-Driving, Fully Autonomous Soil Sampler Covers 100k Acres in 2019
sources.claim: Rogo's SmartCore robots autonomously drive row-crop fields and collect and pack soil cores at prescribed locations, operating commercially over hundreds of thousands of acres.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor soil-core collection for laboratory analysis; the coring and packing motions transfer, but the sampling plan is supplied by an agronomist and there is no hazard screening, decontamination between points, or spill-scene assessment.

sources.system: Robotic swabbing system (UR5e with force-sensing swab holder)
sources.developer: University of Arkansas (Mahmoudi et al., Foods)
sources.title: Evaluation of Robotic Swabbing and Fluorescent Sensing to Monitor the Hygiene of Food Contact Surfaces
sources.claim: A benchtop study evaluated a Universal Robots UR5e arm holding a sponge swab with tactile-pressure feedback to swab food-contact surfaces, compared against human swabbers, as a possible replacement for manual environmental monitoring swabs.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step: collecting surface swabs for microbial analysis as done in outbreak investigations; but the demonstration is a fixed arm swabbing a flat test surface on a bench, not an investigation of a working kitchen.

tasks.label: Record test data and prepare reports, summaries, or charts that interpret test results.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prepare samples or photomicrographs for testing and analysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial or municipal environmental testing lab: aqueous samples (drinking water, wastewater, groundwater) arrive in assorted client bottles. Technician logs them, filters, acidifies/preserves, aliquots into vials, makes dilutions and spikes, and sets up SPE or liquid-liquid extraction for EPA-method organics/metals analysis.

Lab prep of solid samples (soil, sediment, sludge, waste): air-drying, sieving, grinding/homogenizing, splitting, then weighing subsamples into digestion vessels or extraction thimbles and recording weights for metals and semivolatiles analysis.

Air-quality/industrial-hygiene lab: conditioning PM filters in a climate-controlled weigh room, tare and post-sampling weighing on a microbalance, and preparing filters or sorbent media (cutting, digesting, desorbing) for gravimetric or metals analysis.

Microscopy work: mounting material on slides (asbestos PLM/PCM filter mounts, fibers, algae, particulates), clearing/staining and coverslipping, then locating fields under the microscope and capturing photomicrographs for the analyst's report.

Field-side preparation at a sampling site or in a mobile lab: filtering water for dissolved metals, adding preservatives, compositing/splitting samples, labeling and packing bottles on ice, often outdoors in variable weather at an industrial or natural site.

tasks.label: Weigh, analyze, or measure collected sample particles, such as lead, coal dust, or rock, to determine concentration of pollutants.

instances.label: Gravimetric analysis of air-filter samples (PM2.5/PM10 FRM filters, respirable coal/silica dust cassettes) in a lab weighing room: log filters in, equilibrate 24 h at controlled T/RH, neutralize static, weigh tare and post-exposure mass on a microbalance to ~1 µg, run QC check standards and duplicates, upload masses to LIMS.

Lead and other metals in dust wipes, paint chips, or soil: weigh a sample aliquot, acid-digest (hotblock or microwave), dilute/filter, run on ICP-MS/ICP-OES or flame AAS with calibration standards, spikes and blanks, and report concentration (µg/g, µg/ft²) against regulatory limits.

Soil, sediment, rock or coal sample preparation and measurement in a lab prep room: oven-dry, weigh, crush/pulverize, sieve to size fractions, riffle-split, weigh subsamples and residues (percent moisture, grain-size, ash/LOI) before or as part of contaminant determination.

Water solids work in a wastewater/environmental lab: pre-weigh and desiccate glass-fiber filters, filter a measured sample volume, dry at 103–105 °C to constant weight, cool and re-weigh to compute TSS/settleable solids concentration in mg/L.

On-site/field measurement at a project site (brownfield, residential yard, roadway, construction or industrial site): screen collected soil, dust or paint samples with a portable XRF or read direct-reading particulate monitors, in variable weather, uneven terrain and site traffic, and record concentrations for the field report.

instances.label: Bench calibration of water-quality field meters in the environmental lab before a sampling run: rinse and blot the pH/conductivity/DO/turbidity probes, pour fresh buffers or standards into beakers, immerse and wait for stability, accept 2-3 calibration points, check slope/offset against acceptance limits, and log the result in the instrument logbook.

Setting up the calibration curve on a benchtop analytical instrument (spectrophotometer, IC, GC, ICP-MS): prepare a serial dilution series of standards from stock, load vials on the autosampler, run the standards, verify r^2 and the continuing-calibration verification, and re-run if criteria fail.

Pre-deployment bump test and span calibration of portable monitoring gear in the equipment room/shop: 4-gas meters and PIDs challenged with certified span gas from a regulated cylinder, sensors adjusted, and personal sampling pumps flow-calibrated against a primary standard; records printed/filed.

On-site calibration or calibration check during field work: recalibrating a PID or multigas meter, or a water-quality sonde, from the tailgate of a truck or at a well head in wind, heat, dust or rain, with limited bench space and improvised setup.

Microscope setup and calibration in the lab for fiber/particle work: set Köhler illumination, center the phase-contrast annuli, verify resolution with an HSE/RMS test slide, and calibrate the eyepiece graticule or camera pixel scale against a stage micrometer; document the check.

Zero/span and multipoint calibration of continuous analyzers at a fixed ambient air monitoring shelter or a stack CEMS: certified cylinder gas delivered through a dilution calibrator/manifold, analyzer response checked against drift limits and zero/span adjusted, results recorded for the QA record.

instances.label: Recurring read-and-observe compliance round at a fixed industrial facility (cement/chemical plant, refinery, power plant, gas plant): the technician walks a set route recording emission-control-device operating parameters from analog gauges and local panels (baghouse differential pressure, scrubber liquid flow, thermal oxidizer chamber temperature, fan amps, flare pilot status), notes thermal/acoustic/visual abnormalities, and logs readings against permit limits, flagging out-of-range values.

Checks at a fixed facility that require hands-on measurement, service, or adjustment: sampling scrubber liquor for pH, functional-testing bag leak detectors, changing filters/cal-gas cylinders, cleaning probes and heat-traced lines, verifying daily zero/span drift on CEMS/COMS analyzers, troubleshooting a failed monitor, adjusting dampers or valves, and validating data for compliance reports.

Formal visible-emission work: certified EPA Method 9 opacity readings on a stack or baghouse vent, Method 22 observations on flares and fugitive sources, and fugitive dust surveys at the facility fenceline, performed outdoors under varying sky/lighting conditions and documented on compliance forms.

Recurring fugitive-emission and vapor-control survey at upstream oil & gas sites (well pads, tank batteries, compressor and gas-processing stations): OGI survey of closed vent systems, thief hatches, separators and connectors under NSPS OOOOa/OOOOb, identifying and documenting emission events for repair.

Component-level LDAR survey inside a refinery or chemical plant process unit: screening thousands of valves, flanges, pumps and connectors with a Method 21 analyzer probe or close-range OGI camera, tagging leakers, and recording results in the LDAR database.

Visits to dispersed or unfamiliar sites: consultant or agency checks of small sources (gas station Stage I/II vapor recovery, dry cleaner, asphalt plant, emergency generator), and landfill gas control system work (wellhead monitoring and valve tuning plus quarterly surface emissions monitoring), where layout differs site to site and the technician has not pre-mapped the location.

instances.label: Routine unannounced sanitary inspection of a retail food establishment (restaurant, deli, grocery kitchen): walk the kitchen, dish room, walk-in coolers and dry storage; probe internal food temperatures with a thermometer; test dish-machine/sanitizer bucket concentration with test strips or titration; check handwash sinks, employee hygiene practices, cross-contamination, chemical storage; look under and behind equipment for grease and rodent/insect evidence; discuss findings with the person in charge and write a coded violation report.

Sanitary inspection of an institutional facility kitchen and common areas — school cafeteria, hospital or nursing-home dietary department, jail, childcare center: same food-safety checks plus inspection of restrooms, dishwashing, waste handling, ventilation and general sanitation, with records review and staff interviews.

Inspection of a public swimming pool or spa at a hotel, apartment complex, YMCA or municipal aquatic center: collect and test pool water for free/combined chlorine, pH, cyanuric acid and clarity; check recirculation and filtration equipment room, drain covers, safety equipment, deck cleanliness, showers and locker-room restrooms; record results and issue closure if imminent hazard.

Inspection of temporary and mobile food operations at fairs, festivals, farmers markets and food-truck lots: outdoor site with improvised layout, generators, tents, ice chests and hand-wash setups; check cold/hot holding temperatures, water and wastewater arrangements, hand-washing, overhead protection, in variable weather and crowds.

Sanitary condition inspections of other public premises taken as found — park and beach restrooms, campgrounds, public bathhouses, lodging complaints, mass-gathering sites: assess cleanliness, plumbing and sewage, vermin harborage, refuse handling, water supply; often complaint-driven with unpredictable conditions and no fixed layout.

Airborne fiber analysis: technician reads prepared air-filter samples (acetone-collapsed PCM slides per NIOSH 7400, or coated filter sections for ISO 14966 SEM) from abatement clearance or personal exposure monitoring, scans fields, applies counting rules, and reports fibers per cc; sometimes done in an on-site trailer/room at an abatement job.

instances.label: Commercial/mine-site minerals assay or geochemical lab: a batch of drill or grade-control samples is logged in, crushed, split, pulverized, weighed, then fused/digested and run on XRF, TGA, AAS or ICP; results QC'd and reported. Dusty, hazardous, high-throughput lab bays.

Wellsite mud logging, chemostratigraphy portion: catching drill cuttings at the shale shaker at set depth intervals during rapid drilling, washing/drying them, and running elemental (XRF) analysis for chemostratigraphic correlation and geosteering support, 24/7 in all weather.

Wellsite mud logging, classical evaluation portion: washing and sieving cuttings, binocular-microscope lithology description, calcimetry, UV fluorescence/cut tests for hydrocarbon shows, and reconciling with gas chromatograph readings inside the logging unit.

Core analysis facility: whole and slabbed core sections/boxes measured for density, magnetic susceptibility, continuous XRF geochemistry, imaging and RQD; plug-scale porosity/permeability and grain density runs in a core lab.

Petrography/mineralogy lab: thin sections, polished grain mounts and epoxy blocks examined by petrographic microscope or automated SEM-EDS to identify minerals, modal mineralogy, liberation and textures; results tabulated into a report.

On-site field testing at an exploration property, outcrop, soil grid, trench or core-shed pad: hand-held pXRF/LIBS readings on rock faces, soils and samples, magnetic susceptibility, effervescence and hardness checks, with GPS/interval logging; variable terrain, weather and access.

instances.label: Wellsite mudlogging on an active oil/gas rig: catching drill cuttings from the shale shaker/possum belly at prescribed depth intervals (often every 10-30 ft, faster in rapid drilling), washing/sieving off drilling fluid, drying, bagging and labeling wet and dry sample sets by lagged depth, plus periodic drilling-fluid samples; done 24/7 on a pad or offshore rig in all weather.

Sample preparation in a minesite or commercial assay/geochemical laboratory: receiving numbered rock, core, RC chip and soil samples, drying, jaw crushing, riffle/rotary splitting, pulverizing to pulp, weighing and packeting pulps, labeling and logging into LIMS, and cleaning equipment between samples to prevent cross-contamination.

Field geochemical/environmental soil or sediment sampling on a grid over open, vehicle-accessible ground (farmland, rangeland, cleared exploration ground, brownfield lots): navigating to GPS points, augering/coring to a set depth, compositing, bagging, labeling and recording each site.

Rugged/remote hand sampling on foot: hammering rock chips or cutting channel samples from outcrops, road cuts, cliff faces and float; scooping stream sediments while wading; choosing representative fresh material of the target lithology, bagging, tagging and photographing, carried out in steep, brushy or trackless terrain.

Sample catching at exploration/grade-control drill rigs: standing at the RC cyclone or blasthole drill collecting cuttings per drilled interval into a splitter, changing sample bags, labeling and racking them, and inserting QC standards/blanks, on an open-pit bench or underground drift controlled by the mine.

Core shed/core yard processing at an exploration project: laying out core trays, aligning and orienting core, marking sample intervals from the geologist's log, cutting core lengthwise on a core saw, bagging and tagging half-core samples with QC inserts, and dispatching batches to the lab.

instances.label: Mud logging on a working oil/gas drilling location: over a 12-hour tour the technician catches drill cuttings at the shale shaker at set depth intervals, sieves/washes and describes them under a binocular scope, tracks gas-detector and drilling-parameter feeds, calls formation tops, and keeps the mud log current for the operator's geologist. Outdoor rig site, mud, noise, weather, controlled access.

Wireline/openhole-cased-hole logging operations at a wellsite: helping rig up the logging unit and sheaves, making up and testing the downhole tool string, running in and out of hole, monitoring log quality during acquisition, then rigging down and securing radioactive/pressure-control equipment.

Exploratory core-drilling program support: receiving core from the driller at the rig, orienting, marking and boxing it, measuring recovery and RQD, photographing trays, logging lithology/alteration/structure at the core shack, then marking, cutting and bagging assay intervals with QA/QC standards inserted.

On-foot ground field programs: prospecting field trips and geochemical sampling (soil grids, stream sediments, rock chips), outcrop mapping and GPS station work in roadless bush, desert or mountain claims; plus ground geophysics line work (laying geophone/node or electrode arrays, occupying gravity/mag stations) across variable terrain and weather.

Airborne/UAV geophysical survey acquisition over a prospect: flying programmed low-altitude magnetic, radiometric or LiDAR lines with terrain following over hilly or hazardous ground, monitoring data quality and diurnal base station, and delivering a gridded dataset to the geophysicist.

Survey acquisition from uncrewed/remote platforms in places people cannot easily work: hydrographic and oceanographic survey legs (multibeam bathymetry, sonar/CTD lines) in coastal and open water, and underground mine survey programs scanning stopes, voids and inaccessible workings for as-built volumes.

Laboratory bench: adjusting, calibrating and repairing test instruments — balances, sieve shakers, ovens, permeameters/porosimeters, XRF and other spectrometers, core-testing rigs — including opening housings, chasing leaks or loose connections, replacing fuses/tubing/sensors and re-zeroing after the fix.

Sample-prep shop / core facility: servicing mechanical equipment — jaw crushers, pulverizers, riffle splitters, core saws, vacuum pumps, dust collectors, compressors — replacing worn screens, plates, belts, seals and blades, adjusting gaps and drives, then test-running the machine.

Pre-deployment routine servicing of portable instruments in the field office or equipment shop: bump-testing and calibrating portable gas monitors and handheld detectors, swapping battery packs and sensor/payload modules, and confirming the unit reads correctly before it goes out.

Shop repair of downhole/wireline and drilling instrumentation: opening logging sondes and probe housings, replacing O-rings, seals, feedthrough connectors and failed sensor cards, torquing housings and bench-testing the tool before it returns to the truck.

instances.label: Assay/geochemical/core-analysis laboratory: technician sets up analytical instruments on geological samples — loads pulps and crucibles into XRF/TGA or ICP autosampler racks, mounts sample cups and standards, runs calibration checks, loads core plugs or splits into scanners/particle-size analyzers, and confirms the instrument is producing acceptable readings before a batch runs. Indoor, fixed benches, standard glassware and instrument models, institution controls access.

Active land drilling rig: technician (mud logger/wellsite geologist assistant) rigs up and calibrates surface instrumentation — installs the gas trap in the possum belly or flowline, mounts pressure/hookload/RPM/pit-level sensors on rig equipment, runs and terminates cables to the logging unit, and calibrates gas detectors/chromatograph with calibration gas. Muddy, weather-exposed pad, moving rig equipment, layout varies by rig.

Drill floor: technician assists or directs make-up of an instrumented downhole tool string — LWD/MWD subs or downhole gauges picked up from the catwalk, stabbed and torqued into the bottom-hole assembly, memory/telemetry checked before running in hole. Standard API tubular connections, heavy tools, rig crew and handling equipment present.

Seismic survey in open country (desert, farmland, brush, forest, foothills): technician lays out and plants geophone strings or nodal recorders on hundreds to thousands of surveyed points, ensures ground coupling and level/orientation, arms and QCs the units, and records positions; also assists with source/recorder setup. Terrain and vegetation taken as found.

Exploration ground or outcrop: technician sets up portable survey instruments — tripod-mounted magnetometer or gravimeter with leveling, GNSS base station over a control point, GPR antenna cart, resistivity/IP electrode arrays and cable spreads, handheld XRF on outcrop faces — on unimproved ground reached by truck or on foot.

Mine, quarry, geothermal, or CO2-storage monitoring site: technician installs semi-permanent instrumentation — excavates and levels a seismograph or tiltmeter pad, orients and couples the sensor, lowers piezometers/extensometers/inclinometer casing or a downhole probe into a borehole, wires solar panel, battery and telemetry, seals the enclosure and verifies data are logging.

instances.label: Mud logging on an active land rig (e.g., Permian horizontal well): on 12-hour tours the technician catches drill cuttings at the shale shaker on lag-corrected 10-30 ft intervals, carries them to the logging unit, and monitors total gas and chromatograph output from the gas trap, producing a depth-indexed sample set and gas curve. Outdoors/trailer, 24/7, all weather, rig traffic.

Sample preparation and instrumental measurement of cuttings and core, in the mudlogging unit or a core-analysis lab: washing/sieving/drying chips, binocular-microscope examination, UV fluorescence and solvent cut tests, XRF/XRD chemostratigraphy on prepared cuttings, and core scanning for spectral gamma, density, velocity and imaging logged against depth.

Openhole wireline logging run at a well: rigging up the logging unit, sheaves and pressure-control equipment, making up a tool string (gamma ray, resistivity, density-neutron, sonic), running in hole while recording logs at controlled speed, monitoring tension and log quality, retrieving the string and rigging down.

Land seismic acquisition on a prospect: laying out and planting nodal receivers/geophones along lines across ranchland, desert, brush or farmland, GPS-positioning each station, checking node health, then retrieving units and harvesting data. Rough terrain, fences, livestock, weather.

Airborne geophysical survey over a prospect or basin: flying magnetic (and radiometric) survey lines at low altitude on a pre-planned grid with terrain following and a ground base station, to map basement/structure for petroleum prospecting. Open, uncontrolled terrain.

Ground surface survey work: occupying gravity-meter stations along traverses, ground magnetic/EM readings, soil-gas and geochemical sampling on a grid, and outcrop measurements with compass, portable gamma spectrometer or handheld XRF. Roadside, pasture, desert; access by truck and on foot.

tasks.label: Evaluate and interpret core samples and cuttings, and other geological data used in prospecting for oil or gas.

instances.label: On an active drilling rig, inside the mudlogging unit: washed and dried cuttings arriving every 10-30 ft are examined under a binocular microscope; the technician estimates lithology percentages, color, grain size, cement and visible porosity, checks staining/fluorescence and solvent cut under UV, ties the description to gas-chromatograph and ROP data, and posts the interpretation to the mud log in real time so formation tops and casing points can be called.

In a core laboratory or core-analysis facility: slabbed conventional core or sidewall cores from an exploration well are laid out on tables; the technician describes lithofacies, grain size, sedimentary structures and fractures, checks shows under UV, marks plug/sample points, photographs the core, and reconciles the description with routine core-analysis porosity and permeability data.

At a company sample library, state core repository or office lab: archived cuttings sample sets and core chips from offset wells are examined under a microscope, wetted and acid-tested, to build a lithologic strip log that is depth-correlated with wireline logs for a prospect area.

At the wellsite when a core is cut: the core barrel is laid down on the catwalk, the technician lays out and marks the core, makes a quick lithologic description, checks fluorescence and cut in a portable UV box, and recommends preservation and sampling - outdoors, under rig tempo and weather.

Desk-based prospect evaluation: assembling existing cuttings and core descriptions, mud logs, wireline logs and seismic or geochemical data into cross sections and pay summaries and interpreting them to evaluate an oil or gas prospect, with no sample handling.

tasks.label: Inspect engines for wear or defective parts, using equipment or measuring devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine condition check of the engines that power a controlled wellsite or production site (rig diesel gensets, engine-driven mud pumps, skid-mounted gas compressor engines): walk the fixed round, read oil-pressure/coolant-temp/RPM/hour gauges, scan for hot bearings and exhaust leaks with an IR thermometer or thermal camera, listen for knocking, note visible wear or leaks, and log condition in the daily report. Operator-controlled pad or plant with standard equipment layout.

Field check of small engines on exploration equipment at a remote camp, roadside, or open ground - crew truck or ATV, portable generator, water/sampling pump, portable core drill: open the hood or cover, pull the dipstick and judge oil condition, inspect belts, hoses, air filter and plugs for wear, run a compression or multimeter check, and note parts needing replacement. Mud, dust, cold, no fixed layout.

Inspection round inside a sample-prep lab, mine surface plant, or core facility of the motors and engines driving crushers, pulverizers, compressors, and dust collectors: take vibration-meter and thermal readings at set points, check tachometer/gauge values against baseline, flag bearing wear or overheating, record readings in the maintenance log. Indoor, institution-controlled, fixed asset positions.

Bench inspection in the company maintenance shop of a disassembled engine or pump end mounted on a stand: measure cylinder bore, journals, and clearances with micrometers, bore gauges, and feeler gauges, inspect parts for scoring, cracks, or scuffing, compare to service-manual specs, and write up wear findings and reusability. Shop with benches and standard metrology tools.

Inspection of engine-driven equipment in a hazardous, Ex-classified area of an offshore platform, FPSO, or gas plant: follow the permitted route, read local instruments, take thermography and vibration readings on engines/compressors, monitor for combustible gas, and report anomalies to the control room. Grated decks, confined passages, institution-controlled access.
