sources.transferJustification: Exploration coring is the closest analogue to drilling-side subsurface data collection; the source shows automation is confined to rod handling under operator supervision, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion of wellsite data-collection duties.

tasks.label: Collect geological data from potential geothermal energy plant sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aerial reconnaissance of a prospect: flying drone surveys over a few km2 of a candidate geothermal site - pre-dawn thermal-infrared to map warm ground and springs, RGB photogrammetry for orthomosaics/DSM, and magnetometer or EM payloads to trace buried faults; setting ground control, then delivering georeferenced data products.

Ground geophysical survey support across open desert/volcanic terrain: hauling, siting, leveling, burying and later recovering MT/TEM electrodes and coils, gravity meter stations with GNSS ties, and seismic nodes, over kilometers of brush, talus and washes in heat, wind and dust.

Surface geologic mapping and rock sampling: traversing outcrops, sinter and altered ground on foot, hammering off representative hand samples of lithology/alteration, measuring fault and fracture orientations, photographing, bagging, labeling and GPS-tagging samples, and logging field descriptions.

Geothermal fluid geochemistry: sampling hot springs, seeps, fumaroles and existing wells - measuring temperature, pH and conductivity in situ, drawing filtered/preserved water splits and gas samples, and handling labeling and chain of custody in rough terrain around boiling or steaming features.

Thermal measurements in the ground: driving 2-m temperature probes on a grid and reading them, and running temperature/pressure probes on a reel or wireline down shallow temperature-gradient holes and existing exploration boreholes on the lease to record temperature-depth profiles and water levels.

Wellsite data collection while an exploration/production well is drilled on the pad: catching and washing drill cuttings at the shale shaker at set depth intervals, examining and describing them, sampling core, and recording drilling and gas parameters against depth.

sources.system: Autel Evo II Pro / DJI Mavic 3T thermal UAS survey (Ormat Technologies)
sources.title: Small Unoccupied Aerial Systems (UAS) and Thermal Cameras in Geothermal Exploration and Operational Fields; a Review of UAS Equipment and Case Study at Brady Geothermal Field, Nevada USA
sources.claim: Ormat contracted small UAS flights that collected daytime RGB and pre-dawn calibrated thermal imagery over 1.39 km2 of the Brady geothermal field, Nevada, producing orthomosaics and DSMs used to map surface manifestations and refine geologic mapping of the field.

sources.claim: A magnetometer-equipped drone flew predefined autonomous flight scenarios to survey the Lavrion district, Greece, mapping geological composition and material distribution from high-resolution magnetic field data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drone aeromagnetic surveying for mineral exploration. Same instrument class, same low-altitude open-terrain flight profile and the same geological product (magnetic maps of faults and contacts) as the magnetic surveys flown over geothermal prospects.

sources.claim: Hatch used a drone-mounted water sampling system on autonomous flights to collect water samples and in-situ profiles of temperature, conductivity and density from mine pit lakes to 80 m depth for clients including Goldcorp, Kinross and the Nevada Division of Environmental Protection, replacing boat- and shoreline-based sampling crews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pit-lake water sampling for a monitoring program. Same object (a natural surface water body and its lab-bound sample), same actions (retrieve a sample plus in-situ temperature/conductivity readings at a located point) and the same unstructured outdoor setting as sampling a thermal spring or seep on a geothermal prospect.

sources.title: Volcanic carbon emissions measured using long-range drones - UCL Earth Sciences
sources.claim: Long-range drones carrying miniaturised gas sensors, spectrometers and automatically triggered sampling devices flew to the summit of Manam volcano, Papua New Guinea, and captured volcanic gas samples for isotopic analysis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sampling volcanic vent gases in the field - the same act as collecting fumarole gas samples on a geothermal prospect (same media, same sample vessels, same rough volcanic terrain).

sources.title: IADC/SPE-189680-MS Automation Provides Unique Insights of The Rock Record and Subsurface Through the Delivery of a Robotic Sample Collection and Analysis Device
sources.claim: The Automated Remote Mudlogger (ARM), a robotic cuttings collection and analysis device installed on the rig's mud system, was deployed on Permian Basin wells and automatically collected depth-indexed drill cuttings at 5-30 ft intervals, far finer than a human mudlogger's three collections per hour, reducing rig-site personnel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mudlogging cuttings collection on oil and gas wells. Geothermal exploration wells are drilled with the same rotary rigs and shale shakers, so a collector plumbed to the shaker performs the identical sampling act on the same material.

tasks.label: Conduct geophysical surveys of potential sites for wind farms or solar installations to determine their suitability.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility-scale solar project on 200–1,000 acres of former cropland/pasture/scrub: technician lays out seismic refraction and MASW lines with a GPS, plants geophones or nodes in the soil, strings takeout cables, operates a sledgehammer or accelerated weight-drop source at multiple shot points, monitors record quality on the seismograph, and moves the spread line to line over fences, ditches, mud and crop stubble to map depth to bedrock, rippability and seismic site class.

Onshore wind farm: shear-wave velocity profiling (MASW/ReMi, downhole or PS suspension logging in a geotechnical borehole) plus refraction spreads at individual turbine pad locations on rural ridgetops and pasture reached by two-track access roads; technician hauls gear on foot, couples geophones/borehole probe, runs the acquisition, and logs positions for each pad.

Electrical methods at a candidate solar or wind site: 2D electrical resistivity imaging lines for karst, voids and depth-to-rock, plus IEEE-81 Wenner four-pin soil resistivity and in-situ thermal resistivity testing for grounding-grid and buried-cable design; requires driving stainless electrodes into the ground, reeling out multi-electrode cable, checking contact resistance and re-watering electrodes in dry soil.

Non-intrusive reconnaissance mapping over a greenfield renewable-energy parcel: magnetometer/gradiometer, EM and GPR grid coverage to find buried utilities, abandoned oil/gas well casings, drums, old foundations or UXO before pile driving and trenching, over open pasture and cropland with scattered vegetation and fences.

Offshore wind lease area or export cable corridor: marine geophysical survey along pre-planned line grids using multibeam echosounder, side-scan sonar, sub-bottom profiler and magnetometer to characterize seabed and shallow soils; technician runs the acquisition watch, monitors data quality and line keeping, and logs the survey.

sources.title: Setanta Offshore Wind Farm Survey Delivered Using XOCEAN's Cutting Edge Uncrewed Technology
sources.claim: A fleet of XOCEAN uncrewed ... completed a seabed geophysical survey (multibeam echosounder) of SSE Renewables' proposed 1GW Setanta offshore wind site, i.e. site characterisation of a potential wind farm site performed by robotic vessels.

sources.title: Autonomous Survey in Northern Environments – International Hydrographic Review
sources.claim: XOCEAN's survey USVs run survey lines autonomously over the horizon; shore-based pilots keep watch and take manual control only when required (e.g. collision avoidance), i.e. supervised autonomy rather than continuous teleoperation.

sources.title: Seafloor mapping with remotely controlled USVs – Spatial Source
sources.claim: XOCEAN's uncrewed vessels carry the full marine geophysical sensor suite used for offshore wind site suitability work (multibeam echosounders, sub-bottom profilers, side-scan ..., magnetometers) on ~10-day offshore missions.

sources.title: Faversham UXO Survey | Cleve Hill Solar Park Development
sources.claim: A commercial drone-mounted magnetometer survey covered all 316 hectares of the Cleve Hill Solar Park development site in 25 days (versus an estimated 150 days by ground push-cart methods), producing the magnetometry dataset used to clear the site before groundworks.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: non-intrusive geophysical (magnetometry) survey of a candidate solar installation site to determine constraints on suitability/constructability; same sensors, same open-field conditions.

sources.system: SPH Engineering SkyHub / UgCS drone GPR and magnetometer systems (DJI M300/M350/M400 platforms)

sources.claim: Drone-borne GPR and magnetometer survey systems fly the survey grid autonomously with terrain following, logging georeferenced geophysical data; the vendor markets and field-proves the approach for pre-construction surveys of solar farm sites and greenfield developments, with the pilot only monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Buried-utility/ferrous-object mapping over open greenfield and solar-farm parcels uses the same airborne magnetometer/GPR methods, targets and terrain as pre-development geophysical screening of renewable sites.

sources.system: DJI Matrice 600 hexacopter with Geometrics MFAM magnetometer
sources.developer: Binghamton University research group (Nikulin & de Smet)

sources.transferJustification: Detecting buried ferrous hazards (well casings, utilities, ordnance) over rural US farmland is the same measurement, sensor and environment as magnetometer screening of candidate solar/wind parcels.

tasks.label: Collect water and soil samples to test for physical, chemical, or biological properties, such as pH, oxygen level, temperature, and pollution.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine/event water sampling at an instrumented stream or river gaging station: technician visits the gage, records field parameters (temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, specific conductance) with a sonde, collects point/grab or storm-event bottles for nutrients, sediment, or bacteria near the fixed intake, ices and logs them.

Wading or synoptic sampling tour of ungaged sites: technician hikes/wades into a creek or river reach, measures pH, DO, temperature in situ, collects an isokinetic depth- and width-integrated (EWI/EDI) sample with a hand-held or cable sampler, composites in a churn splitter, filters and preserves subsamples, labels bottles under chain of custody; footing, flow, weather and access vary site to site.

Groundwater monitoring-well sampling at a landfill, farm, industrial or Superfund site: open the well, measure depth to water, install/operate a pump, purge with low-flow while watching field parameters stabilize in a flow-through cell, then fill preserved bottles and VOC vials, decontaminate equipment, complete chain of custody.

Lake, reservoir or large-river sampling from a boat: navigate to fixed stations, run a vertical profile with a multiparameter sonde, collect discrete-depth samples with a Van Dorn/Niskin or depth-integrating sampler, and bottle/preserve them onboard in wind, waves and traffic.

Soil or streambed sediment sampling: auger or core soil at georeferenced points to a specified depth (or scoop/core bed sediment), composite into bags or jars, label and store for lab analysis of chemistry, moisture or contamination, on farm fields, floodplains, and disturbed sites.

Sampling at a controlled facility: wastewater treatment plant, industrial outfall, or permitted stormwater station, where the technician programs/services an automatic composite sampler, pulls grab samples at sample ports or channels, and records pH, temperature and DO for NPDES-type compliance reporting.

sources.claim: USGS studies pair continuous water-quality monitors with autosamplers at stream sites so that a turbidity threshold triggers unattended hourly sample collection into up to 24 bottles, with monitor data and collection times logged automatically.

sources.title: Refrigerated Water and Wastewater Samplers | Teledyne ISCO
sources.claim: Refrigerated automatic samplers are standard commercial equipment that sit outdoors at wastewater and stormwater facilities and collect time- or flow-paced composite samples for permit compliance without an operator present.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: physically drawing water into labeled bottles, chilled/preserved, for laboratory testing of chemical and physical properties; output is accepted by regulators in place of technician-collected samples.

sources.title: Portable Automatic Sampling Pumps | Geotech
sources.claim: Commercial auto-samplers perform unattended collection of water for later laboratory analysis from either open channels or closed conduits (e.g., a pumped well or process line), filling discrete or composite containers.
sources.transferJustification: Closed-conduit unattended sampling is the fixtured-presentation analogue of well sampling: water is delivered by a dedicated pump line and the machine fills the sample containers.

sources.claim: The ESM30 is a commercially sold uncrewed surface vessel that navigates to multiple points on a water body and autonomously collects bottled water samples plus onboard water-quality data, used for emergency pollution response.

sources.claim: A moored freshwater Environmental Sample Processor has operated in western Lake Erie since 2017, autonomously sampling lake water and reporting algal-toxin levels to drinking-water managers in near real time.

instances.label: Manual snow-course / snow-survey trip: technician travels by ski, snowshoe, snowmobile or helicopter to an established backcountry mountain snow course, drives a Federal snow sampler to the ground at each marked point, reads depth, weighs the core for SWE, sometimes digs a snow pit for density/stratigraphy, and reports the site values for water-supply forecasting.

Winter streamflow measurement under ice cover: technician augers a line of holes through river ice, measures ice and slush thickness and effective depth, lowers a current meter or ADCP through each hole to compute discharge, and records the ice-affected gage record.

Installing and servicing automated snow/ice/permafrost monitoring stations (SNOTEL-type snow pillows, ultrasonic depth sensors, snow scales, ground-temperature strings, time-lapse cameras): digging out and leveling sensors, replacing cables/batteries/desiccant, calibrating, downloading loggers, in remote mountain or tundra sites.

Geophysical / aerial mapping surveys of snowpack, glacier ice, or lake and river ice: running GPR transects over a snowfield, glacier, or frozen river, or flying lidar/photogrammetry/radar survey grids, to map snow depth, layering, and ice thickness over a defined area, then delivering the georeferenced thickness/depth product.

Glacier mass-balance fieldwork on a benchmark glacier: locating and re-drilling ablation stakes, reading stake emergence, probing to last summer's surface, digging accumulation pits for density, and surveying stake positions with GPS on crevassed ice in variable weather.

Permafrost and frozen-ground monitoring: logging borehole ground temperatures with a probe or downloading thermistor strings, mechanically probing active-layer thaw depth across a CALM grid, taking frozen-ground/ground-ice cores, and measuring thaw subsidence on Arctic tundra.

instances.label: Wading discharge measurement at a small-to-medium wadeable stream: technician strings a tag line, wades the cross-section, and measures depth and velocity at 20-30 verticals with a price/pygmy current meter or handheld ADCP, then computes discharge; cobble or silt bed, brush, cold or turbid water, variable stage.

Moving-boat ADCP discharge measurement on a larger river from a manned boat, bridge, or cableway: four reciprocal transects with edge estimates, in typical to moderately high flow with drift and some debris.

Station visit to determine water level/stage: read the outside staff or wire-weight gauge, check the float/bubbler/pressure recorder against it and against the gauge datum and reference marks, and record stage to 0.01 ft at a remote streamside gauge house.

Groundwater level round: open well vaults or caps at scattered observation/monitoring wells on roadsides, farms, and industrial sites, sound depth-to-water with an electric or steel tape to 0.01 ft, measure total well depth, and record.
Lake or reservoir survey: run echosounder survey lines from a boat plus a lake-level reading to compute storage volume/capacity or sediment change on a reservoir or pond.

Flow measurement at engineered structures inside an institution-controlled facility: lined irrigation-district canal, flume or weir at a treatment plant, hydro tailrace or headgate, with standard structures and controlled access.

instances.label: Scheduled service visit to an operating streamgage on a stream or river (roadside or walk-in, weather as found): open the gage shelter, inspect and clean the stage sensor (bubbler orifice line, pressure transducer or radar), purge the orifice/desiccant, check the recorded stage against the staff gage and reference marks, service battery/solar panel and satellite telemetry, correct wiring or mounting problems, verify the recorder is logging correctly before leaving.

Install or rebuild a station: anchor and mount a radar or pressure sensor on a bridge, piling or bank; set a staff gage; run conduit/cable and seal enclosures; lower and secure a water-level recorder in a groundwater monitoring well; wire, program and telemeter the data logger; survey the datum and reference marks and document the installation.

Deploy, retrieve and swap continuous water-quality sondes and automatic samplers at open field sites (bridge pier deployment pipe, canal, storm drain, lake buoy): pull the fouled instrument, verify readings against a check sonde, clean it, mount the replacement in the deployment pipe, reconnect power/comms and confirm data transmission.

Routine bench preparation in the field-office shop/lab before deployment: rinse and clean sondes and water analyzers, calibrate pH, conductivity, dissolved-oxygen, turbidity and nitrate sensors against standard solutions in calibration cups, run post-deployment verification checks and record the calibration sheet.

Bench repair and refurbishment in the shop: diagnose a failed logger or sensor returned from the field, replace DO membrane caps, O-rings, desiccant, corroded cables/connectors and batteries, re-solder or re-terminate wiring, reconfigure firmware and bench-test the repaired unit against a reference before it goes back out.

Service fixed monitoring equipment at an institution-controlled facility (water or wastewater plant, dam outlet works, canal headworks, irrigation district gaging station): keep in-line water analyzers and pH/conductivity sensors clean and calibrated, replace reagents and consumables, verify against grab-sample checks and log the maintenance.

tasks.label: Provide real time data to emergency management and weather service personnel during flood events.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Duty station / district office during a rising river event: the technician watches the telemetered gauge network (satellite/cell telemetry feeds), screens incoming stage and computed discharge values for sensor drift, ice, or debris effects, and relays verified current readings and trends by phone, email, or chat to the NWS River Forecast Center hydrologist and county emergency managers.

Field relay during a flood peak: after making a high-flow measurement at a bridge or cableway, the technician immediately communicates the observed stage, measured discharge, and rating shift by radio/cell phone to the NWS forecaster and the local EOC so crest forecasts and evacuation decisions can be updated.

Gauge outage or out-of-range sensor during an event: telemetry fails or the stage sensor is exceeded, and the technician provides substitute real-time observations (outside staff/wire-weight readings, high-water marks, or manual readings called in at intervals) to NWS and emergency management until the automated feed is restored.

Temporary/event-driven monitoring: the technician confirms that newly sited rapid-deployment gauges or storm-tide sensors are streaming to the public real-time website and notifies NWS/emergency management of the new station IDs, thresholds, and data links so responders can use them during the event.

Coordination role: the technician participates in NWS/state EOC conference calls or is stationed at an activated emergency operations center, presenting current stage and discharge data, gauge status, and data-quality caveats, and answering responders' questions in real time.

Public/agency-facing data products: the technician updates flood-event dashboards, WaterAlert threshold notifications, and situation-report tables of current stages versus flood stage, distributing them to emergency management, weather service, and partner agency distribution lists during the event.

tasks.label: Follow nuclear equipment operational policies and procedures that ensure environmental safety.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Operating nuclear power plant: routine radiological surveillance rounds per RP procedures — walking a defined route through auxiliary/turbine building areas with a survey instrument, taking dose-rate readings at designated points, recording them, and flagging changed radiological conditions for ALARA/job planning.

Job-site contamination control inside the radiologically controlled area per procedure: frisking personnel and tools, taking smear/swipe samples, erecting and posting contamination boundaries, bagging/labeling contaminated material at the work face, and controlling material released from the area.

Radwaste handling per waste-management procedures at a plant/decommissioning waste facility: sorting and size-reducing contaminated components and dry active waste, packaging into drums/boxes/skips, surveying and labeling containers for storage or shipment.

Laboratory or research facility: operating hot cells, gloveboxes, irradiators, or research-reactor sample systems per operating procedures — transferring, weighing and measuring radioactive samples, maintaining containment/confinement, and segregating the resulting waste.

Environmental and effluent-pathway monitoring field work per REMP/ODCM procedures: swapping air-sampler filters and dosimeters at monitoring stations, collecting surface water, soil, and vegetation samples at off-site locations, and chain-of-custody transfer to the counting lab.

tasks.label: Conduct surveillance testing to determine safety of nuclear equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quarterly in-service test of a safety-related pump (e.g., auxiliary feedwater, service water, RHR) at an operating nuclear power plant: start the pump per procedure, record suction/discharge pressure and flow, take contact vibration readings at prescribed bearing points with a handheld analyzer, check seal leakage, compare to IST reference values and acceptance criteria, and document; performed in cluttered pump rooms with stairs, insulation, and radiological controls.

Valve surveillance testing at a power plant: stroke-time testing of motor- and air-operated valves, exercising check valves, verifying remote position indication, and seat-leakage/local leak-rate checks; involves local observation, hooking up test connections or diagnostic sensors, coordinating with the control room, and restoring the system line-up.

Periodic calibration/channel functional test of safety-related instrumentation (pressure, level, flow transmitters, bistables) either at a rack in the plant or on a bench in the I&C shop: connect calibration equipment, apply input signals across the range, record as-found and as-left data, adjust setpoints, and document against tolerance.

Radiation protection instrument surveillance in the calibration lab/RP shop: daily source response checks, battery/electronic checks, and periodic calibration of portable survey meters, friskers, area radiation monitors and dosimeters against known sources, with pass/fail documentation and stickering.

Monthly emergency diesel generator (or other standby equipment) surveillance run: start the machine, load it, log local parameters (temperatures, pressures, voltage/frequency, fuel oil level), walk down for leaks and abnormal noise, verify acceptance criteria, then secure and restore standby readiness.

Research reactor or national-laboratory facility surveillance checkout: daily/weekly and annual checks of reactor instrumentation, scram/rod-drop timing, interlocks and alarms, area monitors, ventilation and confinement equipment, spanning several systems throughout the building and documented against technical specifications.

tasks.label: Monitor nuclear reactor equipment performance to identify operational inefficiencies, hazards, or needs for maintenance or repair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Control-room / local control-panel shift surveillance at a power or research reactor: the technician watches reactor and balance-of-plant parameters on control boards and plant-computer displays, logs periodic readings, interprets alarms, spots adverse trends, and reports off-normal indications for maintenance follow-up.

Routine field monitoring rounds through turbine hall, auxiliary building, pump and heat-exchanger rooms and the outdoor yard: read local gauges and sight glasses, check pump/motor bearing temperatures, look for oil, water or steam leaks, listen for abnormal noise, note fouled filters or tripped indicators, log readings and write up deficiencies/work requests. Fixed layout, stairs, congested walkways, plant-controlled access.

Scheduled condition-monitoring surveys with portable sensing instruments: infrared thermography of motors, breakers, transformers and piping; ultrasonic/acoustic surveys for air, steam and valve leaks and abnormal machine noise; results trended against baselines to flag degrading equipment.

Vibration-route data collection on rotating machinery: the technician walks a route of pumps, fans and motors, attaches a contact accelerometer at specified bearing points (often behind guards or in tight spaces), collects spectra with a handheld analyzer, and downloads them for analysis to detect bearing wear or imbalance.

Radiological monitoring inside the radiologically controlled area: dose-rate and contamination surveys around reactor coolant systems, filters and waste-processing equipment; mapping hot spots that indicate leakage or crud buildup; documenting results and posting hazards, often during outages with elevated dose fields.

Outage in-service inspection of reactor components: setting up and running remote tooling for steam-generator eddy-current tube examinations and underwater reactor-vessel/internals visual and ultrasonic inspection, then evaluating the acquired data for tube wear, cracking or wear of internals, inside containment/refueling cavity.

tasks.label: Test plant equipment to ensure it is operating properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine operability/condition round on running plant equipment in the turbine and auxiliary buildings of an operating nuclear station: walk a fixed route, read local pressure/flow/temperature gauges and panel indications, thermal-check pumps, motors and instrument cabinets, look and listen for leaks or abnormal noise, log readings and flag out-of-spec equipment for a work order.

Scheduled surveillance/functional test of installed equipment per a written procedure: locally start and stop a pump or diesel, stroke valves and dampers, position handswitches or breakers, hook up test gauges and vibration probes to installed test points, record parameters at several operating points, compare against acceptance criteria, restore the system to standby and sign the procedure. Tight spaces, ladders, PPE, radiological controls.

Routine bench functional/calibration check in the instrument shop or lab on a standard component brought to the bench (pressure/level transmitter, radiation monitor module, detector, small motor/actuator): connect to test set or test stand, exercise it over its range, compare against the standard, record as-found/as-left data, pass/fail against tolerance.

Bench troubleshooting of a malfunctioning or non-standard unit: isolate the fault with meters and scopes, open the case, adjust or swap internals, retest and requalify - the outcome is not predictable from a fixed test script.

Response/source checks and QC on radiation detection equipment: daily source-response and battery checks on portable survey meters and friskers, functional checks of personnel contamination monitors and portal monitors, counting-room detector QC with check sources and background counts, with pass/fail logged in the instrument record.

Equipment checks in radiologically controlled, hot or hard-to-reach areas during an outage or abnormal condition (containment, aux building, spent-fuel pool area, pipe chases): confirm equipment is running as indicated, spot leaks and hot spots, take radiation and temperature readings, report status back to the control room / RP.

tasks.label: Apply safety tags to equipment needing maintenance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hanging 'Danger — Do Not Operate' clearance tags on manual valves in an operating plant's auxiliary/turbine building: technician walks the clearance order, locates the valve by its ID plate among congested pipe runs, verifies position, and secures a card tag with a nylon tie or wire to the handwheel/stem, at heights from floor level to overhead platforms.

Tagging electrical isolation points in switchgear/MCC rooms: opening cubicle doors, verifying breaker/bucket identity, opening or racking out the disconnect, and attaching the tag (often with a lock/hasp) to the operating handle so it is plainly visible.

Tagging hand switches, control-board handles and panel-mounted controls in the control room or at local control panels: small tags clipped or tied to one specific switch handle among dozens of near-identical switches, without disturbing adjacent controls.

Hanging tags on components inside the radiologically controlled area/containment during an outage: dressed-out worker in anti-C clothing, congested scaffolded spaces, dose and stay-time limits, tags applied to valves, pumps, dampers and instrument isolation valves.

Tagging outdoor/yard equipment inside the protected area: transformers, emergency diesel generator controls, service-water and intake-structure valves, in weather, sometimes requiring ladder or platform access.

Tagging equipment in a research reactor, hot-cell or accelerator/laboratory facility: instrument racks, power supplies, glovebox and sampling-system valves, using small hang tags or adhesive caution tags on benchtop and rack-mounted apparatus.

sources.title: Robotic Hang Tag Applicator Machine
sources.claim: Commercially available robotic hang-tag applicator machines autonomously pick pre-printed paper/paperboard/plastic tags and attach them over the necks of products presented and positioned by timing screws and conveyors on a guarded production line, at up to 150 tags per minute, optionally affixing the tag with hot-melt glue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching hang tags to workpieces presented in a purpose-built line. The physical act — placing a card tag over or around a protruding feature and securing it — matches hanging a safety tag on a valve handwheel or switch handle when the component is fixtured and presented to the machine; tag size, weight and placement precision are comparable.

sources.title: IdentifEYE Dynamic Robotic Labelling System Utilises 3D Vision
sources.claim: A 6-axis robotic labelling system uses 3D vision to scan each item, read its existing label, choose a placement location and apply a printed tag/label to items of varying shape, orientation and position on a moving conveyor, with 5 mm placement accuracy and up ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided application of an identifying tag to a workpiece brought to the machine. It substantiates that a purpose-built cell can verify an item's identity from its existing markings and place a new tag at a specified, visible location on an irregular object — the perception and placement demands of hanging a safety tag on a fixtured component.

sources.system: Spot / Spot Arm with Orbit and Autowalk
sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot arm manipulation inside facilities is operator-driven or semi-autonomous; as of the October 2025 software release the only manipulation available within autonomous missions is opening doors, and that as a beta feature. No autonomous tag-attachment capability is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound facility-roaming (E2) manipulation autonomy: the most widely deployed legged inspection robot autonomously manipulates only doors, not small fasteners, ties or tags.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics (with nuclear utilities and Sellafield)
sources.title: How to Gather Better Data and Reduce Dosage in Nuclear Facilities
sources.claim: Spot is deployed in operating and decommissioning nuclear facilities, where it performs inspection and radiation-survey missions autonomously or under remote control in radiation zones; the deployed work is sensing and data collection, not attaching hardware or tags to plant components.
sources.transferJustification: Shows what autonomous robots actually do inside the E2 nuclear plant setting (inspection and radiation survey), establishing that tag application in that setting is not substantiated.

tasks.label: Follow policies and procedures for radiation workers to ensure personnel safety.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Radiologically controlled area (RCA) access at an operating power reactor: read and sign onto the radiation work permit, draw and wear TLD plus electronic dosimeter, dress out in anti-contamination coveralls, hood, booties and double gloves in the dress-out area; on exit, doff in the prescribed sequence at the step-off pad, whole-body frisk at a personnel contamination monitor, and close out recorded dose.

Dose and contamination monitoring compliance while carrying out monitoring duties inside plant or laboratory radiological areas: taking dose-rate and smear/swab surveys with calibrated instruments, watching accumulated dose and dose-rate alarms against RWP limits, avoiding contaminated surfaces, and recording/reporting readings that exceed expectations.

Compliance with radiological postings, boundaries and access controls during routine rounds in a plant, accelerator or laboratory: staying on approved routes, not entering high-radiation or contaminated zones without authorization, passing correctly through barriers, doors and access points, and logging the round.

Handling unsealed radioactive material and samples in a lab, counting room or hot-cell/hood setting per radiation-safety procedures: using shielding, remote tools and containment, minimizing handling time, controlling contamination, surveying the work area and hands afterward, and segregating radioactive waste.

Abnormal and changing radiological conditions: re-posting and roping off an area whose dose rates changed, erecting temporary shielding or a containment tent, responding to a contamination alarm, donning a respirator, and performing/supporting personnel decontamination.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with radiation detection payloads
sources.title: Making Radiation Mapping Safer & More Reliable | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot quadrupeds carrying radiation-detection payloads conduct autonomous radiation mapping operations inside radiologically controlled areas of nuclear facilities, living onsite within radiation zones and running repeatable survey missions without personnel present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic radiological survey/dose-rate mapping. It is the physical monitoring element of radiation-worker procedure compliance (instrument survey, dose tracking) carried out in the same institution-controlled nuclear facility the technician works in.

sources.developer: University of Manchester / RAICo / Sellafield Ltd / Ice Nine Robotics
sources.title: CARMA II: A ground vehicle for autonomous surveying of alpha, beta and gamma radiation (Frontiers in Robotics and AI, PMC)
sources.claim: CARMA II, an autonomous ground vehicle, performed the first autonomous radiometric survey on the active Sellafield nuclear site, detecting alpha/beta/gamma contamination and autonomously re-planning its path to avoid driving over contamination (a contamination-control rule executed by the machine).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous health-physics contamination survey. It substitutes for the surveyor's monitoring and contamination-avoidance procedures, in the same class of institution-controlled active nuclear facility rooms.

sources.system: CERN mobile manipulators with Autopilot (SPS radiation survey robots, MIRA campaign)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Execution of Safe and Precise Robotic Radiation Surveys in the Super Proton Synchrotron
sources.claim: Two mobile manipulators at CERN execute fully autonomous radiation surveys in the SPS accelerator tunnel, including navigating along beam components, crossing safety doors, maneuvering in the beam-dump area and access points, and docking at charging stations, replacing surveys that would otherwise expose personnel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous radiation survey rounds in a controlled nuclear/accelerator facility. Route adherence, authorized door/access-point crossing and survey execution are precisely the boundary-and-monitoring procedures a radiation worker must follow on rounds.

sources.title: THEODORICO 2 Robotic Dispenser for Radiopharmaceuticals - Comecer
sources.claim: Theodorico 2 is a commercially sold, fully automated shielded dispensing cell in which a robot handles radiopharmaceutical vials through all stages of dispensing behind 75-100 mm lead shielding, eliminating operator dose.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling unsealed radioactive liquids under radiation-protection controls. Same objects (vials, syringes, unsealed activity), same precision, and the radiation-safety controls (shielding, containment, minimized handling) are executed by the machine inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Multiradionuclide automatic dispensing system (ADS) for radiopharmaceutical syringes
sources.developer: hospital radiopharmacy (reported in Journal of Nuclear Medicine Technology)
sources.title: A Multiradionuclide Automatic Dispensing System for Syringes of Radiopharmaceuticals: The Effect on Operator Hand Dose
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed hospital study found that introducing a multiradionuclide automatic dispensing system for radiopharmaceutical syringes cut technologists' hand dose by 69%, showing routine clinical operation of robotic radioactive-material handling in place of manual handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dispensing/handling unsealed radioactive material in a shielded automated cell, which is the lab instance's radiation-safety-controlled material handling performed to accepted clinical quality.

sources.system: Spot at Chornobyl / Sellafield (with protective suit and rubber socks)
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / University of Bristol / Sellafield Ltd / UKAEA
sources.title: The robots working in the UK's most radioactive places - Ingenia
sources.claim: Robots sent into highly contaminated areas are protected and decontaminated by human crews: Spot wore protective suits/rubber socks at Sellafield and Chornobyl that people removed and discarded afterwards; no robot dresses itself or surveys itself out of a contaminated area.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the PPE/personnel-monitoring instance: the contamination-control steps around the robot are performed by human staff, so no cited system completes dress-out, frisking or decontamination itself.

sources.system: Quadruped robot with RAICo contamination-swabbing attachment
sources.title: Sellafield and RAICo trial contamination swabbing quadruped robot
sources.claim: Sellafield and RAICo completed a first field trial of a contamination-swabbing tool on a quadruped robot in an area containing radioactive material, replicating a routine health-physics swab task; the trial is a prototype demonstration and autonomy level is not stated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine contamination swab sampling by a mobile robot in an active nuclear facility; autonomy is unstated, so it is treated as teleoperated and does not carry a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Modify, devise, or maintain nuclear equipment used in operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Instrument shop / calibration lab: technician performs periodic calibration, response (source) checks, battery/probe replacement and minor repair of portable radiation survey meters, friskers, air samplers and count-rate instruments — mounting each unit on the calibration bench, exposing to sources, reading and adjusting the instrument, documenting results and affixing calibration stickers.

Dosimetry lab: batch calibration/QA irradiation and functional verification of personnel dosimeters (OSL/TLD badges, electronic personal dosimeters) — loading carriers, exposing to known doses, reading responses, generating pass/fail calibration records.

Radiologically controlled areas of an operating power plant: corrective and preventive maintenance on installed nuclear equipment (area radiation monitors, continuous air monitors, process/effluent radiation monitor skids, sampling panels) — troubleshooting electronics, replacing detectors, pumps, filters and cabling in place, then recalibrating and returning to service.

Plant chemistry/counting room or research-lab: maintaining and repairing counting and analytical nuclear equipment (HPGe/NaI detector systems, LN2 and gas supplies, shield doors, sample changers, gloveboxes/fume hoods, vacuum pumps, electronics racks), including diagnosing faults and replacing modules.

Shop/lab bench: devising, fabricating and modifying apparatus for a specific job — custom shielding, detector mounts and collimators, sample holders, cabling harnesses, jigs and modifications to an experimental rig — measuring, cutting, machining/welding, assembling, fitting and functionally checking against the intended use.

Field/outage or decommissioning work: installing or modifying temporary monitoring and support equipment in congested, taken-as-found locations (containment during outage, legacy facility, scaffolded or contaminated spaces) — mounting monitors, routing cable and hoses, adapting mounts on the spot under contamination controls.

sources.system: Utility robot fleets (Boston Dynamics Spot, Flyability Elios, Deep Trekker ROVs, magnetic crawlers) at seven U.S. nuclear utilities
sources.developer: Idaho National Laboratory (survey); Boston Dynamics, Flyability, Deep Trekker, Gecko Robotics (platforms)
sources.title: Robotic automation of maintenance work in nuclear power plants: a cross-sector survey and roadmap (INL/JOU-26-90002)
sources.claim: A 2026 Idaho National Laboratory cross-sector survey of seven U.S. nuclear utilities found robots in operating plants are used almost exclusively as mobile sensing platforms; physical interaction with plant equipment (operating valves, using tools, mechanical adjustments) is rare and considered a future objective.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers maintenance work (servicing, repair, replacement) on nuclear plant equipment — the same activity as this task — and establishes that deployed nuclear-plant robots do not perform it.

sources.system: Nuclear utility robotics programs (survey of U.S. NPPs)
sources.title: Robotic automation of maintenance work in nuclear power plants: a cross-sector survey and roadmap
sources.claim: The same INL survey reports that nuclear robotic use remains concentrated in inspection with limited application to physical maintenance, and that utilities still want, as a future capability, robots able to do cleaning, torquing, valve manipulation and simple adjustments.

sources.system: Hopewell Designs automated dosimetry calibration systems / automated sample changers (multi-axis motion systems with Automated Irradiator Software)
sources.title: Hopewell Designs: APPLICATIONS: Automated Radiation Systems
sources.claim: Hopewell Designs supplies purpose-built automated radiation calibration systems, including dosimetry calibration systems that process 100 dosimeters automatically and issue pass/fail reports, and automated sample changers that run without operator interaction.
sources.transferJustification: Periodic calibration and QA verification of dosimetry equipment is the maintenance activity performed on this class of nuclear monitoring equipment; the machine handles, irradiates, reads and dispositions the units end-to-end in a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.system: Mirion Robotic Table (automated BeOSL dosimetry system)

sources.transferJustification: Verifying calibration factors and running QA irradiations is the routine upkeep performed on dosimetry equipment used in radiological operations; the device performs the physical handling and exposure automatically.

sources.system: Hopewell Designs Automated Irradiator Software (AIS) calibration irradiators
sources.title: Hopewell Designs: APPLICATIONS: Calibration Irradiators and Service
sources.claim: Hopewell's Automated Irradiator Software automates irradiator setup, exposure-rate calculation and data capture for survey-meter calibration, but the human operator remains in control of the process; instrument mounting, reading and adjustment are not automated.

sources.system: AutoInspect autonomy stack on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.developer: Oxford Robotics Institute / UK Atomic Energy Authority
sources.title: Autonomous robot paves the way for future fusion maintenance | Oxford Robotics Institute
sources.claim: The first fully autonomous robot deployment in a fusion (nuclear) facility, a 35-day trial of Boston Dynamics Spot running Oxford Robotics Institute's AutoInspect at UKAEA's JET, performed mapping and sensor readings — inspection only, with no physical maintenance manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Marks the state of the art for autonomy inside nuclear facilities: sensing and navigation, not repair, modification or fabrication of equipment, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.developer: UK Atomic Energy Authority (RACE) and partners
sources.title: Robot-Assisted Glovebox Teleoperation for Nuclear Industry (Robotics 10:85)
sources.claim: Robotic handling in nuclear gloveboxes — the setting for much laboratory nuclear-equipment work — is pursued as tele-manipulation with at most shared autonomy, not autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Glovebox/hot-cell manipulation is how nuclear laboratory equipment is serviced and modified remotely; the state of practice being teleoperation means it cannot support an autonomous-completion judgment.

sources.system: Westinghouse Pegasys / SM-10W / ROSA steam generator service manipulators
sources.title: Steam Generator Maintenance Robot Design and Obstacle Avoidance Path Planning (Sensors 25:514)
sources.claim: Steam generator maintenance in nuclear plants is performed by special-purpose remote tooling and robotic arms (e.g., Westinghouse Pegasys, SM-10W, ROSA) delivered into the channel head and operated remotely by crews from outside.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing case of robotic maintenance on nuclear equipment; it is remotely operated special-purpose tooling for one known component, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of general instrument and equipment maintenance.

tasks.label: Perform testing, maintenance, repair, or upgrading of accelerator systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled preventive maintenance during a machine shutdown inside an accelerator vault/tunnel (research, medical or industrial accelerator): rebuilding an ion source, changing turbo/ion pumps and vacuum seals, servicing cooling-water circuits, filters and RF components. Cramped, activated hardware, hand tools, torque and UHV-cleanliness requirements, work under a radiation work permit.

In-situ diagnostic testing and calibration of installed accelerator subsystems: helium leak-checking a beam line, hi-pot/megger and oscilloscope measurements on magnet power supplies and equipment racks, checking beam-loss monitors, interlocks and safety-system functions by connecting portable instruments, then logging and interpreting results.

Bench testing and acceptance checks of accelerator components and spares in the facility electronics/vacuum shop: fixturing a power-supply module, amplifier, detector or valve on a test stand, connecting it, running the functional/electrical test sequence, and passing, tagging or rejecting the unit.

Unplanned troubleshooting and repair of a failed accelerator subsystem during a run: tracing a water leak, vacuum leak, failed power supply, tripped magnet, or cable/connector fault; diagnosing in place among mixed legacy hardware, swapping or repairing the component, retesting, and restoring beam.

Installation and upgrade work in the enclosure: mounting new magnets, diagnostics, collimators or shielding on a beam line, rigging heavy items, routing and terminating cables and services, aligning to the survey network, and performing commissioning checks.

Radiological survey and condition-monitoring rounds tied to accelerator maintenance: mapping residual dose rates along the beam line/enclosure after beam-off, checking gauges, temperatures and equipment condition on the walkdown, and logging survey data before workers enter the area.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Execution of Safe and Precise Robotic Radiation Surveys in the Super Proton Synchrotron

sources.claim: The MARWIN robot operates at ... performing autonomous radiation monitoring (gamma and neutron dose-rate measurement) along kilometre-long accelerator tunnel sections.

sources.claim: CERN's robotic platforms achieve dexterous maintenance manipulation (screwing, cutting, grasping) only under assisted teleoperation; their autonomous capability is limited to inspections and measurements in the accelerator complex.

tasks.label: Warn maintenance workers of radiation hazards and direct workers to vacate hazardous areas.

tasks.label: Calculate equipment operating factors, such as radiation times, dosages, temperatures, gamma intensities, or pressures, using standard formulas and conversion tables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Measure the intensity and identify the types of radiation in work areas, equipment, or materials, using radiation detectors or other instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine scheduled radiation (dose-rate) survey round of accessible radiologically controlled areas at an operating plant or research facility: walk a set route through rooms, corridors and equipment bays with ion chamber/teletector, take general-area and near-equipment dose rates at fixed survey points, note gamma/beta/neutron fields, log readings and produce the survey map/report.

Pre-entry characterization survey of a high-dose, seldom-entered or unentered space (containment penetration room, valve gallery, legacy cell, decommissioning building) before human work: map dose-rate fields, locate hot spots, and use spectrometry to identify the isotopes/radiation types present.

Room- or floor-scale contamination survey of a work area with alpha/beta/gamma instruments: scan floors and large surfaces at prescribed speed, flag and locate contamination, map results to support posting, release or decontamination of the area.

Job coverage during maintenance or an outage: stay with the work crew in a cramped, scaffolded, changing work space, take real-time and contact readings on components as systems are opened, frisk tools and hard-to-reach surfaces, take and count smears immediately, and adjust boundaries and stay times as fields change.

Bench/station measurement of items and samples brought to the instrument: count smears, air-filter and process/environmental samples on alpha-beta counters and gamma spectrometers for nuclide identification; assay waste drums, packages and tools/materials in clearance monitors for release; measure deposits inside process equipment.

Outdoor field/environmental radiological survey taken as found: site boundary and land-area gamma survey, soil/spill or lost-source search, characterization of open ground around a legacy or decommissioning site, with mapping of intensity and identification of radionuclides.

sources.title: Making Radiation Mapping Safer & More Reliable | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics offers Spot commercially with gamma, neutron and alpha radiation payloads plus gamma cameras/spectrometers, running repeatable autonomous radiation-mapping missions inside nuclear plants and decommissioning sites.

sources.title: Autonomous Radiation Mapping Using a Manipulator-Equipped Quadruped with Flexible Behavior Design (Applied Sciences)

tasks.label: Identify and implement appropriate decontamination procedures, based on equipment and the size, nature, and type of contamination.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ spot/area decontamination inside an operating plant's radiologically controlled area: after a leak, valve repack or maintenance job, the technician surveys the affected floor, wall, scaffold or equipment exterior, picks a method (wipe-down with decon solution, HEPA vacuum, strippable coating, hand scrubbing), performs it around installed plant equipment and other workers, then re-surveys to release the area.

Decontamination of removable tools, hardware, hoses, scaffold sections and dismantled components in the plant/decommissioning-site decon shop: items are brought in bagged, staged on racks or fixtures, cleaned by wiping, hot wash, ultrasonic bath, or abrasive/UHP water blasting inside a booth or cell, then frisked/clearance-monitored for release.

Personnel and PPE decontamination at the control point: a worker alarms a frisker or portal monitor; the technician identifies the nuclide/extent, removes and bags contaminated protective clothing or respirators, directs and assists skin/hair washing with mild decon agents, re-frisks, and documents the event.

Hot lab, radiochemistry lab or radiopharmacy: a liquid or powder spill on a bench, fume hood, sink or glovebox interior; the technician contains it, selects the decon agent for the nuclide and surface (absorbents, detergents, complexants, acid wipes), cleans small fixed and portable apparatus, and verifies with swipes/counting.

Large-scale decontamination during an outage or decommissioning: chemical decon of a system or loop, concrete scabbling/milling of building surfaces, cell or cubicle cleanout, tank and pit cleaning; long-duration work in cluttered, sometimes high-dose in-plant spaces with temporary containments and ventilation.

Decontamination of large removable items brought to a wash/blast station: waste boxes and containers, casks, large pumps, motors and valves; survey, wash or blast the exterior, spot-treat hot areas, re-survey for shipment or free release.

tasks.label: Decontaminate objects by cleaning them using soap or solvents or by abrading using brushes, buffing machines, or sandblasting machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small contaminated hand tools, fittings, fasteners and portable instruments brought to the plant's decontamination shop on carts: technician scrubs them in a sink or decon tank with detergent and brushes, runs an ultrasonic bath, wipes with solvent, dries, then frisks/surveys each item and repeats until it meets free-release or reuse limits; rinse water and rags collected as radwaste.

Radiochemistry / health-physics laboratory: glassware, sample vials, planchets, sample holders, tongs and small lab tools contaminated during sample prep are cleaned with detergent, dilute acid or solvents, brushed and rinsed at a bench sink or washer, then smear-tested and re-cleaned until swipes are clean.

Decon bay work on larger components - valve bodies, pump internals, motors, scaffold sections, tool boxes, contaminated steel parts - decontaminated by abrasive blasting in a blast cabinet/booth, high-pressure water washing or hydrolasing, with the technician manipulating the nozzle in PPE or through glove ports, then surveying and re-blasting missed areas.

In-field decontamination during an outage inside the radiologically controlled area: wiping and scrubbing installed equipment, cabinets, handrails, floors and walls in containment or the auxiliary building with rags, detergent, solvents or strippable coatings, in cramped cluttered high-dose spaces with hoses, scaffolding and other crews working nearby.

Hot cell or glovebox work: contaminated items, sample containers and in-cell tooling cleaned with solvents, wipes and brushes using master-slave manipulators or glove ports before transfer out of the shielded enclosure, with smear surveys at the transfer port.

Decommissioning/dismantling site: removing contaminated surface layers from concrete and structural steel in a partially dismantled building by scabbling, hydroblasting or sandblasting, with variable access, temporary lighting and containment tents, and no fixed layout.

sources.system: ROBBE (robot-operated UHP water jet decontamination cell)
sources.developer: Fraunhofer IGD / TSE Wassmann (at RWE Biblis NPP)
sources.title: ROBBE - Autonomous Robot-Operated water jet blasting of assemblies during dismantling of nuclear power plants (INIS record)
sources.claim: ROBBE is a robot-operated, autonomous decontamination system that removes contaminated surface coatings from dismantled nuclear power plant components by ultra-high-pressure water jet blasting inside an enclosed decontamination cabinet; components are clamped on a zero-point plate and the robot autonomously 3D-scans each arbitrary part and plans its own blasting trajectories. An industrial-scale prototype was built and made operational at the Biblis NPP dismantling site.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: removing radioactive contamination from objects by high-pressure/abrasive blasting to a releasable standard, with the object presented fixtured to the machine, at a nuclear site.

sources.title: ROBBE - Robot-aided processing of assemblies during the dismantling of nuclear power plants (EPJ Nuclear Sciences & Technologies)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed account of ROBBE: the robot autonomously digitizes arbitrary object geometries with no CAD model and no manual teaching, plans trajectories covering the component's visible surfaces, carries out the decoating inside the decontamination cabinet, and may reposition and re-clamp the component to ensure all its surface is thoroughly cleaned.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (abrasive/high-pressure decontamination of contaminated objects); establishes that the cell handles one-off, non-repeating part geometries rather than a single fixed product.

sources.system: Blastman B20S / B20CX blast cleaning robots
sources.title: BLASTMAN BLAST CLEANING ROBOTS IN DIFFERENT INDUSTRIES
sources.claim: Blastman supplies commercial gantry- and wall-mounted abrasive blast-cleaning robots that work inside enclosed blast chambers, running in automatic programmed mode to clean workpieces of widely varying size and shape to a specified surface cleanliness (Sa 2.5) with no human in the chamber.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive blast cleaning of component surfaces to a specified cleanliness standard - same tooling (blast nozzle), same class of objects (metal components and structures), same enclosed-cabinet presentation as a nuclear decontamination blast booth.

sources.title: RoboWash Robotic Industrial Parts Washer
sources.claim: Fives RoboWash is a commercially supplied robotic industrial parts washer in which a 6-axis robot manipulates each part through pre-wash, high-pressure aqueous wash, deburring and drying stages inside a sealed machine, cleaning complex external and internal surfaces to production cleanliness specifications; Fives washers are installed in tier-1 automotive plants across Europe, Asia and the Americas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing objects clean with aqueous detergent solution and high-pressure jets to an accepted cleanliness spec - the same physical act as soap/solvent cleaning of tools and glassware, with the part fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.system: Diakont robotic cavity cleaning and decontamination ROV-crawler
sources.developer: Diakont (for FirstEnergy, Perry Nuclear Power Plant)

sources.claim: In-plant decontamination of installed surfaces (refueling cavity walls, floors and pool surfaces) at US nuclear plants is performed with a self-propelled ROV-crawler driven by an operator; the deployed service is described as remotely operated rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly matches the in-field decontamination instance; cited to show the fielded capability there is teleoperated and therefore cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: SaND / ROBDEKON automated wall decontamination platform

sources.claim: Robotic decontamination of walls and surfaces inside nuclear facilities remains a research prototype in the German ROBDEKON programme: a mobile elevating platform is being converted into a decontamination system intended to run in teleoperation as well as automatic mode.
sources.transferJustification: Directly matches the in-situ surface decontamination instance; cited as evidence that no fielded autonomous system exists for it.

sources.system: Nuclear decommissioning robotic deployments (review of fielded practice)
sources.title: From traditional robotic deployments towards assisted robotic deployments in nuclear decommissioning
sources.claim: A 2025 review of robotics in nuclear decommissioning states that regulation in countries such as the UK generally requires the operator to remain in complete control of any ... or tool during its deployment, so fielded nuclear cleanup robots are teleoperated rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the negative judgments on in-situ decontamination in occupied nuclear facilities and on dismantling sites.

tasks.label: Collect air, water, gas or solid samples for testing to determine radioactivity levels or to ensure appropriate radioactive containment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine plant chemistry grab sampling at a nuclear power plant sample room/sample sink: technician lines up valves, purges the sample line, fills shielded vials/bottles with reactor coolant, secondary-side, or liquid radwaste tank samples, caps, wipes down and surveys the container, labels it and carries it to the counting lab, all under ALARA/dose and contamination-control rules.

Air sampling in radiologically controlled areas and effluent paths: placing and retrieving portable low-volume air samplers near work in containment/auxiliary buildings during outages, changing particulate filters and charcoal iodine cartridges on continuous air monitors and ventilation-stack samplers, bagging and delivering media to the count room. Areas are cluttered with scaffolding, hoses and temporary shielding.

Gas grab sampling: drawing samples from waste gas decay tanks, containment atmosphere, off-gas/hydrogen headers and stack noble-gas sample points into evacuated gas bombs or syringes at fixed sample stations, then transferring to the lab for gamma counting.

Bulk liquid/slurry and solid process-media sampling: spent resin beads, sludge, evaporator bottoms, tank waste, spent filter media and waste-drum characterization samples drawn from tanks and process lines into vials/bottles, often through shielded sample stations because of high dose rates.

Smear/swipe sampling and miscellaneous solid item sampling in plant areas: wiping 100 cm2 of floors, tool surfaces, equipment, laundry and shipping containers with filter paper, mounting the smears in planchets, plus scraping/collecting bits of scale, insulation, concrete or debris for isotopic analysis. Surfaces vary in shape, height and accessibility.

Off-site environmental (REMP) sampling round: driving to scattered perimeter and control locations to collect surface water, well/drinking water and discharge-canal water, shoreline sediment/soil, and to retrieve filters and cartridges from perimeter air-sampling stations (with occasional vegetation or milk grab samples at nearby farms), bottling, preserving and labeling each with chain-of-custody.

sources.title: Robot dog fetches radiation data: Surry's award winner makes new strides (ANS Nuclear Newswire)

sources.transferJustification: Related task (in-plant autonomous radiological rounds); cited to bound E2: what mobile autonomy in a working plant currently delivers is in-situ measurement, not valve line-ups, vial filling, smear wiping or sample transport, so it does not substantiate E2 completion of this task.

tasks.label: Set up equipment that automatically detects area radiation deviations and test detection equipment to ensure its accuracy.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic source check / operability and alarm test of installed monitoring equipment in a nuclear plant: technician walks the rounds with a check source, exposes each area radiation monitor, portal/personnel contamination monitor and continuous air monitor, verifies indicated dose rate, alarm actuation and control-room indication, and documents the surveillance.

Instrument calibration lab (plant instrument shop, DOE/utility cal lab): bench calibration and accuracy testing of portable survey meters, friskers, ion chambers and electronic personal dosimeters using a shielded irradiator with positioning bench — as-found readings on each scale/decade, adjustment if out of tolerance, as-left readings, sticker and calibration record.

Setting up temporary/portable radiation detection equipment for a job or outage: carrying a portable area radiation monitor, continuous air monitor or teledosimetry unit into a congested work area (scaffolding, hoses, contamination boundaries), siting it for coverage, powering/connecting it, entering alarm setpoints, source-checking it and posting it.

Installing or replacing a permanent area radiation monitor channel: mounting the detector/bracket on wall or structure, routing and terminating signal and power cable to the readout module, configuring the channel, then performing the post-installation functional/loop test with a source and verifying remote indication.

Laboratory counting room (research reactor, radiochemistry/environmental lab): setting up counting geometry and running routine performance verification of detection instruments — check-source counts, energy/efficiency calibration checks and control charting of gamma spectrometers and alpha/beta counters.

Outdoor/field setup of environmental or emergency-response radiation monitoring: placing perimeter monitoring stations, TLD posts or portable telemetered monitors at off-site or laydown locations on varied terrain, powering and communications setup, then field response check.

roles.title: Nuclear Monitoring Technicians
roles.description: Collect and test samples to monitor results of nuclear experiments and contamination of humans, facilities, and environment.

tasks.label: Monitor personnel to determine the amounts and intensities of radiation exposure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Operating nuclear power plant control point: a worker leaving the radiologically controlled area is monitored for external contamination and has their electronic dosimeter read and dose logged; no contamination is found and the worker is released. High volume (hundreds to thousands of exits per shift during outages).

Same control point, but the exit monitor alarms or the tech suspects contamination: technician performs a hand-held pancake-probe frisk over the worker's body and clothing to locate the activity, removes/decontaminates skin or clothing, re-surveys, assesses shallow/skin dose, and writes the personnel contamination event record.

Job coverage: RP technician accompanies or covers a work crew in a radiation area (containment during outage, steam generator platform, glovebox line, or a field job such as industrial radiography or emergency response), taking dose-rate readings at the workers' positions, watching electronic-dosimeter telemetry, adjusting stay times, and pulling workers out as dose or dose-rate limits are approached.

Dosimetry program: issuing/returning legal dosimeters (TLD/OSL cards, EPDs) to monitored workers and periodically processing them to determine each person's dose of record - loading badge cards into the reader, running the batch, checking readings against electronic dose, and posting results to the exposure record.

Internal dose monitoring: routine or for-cause in vivo whole-body count of a worker in the counting room - setting the subject up in the counter, running the count, identifying nuclides in the spectrum, computing committed dose and issuing the report.

Non-power facility (hospital nuclear medicine/radiopharmacy hot lab, university research lab, radiopharmaceutical production): screening staff hands, feet and clothing for contamination when leaving the handling area and checking/exchanging their personal dosimeters and reading dosimeter results.

sources.title: Argos™ PAB Whole Body Contamination Monitors | Mirion
sources.claim: Argos whole-body surface contamination monitors are commercial, widely installed machines that automatically screen personnel for external contamination at radiologically controlled area entrances/exits, with contoured whole-body detector geometry and an automatic release-limit algorithm.

sources.claim: A field-proven automatic TLD card reader mechanically feeds, heats and evaluates personnel dosimeter cards from a 1400-card carousel at 140 cards/hour, producing whole-body, extremity and neutron dose values with chain-of-custody records - machine determination of personnel dose of record.

sources.developer: University of Manchester / RAICo / Sellafield / Ice Nine Robotics
sources.title: CARMA II: A ground vehicle for autonomous surveying of alpha, beta and gamma radiation
sources.claim: An autonomous ground robot performed the first autonomous radiometric survey on the ..., mapping alpha/beta/gamma contamination and correctly locating a known alpha source, taking over monotonous room-scale survey work from health physics surveyors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: area/surface radiological survey inside a nuclear facility. It shows a mobile robot can autonomously measure radiation and contamination in plant spaces, but it measures places, not people, and neither frisks a worker nor supervises an individual's exposure, so it does not transfer to personnel monitoring.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with radiation detection payloads

sources.claim: Spot quadrupeds carrying radiation-detection payloads conduct autonomous radiation mapping in nuclear plants and have measured radiation dose during Fukushima Daiichi decommissioning work since 2022.

It demonstrates autonomous measurement of radiation intensity where people work, but the payload records the robot's own exposure, not a worker's, and no cited system escorts, times or withdraws workers, so job-coverage personnel monitoring is not substantiated.

tasks.label: Provide initial response to abnormal events or to alarms from radiation monitoring equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fixed area radiation monitor or continuous air monitor alarm in an operating nuclear plant's radiologically controlled area where the response is verification only: the technician carries a calibrated portable survey instrument to the alarming monitor's location, confirms and maps the elevated dose rate or airborne activity, determines the affected extent, and reports readings to the control room. Fixed, known indoor locations; corridors, stairs, shield-maze entrances; PPE worn.

Alarm signalling a real radiological hazard requiring immediate protective action: the technician stops work and moves workers out of the space, ropes off and posts a new high-radiation or airborne-radioactivity boundary, locks a door or repositions/shields the source or closes a valve, then re-surveys and notifies supervision. Cluttered plant or hot-shop spaces, time pressure, anti-C clothing.

Personnel contamination monitor, hand-and-foot monitor, portal, or worker electronic-dosimeter alarm at a control point: the technician responds to the alarming individual, frisks body and clothing with a hand probe held ~1 cm from the surface, locates and quantifies the contamination, decontaminates skin/clothing with tape and wipes, re-surveys until release criteria are met, takes nasal smears if warranted, and documents the event and dose.

Alarm caused by monitoring-equipment failure or a spurious trip: the technician goes to the instrument (CAM, area monitor, effluent monitor, count-room detector), inspects it, performs a check-source response test, replaces filter paper, pump, battery or detector, resets or recalibrates, tags out the unit and stages a temporary monitor if needed, and documents the failure.

Loose-contamination event or spill in a laboratory, hot shop, or plant area: the technician responds, delineates and posts the contaminated area, takes smears/swipes and counts them, contains the spill with absorbent pads and plastic, surveys floor paths and any personnel who left the area, and starts decontamination.

Alarm or off-normal reading from an outdoor environmental/effluent monitoring station or site perimeter station: the technician drives to the field station, checks the equipment and power, collects the air filter or sample for counting, and surveys the surrounding ground with handheld instruments in open terrain and whatever weather is present.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot (Spot CAM+IR / EAP payloads) at Surry Nuclear Power Station
sources.title: Dominion Energy | Boston Dynamics (case study)
sources.claim: Spot with radiation-detection payloads ran fully autonomous, unsupervised radiation-survey missions inside Dominion's Surry Nuclear Power Station, producing the same readings as human technicians with better consistency.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine radiological dose-rate survey in a plant RCA. The initial verification response to a fixed-monitor alarm uses the same detector, the same fixed indoor locations, and yields the same output (dose-rate readings/map relayed to the control room), so survey performance carries over.

sources.title: CARMA II: A ground vehicle for autonomous surveying of alpha, beta and gamma radiation (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: CARMA II, an autonomous ground vehicle, performed the first autonomous alpha/beta/gamma radiometric survey on the Sellafield ..., locating and correctly mapping a known alpha contamination source while re-planning to avoid spreading contamination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: room-scale radiation/contamination survey in an operating nuclear facility. Locating and mapping an unexpected source is the measurement core of investigating an abnormal radiological indication, with the same detectors in the same class of facility.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot radiation mapping solution
sources.title: Making Radiation Mapping Safer & More Reliable | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot is sold and used for autonomous radiation mapping inside nuclear facilities, able to be stationed within radiation zones and run survey missions autonomously on demand or on schedule.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (nuclear plant RCA) and same sensing work as the verification survey done on an alarm response; establishes commercial availability of on-demand autonomous survey missions.

sources.claim: Spot's arm can open doors autonomously during recorded Autowalk missions, allowing an autonomous inspection mission to traverse a plant's internal doors without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Supports only the navigation portion of an autonomous alarm-verification mission inside a plant (doors between rooms); it is not evidence of dexterous radiological work.

sources.claim: The most advanced robotic response to a radiological spill and contamination swabbing at Sellafield was driven by an operator's hand movements captured by a haptic controller - continuous teleoperation, not autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point for spill/contamination-event response; it shows the state of the art for the hands-on portion is haptic teleoperation, so it cannot support a positive judgment.
