sources.claim: IAEA UAV systems carrying radiation detectors, cameras and GPS were validated with Fukushima Prefecture for radiological mapping in routine and emergency situations, but they are operator-run measurement campaigns that perform no equipment checks or sample collection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor environmental radiation mapping. Relevant to the field-station instance, but autonomy is not established and the system does none of the station check or sample retrieval.

tasks.label: Determine intensities and types of radiation in work areas, equipment, or materials, using radiation detectors or other instruments.

instances.label: Routine scheduled area radiation (dose-rate) survey along an established route inside the radiologically controlled area of an operating nuclear power plant or licensed facility: walk the route with an ion chamber/GM survey meter, take gamma dose-rate readings at fixed survey points, check for hot spots, and log readings onto a survey map used to set entry and PPE requirements.

Direct scan (frisk) contamination survey of floors and large open surfaces in a controlled facility area with alpha/beta/gamma probes: systematic coverage of a room or corridor floor, discriminating radiation type, locating and marking any contaminated spots, producing a survey map.

Survey requiring wipe/smear sampling for removable contamination on benches, tool surfaces, equipment casings, glovebox faces and hard-to-reach geometry: perform the dexterous wiping motion over a defined area, then count the smear and record alpha/beta activity against release limits.

Pre-job / job-coverage characterization survey in congested, high-dose or infrequently entered plant spaces during maintenance and outages: pipe cubicles, containment penetrations, spent-fuel and waste-processing areas; map gamma dose rates in three dimensions, distinguish neutron and gamma fields, identify hot spots and isotopes for ALARA work planning.

Measurement of discrete items and materials at a facility control point: tools, packages, waste drums, scrap and vehicles checked for contact and 1-m dose rates, contamination, and isotope identification before release, shipment or receipt.

Field survey of a setting taken as found: characterizing legacy, damaged or long-sealed structures, contaminated land and site perimeters, or responding to a spill or unknown-source event, where layout, obstacles and source distribution are unknown in advance and results must be located on a map of the area.

instances.label: Air particulate/charcoal filter samples from plant or perimeter air samplers are analyzed in the facility counting room: filter is mounted in a planchet/holder, loaded into a low-background alpha/beta counter or gamma spectrometer, counted for a set time, activity computed and compared with action levels, results logged.

Liquid samples (reactor coolant, liquid effluent, environmental or drinking water) analyzed in the plant chemistry/count lab: measured aliquot transferred to a Marinelli beaker or LSC vial with cocktail, counted by HPGe gamma spectroscopy or liquid scintillation (tritium, gross alpha/beta), spectrum quantified and nuclides identified.

Batches of smear/swipe samples (equipment, floors, personal items, shipping packages) counted in a count room or satellite counting station on an automatic or single-sample alpha/beta counter, results compared with contamination limits and recorded for the survey record.

Wet-chemistry radiochemical or elemental analysis in a radiochemistry lab with fume hoods and glassware: sample digestion/evaporation, precipitation or extraction-chromatography separation (e.g., Sr-90, isotopic actinides), mounting on planchets or vials, and counting or ICP-MS elemental determination, with tracer/yield QC.

On-site/field screening of grab samples at outdoor sampling points, environmental monitoring stations or remediation sites: water, soil or vegetation samples screened with portable counters/field instruments under weather and variable terrain, results used for immediate release or resampling decisions.

tasks.label: Set up equipment that automatically detects area radiation deviations and test detection equipment to ensure its accuracy.

instances.label: Instrument shop / calibration range: technician calibrates and accuracy-checks portable survey instruments (ion chambers, GM count-rate meters, frisk-ers with alpha/beta probes) — battery and physical check, mounting the meter and its probe on the calibration bench in the correct geometry, exposing at several known dose rates, adjusting response, recording data, applying the calibration sticker and returning the meter to service.

Instrument lab: batch accuracy verification/calibration of electronic personal dosimeters and teledosimetry units — devices loaded into a shielded calibrator, irradiated to known doses, response compared to the standard, pass/fail decided and records/reports generated before the devices are re-issued.

Inside the radiologically controlled area: setting up temporary/portable area radiation monitors, continuous air monitors and telemetered dose-rate monitors for an outage job — carrying the units through a cluttered plant space with scaffolding and hoses, placing them on stands at the specified locations, connecting power/telemetry, entering alarm setpoints, doing a check-source response test, and posting/roping the area.

Periodic operability and accuracy test of installed fixed area radiation monitors, process and effluent monitors in the plant — carrying a check source to the wall/ceiling-mounted detector, positioning it in the specified geometry, verifying indicated reading and alarm at the local readout and in the control room, resetting the monitor and logging the surveillance.

Environmental/perimeter monitoring: installing and functionally testing offsite gamma monitoring stations, TLD posts and air-sampler/monitor stations at fencelines, roadside poles and host-property locations — mounting hardware, weatherproofing, powering, verifying detector response with a source, and retrieving/verifying data in all weather.

Field environmental-monitoring or decommissioning/remediation site (outdoor, temporary, layout varies site to site): contaminated sampling supplies, soil, filters and debris are drummed or overpacked on the spot for shipment.

Hot cell / shielded glovebox work at a research reactor, hot lab or radiopharmacy: high-activity waste (spent vials, broken hot-cell sample containers, swipes, small tools) is transferred with remote manipulators into shielded waste pots and posted out into shipping drums.

instances.label: Nuclear plant decon area / hot machine shop: technician decontaminates hand tools, small parts, scaffold clamps, portable instruments and fixtures carried in from the RCA - scrubbing in a sink with detergent, ultrasonic bath, solvent wipe, hand wire-brushing - then re-surveys the item before release.

In-situ decon inside the radiologically controlled area: wiping/scrubbing hot spots on installed piping, valve handwheels, pump housings, hood interiors, racks and floors in cramped, cluttered, high-dose spaces while suited up, on equipment that cannot be moved.

Field / emergency-response decon: vehicles, heavy equipment, sampling gear, boots and monitoring instruments pressure-washed, scrubbed with soap or wiped with solvent at an outdoor decon pad, spill site or environmental monitoring location, in weather and with no fixed layout.

instances.label: Routine standardization/calibration of benchtop chemical measurement instruments in the plant chemistry lab (pH meters, conductivity meters, ion-selective/sodium and dissolved-oxygen meters, titrators): rinse and condition the electrode, run it through buffer/standard solutions, check slope/offset against acceptance criteria, adjust, and document before returning the meter to service.

Calibration of laboratory analytical instruments that require multi-point standard curves (spectrophotometric/colorimetric analyzers, ion chromatographs, lab sodium/silica analyzers): prepare or load working standards, run the calibration series, verify QC/check standards against limits, accept or repeat the calibration, and record results.

Periodic calibration, verification and adjustment of installed in-line chemical sensing elements and analyzers at plant sample panels / the sample room (pH-ORP, conductivity cells, online sodium, silica, dissolved oxygen, hydrogen): isolate or retract the sensor, clean/condition it, expose it to buffer or standard solution or compare against a grab sample, adjust the transmitter, and return the loop to service.

Preventive and corrective maintenance of sensing elements and analyzer hardware using hand tools: replacing worn glass/reference electrodes, membranes and electrolyte, changing in-line filters, reagent and standard containers, replacing peristaltic tubing, compression fittings and o-rings, then leak-checking and re-standardizing the instrument.

Maintenance and repair of sampling system equipment in plant areas: unplugging or flushing sample lines, repairing/replacing isolation and flow-control valves, sample coolers, pressure regulators and sample pumps, adjusting sample flow; work occurs at varied elevations and inside radiologically controlled areas with contamination controls and protective clothing.

Field calibration and maintenance of environmental and effluent sampling/monitoring equipment at on-site and off-site stations: flow calibration of low-volume air samplers and iodine cartridge/particulate filter changes with a reference flow standard, servicing effluent sample pumps and monitors, weatherproofing and minor repairs, outdoors in variable weather.

tasks.label: Thin and space trees and control weeds and undergrowth, using manual tools and chemicals, or supervise workers performing these tasks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Precommercial thinning/spacing: technician walks a dense young conifer plantation or natural regeneration stand with a chainsaw or clearing saw, selects crop trees by species, vigor and target spacing, and cuts competing stems 1-6 in. diameter; sloped ground, slash, brush, stumps, variable visibility.

Area chemical vegetation control: mixing and applying labeled forestry herbicide over whole units for chemical site preparation after harvest, herbaceous weed control, or seedling release on a planted tract; must cover acres uniformly, honor buffers/streamside zones and avoid drift onto crop trees.

Spot/area treatment of invasive herbaceous infestations in open natural areas — phragmites or cattail in a wetland, knapweed/thistle on a prairie or rangeland unit, noxious weeds along a road corridor — mapping the patches and spraying them while sparing surrounding native vegetation.

Selective stem-by-stem chemical work inside a stand: cut-stump treatment of woody invasives, basal bark spray, hack-and-squirt injection, and directed backpack spray around planted seedlings under a residual canopy, working on foot among brush and desirable vegetation.

Mechanical control of weeds and undergrowth in maintained open areas: mowing or brush-cutting firebreaks, wildlife openings, fence lines, trail and road corridors, seed-orchard/nursery rows and campground margins with a mower, brush saw or string trimmer.

Supervising a thinning/vegetation-control crew or contractor: laying out and marking units and leave trees, briefing workers on prescription and safety, walking plots to check spacing, stump height and residual damage, and accepting or rejecting the work.

Dust, mud, deadfall, changing weather.

Foot patrol of trails and backcountry areas: hiking several miles of trail and visiting dispersed campsites, providing visible presence, checking for illegal camping, cut trees, off-trail damage and litter, contacting hikers, doing minor cleanup, and reporting conditions back to the district office. Steep, rough, unmapped natural terrain.

Rounds of developed recreation sites (campground loops, day-use areas, trailheads, boat ramps): checking site occupancy and fee/permit compliance, inspecting and cleaning fire rings, dousing abandoned campfires, hauling litter, unlocking/locking gates and restrooms, noting vandalism and hazards, and talking with campers about rules. Paved or graded loop roads inside an agency-controlled recreation site.

Fire-season detection patrol during high fire danger/red-flag conditions: covering an assigned block of forest to spot smoke or heat early, pinpointing and verifying the location, and reporting it to dispatch so an engine or crew can respond.

Boundary, timber-sale and project-area patrol: traversing brushy off-trail unit boundaries and active project areas to check for timber trespass, encroachment, unauthorized cutting, dumping or equipment damage, and recording locations of what is found for follow-up.

Directing a suppression response as the unit's fire duty officer or type 4/5 incident commander: taking the detection report, sizing up the incident, assigning engines and hand crews to divisions, ordering additional resources through dispatch, and managing radio command and incident documentation until the fire is controlled and released.

Running the fire crew training program: scheduling and delivering basic wildland (S-130/S-190) and annual refresher (RT-130) instruction, arranging arduous pack tests and field exercises, evaluating trainees and task books, and maintaining red-card qualification records for seasonal crews.

Coordinating the fire detection program: staffing and rostering lookouts, setting monitoring protocols for the detection camera network and aerial detection flights, determining and posting daily fire danger ratings, and routing reports of smokes to dispatch.

Coordinating fire prevention and public education programs: planning and giving school and community presentations, Smokey Bear/Firewise outreach and fair booths, directing placement of fire danger and restriction signage, and issuing public messaging on burn bans and permits.

tasks.label: Monitor activities of logging companies and contractors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During-operations ground inspection of an active harvest unit on a timber sale (federal, state, industrial or private-landowner job). The technician walks the unit through slash, stumps, mud and slopes while skidders/harvesters are working; verifies only designated/marked trees are cut, checks stump heights, top-diameter utilization and merchantable material left, damage to residual and reserve trees, leave-tree and SMZ boundaries, and locations of skid trails and landings; checks loads and log decks at the landing; talks with the operator and writes an inspection record or notice of noncompliance.

Inspection of haul roads, spur roads, landings and stream crossings for BMP and erosion-control compliance during and after operations: walking/driving rough forest roads, often after rain, checking water bars, culvert and crossing installation and function, rutting, silt fence and slash filter windrows, and sediment delivery to streams; directing the contractor to correct problems.

Closeout / post-harvest acceptance inspection of a completed unit: verifying slash treatment and lopping, landing and deck cleanup and trash removal, road closure, water-barring and seeding, retention and regeneration requirements, then signing off the contract and releasing performance bond.

Volume and load accountability at the mill scale or weigh station: verifying delivered truckloads against load tickets and contract terms, checking measured volume/weight, species and utilization, and reconciling scale slips to the sale account.

Remote/aerial monitoring of an ongoing job between site visits: flying the tract with a small drone (or tasking imagery) to map the cut boundary, measure acres harvested, track progress against schedule and spot obvious problems such as cutting outside the unit, producing an orthomosaic/report for the sale file.

tasks.label: Perform reforestation or forest renewal, including nursery and silviculture operations, site preparation, seeding and tree planting programs, cone collection, and tree improvement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hand-planting a regeneration unit: the technician and crew carry bare-root or container conifer seedlings in planting bags across a recently harvested or burned unit, pick microsites among slash, stumps, rocks and brush on uneven, often steep ground, and set each seedling upright at correct depth and spacing (~400-500 trees/acre) in variable weather.

Mechanical site preparation on a regeneration unit before planting: scarification, spot mounding, disc trenching, ripping or slash piling with heavy equipment across a cutover strewn with stumps, logging debris and rocks.

Chemical site preparation and herbaceous release: mixing and applying forestry herbicide over a regeneration tract (backpack, skidder-mounted or aerial application) at labeled rates, respecting stream buffers and drift limits, and documenting acres treated.

Direct or aerial seeding program: broadcasting conifer or native seed over post-fire, remote or otherwise inaccessible ground at a prescribed sowing rate, achieving uniform coverage of the mapped unit and recording acres seeded.

Nursery operations at a forest tree nursery/greenhouse: sowing container or bare-root crops (media fill, dibble, sow, cover, irrigate), transplanting plugs, thinning and culling, then lifting, grading, counting, bundling/packing and cold-storing seedlings for shipment to planting projects.

Cone/seed collection and tree improvement: collecting cones from crowns of standing or freshly felled trees (climbing, bucket lifts, squirrel caches) in stands and seed orchards, plus orchard work such as grafting scions, bagging flowers for controlled pollination, collecting pollen and tagging clones.

sources.system: Autoplant autonomous forest regeneration machine (Bracke planting/scarifying head on autonomous vehicle platform)
sources.developer: Skogforsk / Luleå University of Technology / KTH / Bracke Forest AB
sources.title: Autoplant—Autonomous Site Preparation and Tree Planting for a Sustainable Bioeconomy (Forests)
sources.claim: The Autoplant project (Skogforsk, LTU, KTH, Bracke Forest, Swedish forest companies) demonstrated an autonomous machine that scarified planting spots and planted seedlings on a clearcut in Sweden, but as a one-week research integration test with open problems in operating speed, sensor robustness and obstacle detection.

sources.system: PlantMax (PlantMa X) soil-prep and planting machine
sources.title: PlantMax premiere draws attention at Elmia Wood 2025 | Bioenergy International
sources.claim: The most advanced commercially sold mechanized forest planting machine still requires human operators in the cab controlling driving and planting, so machine planting of forest sites is not autonomous.

sources.system: Heavy-lift agricultural spray drones operated by forestry aerial applicators (e.g., Carter Aerial Land Management, LLC)
sources.developer: drone applicator service providers (Part 107 / 44807 exemption operators)
sources.title: What A Landowner Should Expect When Hiring a Drone Aerial Applicator for Forestry Herbicide Application (Clemson Land-Grant Press)
sources.claim: Commercial drone aerial applicators perform chemical site preparation and seedling release on forest tracts in the US South; the drone flies its spray mission autonomously within a geofence, with the operator only intervening on obstacle stops.

sources.system: Reforestation seeding drone swarms (Mast Reforestation/DroneSeed, AirSeed Technologies)
sources.title: New Tree Tech: Cutting-edge drones give reforestation a helping hand (Mongabay)
sources.claim: Seed-sowing drones fly pre-planned routes autonomously and drop seed pods over degraded and burned forest land, in swarms supervised by one person; Mast Reforestation used drone seeding on a 121-hectare reforestation project in western Oregon.

sources.system: BCC Nursery Production System (automatic filling and seeding line, BCC Precision Seeder)
sources.title: Nursery production systems and equipment - BCC
sources.claim: BCC AB supplies forest nurseries with automatic tray filling and seeding lines (de-stacker, filler, dibbler, precision seeder, seed covering, watering) that sow containerized forest seedling crops to better than 95% accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sowing/dibbling containerized forest seedling trays on a purpose-built line is the fixtured presentation of the same seed-sowing and planting-spot work, with the same objects (forest seed, Hiko-type trays) and depth/spacing precision.

sources.system: Automatic plug transplanters/sticking robots (Visser, TTA, AgriNomix RW 1500)
sources.title: 8 Transplanters to Help Right-Size Labor in Your Growing Operation (Greenhouse Grower)
sources.claim: Commercial greenhouse/nursery transplanting robots pick seedling plugs from trays and set them into containers or larger cells at high speed with servo-driven accuracy, including removing bad plugs and filling empty cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transplanting seedling plugs is the purpose-built-line form of seedling planting — same objects (containerized conifer/plug stock), same accepted output (seedling set upright at correct depth and spacing), performed under machine control.

sources.system: Burro / Burro Grande autonomous work robots
sources.title: Petitti Family Farms deploys 25 Burro autonomous robots (Landscape Management)
sources.claim: Burro autonomous robots are deployed in commercial nursery production, navigating around people to move plants and plant materials between propagation, growing areas and shipping, with fleets of 25 units at one grower.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-nursery haulage of plants and materials covers the transport legs of nursery seedling production, in the same nursery facilities and with the same containerized stock.

sources.date: 2014 (case studies; still described in 2019 trade press)
sources.title: Harvest Automation Robots Reduce Production Costs and Increase Capacity (RoboticsTomorrow)
sources.claim: Harvest Automation's HV-100 mobile robots autonomously space, consolidate and collect containerized plants in nurseries and greenhouses and have been used across grower operations in the US.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: container spacing/consolidation in nurseries is the same handling of potted seedling stock in the same forest/ornamental nursery growing areas.

sources.system: Stora Enso Plant Packer (automated seedling packing system)
sources.title: Automated packing of seedlings – Packaging Machines | Stora Enso
sources.claim: An automated packing machine designed specifically for nurseries packs and compresses seedlings into shipping boxes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: packing seedlings for shipment is the final step of the nursery instance; the machine handles the same bundled seedling stock on a purpose-built line.

sources.system: John Deere Autonomy / Precision Upgrade Kit on 8R/9R/9RX tractors (autonomous tillage)
sources.title: John Deere autonomous tillage system gets tryout in North Dakota fields (Agweek)
sources.claim: John Deere's autonomy kit ran tractors driverless doing tillage on real farm fields in North Dakota in spring 2025, as a limited production build ahead of full commercial release.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical site preparation is soil cultivation with a tractor-drawn implement; autonomous tillage on a managed field is the structured-facility form of the same ground-preparation work, using comparable implements and pass-coverage precision.

tasks.label: Plan and supervise construction of access routes and forest roads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Locating and laying out a new permanent forest access road on steep, brushy timbered ground: technician walks candidate alignments with clinometer/GPS, sets a grade line within maximum grade, avoids unstable soils and riparian buffers, then flags the centerline, marks clearing limits, and stakes stream-crossing/culvert locations on the ground for the contractor.

Supervising the contractor or agency crew actually building the road: daily on-site inspection of dozer/excavator subgrade work, checking width, grade, ditch and turnout construction, culvert size/placement and bedding, ordering field changes when the ground differs from the plan, enforcing erosion-control BMPs, and accepting the finished section.

Planning and supervising temporary access: skid trails, landings, spur roads, and dozer-line/fire-access routes, often laid out quickly during an active harvest or incident; technician flags the route on the fly and directs the equipment operator, then oversees closure/rehabilitation.

Office/GIS phase of planning: running route alternatives over LiDAR/DEM and soils layers, computing grades and earthwork, drafting road plans, specifications and cost estimates, and preparing environmental-compliance and permit documentation, with periodic field verification.

Reconstruction or improvement of an existing forest road or trailhead access on gentler ground: laying out drainage improvements and aggregate surfacing limits, marking cross-drain and rolling-dip locations, and inspecting/accepting the grader, dump-truck and culvert crews' work.

sources.system: ANYmal legged robot forest inventory system (Oxford Dynamic Robot Systems / DigiForest)
sources.title: Building Forest Inventories with Autonomous Legged Robots -- System, Lessons, and Challenges Ahead (arXiv:2506.20315)
sources.claim: Autonomous quadruped robots (ANYmal) have been demonstrated navigating and mapping forest plots under canopy in field trials, i.e., autonomous data collection in unstructured forest terrain — but only as a research prototype for tree inventory, with no route location, ground marking, or construction oversight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous under-canopy forest survey. It shows mobility and mapping in the same E3 forest terrain where road reconnaissance happens, but it collects inventory data only — it does not select a grade line, flag centerline/clearing limits, or supervise construction, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

sources.title: Solar Farm Layout Tool & GPS Surveying Equipment | Civ Robotics
sources.claim: CivDot autonomous layout rovers commercially mark design coordinates on utility-scale solar construction sites with a few inches of accuracy, taking a design file and spray-marking points for crews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous construction staking/layout. It performs the marking sub-step from a pre-made design, but only on cleared, graded solar sites; it does not choose a road alignment or grade in steep timbered terrain, and it performs no construction supervision, so it cannot complete a whole instance.

sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem | Equipment World
sources.claim: Aftermarket autonomy kits have put excavators to work autonomously on large construction sites (e.g., a 1.1-GW solar farm), showing autonomous earthmoving execution on controlled, prepared jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous earthmoving. It substitutes for the machine operator executing a pre-engineered design on a controlled site, not for the technician who plans the route and inspects/accepts the work; no evidence of autonomous planning, inspection, or acceptance of forest road construction.

tasks.label: Select and mark trees for thinning or logging, drawing detailed plans that include access roads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial thinning marking in a mixed hardwood or mixed-conifer stand on private/state land: technician walks the stand under a silvicultural prescription, judges each stem for species, crown class, form, defect and spacing, applies paint marks (DBH streak plus stump mark) with a marking gun, tallies volume, then drafts the harvest map showing unit boundary, skid trails, landing and access road. Brush, deadfall, uneven terrain, variable visibility.

Federal/state timber sale unit layout (e.g., USFS, BLM, state forest): flag and paint unit boundaries, mark leave/reserve and wildlife trees per prescription, walk and flag temporary road, landing and skid-trail locations with GPS around streams and slope breaks, and produce the sale-area map and road plan for the contract package.

Southern pine plantation thinning designation: laying out and marking a row-plus-selection thinning in a planted, even-aged pine stand — designating removal rows, marking defective or suppressed leave-row stems, and locating the equipment access route and set-out/landing area; regular rows, flatter ground, understory brush and stumps.

Fuels-reduction or precommercial thinning unit in wildland-urban interface or small-diameter stand: mark or flag leave trees and unit edges for hand crews or mastication equipment, avoid structures/utilities, and plan equipment access and staging on steep, rocky or brushy ground.

Small private woodlot harvest for a non-industrial landowner: technician selects and paints trees for a small partial cut balancing timber value, aesthetics, wildlife trees and landowner preferences, checks property lines, and sketches a plan showing the woods road/skid trail and log deck.

sources.title: SAHA: Supervised Autonomous HArvester for selective forest thinning (arXiv:2601.01282)
sources.claim: SAHA is a 4.5-ton robotic harvester that autonomously navigates cluttered Nordic forest stands over kilometer-long missions to reach trees that have already been designated for selective thinning; it executes cutting, but the selection of which trees to remove and any marking/plan output are not performed by the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-stand navigation and tree-level intervention in the same forest environment. It substantiates mobility to individual trees but not the silvicultural selection judgment, paint marking, or road/plan deliverable that define this task.

sources.system: Fly4Future/MRS modular drone T650 with paint-spraying marking device
sources.title: Drones In Forest Inspection — Fly4Future
sources.claim: A modular T650 drone prototype flies into a stand, images trunks, classifies bark-beetle infestation with a deep-learning model, and sprays a paint mark on confirmed trees — the closest demonstrated robotic analog to physically marking selected trees in a forest, but it is a single-criterion prototype, not a stand-wide silvicultural marking system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of a target tree under canopy followed by physical paint application. Transfer is limited: the decision rule is a single visible pest symptom rather than a multi-attribute thinning prescription, and it is a development prototype, not a stand-scale marking deliverable.

sources.title: Treeswift raises $4.8 million to capture forest data with LiDAR drones — DroneDJ
sources.claim: Treeswift's autonomous LiDAR drones are piloted with commercial timberland owners to collect tree-level inventory data (volume, carbon), reducing timber-cruising fieldwork; the system measures and maps trees but does not select trees for removal, mark them, or lay out access roads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic under-canopy forest inventory, the data-collection precursor to tree selection. It shows autonomous data capture in the same environment but stops short of the selection decision and of any physical marking.

sources.system: DigiForest robotic pipeline (aerial/legged robots, DSS, autonomous harvester)
sources.developer: DigiForest EU consortium (Oxford, ETH Zurich, TUM, WSL and partners)
sources.title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry (arXiv:2604.14652)
sources.claim: The DigiForest project pairs robot-collected inventories with a Decision Support System that informs which trees to remove or ... with an autonomous harvester; the DSS is decision support for human managers and the pipeline produces no painted marks or contract-ready access-road plan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stand assessment feeding thinning decisions. It is decision-support software plus research robots validated in test forests; the human still makes and communicates the designation, so it does not substantiate completion of the marking-and-plan task.

sources.title: Kodama Systems uses robotics to mitigate wildfire risk — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Kodama Systems fits teleoperation and autonomy kits to skidders used in commercial California forest-thinning operations; the deployed capability is remote human operation of extraction machinery, not autonomous tree selection or marking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic machinery working inside thinning units. Because operation is teleoperated it cannot support a positive judgment, and skidding does not involve tree selection, marking, or plan drafting.

tasks.label: Supervise forest nursery operations, timber harvesting, land use activities such as livestock grazing, and disease or insect control programs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Overseeing an active commercial timber sale on public or industrial forest land: driving/walking the harvest unit while feller-bunchers, skidders and log trucks work, checking that the operator stays inside painted boundaries and leave-tree marks, that stump heights, skid trails, stream buffers and landing cleanup meet contract/BMP specs, flagging corrections with the logging foreman, shutting work down in wet conditions, and documenting the inspection. Steep, slash-covered ground, mud, dust, moving heavy equipment.

Supervising a forest nursery (bareroot beds and/or greenhouse containers): scheduling and directing seasonal crews and equipment through sowing, irrigation/fertigation, weeding, root pruning, lifting, grading, packaging and cold storage; sampling seedlings for caliper/root-shoot quality and disease; adjusting operations when weather or germination deviates. Institution-controlled facility with fixed beds, benches and standard machinery.

Administering grazing allotments / land-use permits on rangeland: riding or driving allotment pastures to check livestock numbers, on/off dates, forage utilization and riparian condition, inspecting fences, cattle guards and water developments, meeting the permittee on the ground to require moves or repairs, and writing up non-compliance. Open range taken as found, no fixed layout, weather and terrain uncontrolled.

Running a forest insect/disease control program: laying out and checking pheromone trap lines and survey plots, ground-truthing aerial detection flags of beetle or defoliator damage, then directing and monitoring the treatment crew (aerial or ground spray, tree injection, sanitation/salvage felling, seedling sanitation), checking calibration, drift and buffer compliance, and assessing post-treatment efficacy. Off-trail forest, brush, variable weather.

Monitoring other land-use activities under permit - firewood or special-forest-product cutting, rights-of-way, gravel pits, recreation/OHV use, prescribed grazing on state or federal tracts: visiting scattered sites, verifying the permittee is operating within the authorized footprint and conditions, and correcting or reporting violations. Dispersed, unimproved sites reached by two-track roads.

sources.developer: University of Oxford Dynamic Robot Systems Group / ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab
sources.title: Autonomous Forest Inventory with Legged Robots: System Design and Field Deployment
sources.claim: A legged robot (ANYmal) autonomously navigated forest plots and collected tree-inventory data (DBH, stem maps) in field deployments, showing autonomous mobility and sensing under canopy but no supervisory function.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forest data collection. It shows a robot can move and sense in unstructured forest, a sub-step of monitoring, but it does not judge contract or BMP compliance, direct a logging or treatment crew, or order corrective action, so it cannot complete the supervision instances.

sources.title: Case Study: Practical Autonomy on Construction Sites | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot with Field AI autonomy performs repeated autonomous inspection and monitoring rounds ('job walks') on active construction sites, capturing progress and condition data that humans then interpret.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous job-walk inspection of a work site, the closest analog to walking a harvest unit or permit site. Transfer is only partial: the robot follows mapped routes on a graded site and outputs data, whereas supervision requires on-the-spot compliance judgment and direction of the contractor's crew.

sources.title: Harvest Automation - HV-100 product listing
sources.claim: The HV-100 is a commercially sold mobile autonomous robot that performs container-plant spacing, consolidation and collection inside nurseries and greenhouses - a single material-handling step, not management of nursery operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nursery material handling. It shows autonomous operation inside a nursery facility, but covers one repetitive step; it does not schedule crews, grade seedling quality, detect disease outbreaks or adjust the growing regime, which supervising nursery operations requires.

sources.system: Experimental unmanned forestry machine (autonomous forwarder platform)
sources.developer: Umea University (La Hera et al.), Journal of Field Robotics
sources.title: Exploring the feasibility of autonomous forestry operations: Results from the first experimental unmanned machine
sources.claim: The first unmanned forestry machine capable of autonomous navigation and crane/log manipulation was reported as an experimental research result, not a fielded harvesting system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized timber harvesting itself. Even performing the harvesting work autonomously is at experimental stage, and nothing in it addresses overseeing a contractor's operation against a timber sale contract.

sources.developer: Australian Centre for Field Robotics, University of Sydney (Agerris)
sources.title: Robots Are Herding Cattle, But Wyoming Wranglers Say They Can't Replace Them
sources.claim: SwagBot is an autonomous ground robot that moves cattle to grazing areas and assesses pasture condition on rangeland; ranchers report it does not replace the human stockman's judgment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: livestock movement and pasture assessment on rangeland. It shows autonomous rangeland mobility, but grazing-permit administration requires verifying permittee compliance, inspecting range improvements and negotiating corrective action, none of which the robot does.

tasks.label: Develop and maintain computer databases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Inspect trees and collect samples of plants, seeds, foliage, bark, and roots to locate insect and disease damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Walk-through pest/disease survey of a forest stand: technician hikes off-trail over slopes, brush and slash in mixed conifer/hardwood timber, examines crowns for fading/defoliation and boles for pitch tubes, frass, cankers and woodpecker flecking, chips bark with a hatchet to expose beetle galleries, clips symptomatic twigs/foliage with a pole pruner, bags, labels and GPS-tags samples for the lab, and writes up damage locations and severity.

Plot-based or roadside ground-truthing of aerial detection survey polygons: drives forest roads to flagged points, inspects a set number of trees per plot, photographs symptoms, collects foliage, twig, bark or insect specimens from selected trees, records host/damage codes, and ships samples to a forest health lab.

Inspection and sampling of individual high-value trees at developed sites — campgrounds, park and street trees, administrative sites, rights-of-way — for emerald ash borer, oak wilt, needle blights, etc.; branch and bark samples cut with pole saw or from a ladder/bucket amid pedestrians, vehicles and landscaping.

Root-disease sampling: excavating around root collars with shovel/pulaski in forest or landscape soil, cutting root and root-collar bark sections showing mycelial fans or resinosis, collecting rhizosphere soil for Phytophthora baiting, cleaning tools between trees, and labeling/shipping samples.

Nursery, greenhouse and seed-orchard stock inspection: scouting beds/benches of bare-root and container seedlings in an agency or company nursery for damping-off, root rot, needle cast and insects; lifting sample seedlings to inspect roots, clipping foliage, and collecting cone/seed samples to check for cone and seed insect damage; samples bagged for the diagnostic lab.

sources.system: ANYmal forest inventory system (Oxford Dynamic Robot Systems Lab / ETH)
sources.developer: University of Oxford, ETH Zurich, ANYbotics
sources.title: Autonomous Forest Inventory with Legged Robots: System Design and Field Deployment
sources.claim: Legged robots (ANYmal) autonomously navigate under forest canopy and build tree inventories (position, DBH), but the demonstrated capability is mapping and trait estimation only — no manipulation, sample cutting, or pest/disease diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forest plot inventory. It establishes that autonomous mobility in real stands exists, but the system carries no manipulator and performs no sample collection or damage diagnosis, so it cannot complete this task.

sources.title: Treeswift Raises $4.8 Million to Build Next Generation of Forest Monitoring System
sources.claim: Under-canopy drones are used commercially to collect forest data (timber volume, tree metrics) with automated navigation, but they only sense — they do not collect plant tissue samples or diagnose insect/disease damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forest cruising/monitoring in the same E3 forest environment; shows the mature commercial offering is remote sensing, with no physical sampling capability to transfer to this task.

sources.title: The DeLeaves: a UAV device for efficient tree canopy sampling
sources.claim: The only fielded tool for cutting branch samples from tree canopies is a drone-mounted cutter that requires a pilot plus a second operator running the sampling head; the cutting sequence can be automated but target selection and flight to the branch are human-controlled.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task: collecting foliage/branch samples from standing trees in forests. It is teleoperated, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: NEON DJI Matrice 300 RTK with DeLeaves sampler
sources.developer: NSF NEON / Battelle with Outreach Robotics
sources.title: Branching Out Again with Remote Controlled Canopy Sampling | NSF NEON
sources.claim: NSF NEON's operational canopy foliar sampling protocol uses a piloted drone flown to pre-entered target-tree coordinates; a human pilot positions the cutting tool and the samples are handled by field crews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: foliage sample collection from forest canopies. Flight is waypoint-automated but branch selection and cutting are remote-controlled by operators, so it does not demonstrate autonomous completion.

sources.title: P-AgBot: In-Row & Under-Canopy Agricultural Robot for Monitoring and Physical Sampling (IEEE RA-L)
sources.claim: An autonomous under-canopy field robot detects and physically cuts crop leaf samples in corn rows with better than 80% success — the closest demonstrated autonomous plant-tissue sampling, in a row-crop field, for nutrient analysis rather than pest/disease diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical leaf sampling. Transfer is limited: corn leaves in a graded, row-planted field, ~80% success, no targeting of insect/disease symptoms and no bark, root, or seed sampling.

sources.title: RoMu4o: A Robotic Manipulation Unit For Orchard Operations Automating Proximal Hyperspectral Leaf Sensing
sources.claim: A crawler robot with an arm autonomously grasped leaves and took hyperspectral readings in a pistachio orchard with 70% overall success; it senses leaves in place rather than detaching and retaining diagnostic samples.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic foliage handling on trees in an orchard (a structured E2-style facility). Success of 70% is well below worker quality and no physical sample is retained for laboratory diagnosis.

sources.developer: ecoation Innovative Solutions / Bogaerts Greenhouse Logistics
sources.title: Autonomous Robot Does the Greenhouse Scouting for You - Greenhouse Grower
sources.claim: An autonomous scouting robot for greenhouses inspects crops and flags pest and disease problems commercially, but it only images and sensors plants — it collects no plant tissue, insect, or root samples.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pest/disease scouting of plants inside a structured facility (E2). It substantiates inspection only; the sampling half of this task (clipping foliage, lifting seedlings, bagging for the lab) is not demonstrated.

sources.title: Autonomous soil sampling: Robo sampling improves accuracy - Top Crop Manager
sources.claim: A commercially operated autonomous soil-sampling robot drives crop fields on a pre-programmed grid and extracts cores without an operator, showing autonomous field sample collection exists for tilled cropland soil but not for root-collar excavation or tree tissue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous collection and bagging of soil samples. Transfer fails for root-disease sampling: it augers prescribed grid points in cleared farm fields, and does not excavate root collars, cut root/bark tissue, or judge symptoms.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic forest rover for resin tapping
sources.developer: Georgia Southern University / B&L Naval Stores
sources.title: Robot Operations for Pine Tree Resin Collection (Technologies)
sources.claim: Robotic drilling into pine trunks from a rover has only been shown as a feasibility study of the required operations, not as a deployed autonomous system working through real plantation conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine contact with tree bark/xylem in a pine plantation, the nearest analogue to chipping bark or taking bark/wood samples. It is a feasibility demonstration with unclear end-to-end autonomy, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Viscon vision grading and replugging machines
sources.title: Vision Plant Grading & Replugging Machines - Viscon Group
sources.claim: Commercial conveyor-fed vision machines inspect and sort trays of young nursery plants, but they grade plant size/quality and re-plug trays rather than diagnose insect and disease damage or set aside labeled diagnostic samples.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated inspection of nursery stock with the work brought to the machine (E1). Grading targets plant quality/size, not identification of pest and pathogen damage with collection of samples for laboratory diagnosis.

tasks.label: Measure distances, clean sightlines, and record data to help survey crews.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Boundary/property-line retracement in dense second-growth timber: the technician swamps the line with machete, brush saw and loppers so the instrument can see the prism, chains slope distances, holds rod/prism at corners, blazes and paints witness trees, and records bearings, distances and notes for the survey crew. Steep, off-trail, brushy ground.

Corridor survey support (forest road relocation, utility right-of-way, cutline): cutting brush and limbs along the corridor with chainsaw/brushcutter to open sightlines, driving hubs and stakes at measured stations, taping distances and offsets, recording station data for the crew.

Point layout and distance measurement in open or lightly vegetated terrain (rangeland, harvested unit, burn area, gravel pit): navigating to design/plot coordinates with GNSS, measuring distances with tape or laser rangefinder, marking/staking points, recording coordinates and ground elevations for the crew; little or no vegetation to clear.

Survey support inside an agency-controlled developed site (ranger/administrative site, tree nursery, campground, dam or reservoir works, an active road-project work area controlled by the agency): setting up and holding rod/prism or scanner targets, measuring distances between features, recording as-built/topographic data on a data collector.

Stream cross-section, wetland delineation and riparian survey support: wading a wadeable stream or brushy wetland margin, cutting overhanging brush and willows to open the sightline, holding the rod at bank and channel breakpoints, measuring widths and depths, recording cross-section data.

sources.title: Robots Powered with Reach Speed up Stakeout for Construction Projects - Emlid Blog
sources.claim: CivDot is a GNSS/RTK ground robot that drives itself to a list of design coordinates and marks each point to 1-2 cm, performing the stakeout/point-measurement role of a survey crew helper on open outdoor sites.
sources.transferJustification: Stakeout/layout is the same work as a survey helper measuring distances to points and marking them: the robot carries the position measurement to the ground point and records it, on unimproved open terrain comparable to rangeland or a harvest unit.

sources.title: Automated Layout Startup Civ Robotics Secures $7.5M Series A Funding Round | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: CivDot robots are in multi-year commercial use by a major contractor (Bechtel) on utility-scale solar construction sites, replacing much of the manual survey-helper stakeout labor.

sources.title: Video: Civ Robotics' robots can perform autonomous surveying | Equipment World
sources.claim: CivDot marks coordinates on the ... and also records ground elevation, and is used across varied unimproved site terrain - the measure-and-record half of survey-crew support.
sources.transferJustification: Recording elevations and marked point positions for a survey crew is the same deliverable a technician produces when measuring distances and recording data for the crew.

sources.system: Spot (with Trimble X7 / laser scanner payload)
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot with a laser-scanner payload runs programmed Autowalk routes and captures survey-grade 3D scans without operator intervention on active jobsites and facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Laser-scan reality capture is measuring distances and recording survey data for the crew; it substitutes for a helper carrying targets and logging measurements inside a controlled work site.

sources.system: ANYmal D with DigiForest autonomy and forest-inventory stack
sources.developer: Oxford Robotics Institute / ETH Zurich / DigiForest consortium
sources.title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry (arXiv)
sources.claim: DigiForest's ANYmal D legged robots autonomously survey forest plots under canopy, covering about 1 ha in 20-30 minutes and producing tree measurements (DBH to 2-3 cm) as an on-line inventory - measurement and data recording in unstructured forest.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous under-canopy traverse with dimension measurement and data logging is the measuring-and-recording component of survey-crew support in the same forest conditions; it does not cover line clearing or rod work.

sources.title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry (arXiv)
sources.claim: Even the most advanced forest cutting robot in the DigiForest programme is only semi-autonomous: a human operator selects the intervention and authorizes each cut, so vegetation cutting in forest is not done autonomously end to end.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting brush and small stems to open a sightline is the same class of work as selective cutting; the state of the art still requires operator authorization per cut.

sources.system: Kodama Autopilot retrofit for forestry machines
sources.title: Restoring wildfire resilience in our forests with Kodama Systems
sources.claim: Commercial forest vegetation/thinning machines in the US are run by teleoperation with only limited autonomous sub-functions, not autonomous brush clearing.
sources.transferJustification: Forest fuel/brush removal is the closest commercial analogue to swamping a survey line; it is delivered as teleoperation, which cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Issue fire permits, timber permits, and other forest use licenses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Survey, measure, and map access roads and forest areas such as burns, cut-over areas, experimental plots, and timber sales sections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Timber sale / harvest unit boundary survey and layout: technician runs a compass-and-GPS traverse through standing timber and brush on a national forest or industrial tract, recovers property corners or monuments, chains or lasers distances, hangs flagging and paints the boundary line so loggers can see it, computes acreage, and produces the sale area map.

Post-harvest cut-over unit survey and mapping: after a clearcut or thinning, the technician delineates the harvested unit perimeter, measures acreage, and maps landings, skid trails, stream buffers, rutting and residual/regeneration conditions to produce the as-built unit map and acreage record.

Burn area survey and mapping: after a wildfire or prescribed burn, the technician maps the burn perimeter, severity/mortality patches and acreage across steep, snag-filled terrain for rehabilitation, salvage or reforestation planning.

Access road location survey and mapping: capturing alignment, length, grade, width and surface geometry of an existing or proposed forest road corridor under partial canopy, to update the GIS road layer/travel map or supply design data for a new spur.

Access road condition inventory: driving or walking a gravel/native-surface forest road system, logging culverts and drainage structures, ditch and surface condition, washouts, slumps and blowdown, rating maintenance needs and mapping each feature.

Experimental / permanent plot installation and measurement: navigating off-trail to a plot coordinate, monumenting plot center, laying out the fixed-radius or rectangular plot, tallying and measuring trees (species, DBH, height, damage codes), recording understory or regeneration counts, and mapping the plot location.

sources.developer: Oxford Robotics Institute / ETH Zurich / TUM (EU DigiForest project)
sources.title: Building Forest Inventories with Autonomous Legged Robots -- System, Lessons, and Challenges Ahead
sources.claim: The ANYmal quadruped, in the DigiForest project, autonomously navigates and surveys forest plots under canopy, detecting trees and estimating DBH; trials ran over 1.5 years in forests in three ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: under-canopy plot inventory. It is the closest robotic analogue to plot survey work — same forest setting and same measurement objects — but it delivers only stem positions and diameters (±2 cm), not species, heights, defect codes or a monumented plot.

sources.system: ANYmal D autonomous forest inventory system

sources.claim: Field campaign at the Forest of Dean: the legged platform completed an autonomous survey of a ~1 ha forest plot in 20 minutes, mapping over 100 trees.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic under-canopy plot measurement, offered as the nearest evidence for the experimental-plot instance; the deliverable is a stem map with diameters, not the full tree-level plot record a technician produces.

sources.claim: A prototype autonomous under-canopy photogrammetric drone flew inside boreal forests without GNSS and estimated tree diameters, but stem detection and DBH accuracy remain well short of caliper measurement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous under-canopy forest data collection; cited as the state of the art for robotic ground-level plot measurement, showing accuracy and stem-detection completeness below what a technician's plot tally requires.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial area and corridor survey. The flight execution and imagery capture are the same operation whether the polygon is a construction site, a harvest unit, a burn, or a road corridor; only the polygon differs.

sources.claim: A US forestry consulting firm runs an operational drone mapping program over client timberland across the Southeast, Arkansas/Texas and Northeast, using Site Scan for flight planning and data capture to produce imagery and maps for site prep, planting, harvest planning and inspection reports.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: surveying and mapping cut-over and treatment areas on working forest tracts; the flights are planned and executed as Site Scan/ArcGIS Flight autonomous area-survey missions.

sources.claim: The US Forest Service flies drones over the Cameron Peak Fire ..., processing the imagery into high-resolution orthomosaics and maps of natural regeneration used to decide where crews must plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-fire regeneration survey over a burn area; it is the same aerial survey-and-map operation as delineating burn extent and severity, in the same burned-forest setting. Autonomy of the flight is not stated, so it is used as context only.

sources.system: UAV RGB photogrammetric survey (SfM) for forest road design

sources.transferJustification: Same task: field survey of a forest road for design/mapping. Establishes that drone-collected data meets or beats the accuracy of the ground survey a technician would otherwise perform; flight autonomy is not described, so autonomy rests on the ArcGIS Flight and Wingtra evidence.

sources.title: LIDAR drone survey: Step by step video guide | Wingtra
sources.claim: A commercial VTOL survey drone executes the planned LiDAR mapping mission autonomously after launch, with automatic sensor calibration and return-to-home, over sites including forested and confined terrain.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous LiDAR survey of a user-defined area. Establishes that survey-grade aerial mapping missions run autonomously from launch to landing, the flight capability assumed for mapping burns, cut-over units and road corridors.

tasks.label: Provide technical support to forestry research programs in areas such as tree improvement, seed orchard operations, insect and disease surveys, or experimental forestry and forest engineering research.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Insect and disease survey field work: technician drives and walks to survey points in forest stands and plantations, hangs and services pheromone/funnel traps, inspects bark, foliage and crowns for defoliation, cankers, borer galleries and dieback, collects insect and foliage specimens into vials/bags, records plot location and severity codes for a research or forest-health program.

Field support to experimental forestry / forest engineering studies: establishing and re-measuring research plots (numbering and tagging individual trees, diameter-tape DBH, hypsometer heights, survival, form and damage scoring, brushing plot boundaries) and installing/servicing study infrastructure (soil moisture and sap-flow sensors, weather stations, stream gauges, erosion plots), plus soil and water sampling on rough forest terrain.

Stand-scale data collection over an experimental forest or research tract for a research program: tree counts, stem sizes, species composition, stand structure and fuel-load mapping across many hectares, delivered as a dataset for researchers rather than as per-tagged-tree records.

Seed orchard and tree-improvement operations: cone crop surveys, collecting and processing pollen, isolation-bagging female strobili and applying pollen for controlled crosses, harvesting cones from lifts or by climbing, bench and field grafting of scions from selected clones, maintaining clone maps and orchard records.

Nursery and seed-lab support for research seedlots: cleaning, counting and stratifying small identified seedlots, filling and sowing trays or containers seedlot-by-seedlot for progeny tests and provenance trials, running germination tests and recording results.

Handling research nursery stock and materials inside the greenhouse/shadehouse and nursery yard: moving, spacing and consolidating containerized seedlings between beds, hauling trays, media and supplies for research plantings.

sources.title: Drones in Forestry: TreeSwift Raises $4.8 M - DRONELIFE
sources.claim: Treeswift's under-canopy forestry drones, described as autonomous flying robots with LiDAR, are used commercially to inventory and map timberland for large forest owners.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial timber inventory. It transfers to stand-scale research data collection because the same under-canopy platform measures individual stems, species and quality over large forest tracts, which is the output a research program needs for stand-level datasets.

sources.title: Treeswift to automate forestry with swarms of drones
sources.claim: Treeswift's platform is described as swarms of autonomous flying robots carrying LiDAR that monitor, inventory and map timberland.

sources.claim: A lightweight under-canopy drone flew autonomously inside forests and estimated stem diameters, but with errors of several centimetres.

sources.title: Building Forest Inventories with Autonomous Legged Robots -- System, Lessons, and Challenges Ahead
sources.claim: An autonomous legged robot performed under-canopy forest inventory in an ecological forest, with stem-diameter accuracy far coarser than tape measurement.

sources.title: Harvey: A working robot for container crops - Robohub
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots distribute and collect container-grown ... commercial greenhouses and nurseries and have been purchased and used in everyday production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: container spacing/collection in commercial nurseries. Transfers to moving and spacing containerized research seedlings because the objects (potted nursery stock), placement precision, and greenhouse/shadehouse setting are the same.

sources.title: Petitti Family Farms using Burro autonomous robots, with plans to add more - Garden Center
sources.claim: Fleets of autonomous outdoor robots are in production use at a commercial nursery, towing plants and plant materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport of plants/materials in an outdoor nursery. Transfers to hauling trays, media and containerized research stock around a research nursery yard: same loads, same institution-controlled nursery setting.

sources.title: Williames Seeder - Advanced Automatic Nursery Seeder
sources.claim: Commercial automatic nursery seeders dib trays and singulate seed into seedling trays accurately on a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production sowing of seedling trays. Transfers to sowing research seedlots because the objects (small conifer/hardwood seed, cell trays), the one-seed-per-cell precision, and the fixtured line presentation are the same as nursery sowing of research stock.

sources.title: Germination Scanalyzer - LemnaTec
sources.claim: Commercial germination-testing systems provide automated seed imaging and, in higher models, automated handling of germination trays for seed screening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated germination testing. Bench models still require manual loading, so autonomy of the handling step is unclear and it is treated as non-supporting.

sources.title: Dropcopter, Beak & Skiff Partner for First in Nation Pollination Program
sources.claim: Drone-based pollination of a commercial apple orchard was demonstrated autonomously, applying pollen broadcast over trees.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supplemental orchard pollination. It does NOT transfer to seed orchard controlled crosses, which require bagging individual strobili, pedigree tracking, pollen collection and cone harvest; the drone only broadcasts pollen over a canopy.

sources.title: Breaking the field phenotyping bottleneck in maize with autonomous robots
sources.claim: Autonomous under-canopy robots have been deployed at scale to collect phenotypic data in maize breeding research programs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic data collection for a plant breeding research program. It does not transfer to forest progeny tests: the platform drives flat, cultivated row-crop alleys and measures herbaceous plants, not tagged woody stems on brushy, uneven forest ground, and it cannot tag trees or score damage.

tasks.label: Conduct laboratory or field experiments with plants, animals, insects, diseases, and soils.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Remeasurement/data collection in established silvicultural or vegetation trial plots in a forest stand: relocate plots, measure stem diameters and heights, count seedling survival, estimate cover/vigor, record data for the trial.

Establishing and maintaining field trials in the woods: laying out and marking plots, hand-planting seedlings at set spacing, numbering/tagging individual experimental units, applying treatments (fertilizer, herbicide, thinning), installing exclosures or instruments.

Field soil work for experiments: driving/augering cores at plot grid points in forest soils, digging pits, describing horizons, bagging and labeling samples, running in-situ tests (infiltration, penetrometer, bulk density).

Insect and disease field experiments: hanging and baiting pheromone/funnel/pitfall traps on a route, servicing and emptying them, collecting and sorting specimens, cutting bark or foliage samples from symptomatic trees, rating damage/infection on marked trees.

Wildlife and habitat field experiments: setting and checking live traps, running browse-utilization or exclosure comparisons, handling and marking animals, deploying and retrieving camera/acoustic arrays in rough terrain.

Indoor experimental work at a lab/greenhouse/nursery: drying, grinding, sieving and weighing soil and foliage samples, extractions and colorimetric/nutrient assays, seed germination and propagation trials with watering/treatment regimes, growth measurement and record-keeping.

sources.developer: EarthSense, Inc. / Corteva Agriscience / University of Illinois
sources.title: Breaking the field phenotyping bottleneck in maize with autonomous robots — Communications Biology
sources.claim: TerraSentia autonomous under-canopy ground robots collected commonly measured plant phenotypes from ~200,000 experimental units across 142 research trial fields in the US and Canada (2019-2023) for Corteva/EarthSense/Illinois breeding and agronomy trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plot-level trait measurement in replicated field trials. This is the measurement half of 'conducting field experiments with plants' — locating each experimental unit, measuring plant size/stand/health, and delivering trial data — in institution-controlled research plots.

sources.title: Rogo's Self-Driving, Fully Autonomous Soil Sampler Covers 100k Acres in 2019 | AgriTechTomorrow
sources.claim: Rogo's SmartCore robot autonomously navigates managed crop fields, pulls soil cores at prescribed georeferenced points and bags the samples, operating as a commercial soil-sampling service over hundreds of thousands of acres.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: georeferenced soil sample collection for agronomic testing. Same physical act as experimental soil sampling — locating sample points, extracting cores to depth, compositing, bagging and labeling — in an institution-controlled outdoor working field.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA mobile manipulator platform)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist (Burger et al., Nature 2020) — Strathprints record
sources.claim: A mobile robot with a manipulator worked unattended in an ordinary human chemistry laboratory, moving between human-scale instruments and running a closed-loop experimental campaign of hundreds of experiments over eight days.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running laboratory experiments in a human-built lab. Comparable objects and precision to soil/foliage sample workflows — handling vials and racks, dispensing solids and liquids, and operating benchtop analytical instruments — without rebuilding the lab around the machine.

sources.title: PhenoRob-P: An autonomous robotic system for high-throughput phenotyping of potted plants
sources.claim: PhenoRob-P, an autonomous wheeled robot with a 6-DOF arm, navigated the aisles of a research glasshouse and imaged potted plants at hundreds of pots per hour, validated in greenhouses at Huazhong Agricultural University.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: per-pot measurement in greenhouse plant trials. It is the measurement/recording half of a propagation or germination trial, performed in a greenhouse laid out for human work rather than a conveyor cell.

sources.title: PhenoAIxpert HT — LemnaTec
sources.claim: Commercial conveyor-based phenotyping platforms move potted plants through imaging cabinets and ... stations, running controlled watering treatments and repeated growth measurements on hundreds of plants in research greenhouses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: greenhouse growth trials. The platform applies the watering/treatment regime and takes the repeated growth measurements that constitute a propagation or germination experiment, with plants brought to the machine on conveyors.

sources.system: Automated soil laboratory systems (Fugro soil testing labs)
sources.title: Transforming Soil Lab Testing with AI Technology | Fugro
sources.claim: Soil testing laboratories run automated sample preparation and instrument loading — sieving, moisture conditioning, specimen loading and automatic calibration — as part of routine commercial lab workflows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: soil sample preparation and testing in a laboratory. Same physical operations as forest soil sample processing (sieving, conditioning, weighing, loading test apparatus) with the samples brought to purpose-built machines.

sources.developer: University of Oxford Dynamic Robot Systems / ANYbotics
sources.title: Building Forest Inventories with Autonomous Legged Robots — System, Lessons, and Challenges Ahead (arXiv:2506.20315)
sources.claim: An ANYmal quadruped autonomously navigated and mapped forest plots under canopy in three European countries, detecting trees and estimating DBH with typical 2 cm accuracy; the authors describe it as a prototype system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: under-canopy forest plot survey. It shows autonomous locomotion and tree measurement in real forest, but only remote-sensed stem geometry at ~2 cm accuracy, short of caliper-grade remeasurement of tagged experimental trees, and with no manipulation.
