roles.title: Forensic Science Technicians
roles.description: Collect, identify, classify, and analyze physical evidence related to criminal investigations. Perform tests on weapons or substances, such as fiber, hair, and tissue to determine significance to investigation. May testify as expert witnesses on evidence or crime laboratory techniques. May serve as specialists in area of expertise, such as ballistics, fingerprinting, handwriting, or biochemistry.

tasks.label: Collect evidence from crime scenes, storing it in conditions that preserve its integrity.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential burglary/property-crime scene in a private home or apartment taken as found: tech walks through disturbed rooms, decides what is evidentiary (point of entry, tool marks, ransacked drawers), photographs and measures, powders and lifts latent prints from door frames/glass/jewelry boxes, swabs touch-DNA on handles, collects pry bars or discarded gloves, packages each item in the correct paper/plastic/box container, seals with tamper-evident tape initialed across the seal, labels and logs chain of custody, then transports and places into secure/dry storage.

Violent-crime scene (homicide, shooting, assault) inside a private residence: fragile, transient, and biohazardous items among clutter and body fluids — swabbing and cutting bloodstains, collecting cartridge casings, projectiles, a firearm made safe, knives, clothing, hairs and fibers, trajectory rods and scales in photos; each item packaged separately, wet biological items air-dried before packaging, biological samples refrigerated/frozen, all documented for court admissibility.

Outdoor scene taken as found — street/parking-lot shooting, roadway crash, alley, field or wooded body-recovery site — in variable light and weather: grid-searching ground cover for casings, blood drops, discarded weapons or bones; marking and photographing positions; casting shoe/tire impressions; collecting soil/vegetation and skeletal or decomposed remains; protecting items from rain and heat and getting biological evidence into cooled storage before degradation.

Scene inside a commercial or institutional building the operator controls (convenience store robbery, bank, school, hospital, jail): standard fixed layout but disturbed by the incident and by bystanders; collecting casings, blood, fingerprints from counters and doors, seized items and clothing, plus swabs and packaging, with the premises secured by police and staff during processing.

Vehicle processed in the agency's secure, lit processing bay/garage: towed suspect or victim vehicle searched systematically — interior and trunk contents inventoried, blood and touch DNA swabbed, latent prints powdered and lifted from glass and door edges, projectiles and casings recovered from upholstery, gunshot residue and trace collected, each item packaged, sealed, labeled and moved into the evidence facility.

Post-scene evidence handling at the agency's evidence facility/laboratory intake: hanging bloody clothing in drying cabinets and repackaging when dry, sealing and initialing packages, applying barcodes, logging items into the LIMS/property system, and placing items in the correct condition-controlled location (refrigerator, freezer, dry secure shelf, firearms rack, narcotics vault) with chain of custody maintained.

sources.system: PRIME (Police Robot for Inspection and Mapping of underwater Evidence)
sources.developer: University of Bath / UK police collaboration
sources.title: A prototype autonomous robot for underwater crime scene investigation and emergency response - Journal of Field Robotics
sources.claim: The closest fielded 'crime scene robot' is an autonomous uncrewed surface ... maps and inspects underwater scenes with sonar; it images and localizes potential evidence but does not physically collect, package, or store items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crime-scene search. Cited to show that even the flagship autonomous police 'evidence' robot performs sensing/mapping only, so it does not transfer to physical collection, packaging, or preservation of items.

sources.system: Skydio drones with Axon Evidence / SkyeBrowse scene mapping
sources.title: How to use drones for crime and accident scene documentation
sources.claim: Police drones used at crime and collision scenes perform documentation only — capturing photos/video and 3D models that upload to digital evidence systems — with no physical evidence collection or packaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crime-scene documentation. Cited to bound capability: deployed autonomous police robots at scenes are imaging platforms, so nothing carries over to grasping, swabbing, packaging, or sealing physical evidence.

sources.developer: Modern Handling / AS/RS vendors for public safety
sources.title: 7 Public Safety Evidence Room Space Saving Storage Ideas
sources.claim: Automated storage and retrieval systems marketed for police evidence rooms move sealed bins/carriers robotically to a secure operator station; the human still packages, seals, and deposits the item at the station and unpacks at retrieval.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated bin storage/retrieval in an evidence facility. It covers only the shelving step of 'storing evidence'; the packaging, drying, sealing, labeling and condition decisions that define the instance remain manual, so it cannot complete the whole instance.

sources.system: Azenta BioStore -80°C Automated Sample Storage System
sources.title: Azenta BioStore Automated Sample Cold Storage System at -80°C Temperatures
sources.claim: Commercial robotic cold-storage systems keep biological samples in controlled ultra-low-temperature conditions and manage their inventory, but they accept standardized tubes/racks loaded by humans rather than arbitrary forensic items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic preservation storage of biological samples. Objects are uniform barcoded tubes in a purpose-built store, not clothing, weapons, or swab kits, and no collection or packaging is performed, so it does not substantiate the whole task.

sources.system: Mobile manipulator for grasping/retrieving unknown hazardous objects
sources.title: Grasping and retrieving unknown hazardous objects with a mobile manipulator
sources.claim: Recovery of unknown objects in cluttered, unstructured settings with a mobile manipulator remains a shared-control research problem: perception and grasp assistance are automated but a human operator directs the mission.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating and retrieving unknown objects in cluttered unstructured scenes — the core manipulation demand of evidence collection. It is operator-directed shared control, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Keep records and prepare reports detailing findings, investigative methods, and laboratory techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Use photographic or video equipment to document evidence or crime scenes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full photographic documentation of an indoor crime scene taken as found (apartment, house, convenience store): overall, mid-range and close-up images of rooms, bodies, blood, weapons and latent evidence, with and without scales and evidence markers, working around clutter, mixed/low light, painting with flash, kneeling and climbing for angles, plus video walk-through.

Ground-level photographic documentation of an outdoor scene taken as found (roadway shooting, fatal collision, wooded body recovery, clandestine grave): overall and close-up images of shell casings, tire marks, blood, remains and terrain, in rain, wind, darkness or glare, over hours and shifting conditions.

Overhead/overview photographic documentation of a large outdoor scene for mapping and reconstruction: capturing a systematic, overlapping photoset of a multi-lane crash site or expansive outdoor scene from above so a scaled orthomosaic/3D model can be produced for the case file.

Bench photography in the laboratory or evidence-intake area of items received in a case: clothing, firearms, knives, drug packaging, questioned documents, sexual-assault kit items - laid out on paper, photographed overall and in detail from several angles with an ABFO scale and case-number placard, under controlled studio/copy-stand lighting.

Close-up, macro and instrumented imaging of small evidence in the lab: fired cartridge cases and bullets for NIBIN entry, toolmarks, developed latent prints, hairs/fibers/tissue on slides, and alternate-light-source/UV/IR captures - repeatable, standardized, high-magnification image sets used for comparison and databasing.

Photographic documentation of a vehicle or other large item processed in a secured impound bay or evidence garage: all four sides, VIN, damage and defects, undercarriage, then interior seats, footwells, trunk, blood/bullet defects and evidence in situ before and after removal.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan for Documenting Evidence for Public Safety | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan lets a Skydio drone autonomously plan and fly the flight pattern needed to capture a complete photoset ... a scene; the operator only selects the scan volume and resolution. Marketed and used for crime and crash scene documentation (Boston PD crime-scene scan shown).

sources.title: How to use drones for crime and accident scene documentation | Police1
sources.claim: Law-enforcement trade press describes Skydio 3D Scan as automating the data-capture flight for crime and accident scene documentation with full obstacle avoidance and minimal pilot input.

sources.developer: Ultra Forensic Technology / ATF NIBIN program
sources.title: Automated Firearms Ballistics Technology | Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives
sources.claim: IBIS BrassTRAX is an automated bench-top acquisition station installed in US crime labs (ATF NIBIN) that images fired cartridge cases for the national database - the machine itself performs the photographic documentation of the evidence item.

sources.title: Advanced Cartridge Case Imaging System | LeadsOnline
sources.claim: Vendor documentation confirms hands-off, operator-independent automated acquisition by BrassTrax of 2D imagery and 3D topography of breech-face, firing-pin and ejector marks on cartridge cases.

sources.title: Aperio GT 450 DX - Automated Digital Pathology Slide Scanner
sources.claim: Automated whole-slide scanners with robotic rack handling capture high-resolution documentary images of specimens on slides with no-touch, continuous loading of hundreds of slides; FDA-cleared and in routine laboratory use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated microscopic imaging of mounted specimens. Forensic technicians photograph hairs, fibers and tissue on slides for the case record; the scanner handles the same objects at the same magnifications in the same kind of institutional lab and produces the archival image set autonomously once slides are racked.

sources.system: Ortery Office Photo Machine / PhotoCapture 360 / 3D PhotoArm
sources.title: Automated Product Photography Solutions for still, 3D, 360 product photos | Ortery
sources.claim: Commercial automated photography systems position a camera on multiple motorized axes and rotate the object on a turntable, capturing a standardized multi-angle image set with controlled lighting after a human simply places the item in the enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: studio documentation photography of hand-held objects. Bench evidence photography involves the same object sizes, the same copy-stand/studio lighting, the same demand for even exposure and colour fidelity, and the same fixed presentation of the item to the camera.

sources.title: Smithsonian to Photograph 200,000 Insects With Custom Conveyor System | PetaPixel
sources.claim: A purpose-built conveyor imaging line at the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History automatically photographs placed specimens together with their labels, capturing three standardized high-resolution views of each at 1,500 specimens per day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: standardized multi-view documentary photography of small, fragile objects presented with an identifying label. This matches lab evidence photography (item plus case-number placard and scale, several fixed views) in object size, required detail and fixed presentation.

sources.title: How It Works - UVeye
sources.claim: Drive-through automated vehicle inspection gateways capture over a thousand synchronized high-resolution images of a vehicle's exterior, roof, tires and underbody with no manual input; installed at hundreds of dealerships, ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated photographic condition documentation of a whole vehicle. It covers the exterior and undercarriage portion of forensic vehicle documentation, but no cited system images vehicle interiors or evidence in situ.

tasks.label: Use chemicals or other substances to examine latent fingerprint evidence and compare developed prints to those of known persons in databases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crime lab, non-porous evidence (handgun, magazine, cartridge cases, plastic baggies, bottles, glass, phone): examiner selects sequence, superglue-fumes the item in a cabinet, applies fluorescent dye stain or powder, searches the item under ALS/RUVIS for ridge detail, photographs AFIS-quality marks with scale, then encodes and searches AFIS and performs ACE-V comparison to candidate exemplars.

Crime lab, porous evidence (checks, ransom notes, currency, paper drug packaging, cardboard): sequential chemical processing (DFO or 1,2-indanedione, then ninhydrin, sometimes physical developer), oven/humidity development, fluorescence examination and imaging, then AFIS search and comparison of any developed marks to known prints.

Crime lab vehicle/evidence bay, large or awkward items (recovered vehicle, door, safe, tools, bulky packaging): black/magnetic powder or small-particle reagent processing over large surfaces, tape lifts onto backing cards, photography of marks in place, then scanning, AFIS search and comparison.

Crime scene work by a latent/CSI technician: dusting counters, window glass, door frames, vehicle interiors and exteriors at burglarized homes and businesses, occasionally portable superglue fuming of small items, lifting and photographing marks in varied lighting, dust and weather; prints later scanned, searched in AFIS and compared.

Office/lab workstation comparison casework: examiner receives lift cards and photographs submitted by scene technicians, assesses each mark for suitability, scans/encodes minutiae, launches AFIS/ABIS searches, reviews candidate lists, performs ACE-V comparison with known exemplars, obtains verification and documents conclusions.

sources.title: MVC/D Cabinets — Cyanoacrylate fuming chambers
sources.claim: Commercial cyanoacrylate fuming cabinets (Foster+Freeman MVC/D series, used in US crime labs such as DC DFS) run the humidification, glue fuming and fume-extraction cycle automatically once an operator has loaded and hung the exhibit; they do not handle exhibits, choose the processing sequence, dye-stain, examine, photograph or compare prints.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, but only the chemical-development sub-step: the machine acts on an exhibit a human has fixtured, and the examination, imaging and database comparison that complete the instance remain manual, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.system: Crime-lite AUTO / Crime-lite ML PRO 2 / DISCOVER imaging workstation
sources.title: Crime-lite AUTO | Foster + Freeman
sources.claim: State-of-the-art forensic fingermark imaging products are human-operated handheld or dock-mounted cameras with automated illumination presets, i.e. semi-automated screening tools, not autonomous evidence-examination machines.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the imaging step of this task; the device is hand-held/operator-driven, so it shows the capture step is not performed autonomously by a machine.

sources.system: NIST/Michigan State University latent-print quality algorithm with AFIS
sources.title: Scientists Automate Key Step in Forensic Fingerprint Analysis | NIST
sources.claim: Automation in latent print work is software automating discrete decision steps (e.g., assessing whether a latent has sufficient detail); AFIS then returns candidate lists that a human examiner must evaluate to reach a conclusion.
sources.transferJustification: Same task's comparison half, but software-only and covering one step; it is not a robotic system and does not deliver the examiner-quality conclusion that completes an instance.

sources.system: AI-enhanced AFIS/ABIS systems (review of deployed and benchmarked systems)
sources.title: Automated Fingerprint Identification: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Crime Scene Investigation
sources.claim: A 2026 systematic review of AI in fingerprint and latent print identification concludes that hybrid workflows in which human examiners retain decision authority are currently the most reliable model, i.e. fully automated latent identification is not established practice.

sources.title: Defining AFIS latent print "Lights-Out"
sources.claim: Analyses of 'lights-out' latent AFIS operation conclude that end-to-end latent searching without human intervention is not achievable; automation can only reduce the amount of expert assistance required.

sources.title: Sherlock Drones – automated investigators tackle toxic crime scenes
sources.claim: Robots proposed for crime-scene evidence collection (including fingerprint samples) are remote-controlled ground vehicles from a research project aimed at hazardous scenes, not autonomous latent-print processors.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic work at crime scenes; it is remote-controlled and forward-looking, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment for scene-side latent processing.

sources.system: UR5e collaborative robot integrated with Gemini AS slide stainer, ClearVue coverslipper and Pannoramic 1000 scanner
sources.title: Mapping Manual Laboratory Tasks to Robot Movements in Digital Pathology Workflow
sources.claim: The closest demonstrated laboratory analogue — a collaborative robot arm chaining an automated chemical slide stainer, coverslipper and scanner — achieves an autonomous chemical-treatment-plus-imaging workflow, but only for standardized glass slides in magazines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic chemical staining and imaging of specimens in a lab). Transfer fails: the workpieces are uniform slides in fixtures, whereas latent print work involves arbitrary exhibits (firearms, bags, documents, vehicles), examiner-chosen reagent sequences, and an ACE-V identification conclusion, none of which this system performs.

tasks.label: Measure and sketch crime scenes to document evidence.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Death/homicide or shooting scene inside a private residence or apartment: technician establishes reference points, measures room dimensions and positions of the body, weapons, casings and numbered evidence markers amid furniture, clutter, blood and low light, and produces a scaled floor-plan sketch with legend for the case file and court.

Scene inside a commercial or institutional building (convenience store, bar, office, school, hotel room) after a robbery, burglary or assault: measure point of entry, fixed features and evidence positions inside a fixed, standard layout under building lighting, and produce a scaled floor-plan diagram.

Outdoor urban/suburban scene taken as found (street, alley, parking lot, front yard) after a shooting or body discovery: police tape off an irregular area, technician measures cartridge cases, blood, vehicles and impacts relative to fixed landmarks, often at night or in weather, and produces a scaled overhead diagram.

Fatal or serious roadway collision: closed highway or intersection, technician documents vehicle points of rest, tire and skid marks, gouges, debris field and roadway geometry over a large area under pressure to reopen the road, producing a scaled collision diagram for reconstruction and court.

Outdoor scene away from developed areas: field, ditch, roadside embankment, wooded edge or clandestine grave/body recovery; technician sets a datum or GPS reference, measures scattered evidence and remains over open or lightly vegetated terrain, and sketches a gridded site diagram.

Vehicle or large object processed in a secured agency garage/processing bay: technician measures and diagrams damage, bullet trajectories and evidence positions on an impounded vehicle in a controlled indoor bay with lighting and space to work around the object.

sources.system: SkyeBrowse (drone videogrammetry app + cloud platform on DJI/Autel airframes)
sources.title: SkyeBrowse Comprehensive Knowledge Base
sources.claim: SkyeBrowse's capture app automatically computes and flies a two-orbit drone mission over a small incident scene after the operator only designates a center point; used for accident and crime scene reconstruction.

sources.title: Drone Crime Scene Mapping: 3D Evidence Documentation
sources.claim: SkyeBrowse returns, from the uploaded autonomous-orbit video, a georeferenced 3D model, 2D orthomosaic and an automatically generated scaled sketch diagram with measurements - the deliverable of the measure-and-sketch task.

sources.title: How to use drones for crime and accident scene documentation (Police1)
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan plans its own scan path over an arbitrary outdoor scene and flies it autonomously with obstacle avoidance, capturing the imagery used for crash and crime scene measurement.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Patrol Deployments with Skydio X10
sources.claim: Skydio X10 flies fully autonomously in zero-light conditions with obstacle avoidance and generates 2D maps and 3D models onboard before the scene is cleared, covering night scene documentation.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan | Autonomous Drone Flights for 3D Mapping
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan is marketed and used to document crash and crime scenes and also to generate 3D models of indoor ... such as warehouses and industrial spaces.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Leica BLK ARC
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC now the first certified reality capture device available for Boston Dynamics' Spot (Geo Week News)
sources.claim: Leica BLK ARC on Boston Dynamics Spot runs autonomous reality-capture missions through Spot's Orbit fleet software, producing registered 3D point clouds of plants, warehouses and enclosed structures, including for fire investigation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous as-built reality capture. It yields the same deliverable class as scene measurement - a dimensionally accurate registered point cloud of an interior from which scaled floor-plan diagrams are drawn - at comparable cm-level precision indoors.

sources.system: DJI Mavic Pro drone photogrammetry (3DF Zephyr)
sources.title: Laser scanner and drone photogrammetry: A statistical comparison between 3-dimensional models and its impacts on outdoor crime scene registration
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed comparison of drone photogrammetry against terrestrial laser scanning and a total station for outdoor crime scene registration found the drone-derived 3D models statistically comparable, supporting worker-quality measurement accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Quality corroboration only: establishes that drone-captured scene geometry meets the accuracy of the instruments forensic technicians currently use to measure outdoor scenes.

sources.developer: Windham Police Department / Blue Marble Geographics
sources.title: Police Department Utilizes Drones to Map Crash & Crime Scenes
sources.claim: A US police department uses drone mapping operationally for crash and crime scene documentation, cutting up to 2.5 hours versus traditional total-station scene measurement.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment corroboration: shows drone-captured geometry is accepted in place of technician total-station measurement for the same scene-documentation deliverable.

sources.system: SHINING 3D RobotScan automation cells; Creaform CUBE-R / MetraSCAN 3D-R
sources.title: Automation Solution | RobotScan Series | 3D Inspection | SHINING 3D
sources.claim: Turnkey robotic 3D scanning cells scan a fixtured object automatically and automatically generate detailed dimensional inspection reports without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional inspection of a fixtured object. It is the same act - robot-borne scanning of a presented workpiece plus automatic generation of a dimensioned document - at far tighter precision than a scene sketch requires.

sources.title: Exyn Brings Level 4 Autonomy to Drones (IEEE Spectrum)
sources.claim: ExynAI gives drones Level 4 autonomy: told only the volume to map, the robot takes off and decides on its own how to explore and map unknown, GPS-denied spaces, delivering high-fidelity 3D point clouds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous survey mapping of unknown spaces (mines, structures). Same physical act as scene measurement - self-directed traverse producing a metric 3D record - though demonstrated in industrial voids rather than furnished interiors.

sources.title: Indoor Drone as First Responder with Skydio R10
sources.claim: Indoor drone deployment inside buildings by police is flown by a remote human pilot rather than autonomously, indicating autonomous documentation of cluttered as-found interiors is not established.

tasks.label: Visit morgues, examine scenes of crimes, or contact other sources to obtain evidence or information to be used in investigations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Indoor crime scene inside a private residence or small business (burglary, assault, unattended/suspicious death): the technician walks the scene as found, establishes a path, overall/mid-range/close-up photography and scale mapping, searches cluttered rooms for latent prints (powder, lift, or chemical), swabs suspected blood and touch-DNA surfaces, collects firearms, casings, knives, clothing, drugs and paraphernalia, packages and labels each item separately, and documents chain of custody, often at night and around occupants/officers.

Outdoor scene taken as found: street shooting, officer-involved shooting, fatal collision, or outdoor body recovery. Locate and flag cartridge casings, projectiles, blood drops, tire/shoe impressions in grass, gravel or roadway; cast impressions; photograph and total-station/drone map in rain, wind, darkness or traffic; recover and package biological and trace evidence before it degrades.

Processing at the agency's own facility: a recovered/suspect vehicle in a covered processing bay or items delivered to the evidence-processing room. Search the vehicle interior, dust and lift latents, cyanoacrylate-fume and photograph items, swab for DNA, collect trace, inventory, repackage and log the evidence under controlled lighting with standard equipment.

Visit to the medical examiner's morgue: attend the autopsy, photograph the decedent and injuries, take postmortem fingerprints, collect and dry clothing, bag hands, clip nails, swab for GSR/DNA, receive projectiles and other items handed over by the pathologist, package and transport them to the lab with chain-of-custody paperwork.

Contacting and visiting other sources to obtain evidence or information: driving to a hospital ED to take custody of a sealed sexual assault kit and the victim's clothing, collecting surveillance video from a business, receiving evidence transferred by another agency, plus telephone/e-mail requests for records; verifying the item, sealing/labeling, completing chain-of-custody forms and returning it to evidence intake.

sources.title: Deploying physical AI to aid clinicians using AWS with Diligent Robotics (AWS case study)
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator from Diligent Robotics, autonomously picks up and delivers lab specimens, medications and supplies across hospital floors, navigating crowded corridors, riding elevators and badge-authenticating secure handoffs — the closest deployed analog to taking custody of a sealed package from an institutional source and transporting it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intra-facility pickup and secure delivery of clinical specimens. It transfers to the custody-transfer portion of 'contact other sources to obtain evidence' because the objects (small sealed packages/kits handed over by institutional staff), the precision required (grasp, secure compartment, authenticated handoff) and the environment (a structured human work facility) are comparable; it does not transfer to scene search or evidence recognition.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi is a commercially deployed fleet, not a demo: more than 25 US hospitals and over one million autonomous deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (secure specimen pickup/delivery inside an institution); establishes deployment maturity and reliability rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine
sources.claim: The Virtobot robotic arm in a forensic medicine institute performs automated 3D surface documentation of bodies and CT-guided needle placement for post-mortem tissue sampling, and is used routinely — but it covers only imaging and needle biopsy, not the photography, postmortem printing, clothing/trace collection and packaging that make up a morgue evidence visit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic acquisition of post-mortem documentation and tissue samples from a body fixtured on a CT table. It substantiates only sub-steps of the morgue instance; no evidence covers postmortem fingerprinting, clothing/trace collection, packaging or chain of custody.

sources.system: Skydio X10 with autonomous dock (Drone as First Responder program)
sources.title: Drone as First Responder Program — Montgomery County Police Department
sources.claim: Police drone-as-first-responder systems fly autonomously from docks to incident scenes and capture aerial imagery/documentation, but they only image scenes; no deployed police aerial or ground system recognizes, collects, packages or preserves physical evidence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial documentation/overwatch of incident scenes. It covers only the photographic-documentation sub-step of a scene examination and involves no manipulation, so it cannot substantiate completion of a scene-evidence instance.

sources.system: PRIME (Police Robot for Inspection and Mapping of underwater Evidence)
sources.title: A prototype autonomous robot for underwater crime scene investigation and emergency response (Journal of Field Robotics)
sources.claim: The most advanced dedicated forensic field robot found is PRIME, a prototype autonomous surface vessel for locating and mapping underwater evidence; it searches and maps but does not recover, package or document evidence, and remains a research prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous search/mapping for evidence at a scene. It shows the state of the art in robotic crime-scene work is prototype search-and-map, with no recovery or packaging capability, supporting negative judgments for scene instances.

sources.system: Object-driven optical coherence tomography (OD-OCT) with robotic arm scanning
sources.title: Rapid, autonomous and ultra-large-area detection of latent fingerprints using object-driven optical coherence tomography
sources.claim: Robotic arms can autonomously scan presented objects to detect latent fingerprints over large areas in a laboratory optical setup, but this is a research imaging technique on fixtured items, not a system that searches, develops, lifts and packages prints as casework output.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic detection of latent prints on an object presented to the machine. It is the closest lab-bench analog to facility evidence processing, but covers only detection/imaging of prints, not searching a vehicle, lifting, swabbing, packaging or logging.

tasks.label: Train new technicians or other personnel on forensic science techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench-side mentoring in the crime lab: a senior technician walks a new hire through an analytical protocol (latent print development, DNA extraction/quantitation setup, drug chemistry screening), explains the SOP and quality requirements, observes the trainee perform it, and gives corrective feedback until the trainee is competent.

Field training at a crime scene or mock scene: an experienced technician instructs a trainee or a new evidence tech on scene walk-through, photography and scale placement, sketching/measurement, and evidence packaging and labeling, explaining decisions and critiquing the trainee's work as it is done.

Classroom or briefing-room instruction to non-lab personnel (patrol officers, detectives, hospital or coroner staff) on proper evidence recognition, collection, preservation, chain of custody, and lab submission requirements, delivered as a lecture with slides, handouts, and Q&A.

Competency and proficiency administration: preparing or assigning known training samples and mock casework, reviewing the trainee's notes, worksheets and conclusions, conducting oral boards or moot court prep, and documenting training records against accreditation (ISO 17025 / ANAB) requirements.

Developing and delivering standing training material: writing or updating SOP-based training manuals, recording or presenting in-service and online modules on a new instrument or method, and answering follow-up questions from staff at other agencies.

tasks.label: Operate and maintain laboratory equipment and apparatus.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Seized-drug/toxicology section: technician prepares extracts and standards, fills and caps autosampler vials, loads the tray on a GC-MS/LC-MS/FTIR, runs tune and calibration/verification checks, starts and monitors the analytical sequence, unloads. Accredited crime lab bench, fixed instrument layout.

DNA/biology section: sets up and runs the robotic extraction workstation (deck of tubes, tips, reagents), seals and spins plates, runs thermal cyclers and qPCR, loads plate, polymer and buffers on the capillary-electrophoresis genetic analyzer and starts the run. Accredited crime lab.

Preventive maintenance and troubleshooting: replace GC septa, inlet liners and columns, clean the MS ion source, replace CE capillary arrays and reagent pouches, calibrate balances with check weights, verify pipettes, clean/decontaminate hoods and biosafety cabinets, complete maintenance logs.

General wet-bench apparatus in trace/serology/chemistry: weighing on an analytical balance, centrifuging, vortexing, pH meters, sonication, drying ovens, hot plates and fume-hood work while preparing extractions and reagents. Crime lab bench.

Evidence-processing and imaging apparatus: hang and fume varied exhibits (firearms, bottles, clothing) in a cyanoacrylate cabinet, use forensic light sources, mount cartridge cases/bullets on a comparison microscope or IBIS acquisition station and capture images. Crime lab processing room.

Field/mobile: operate and maintain portable instrumentation and apparatus outside the lab - handheld Raman/FTIR, ALS, portable fuming, vehicle-mounted gear at scenes, and periodic checks of evidentiary breath-alcohol instruments at police facilities. Conditions taken as found.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA KMR iiwa based)
sources.title: A Mobile Robotic Chemist (Burger et al., Nature 2020, author manuscript)
sources.claim: A KUKA-based mobile manipulator ('mobile robotic chemist') autonomously worked eight days in a conventional, unmodified 7.3 x 11 m chemistry laboratory, weighing solids into vials, dispensing liquids, capping, sonicating and operating a headspace gas chromatograph station across 688 experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous photocatalysis screening. Transfer: the physical acts are the ones this task comprises (weighing solids, dispensing liquids, capping vials, sonication, loading and running a commercial chromatograph), with the same objects (vials, racks, benchtop analytical instruments) at comparable mg/uL precision, in a standard analytical laboratory.

sources.system: Twin mobile robots with Chemspeed ISynth, UPLC-MS and benchtop NMR
sources.title: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry (Nature)
sources.claim: Two mobile robots autonomously ran an exploratory synthesis workflow, handling samples and transporting/loading them into unmodified benchtop NMR and UPLC-MS instruments that remain shared with human researchers in an ordinary laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous synthesis and characterization. Transfer: sample handling and loading of standard human-operated analytical instruments (LC-MS, NMR) is the same physical operation a forensic technician performs when loading an autosampler or genetic analyzer, with the same labware in the same kind of facility.

sources.system: Hamilton VANTAGE / Microlab STAR forensic workstations
sources.title: Validation of a High-Throughput Automated Liquid Handling DNA Extraction System to Maximize Efficiency in Forensic Casework (Forensic Genomics)
sources.claim: A robotic liquid-handling workstation (Hamilton VANTAGE) was validated for forensic casework DNA extraction, producing contamination-free, reproducible quantification and profile results from blood, saliva and semen on varied substrates at high throughput.

sources.system: Applied Biosystems RapidHIT ID DNA Booking System
sources.title: FBI Approves Thermo Fisher Scientific's Rapid DNA Solution for use in Law Enforcement Booking Stations
sources.claim: A fully automated sample-to-answer DNA instrument approved by the FBI for booking stations processes a swab through extraction, amplification, separation and profile generation without operator intervention.

sources.system: ABB GoFa laboratory process cells (with Mettler Toledo and Agilent instruments)
sources.title: Turning AI into action: ABB accelerates the future of lab automation at SLAS 2026
sources.claim: Collaborative-robot laboratory cells were demonstrated performing autonomous multi-step analytical workflows: pipetting, decanting, vial capping/uncapping, weighing, titration and oven cycling, plus a complete GC sample-prep and GC loading flow.

sources.title: Advanced Cartridge Case Imaging System - BrassTrax
sources.claim: The IBIS BrassTrax cartridge-case acquisition station, deployed in NIBIN crime laboratories, captures 2D and 3D images of a mounted cartridge case with automated acquisition, automated self-test and adjustment, and hands-off operation.

tasks.label: Collect impressions of dust from surfaces to obtain and identify fingerprints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential burglary scene: technician searches point-of-entry surfaces (window glass, sills, door frames, dusty ledges) with oblique light, brushes on black/magnetic powder to develop latent ridge detail in the dust film, applies lift tape, peels and mounts it on a backing card, labels it, and later runs it through AFIS/comparison. Cluttered home taken as found, variable surface textures, curved and vertical surfaces.

Commercial premises break-in (store, office, warehouse): dusting counters, cash drawers, broken glass edges, dusty shelving and light fixtures for latent prints; scene disturbed by the crime and by responders, mixed surfaces including painted, laminate and metal, sometimes at awkward heights on a ladder.

Vehicle processing in a police impound/processing bay: recovered stolen or suspect vehicle worked indoors under controlled lighting; technician powders exterior glass, door handles, mirrors, interior dash and dusty trim, lifts prints onto cards, photographs dust impressions on seats/door panels before lifting.

Laboratory bench work on submitted items: dusty tools, documents, glass fragments, packaging brought to the crime lab; technician selects powder/gel or electrostatic lift, develops and lifts the impression, photographs it, mounts and packages the lift, and enters the print for identification.

Area dust-impression lifting with an electrostatic dust print lifter: laying Mylar lifting film over floors, thresholds, paper or seat surfaces in unoccupied buildings, sheds or outdoor covered areas, rolling out air pockets, charging the film, peeling and preserving the lift; footwear and finger/palm dust impressions on found surfaces.

Major or hazardous scene (homicide, fire scene, contaminated or damp premises): dusting overhead, undersides and irregular surfaces amid debris, soot or biological fluids, in poor light, with strict contamination and chain-of-custody controls and coordination with other investigators.

sources.system: Sirchie Electrostatic Dust Print Lifter Kit (hand-operated forensic tool)
sources.title: ElectroStatic Dust Print Lifter Kit | Sirchie
sources.claim: Dust/latent impression collection is performed with hand tools: a hand-held electrostatic dust print lifter requires a human to place the film, roll out air pockets with a rubber roller, and carefully peel the sheet from the surface; no robotic execution is described anywhere in the practitioner literature.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the manual, human-operated nature of the collection tool; it is not a robotic system and cannot support any positive tier judgment.

sources.developer: John Jay College / impression evidence practitioner chapter
sources.title: Impression Evidence: Footwear and Tool Marks
sources.claim: The manual procedure for lifting a dust impression involves rolling the lifting sheet flat with a rubber roller while avoiding creases or air pockets and then carefully pulling the sheet from the surface — fine deformable-film manipulation done by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Documents the dexterity and judgment required; performed by human technicians, so it cannot substantiate robotic completion.

sources.title: RECOVER LFT | Foster + Freeman
sources.claim: The most advanced automation in latent print work is a benchtop chemical processing cabinet that semi-automates reagent chemistry on items placed inside by a human; it does not search surfaces, powder, tape-lift, or mount dust impressions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated latent-mark development in a lab cabinet. Transfer fails — it is a fixed chamber that treats items a human loads; it performs no surface search, powder application, tape lift, or lift mounting, which are the substance of this task.

sources.developer: US crime laboratories (census study, Whitford et al.)
sources.title: The Adoption of Robotics by Government Agencies: Evidence from Crime Labs
sources.claim: Robotics adoption in US crime laboratories is confined to liquid-handling automation for DNA/rape-kit backlogs; no robotic systems are reported for latent or dust impression collection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wet-chemistry sample processing in a crime lab. Transfer fails — these robots pipette liquids from labelled tubes in fixed racks and cannot locate, powder, lift, or preserve a dust impression from an arbitrary surface.

sources.system: PRIME (Police Robot for Inspection and Mapping of underwater Evidence)
sources.developer: University of Bath / Wiley Journal of Field Robotics
sources.title: A prototype autonomous robot for underwater crime scene investigation and emergency response
sources.claim: Robotic systems fielded for crime scenes are documentation and mapping platforms (drones, underwater USVs, bomb-disposal robots), not systems that develop and lift impression evidence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crime-scene survey. Transfer fails — the platform senses and maps; it has no manipulator and performs no contact evidence recovery such as powdering or lifting impressions.

tasks.label: Examine and analyze blood stain patterns at crime scenes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Indoor violent-crime scene in a private residence or apartment: analyst walks a cluttered, poorly lit, biohazardous scene, locates and classifies impact spatter, cast-off, transfer, drip and swipe patterns on walls, floors, furniture and bedding; places numbered markers and scales, takes overall/mid-range/close-up scaled photographs, measures representative ellipses with rulers/calipers or software, determines directionality and area of origin, and produces a documented pattern interpretation for the report while avoiding contaminating or altering the stains.

Outdoor or semi-exposed scene (driveway, alley, yard, parking lot, apartment breezeway): stains on asphalt, concrete, grass, gravel or painted metal; variable daylight/night lighting, weather and time pressure to document before degradation; analyst roadmaps blood trails and drip patterns, photographs with scales, measures stains on rough absorbent substrates, and interprets movement and mechanism.

Vehicle processed as the scene at a secured police impound bay or processing garage: confined interior with stains on upholstery, headliner, glass, door panels and exterior; analyst uses controlled lighting, sometimes chemical enhancement (luminol/BLUESTAR) in darkness, documents and interprets transfer and spatter patterns inside the vehicle.

Commercial or institutional premises under an operator's control (convenience store, bar, hospital room, jail cell, office corridor): fixed layout and standard fixtures, access controlled by staff/officers; analyst documents blood trails, transfer patterns, and spatter on standardized surfaces and interprets the sequence of events, often under time pressure to release the premises.

Reconstruction work-up in a controlled setting: return visit for area-of-origin determination (stringing or trajectory software) and re-photography, plus examination of bloodstained items removed from the scene (clothing, weapon, cut-out wall/carpet sections) laid out in a forensic laboratory examination room under standard lighting, with pattern classification and written conclusions.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan for Documenting Evidence for Public Safety
sources.claim: Skydio's 3D Scan lets a drone autonomously capture photogrammetry datasets of crime and crash scenes for police documentation, but it produces imagery/3D models for human reconstruction, not bloodstain identification, measurement or pattern interpretation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous scene documentation imaging. Transfer fails for this task because the deliverable of bloodstain pattern analysis is an analytical determination of stain mechanism, directionality and area of origin, requiring scale placement, close-range ellipse measurement of individual stains and expert classification, none of which the drone performs.

sources.developer: Halmstad University (Cooney, Ponrajan, Alonso-Fernandez), Vinnova project
sources.title: Nano Drone-based Indoor Crime Scene Analysis
sources.claim: A research prototype nano drone for indoor crime scene analysis performs window entry, evidence mapping and blood smear inference at 75-85% performance in mock indoor scenes - a partial, sub-professional capability, not a completed bloodstain pattern analysis.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related (blood smear inference at an indoor mock scene), but the accuracy reported and the 'minimal analysis' scope fall far short of the reliability and interpretive output an employer would accept from a certified bloodstain pattern analyst.

sources.developer: Acampora, Vitiello, Di Nunzio, Saliva, Garofano (IEEE SMC 2015)
sources.title: Towards Automatic Bloodstain Pattern Analysis through Cognitive Robots
sources.claim: The only published robotic framework aimed at automating bloodstain pattern analysis end-to-end (UAV navigating the scene, detecting stains, computing points of origin, drafting a report) is presented as a proposal, not a built and validated system.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task but is an announced framework/proposal rather than a demonstrated system, so under the evidence rules it cannot substantiate completion at any tier.

sources.system: Machine-learning blood pattern classifier (ellipse/shade features, XGBoost)
sources.developer: Li et al., Forensic Science International
sources.title: From images to detection: Machine learning for blood pattern classification
sources.claim: State-of-the-art automated bloodstain pattern work is software-only image classification on curated photographs (e.g., discriminating gunshot backspatter from impact spatter), with no robotic acquisition or scene-side execution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pattern-type classification. It is a software method operating on human-captured images of laboratory-generated patterns, not a physically embodied system, so it cannot substantiate robotic completion of scene examination.

sources.title: HemoVision: An automated and virtual approach to bloodstain pattern analysis
sources.claim: HemoVision automates area-of-origin reconstruction from crime scene photographs, but still depends on a human photographer capturing the scene images and on synthetic test scenes for validation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: area-of-origin computation. It is analysis software requiring human image capture at the scene, so it does not show any robot performing the physical examination and documentation portion of the task.

tasks.label: Analyze gunshot residue and bullet paths to determine how shootings occurred.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crime-lab trace/GSR analysis: sealed GSR kits (hand, face, or clothing tape-lift stubs) arrive from a shooting case; the technician unpacks the kit under chain-of-custody, mounts/inspects the aluminum stubs, loads them into an SEM-EDS, runs an automated particle search for Pb-Ba-Sb spheroids per ASTM E1588, confirms classified particles, and issues a report on whether the subject was near a discharging firearm.

Firearms-unit distance determination: victim's clothing or a target substrate is examined visually and microscopically for soot and stippling, chemically processed (modified Griess on treated photo paper with a hot iron, sodium rhodizonate for lead), then the suspect weapon and matching ammunition are test-fired at known ranges into test panels in an indoor range, and the patterns are compared to estimate muzzle-to-target distance.

Indoor shooting scene in a private residence or bar taken as found (furniture displaced, blood, low light, debris): the technician locates and verifies bullet defects in drywall, doors, furniture and glass, distinguishes them from pre-existing damage, chemically tests suspect impacts for lead/copper, inserts trajectory rods/probes, runs lasers or a laser scanner, measures vertical and horizontal angles, and derives shooter/victim positions.

Outdoor scene (street, parking lot, yard) with casings scattered over a block, defects in siding, fences, parked cars and utility poles, under weather and time pressure with traffic control: the technician documents each bullet path, sights lines between defects, uses total station/scanner or photogrammetry, and reconstructs firing positions.

Vehicle or removed structural item examined later in a secured impound bay or lab garage: the technician searches the body panels, glass and interior for entry/exit defects, probes and rods each path through sheet metal and seats, swabs surfaces for GSR, photographs and measures each trajectory, and reports the shooter's position relative to the vehicle.

sources.system: Thermo Fisher Phenom Perception GSR / Phenom ParticleX GSR desktop SEM
sources.date: 2025 (current product page; product line marketed since ~2020)
sources.title: Desktop SEM | Phenom Perception GSR | Thermo Fisher Scientific - US
sources.claim: Commercial desktop SEM-EDS systems dedicated to gunshot residue perform automated particle search, imaging and elemental classification across a 30-stub sample holder with a fully motorized stage, generating standardized GSR reports.

sources.system: Thermo Fisher Phenom ParticleX GSR desktop SEM
sources.title: Gunshot Residue Testing | Phenom ParticleX GSR | Desktop SEM | Thermo Fisher Scientific
sources.claim: The same GSR SEM platform runs unattended batch scanning of loaded stubs and auto-generates reports with micrographs and EDS spectra of detected particles.

sources.system: Phenom Perception GSR automated particle analysis (ASTM E1588 workflow)
sources.title: Gunshot Residue Analysis | GSR | Automated SEM
sources.claim: Automated software-controlled SEM-EDS screening of GSR stubs is the mandated method in forensic casework under ASTM E1588, with human confirmatory verification of classified particles afterwards.

tasks.label: Prepare solutions, reagents, or sample formulations needed for laboratory work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crime-lab bench: preparing bulk working solutions and buffers from stock chemicals per SOP (e.g., 1 L extraction/wash buffer, TE, dilute bleach, working formalin) - weigh solids on an analytical balance, dissolve with stirring, adjust pH with meter and acid/base, bring to volume in a volumetric flask, transfer to a labeled bottle, record lot, prep date and expiry in the reagent log.

Toxicology/seized-drug unit: preparing calibrator, control and internal-standard spiking solutions from certified reference material ampoules - serial dilution in methanol/acetonitrile into vials and volumetric flasks at uL-mL volumes, mixing, aliquoting into cryovials, labeling and logging; accuracy must survive LC-MS/MS or GC-MS calibration acceptance criteria.

DNA unit clean/amplification-setup room: preparing PCR and quantitation master mixes, quant standard dilution series, and aliquots of extraction reagents/lysis buffer into tubes or 96-well plates under a dead-air box or hood, with contamination controls, documenting kit lots.

Latent print or trace chemistry unit: mixing chemical development reagents in a fume hood with volatile/hazardous solvents (ninhydrin or DFO in HFE/petroleum ether, physical developer, amido black, acid yellow, silver nitrate), often 0.5-2 L batches in glassware, then bottling, labeling and quality-checking the reagent against a known print.

Small ad hoc reagents and sample formulations at the bench: presumptive test solutions (phenolphthalein/Kastle-Meyer, LMG), staining solutions (Christmas tree stain, hematoxylin), microscope mounting media and refractive-index liquids, small volumes made occasionally per SOP alongside casework.

Crime scene / mobile lab: mixing working reagent on site immediately before use (luminol/BLUESTAR tablets in water, leucocrystal violet, fixative or casting mixes) from field kit components, in variable light, weather and space, with no bench, balance or fume hood.

tasks.label: Examine footwear, tire tracks, or other types of impressions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outdoor crime scene (yard, field, roadside, ditch): locate three-dimensional shoe or tire impressions in soil, mud, sand or snow; place scale, shoot examination-quality oblique-light photographs from multiple angles, mix and pour dental stone (or snow-print wax), let cure, lift, clean and package the cast, then examine the recovered cast for class and randomly acquired characteristics. Variable weather, lighting, terrain and fragile substrate.

Indoor scene taken as found (burglarized residence, small business, homicide scene): search floors, counters, doors and paper items with oblique light for two-dimensional dust, residue or blood shoe impressions; photograph with scale, then recover by electrostatic dust lifter, gelatin lifter or adhesive lift, label and package, and examine the lift for detail sufficiency.

Forensic laboratory comparison examination: receive a questioned impression (cast, lift, or photograph) and known footwear submitted from a suspect; document the outsole, produce test impressions (ink/powder/Handiprint, and 3D test impressions where needed), then compare design, physical size, wear and randomly acquired characteristics side-by-side and by overlay under magnification, reach an ACE-V conclusion, and write a court-defensible report.

Laboratory enhancement, imaging and class-characteristic determination: chemically or digitally enhance a faint lift or bloody impression, capture high-resolution 1:1 images, and search reference databases (e.g., SoleMate/EverSole) to determine brand/model and outsole design class for investigative leads; document findings.

Tire impression examination: at the scene, cast a multi-foot length of tire track in several sections; in the laboratory, handle the tire or jacked vehicle, ink and roll test impressions covering the full circumference of the tread onto paper, and compare tread design, dimensions, wear and acquired characteristics to the questioned impression, then report.

sources.title: Automated Shoeprint Matcher System | Everspry
sources.claim: The leading automated footwear tool is a software matcher that ranks candidate outsole patterns in a database; it performs no physical handling of shoes, casts or lifts and does not produce the examiner's source conclusion.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: automated footwear impression comparison. Cited to show the state of the art is software-only, not a robotic system, so it cannot substantiate completion of the physical examination instances.

sources.title: Everspry Outsole Scanner (EverOS)
sources.claim: Known-shoe outsole capture in police stations and labs is done with a human-operated flatbed acquisition scanner onto which a person places or steps on the shoe; there is no robotic manipulation of the footwear.
sources.transferJustification: Related step of the same task (producing known/test impressions). Cited as evidence that this physical step is performed by human-loaded equipment, not by an autonomous robot.

sources.title: 3D documentation of footwear impressions at crime scenes in minutes, no contact | Artec 3D
sources.claim: Crime-scene 3D capture of footwear impressions is performed with a handheld structured-light scanner carried and aimed by a technician; the device digitizes but performs no casting, lifting or comparison.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, documentation sub-step. Shows the only fielded scene-side 3D impression tool is hand-held and human-operated, so it cannot complete the instance autonomously.

sources.title: Cutting-edge Drones for Effective Crime Scene Analysis | Skydio
sources.claim: Autonomous aerial documentation of crime scenes exists, but it produces scene-level photogrammetry only; it involves no contact with impressions, no casting or lifting, and no comparison to known footwear or tires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (crime scene documentation) in the same unstructured settings; cited to show that the closest autonomous robot at scenes captures overview imagery and cannot perform impression recovery or examination.

sources.title: 'Spot' the robot dog assists Mass. State Police in high-risk situations
sources.claim: Robots fielded by US police at scenes are teleoperated reconnaissance platforms used for situational awareness in high-risk incidents, not evidence-processing systems.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robot actually operating in crime-scene settings; cited to establish that its demonstrated role is remote observation, which does not transfer to impression recovery or examination.

sources.title: Quantitative Evaluation of Footwear Evidence: Initial Workflow for an End-to-End System | NIST
sources.claim: Footwear source determinations in the US are made by human examiners applying subjective criteria within a questioned-versus-test-impression workflow; a quantitative end-to-end automated system was still an initial research workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: establishes that the accepted output (a source conclusion) is produced by examiners and that automation of the full comparison remains a research workflow, so no system meets worker-quality output.

tasks.label: Examine physical evidence, such as hair, biological fluids, fiber, wood, or soil residues to obtain information about its source and composition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Evidentiary DNA processing in an accredited crime laboratory: swabs and fabric cuttings from blood, semen or saliva stains are extracted, quantified, amplified (STR) and separated by capillary electrophoresis to produce a profile identifying the biological source; samples are often low-template, degraded or mixtures.

Known/reference and identification samples: buccal swabs from suspects, victims and elimination donors, and remains samples in identification work, typed to a single-source profile for comparison and database entry.

Biological screening and sampling of submitted items: searching clothing, bedding, weapons, vehicle seats and sexual assault kit contents under alternate light, running presumptive tests (phenolphthalein, acid phosphatase, p30), preparing and microscopically examining stained smears for spermatozoa, then cutting or swabbing the located stain for downstream work.

Hair and fiber trace examinations: searching tape lifts and debris, picking and mounting individual hairs/fibers, comparison microscopy (polarized light, comparison scope), microspectrophotometry and micro-FTIR to determine type and whether a questioned trace could share a source with a known.

Gunshot residue and other particulate residue casework: adhesive stubs from hands/clothing examined by SEM-EDS with automated particle search and elemental classification of characteristic Pb-Ba-Sb particles.

Materials examinations of soil, wood, paint, glass and botanical debris: stereo and polarized-light microscopy, physical-fit comparison, density/refractive index, and elemental or spectral analysis to characterize composition and possible provenance.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous laboratory bench work (weighing, dispensing, vial handling, instrument operation) in a lab built for people. It shows E2-level lab mobility exists in research, but the objects and judgments in forensic screening and trace comparison (searching garments, picking single fibres) are not demonstrated, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at E2.

tasks.label: Determine types of bullets and specific weapons used in shootings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rapid triage/intelligence determination on a batch of fired cartridge cases recovered from a shooting scene (no firearm recovered), done in the agency forensic unit or lab: sort the casings, identify the caliber(s) present, determine how many firearms fired them, and flag ballistic associations with other incidents so investigators can act quickly.

Full laboratory examination and reporting on fired cartridge cases from a shooting: caliber/headstamp and class characteristics of breech-face, firing-pin, extractor and ejector marks; NIBIN acquisition; review of correlation candidate lists; microscopic confirmation of candidate associations; written report identifying likely firearm make/model families and same-source conclusions, subject to technical review.

A recovered firearm is submitted with scene evidence: unpack and safety-clear the gun, function-test it (safeties, trigger pull, malfunctions), select and load appropriate ammunition, test fire into a water recovery tank or trap, recover test bullets and cases, then compare the test specimens with the evidence bullets/cases under a comparison microscope and issue an identification/elimination/inconclusive conclusion with verification.

Fired bullets and bullet fragments recovered at autopsy or from a scene, often deformed or jacket-separated: weigh and measure them, determine caliber, bullet design and jacket material, count land and groove impressions, measure their widths and twist direction, search general rifling characteristics files to produce a list of possible firearm makes/models, and determine how many weapons fired the recovered projectiles.

Field determination during response to a shooting scene (street, apartment, vehicle): examine spent casings and projectile impacts in place, call the caliber(s) present and the apparent number of weapons for investigators, in varying light, weather and clutter.

sources.title: IBIS ClearCase — Automated Cartridge Case Triage & Ballistic Analysis for NIBIN
sources.claim: IBIS ClearCase is a commercial, fully automated benchtop cartridge-case triage machine with a rotating carousel that images fired casings in 3D and autonomously reports caliber, how many firearms were involved, and ballistic associations with other cases in the agency's data.

sources.title: IBIS ClearCase — Automated Cartridge Case Triage & Ballistic Analysis for NIBIN
sources.claim: ClearCase processes casings continuously from a rotating carousel without manual sorting, and vendor developmental testing reports 99% caliber prediction accuracy and 85% correct firearm clustering; no ballistics expertise is needed to run it.

sources.title: Virginia Beach Police Department gets first IBIS ClearCase machine in the Commonwealth | WAVY.com
sources.claim: ClearCase units are deployed in US law-enforcement forensic units, e.g. the Virginia Beach Police Department Forensics Science Unit, where the machine groups crime-scene shells by caliber.

sources.title: Volusia Sheriff's Office adopts IBIS ClearCase technology
sources.claim: An earlier US deployment: the Volusia County (FL) Sheriff's Office adopted ClearCase to examine casings from crime scenes and determine the number and ....

sources.title: Advanced Precision Bullet Imaging System | LeadsOnline
sources.claim: IBIS BulletTrax automatically acquires 2D/3D topography of pristine and damaged bullets after the operator mounts the bullet on a stub with a jig; the acquisition itself runs automatically, but the system outputs images/correlation data rather than a class-characteristic determination or source conclusion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (bullet imaging for database correlation): it automates the imaging step of bullet examination on the same objects, but does not itself determine caliber/rifling class characteristics or the firearm used.

sources.title: Fact Sheet - National Integrated Ballistic Information Network | ATF
sources.claim: Automated ballistic imaging systems in the NIBIN workflow produce only candidate lists; trained technicians perform correlation review and a firearms examiner must confirm associations by microscopic examination, so the identification of the specific firearm is not machine-completed.

sources.date: 2020 (NIJ success story); independent performance evaluation published 2025

sources.claim: Cadre Forensics' TopMatch-3D desktop scanner (with an autosampler tray for multiple cartridge cases) is used in casework by agencies including the FBI Firearms/Toolmarks Unit, but it serves as a virtual comparison microscope whose conclusions are reached by firearm examiners.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (3D scanning and algorithmic comparison of cartridge cases): shows automated imaging and scoring of the same evidence, but the accepted source conclusion is still rendered by an examiner.

sources.claim: A robotic firing device exists that mechanically holds and fires handguns for ammunition/firearm testing, showing robotic test-firing is feasible in a purpose-built armory range, though it does not clear or function-test unknown evidence firearms or recover and compare test specimens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic firing of handguns for ammunition testing): comparable act of discharging a firearm in a fixture, but autonomy is unclear and no recovery/comparison of test specimens is shown, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.claim: Automatic classification of fired bullets to firearm brand from 3D scans is a research-stage result using a commercial forensic scanner (BalScan) and a limited set of standard-issue firearms, not a deployed casework capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (bullet class/brand classification from scans): closest published work to determining the weapon type from a bullet, but it is a research study on test-fired bullets from a small firearm set, so it does not establish casework-quality completion.
