tasks.label: Compare objects, such as tools, with impression marks to determine whether a specific object is responsible for a specific mark.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crime-lab firearms unit: examiner compares fired cartridge cases recovered from a scene against test fires from a submitted pistol/rifle - breech face, firing pin and ejector/extractor impressions - mounting each case under a comparison microscope or 3D acquisition station, aligning marks and rendering an identification/inconclusive/elimination conclusion.

Crime-lab firearms unit: comparison of reasonably intact fired bullets (clear land-engraved striations) with test fires from a submitted firearm; bullet mounted on a rotating stage, land-to-land striation comparison, conclusion documented and verified.

Crime-lab firearms unit: difficult ammunition-component comparisons - deformed/fragmented bullets, polygonal or worn rifling, different ammunition brands between evidence and test fires, subclass-characteristic assessment - requiring judgment about mark suitability and reproducibility.

Crime-lab toolmark casework: pry bar, screwdriver, bolt cutter or knife marks on a door strike plate, padlock shackle, cut wire/chain, or a silicone cast of such a mark; examiner makes test marks in lead at several angles and pressures with the suspect tool, then compares striated and impressed marks.

Footwear/tire impression comparison: seized shoes or tires compared to a crime-scene impression (dental-stone cast, gel or electrostatic lift, or scaled photograph); examiner makes test impressions of the outsole/tread and compares class, wear and randomly acquired characteristics by overlay.

On-scene or large-item comparison: examiner brings a suspect tool or firearm to a scene, vehicle or bulky item (safe door, damaged doorframe, cut fence, wall) that cannot be brought to the bench, and assesses correspondence of the mark to the tool in situ under field lighting.

sources.title: Advanced Cartridge Case Imaging System | LeadsOnline
sources.claim: BrassTrax (IBIS) is a deployed benchtop acquisition station that, once a cartridge case is placed in its holder, automatically captures high-definition 2D images and 3D topography of breech face, firing pin and ejector marks for machine correlation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: NIBIN acquisition/correlation of cartridge cases. It uses the same specimens, the same impression marks (breech face, firing pin, ejector) and the same micron-scale imaging and alignment a source comparison requires, so the physical acquisition and alignment work transfers directly.

sources.title: Advanced Precision Bullet Imaging System | LeadsOnline
sources.claim: BulletTrax is a deployed bullet imaging station that operates automatically after initial setup, digitizing bullet surfaces in 2D and 3D, including damaged bullets, on a motorized mount.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated ballistic database acquisition and correlation of bullets. Same objects (fired bullets), same land-engraved striation marks, and the same sub-micron imaging and registration needed for a source comparison.

sources.title: IBIS - Integrated Ballistic Identification System | LeadsOnline
sources.claim: The IBIS platform is in operational use at thousands of agencies and automatically correlates bullet and cartridge case signatures to rank candidate same-source pairs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated database matching. The correlation engine performs the same striae/impression similarity computation used to decide whether a given firearm produced a given mark; only the reference set differs.

sources.title: Validation and Implementation of the Evofinder Automated Ballistic Identification System at the DC Department of Forensic Sciences
sources.claim: Evofinder, an automated ballistic identification scanner with 4-motor mechanics, was validated and implemented for casework in a US crime laboratory (DC Department of Forensic Sciences), producing 2D/3D images of bullets and cartridge cases ... comparison.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated scanning and correlative searching in a crime lab. The motorized scanning of a fixtured cartridge case or bullet is the same physical operation the comparison task requires.

sources.system: Congruent Matching Cells (CMC) method / NIST Ballistics Identification System
sources.title: An Improved Algorithm of Congruent Matching Cells (CMC) Method for Firearm Evidence Identifications
sources.claim: The Congruent Matching Cells method applies a numerical decision rule to 3D/optical topographies of cartridge case impressions, declaring same-source or different-source without human interpretation.

sources.title: Validation Tests for the Congruent Matching Cells (CMC) Method Using Cartridge Cases Fired With Consecutively Manufactured Pistol Slides | NIST
sources.claim: Validation tests of the CMC decision rule on cartridge cases fired from consecutively manufactured pistol slides (the hardest known-source scenario) produced no false identifications or false eliminations.

sources.title: Performance evaluation of a Cadre Forensics TopMatch-GS 3D system for cartridge case comparisons
sources.claim: A commercial desktop 3D scanning system with vendor comparison algorithms was evaluated on 300 cartridge cases from 10 casework firearms and six ammunition brands, performing ~45,000 automated same/different-source comparisons scored by ROC/AUC; performance varied with ammunition brand.

sources.system: Automatic bullet land matching (bulletxtrctr / random forest)
sources.developer: Iowa State University / CSAFE (Hare, Hofmann, Carriquiry)
sources.title: Automatic Matching of Bullet Land Impressions (arXiv preprint)
sources.claim: An automated algorithm matching 3D scans of bullet land impressions reached a land-to-land false positive rate of 0.0001, though its false negative rate at the individual-land level was high, improving when lands are aggregated per bullet.

sources.title: Accuracy and Reproducibility of Bullet Comparison Decisions by Forensic Examiners
sources.claim: NIST/Noblis study of 49 examiners and 3,156 bullet comparisons notes that operational automated ballistic systems flag candidates but cannot render final source determinations, and that decision rates degrade sharply with bullet quality and with different ammunition types fired from the same gun.

sources.developer: University of Lausanne, School of Criminal Justice
sources.title: Automated comparison and evaluation of striated cutting plier toolmarks on metal wires
sources.claim: A 2024 research method automates comparison of striated cutting-plier toolmarks on wire from 3D topographies, yielding likelihood ratios with misleading-evidence rates of 0-4%; it is confined to one toolmark type and does not create the test marks or handle bulky substrates.

sources.title: NIST Footwear Impression Comparison System | National Institute of Justice
sources.claim: NIST's footwear impression comparison workflow remains analyst-driven: the examiner manually annotates the test impression against the questioned impression before algorithmic assistance, with further advances identified as still needed.

tasks.label: Identify and quantify drugs or poisons found in biological fluids or tissues, in foods, or at crime scenes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Antemortem toxicology casework in a crime-lab/tox section: DUID or drug-facilitated-crime blood and urine specimens arrive as sealed evidence tubes; technician aliquots, adds internal standard, extracts (protein crash/SPE/LLE), runs headspace GC-FID for alcohol and LC-MS/MS for a broad drug panel, builds calibration curves, quantifies, reviews chromatograms and issues a certified result.

Postmortem toxicology on autopsy specimens: clotted or decomposed heart/femoral blood, vitreous, urine, gastric contents, liver or muscle in jars and grey-top tubes; specimen must be homogenized/weighed, extracted, screened and confirmed/quantified by LC-MS/MS or GC-MS in a medical examiner's tox lab.

Seized-drug (controlled substance) analysis in a drug chemistry unit: sealed evidence bags containing powders, tablets, plant material, blotters or residue-bearing paraphernalia are opened and inventoried, net weight taken, a subsample tested presumptively (color test/FTIR/Raman) and confirmed by GC-MS, with purity quantification when required.
High-volume screening of urine specimens (probation, workplace, ME intake) by immunoassay on automated analyzers, with presumptive positives reflexed to mass-spectrometric confirmation and reporting.

Field work: presumptive identification of suspected drugs or poisons at a crime scene, overdose scene or clandestine lab — unknown powders, liquids, residues in cluttered, uncontrolled settings tested with color-test kits or portable Raman/FTIR, plus sampling for later lab quantification.

Suspected poisoning/product tampering: drugs, pesticides, metals or other poisons in food, drink, capsules or other consumer matrices; matrix homogenization, extraction/clean-up and targeted or general-unknown screening plus quantification.

tasks.label: Examine firearms to determine mechanical condition and legal status, performing restoration work on damaged firearms to obtain information, such as serial numbers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crime-lab firearms/toolmark section: recovered semiautomatic pistol of unknown make/model. Examiner verifies it is unloaded, records make/model/caliber/serial, checks magazine safety/manual safeties, measures trigger pull, cycles and inspects action, examines bore and chamber for damage or obstruction, test fires into a water recovery tank, and records mechanical condition on a worksheet.

Crime lab: revolver or long gun (rifle/shotgun), including possibly sawed-off weapons. Examiner opens/removes the cylinder or action, checks cylinder stop, timing, safeties and trigger pull, measures barrel and overall length with a dowel/rule from the closed breech to determine NFA legal status, checks for illegal modification, and test fires.

Crime lab: firearm that is damaged, corroded, fire-affected or malfunctioning. Examiner diagnoses the malfunction, documents original condition, and performs restoration/repair (replacing a broken firing pin, spring or grip, or using a substitute barrel/receiver) so the weapon can be safely test fired for comparison standards.

Crime lab: firearm with an obliterated serial number. Examiner attempts non-destructive magnetic particle inspection, then polishes the stamped area with a rotary tool and successive abrasives to a mirror finish, swabs on etchant repeatedly, watches under magnification for characters that appear transiently, photographs and records each recovered character.

Crime lab: privately-made / 3D-printed firearm or machine-gun conversion device ("switch"). Examiner assesses whether the item meets the statutory definition of a firearm/machinegun, assembles or installs it as needed, test fires to confirm automatic fire, and documents mechanical condition and legal status.

Field work at a crime scene, residence or outdoor recovery site: firearm found in situ must be photographed in place, rendered safe (magazine removed, chamber cleared, cylinder condition recorded), condition and serial number documented, and packaged for the lab under variable lighting, footing and clutter.

sources.system: NIJ Firearms Examiner Training (manual laboratory procedure; no robotic system)
sources.title: Archived | Firearms Examiner Training | Examination | National Institute of Justice
sources.claim: NIJ's firearms examiner training specifies that every firearm examination includes bore/chamber inspection, trigger pull testing, safety-feature testing, and test firing — a multi-step manual examination of an arbitrary recovered weapon.
sources.transferJustification: Baseline description of what the task requires; not a robotic system, used to define the scope a machine would have to cover.

sources.title: Archived | Firearms Examiner Training | Trigger Pull Measurements | National Institute of Justice
sources.claim: TriggerScan is a commercial forensic instrument in which a firearm is clamped in a mounting fixture and a motorized sensor arm squeezes the trigger and records the force curve — automating only the trigger-pull measurement step, with an examiner mounting the weapon and performing all other examination steps.
sources.transferJustification: Closest automated device acting physically on an evidence firearm. It performs one sub-step (trigger force measurement) on a human-fixtured weapon; it does not unload, disassemble, inspect the bore, test fire, measure legal dimensions, or restore serial numbers, so it cannot complete any whole instance.

sources.developer: Ultra Electronics Forensic Technology (IBIS) / ATF NIBIN
sources.title: Automated Firearms Ballistics Technology | Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives
sources.claim: The most automated equipment in US firearms sections is IBIS BrassTrax/BulletTrax, a desktop acquisition station that images fired cartridge cases and bullets for NIBIN; a technician places and manipulates the specimen and an examiner makes all conclusions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated imaging/comparison of fired ammunition components. It does not transfer: the specimens are small loose items loaded by a technician, and the system never handles, disassembles, function-tests, or restores a firearm itself.

sources.system: Maine State Police Crime Laboratory serial number restoration SOP (manual procedure; no robotic system)
sources.developer: Maine Department of Public Safety, State Police Crime Laboratory
sources.title: Firearms Section Serial Number Restoration Methods FA-M001
sources.claim: Published crime-lab SOPs for serial number restoration require the examiner to hand-polish the obliterated area with sandpaper, emery cloth or a rotary tool to a mirror finish and then apply etchant while watching for transiently appearing characters; no automated or robotic apparatus is specified.
sources.transferJustification: Documents the manual, judgment-laden nature of the restoration instance; searches returned no robotic or automated serial-number-restoration system.

sources.title: Humanoid Robots in Industrial Manufacturing: What They Can (and Can't) Do in 2026
sources.claim: As of 2026 the documented industrial deployments of general-purpose humanoid robots are limited to material handling and parts transfer at a small number of pilot sites, not fine tool-using tasks such as disassembling or diagnosing mechanical devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general dexterous manipulation in industry. Cited to show the state of general-purpose robot capability falls well short of unloading, field-stripping, function-testing and etching evidence firearms.

roles.description: Conduct tests to determine quality of raw materials, bulk intermediate and finished products. May conduct stability sample tests.

tasks.label: Conduct routine and non-routine analyses of in-process materials, raw materials, environmental samples, finished goods, or stability samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine assay/impurity (related-substances) testing of finished product and in-process solutions in a pharma/food QC lab: weigh dosage units or aliquots, extract/dissolve, dilute volumetrically, filter, fill HPLC/UV vials, run the validated method, integrate and compare results to specification. Includes assays of stability-pull samples on protocol timepoints.

Pharmacopeial physical/performance testing of solid dosage forms in the QC or in-process lab: dissolution profiles (USP 1/2), disintegration, tablet hardness, weight variation, thickness/diameter, friability, on batches sampled from the press or packaging line.

Raw-material, component and excipient testing: samples drawn in a warehouse sampling booth arrive at the lab for identity (FTIR/NIR/Raman), water content (Karl Fischer), loss on drying, titrimetric assay, residue and purity checks against the monograph.

Scheduled environmental monitoring rounds in classified cleanrooms/production suites: gowning, travel to mapped sampling points, active viable air sampling, placing and retrieving settle plates, non-viable particle counts, timestamped logging of each location.

Microbiology QC lab analyses: plating/membrane filtration of purified-water, in-process bioburden and product samples, loading incubators, reading and enumerating colonies on plates from EM and bioburden testing, recording counts against alert/action limits.

Non-routine analyses: out-of-specification/out-of-trend investigation testing, re-assay of a suspect sample with modified prep, unusual or novel matrices, one-off customer/regulatory requests, method troubleshooting on a misbehaving instrument, and documenting the analytical rationale.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: clinical specimen plating, incubation and colony reading. The objects (liquid samples, agar plates, colonies), precision and lab environment match pharma QC bioburden/water plating and enumeration, so the front-end handling capability carries over to QC micro sample prep.

tasks.label: Interpret test results, compare them to established specifications and control limits, and make recommendations on appropriateness of data for release.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Calibrate, validate, or maintain laboratory equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine periodic calibration/verification of benchtop measuring devices in a QC lab: daily analytical-balance check with OIML certified weights, multi-point pH meter calibration with buffers, conductivity/refractometer standard checks, thermometer verification; apply adjustment, record results in the logbook/LIMS, tag out-of-tolerance instruments.

Pre-run instrument performance verification/system suitability on chromatographs and spectrophotometers: inject replicate standards, evaluate %RSD, resolution and tailing against acceptance criteria, UV wavelength/photometric accuracy checks, MS tune and mass-axis calibration; document pass/fail before releasing the analytical run.

Scheduled preventive maintenance limited to cleaning, flushing and simple consumable exchange: flush pumps and fluid lines with wash solvent, clean electrodes/probes and sample paths, exchange GC inlet liner and septum, change inline filters and tips, refill reagent/eluent reservoirs, log the activity.

Hands-on preventive maintenance and first-line repair requiring disassembly: swap HPLC columns and fittings, replace pump seals/pistons and check valves, change detector lamps, replace tubing and rotor seals, clean flow cells, service dissolution baths/autoclaves/centrifuges, leak-check, troubleshoot faults and coordinate vendor service.

Calibration and verification of piston-operated volumetric devices: gravimetric testing of single- and multichannel pipettes, dispensers and burettes at several volumes per ISO 8655 on a calibration balance, adjustment, labeling and certificate/report generation.

Equipment qualification and validation activities: executing IQ/OQ/PQ protocols, placing thermocouples/data loggers for temperature mapping of ovens, incubators and stability chambers, autoclave load validation, running challenge cycles, and assembling and signing the validation documentation.

sources.system: METTLER TOLEDO Robotic Mass Comparators (with MC Link software)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: calibration of mass standards. It transfers to the QC analyst's balance calibration/verification instance because the physical acts are identical — handling class-E/F certified weights, placing them on a weighing pan without shock or eccentricity error, reading and recording deviations against tolerances — at higher precision than a routine daily balance check.

sources.title: Robotic Mass Comparator 1020g 1µg | RADWAG RMC 1000.5Y
sources.claim: A second vendor sells fully automated robotic mass comparators that run the weight comparison process end to end in an enclosed, purpose-built workspace.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Mettler comparator: automated handling and comparison weighing of calibration weights is the mechanical content of balance/weight calibration performed by QC analysts.

It transfers to the QC analyst's routine cleaning/flushing maintenance instance because the same operations (washing probes and cuvettes, flushing fluid paths, running calibrators and accepting calibration) are performed by machine-controlled mechanisms instead of an analyst.

sources.title: FDA Clears Roche's Cobas c 703 and ISE Neo Analytical Units
sources.claim: The newly cleared ISE analytical unit automates routine maintenance tasks that laboratory staff previously performed by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: independent trade-press confirmation that maintenance work previously done by hand on lab analyzers is now executed by the instrument's own mechanisms.

sources.title: GERSTEL ALEX – Automated Liner Exchange for GC
sources.claim: A commercial robotic autosampler can physically replace a contaminated GC inlet liner automatically at any point in a run, a consumable-exchange maintenance job otherwise done by hand.

sources.title: Automated titration system for up to 28 samples | Metrohm
sources.claim: Robotic titration sample processors run unattended series and automatically clean the measuring electrode and burette tips and empty the vessel at the end of each determination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: electrode conditioning/cleaning on an automated titrator. It transfers to routine sensor maintenance and to sensor calibration because the same robotic tower moves the electrode between vessels presented in the rack, which is the physical act of dipping an electrode into successive buffer beakers.

sources.system: Metrohm OMNIS software with Robotic Sample Processors
sources.title: Introduction to OMNIS - Software Basics – Metrohm USA
sources.claim: Titration/measurement software driving these robotic sample processors includes a pH calibration command with automatic recognition of the calibration buffers, so electrode calibration runs as a programmed step of an unattended method.

sources.system: TECAN Freedom EVO liquid handler with automated gravimetric calibration (online balance)
sources.developer: Tecan / study authors (published in SLAS Technology/JALA)
sources.title: Automated Gravimetric Calibration to Optimize the Accuracy and Precision of TECAN Freedom EVO Liquid Handler
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed automated gravimetric procedure calibrates and adjusts the volumetric accuracy of a liquid handling system across 3–900 µL using an online balance, i.e., the instrument's dispensing is calibrated without a human performing the weighings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: gravimetric calibration of a pipetting device. It transfers to the analyst's pipette-calibration and instrument-calibration instances because it is the same procedure (dispense defined volumes onto a calibrated balance, compute accuracy/precision, apply the correction) on comparable microlitre volumes.

sources.system: ROS-based robot arm with Sartorius Picus 2 electronic pipette and Cubis Pipette Calibration System
sources.title: Development of an Automated Electronic Pipette Calibration System
sources.claim: An engineering thesis built and tested a robot-arm system that operates an electronic pipette against a pipette-calibration balance to perform the calibration workflow, benchmarked against a human operator.

sources.title: Automatic Device for Multichannel Pipette Calibration 18g 1µg | RADWAG AP-12.1.5Y
sources.claim: A commercial bench device performs ISO 8655 gravimetric calibration of single- and multichannel micropipettes with automated weighing and ambient-condition monitoring and report generation.

sources.claim: Chromatography data systems execute system suitability testing automatically on the injections made by the instrument's autosampler and take run-control actions (e.g., halting the sequence) when criteria fail.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated system suitability of a chromatograph. The physical work — the autosampler drawing and injecting replicate standard vials presented in its tray — plus automated evaluation is exactly the analyst's pre-run instrument performance verification.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA mobile manipulator, University of Liverpool)
sources.developer: University of Liverpool (Burger, Cooper et al.)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator navigated an ordinary wet-chemistry laboratory for eight days and autonomously operated analytical instruments and dispensers built for humans, but its work was sample preparation and measurement, not instrument calibration or maintenance.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to test the E2 ceiling: it is the strongest demonstration of autonomous robot work in a human-arranged laboratory, and it covers sample handling and instrument operation only, so it does not substantiate calibration, validation, or maintenance of that equipment.

tasks.label: Ensure that lab cleanliness and safety standards are maintained.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-run cleanup of the analyst's own QC bench: clearing glassware, reagent bottles, standards and consumables off the bench and hood, wiping the bench, balance enclosure and instrument surfaces with detergent and 70% IPA, wiping up minor reagent spills, discarding pipettes/vials into the correct waste stream, and signing the cleaning log. Cluttered human workstation, mixed labware and chemicals.

Labware reprocessing in the lab's wash-up/media area: collecting used volumetric glassware, media bottles and reusable parts, racking them, running the laboratory glassware washer and the autoclave, unloading and returning clean, dried labware to storage.

Housekeeping logistics: moving filled chemical/biohazard waste containers, soiled-material and glassware carts from the lab to the accumulation, decon or dock area on fixed indoor routes, and keeping lab and adjacent corridor floors clean (scrubbing/mopping, spot cleaning).

Documented safety and housekeeping rounds of the lab suite: walking a defined route, checking fume hood face-velocity gauges and certification status, looking for leaks, spills, blocked egress, overfull waste bins and improper storage, capturing readings and observations, logging findings and flagging anomalies for follow-up.

Hands-on safety-equipment upkeep and corrective action: weekly eyewash/safety-shower flush test with tag sign-off, restocking PPE, spill kits and first-aid supplies, replacing full sharps and waste containers, securing gas cylinders, re-labeling or capping containers found out of compliance.

Controlled-area upkeep in a micro/cleanroom QC suite: routine sanitization/decontamination of the classified area between operations plus environmental monitoring (viable air and particle sampling, surface plates) to verify that cleanliness standards are being met, with results reported and trended.

sources.transferJustification: Covers the floor-cleaning part of lab housekeeping: same hard-floor scrubbing job inside an institution-controlled building with corridors and rooms kept to a working standard.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: Autonomous TUG mobile robots haul waste, regulated medical waste, recycling and soiled-material carts through a hospital's corridors at production scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital waste and soiled-material haulage. Same objects (wheeled waste/biohazard carts), same indoor institutional routes, same accepted output (waste removed from work areas to the accumulation point).

sources.system: Steelco ATS (Automated Transfer System) shuttle with automatic loading/unloading for washer-disinfectors and sterilizers

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Orbit / Autowalk automated inspection

sources.claim: Spot runs autonomous inspection missions in industrial facilities, reading analog gauges with computer vision, capturing thermal and acoustic data at fixed checkpoints and raising alerts on out-of-range readings, with results collated in Orbit.

sources.title: Loop Robots - for GMP Cleanrooms
sources.claim: Robot SAM autonomously decontaminates cGMP class B/C/D cleanrooms and hospital pharmacy cleanrooms with UV-C, mapping the room, routing itself and issuing a digital disinfection report; it is in routine use by cleaning specialists at hospital sites.

sources.system: Autonomous UV-C contamination-control robot (AstraZeneca cleanroom study)

instances.label: Pharma/food QC lab: an HPLC/UHPLC or LC-MS behaves abnormally mid-run (pressure spike or drop, leak at a fitting, noisy/drifting baseline, tailing peaks, failed system suitability). The analyst isolates the cause among pump seals, clogged frit/inline filter, air in the lines, degraded column, aged detector lamp or dirty flow cell, performs the fix (purge, tighten/replace fittings, swap frit/column/lamp, wash), re-runs the suitability standard and documents the event in the instrument log.

QC lab: another analytical instrument loses performance or errors out — GC/GC-MS response drop and peak tailing from a matrix-fouled inlet liner/septum/column front, UV-Vis or FTIR failing a wavelength/energy check, Karl Fischer drift, dissolution bath paddle wobble/temperature error, TOC or ICP faults. Analyst diagnoses the subsystem at fault, replaces consumables or realigns/cleans, verifies with a check standard, and documents.

QC lab: an electrochemical meter/probe (pH, conductivity, dissolved oxygen) fails its daily calibration check — slow response, out-of-range slope/offset, fouled or dried junction. Analyst cleans/reconditions the electrode, re-calibrates with fresh buffers/standards, adjusts, re-verifies, and replaces the sensor if it still fails.

QC lab/support areas: general bench and support equipment problems — balance out of tolerance or drifting/unstable readings, oven/incubator/stability chamber temperature excursion, purified-water system alarm, autoclave or centrifuge fault, pipette failing verification. Analyst inspects (leveling, drafts, doors, seals, filters, probes), determines cause, corrects or removes from service and escalates, and documents.

QC lab: an automated system errors out — autosampler tray/needle jam or missed vial, misloaded or misaligned rack, instrument door ajar, liquid handler tip pickup failure or clogged tip, plate-handling robot placement fault. Analyst identifies the cause from the error code and visual inspection, clears/repositions/reseats, and restarts the sequence without losing samples.

Manufacturing floor of a food/pharma/chemical plant during in-process monitoring rounds: analyst finds an equipment problem — an in-line sensor or gauge reading out of range, a leak, an overheating motor or pump, a metal detector/checkweigher alarm — localizes the affected asset, judges whether product quality is impacted, and reports it to maintenance/production with the supporting data.

instances.label: GMP QC lab, small-molecule drug product: execute an ICH Q2 validation protocol for an HPLC/UPLC assay and related-substances method - weigh reference standard and dosage units on analytical balances, prepare a 5-level linearity dilution series, spiked-placebo accuracy samples at 3 levels, 6 replicate repeatability preparations, solution-stability and filter-validation sets, filter and vial, run the injection sequences, integrate chromatograms, compute statistics and assemble the reviewed raw-data package and validation report.

instances.label: Small UAS mapping mission over an outdoor project site (construction site, quarry/open-pit mine, solar farm, farm field, utility corridor, burn scar): plan flight lines, deploy the aircraft, fly an automated grid or corridor collecting RGB/LiDAR/multispectral/thermal imagery, monitor coverage and quality, land, offload and verify data. Variable terrain, weather, obstacles, and site traffic.

Office-based satellite/archive data acquisition: define an area of interest and collection parameters, submit tasking orders to commercial satellite operators or pull scenes from Landsat/Sentinel/commercial archives, schedule and monitor collections and downlinks, verify cloud cover and geometry, ingest the delivered data.

Ground-based scanning at an institution-controlled facility: terrestrial laser scanner setups or mobile/backpack mapping inside and around plants, substations, warehouses, campuses, tunnels and paved road corridors, registering scans and checking point-cloud completeness before leaving site.

Field ground-truth and calibration collection at an open site: establish and measure ground control points and check points with RTK GNSS, lay out calibration/reflectance targets, and take georeferenced spectral, thermal or canopy readings across rough outdoor terrain.

Crewed-aircraft airborne survey: operate the digital aerial camera / LiDAR / SAR console in a survey aircraft over a large project area (county-scale ortho or LiDAR block, high-altitude lines), monitor GNSS/IMU quality, exposure and line coverage in flight, flag and re-fly deficient lines.

Sensor integration and pre-mission preparation in a hangar, shop or lab: mount and cable a camera/LiDAR/thermal sensor and IMU-GNSS unit into an aircraft port, vehicle rack or UAS gimbal, configure the sensor and flight management system, run functional checks and boresight/radiometric calibration.

instances.label: Pre-mission sensor setup and calibration checks at the office, lab or hangar: mounting a mapping camera, multispectral head or lidar payload on the aircraft/UAV or bench, connecting GNSS/IMU and power cables, powering up, running built-in calibration/self-test routines, shooting frames of a target board or checkerboard, and verifying focus, exposure, gimbal alignment and time sync before the flight.

Field radiometric calibration around a survey: carrying calibrated reflectance panels/tarps and ground targets to the site, laying them out, and taking white-reference, dark-current and panel readings with a field spectroradiometer or handheld radiometer under natural sun immediately before and after the overflight, repeating as illumination changes.

Bench/laboratory calibration of an instrument against reference standards: fixing a spectroradiometer, thermal or multispectral camera on an optical bench, running it against an integrating-sphere uniform source, blackbody, lamp standard or collimated target, stepping through the measurement series, computing gain/offset or wavelength coefficients and loading them into the instrument.

On-mission calibration during airborne/UAV collection: executing IMU/INS calibration maneuvers and boresight calibration lines at the start, turns and end of the flight so the inertial navigation solution and point-cloud/image geolocation stay within accuracy spec; checking the resulting accuracy report.

Routine calibration and verification of ground and positioning equipment: setting a GNSS base receiver/antenna over a known mark and checking it against reference values, leveling and re-zeroing instruments, cleaning optics and domes, comparing a field radiometer or weather sensor against a standard, and documenting results.

instances.label: UAV/drone mapping mission over a site taken as found (farm, quarry, corridor, construction site, disaster scene): the technician watches the live downlink, telemetry and captured frames during the flight, checks exposure, blur, overlap/coverage and GNSS-RTK fix, and corrects on the fly - changes camera settings, re-flies gaps, re-launches after a battery change, aborts for wind or a bad payload.

Crewed airborne survey (LiDAR + large-format camera) in a survey aircraft: the sensor operator sits at the operator console for a multi-hour sortie watching raw returns, image histograms, point density, IMU/GNSS lock and disk write status, adjusts scanner PRF/scan angle and camera exposure, restarts or reseats a misbehaving sensor, and calls lines for re-flight.

Ground-based scanning collection - tripod terrestrial laser scanner or mobile mapping system in a building, plant or construction site: the technician checks point density, noise, registration/overlap and image quality on the tablet as scans come in, re-levels/recalibrates the instrument, changes resolution settings and re-scans positions that fail quality checks.

Operations centre / ground-station monitoring of a downlink or tasked collection: the technician watches incoming telemetry and raw data streams during a satellite pass or airborne downlink, checks signal lock, bit-error rate, band saturation and cloud contamination, and corrects the receiving chain (antenna pointing/tracking, receiver and recorder configuration) or reschedules the collect.

Field reference/in-situ instrumentation running during a collection campaign: GNSS base receiver, sun photometer or field spectroradiometer, radiometric reference panels, weather sensors. The technician watches the logged signal for saturation, drift, mistracking or dropouts and corrects the instrument - re-point, re-level, re-optimize integration time/gain, restart logging, protect it from rain.

instances.label: Agricultural/rangeland ground reference: technician goes to designated sample fields, walks or drives transects, records GPS positions of sample points, takes geotagged photos of the canopy and plot, notes crop type/stand/growth stage and canopy cover to validate imagery-derived crop maps. Outdoor, dirt, weather-exposed, uneven terrain.

Urban/roadside land-use and land-cover verification: technician runs a route through city streets or rural roads, capturing geotagged street-level photos of parcels, buildings, impervious surface and vegetation at pre-selected sample points to check a classification; mostly drive-by with occasional short walk-ups on public sidewalks.

Forest/vegetation plot verification in accessible woodland: navigate to a plot center by GPS, delineate the plot, measure trees (DBH, height, stem count) and understory, photograph the plot, and log georeferenced records to validate LiDAR/aerial forest attribute maps.

Ground control and calibration targets for a UAS/aerial collect: lay out and paint or place targets at planned coordinates across open ground, a solar site or a construction site, occupy each with survey-grade GNSS, record coordinates and photograph the target for the photogrammetric block.

Difficult-access verification points: off-trail backcountry, wetlands, steep or flooded terrain, or post-disaster damage assessment sites; long hikes with gear, water crossings, species-level identification, ad hoc judgment about what to sample and photograph.

Verification data collection on institution-controlled premises: substations, industrial plants, ports, airports, or university/agency campuses; walking a defined route to photograph and geolocate assets, take instrument readings, and confirm features seen in imagery or thermal surveys.

Ground-reference field campaign in dense or complex natural forest: hike off-trail to plot centres, establish and georeference the plot under canopy, record species, tag and measure stems, take canopy photos and field spectroradiometer/leaf-area readings, and log understory and site condition data for calibrating remote sensing carbon estimates.

Crewed-aircraft airborne acquisition over a large forest block: mount and boresight a LiDAR/hyperspectral sensor and GNSS/IMU in the survey aircraft at the airfield, load the flight plan, operate the sensor over flight lines for several hours, monitor coverage, sun angle, cloud and trajectory quality, and reflow lines that fail QC.

Installing and servicing in-situ instrumentation that supports the remote sensing/carbon record at forest sites: mounting radiometers, phenocams and met sensors on towers, burying soil probes, placing calibration tarps, corner reflectors and GNSS base stations, swapping batteries and downloading data loggers in remote terrain.

Office-based acquisition of spaceborne and archive data over forest areas of interest: defining AOIs, submitting tasking orders to imaging constellations or selecting archive scenes, monitoring cloud cover and acquisition success, and downloading/verifying the delivered imagery and lidar for the carbon-tracking project.

instances.label: Noise survey and hearing conservation program upkeep at a manufacturing plant: walk the production floor with a calibrated Type 2 sound level meter taking area readings at machine and operator positions during representative production, fit full-shift dosimeters on selected workers across job classifications, note machine operating states, then build/update the noise contour map, identify overexposed job titles, and revise the written hearing conservation program and posting/HPD recommendations.

Personal exposure monitoring campaign for a chemical, metal fume, silica or solvent hazard at an industrial or laboratory facility: calibrate sampling pumps, clip cassettes/sorbent tubes to workers' breathing zones at shift start, observe and log tasks, retrieve and re-calibrate at shift end, package with chain-of-custody to an AIHA lab, then compare results to OELs and update the written exposure assessment and control plan.

Routine area atmospheric monitoring round maintaining a continuous atmosphere monitoring program at an industrial facility (refinery, gas plant, chemical plant, wastewater works): traverse a defined route with direct-reading multi-gas/PID instruments, take readings at established points around compressors, sumps, tanks and process units, log values into the monitoring record and flag any exceedance or suspected leak for follow-up.

Ventilation survey of laboratory fume hoods and local exhaust ventilation in a lab or plant: measure face velocity traverses with a thermal anemometer, run smoke-tube/visualization containment checks, take hood static pressure and duct pitot traverse readings, check fan and belt condition at rooftop or mezzanine units, then write the survey report with pass/fail, stickers and rebalancing recommendations and update the ventilation program records.

Asbestos management plan development and periodic surveillance in older institutional buildings (schools, hospitals, campuses): inspect boiler rooms, pipe chases, crawl spaces, attics and above suspended ceilings for asbestos-containing materials, assess condition and damage, collect bulk samples where needed, photograph and map locations, then update the O&M/management plan, notifications and six-month surveillance records.

Field hygiene monitoring at construction or field job sites with changing layouts: silica, lead, welding fume or noise monitoring during grinding, cutting, abatement or demolition work, checking enclosure ventilation and negative pressure, documenting results and updating the site-specific exposure control plan.

Evaluation of work practices at the point of work: observing employees perform lockout/tagout, confined-space entry, hot work or manual handling, interviewing workers and supervisors, and verifying permits and training records against what is observed.

instances.label: Full-shift personal exposure monitoring in a manufacturing plant, foundry, warehouse or construction crew: calibrate a personal sampling pump, clip it to a worker's belt and place a filter cassette or sorbent tube in the breathing zone, check flow during the shift while the worker moves and works, remove and seal media, post-calibrate, label and complete chain-of-custody for the lab.

Area / fixed-point air sampling inside a facility: set several calibrated pumps with filter cassettes, sorbent tubes, impingers or bioaerosol cassettes on tripods near processes (welding fume, solvent vapors, mold/IAQ complaint, silica), run for a set period, retrieve, cap and ship media for laboratory analysis with blanks and documentation.

Direct-reading survey rounds through an operating industrial facility (refinery, midstream plant, chemical plant, wastewater works): walk fixed routes with multi-gas meter, PID and real-time dust monitor, take grab readings of LEL/O2/H2S/VOC at process areas, locate fugitive gas or vapor sources, and log concentrations by location.

Surface wipe and settled-dust sampling in facilities and buildings: template-defined 100 cm2 wipes for lead, beryllium or other metals on machines, sills and floors, plus swab/tape-lift or vacuum dust samples, each sealed in a labeled container with field blanks for lab analysis.

Bulk material sampling in buildings, renovation/demolition areas, or plant process areas: cut or scrape a portion of suspect asbestos-containing insulation, ceiling tile or mastic, chip lead paint, or scoop bulk powder/dust from a hopper, bag and seal it, patch the sampled spot, and label for lab analysis.

Outdoor field sampling at uncontrolled open sites: fenceline, perimeter or plume grab samples into canisters, bags or sorbent tubes at spill/emergency responses, landfills, demolition or remediation sites and around outdoor process equipment, then delivery of the sealed samples for laboratory analysis.

instances.label: Walkthrough survey of a manufacturing/processing plant production area: move through the operating floor checking general and dilution ventilation, dust/fume/mist and heat conditions, confirm exhaust fans and hoods are running, note burned-out or inadequate lighting, take spot readings (temperature, gas/O2, noise, visible dust) and log conditions against thresholds for a routine condition report.

Performance evaluation of local exhaust ventilation: measure face velocity of a lab fume hood or capture velocity at a grinding/welding/plating hood with a calibrated anemometer on a prescribed grid, run smoke-tube or tracer visualization, take duct static pressure or pitot traverse readings (often from a ladder/platform), compare with ACGIH/ANSI criteria and specify corrections.

Complaint-driven indoor air quality / comfort investigation in an office, school or clinic: interview affected occupants, walk the affected zone, measure CO2, temperature, RH, CO and particulate at desks and returns, inspect diffusers, check above ceiling tiles for water damage or blocked returns, check the air handler outdoor-air setting, and diagnose the cause.

Scheduled quantitative environmental survey along defined sampling points inside a controlled facility (cleanroom, hospital wing, laboratory, plant): viable/non-viable air sampling or CO2/temperature/RH readings and illuminance readings at fixed locations, compared with standards and recorded in a traceable, documented log.

Site check at a construction, renovation or confined-space job: judge adequacy of temporary ventilation and task lighting, test atmosphere (O2, LEL, CO, H2S) before entry, check welding-fume extraction and engine exhaust placement in a changing, cluttered, partly built space.

Mechanical room / rooftop check of the ventilation plant serving occupied spaces: verify supply and exhaust fans operating, read filter differential-pressure gauges, open access panels to check filter loading, belts and damper positions, verify exhaust stack separation from outdoor air intakes.

Hands-on PPE training in a training room or plant area: specialist dons and doffs a respirator, chemical suit, gloves and hearing protection to show correct technique, performs a user seal check, conducts qualitative respirator fit tests on trainees, and corrects each trainee's donning technique by hand.

Equipment- or process-specific training at the machine on a plant floor: demonstrate lockout/tagout by applying locks and tags to energy isolation devices, show machine guarding and interlocks, demonstrate safe forklift or powered-equipment operation and confined-space entry gear, then watch trainees repeat the steps.

tasks.label: Investigate health-related complaints and inspect facilities to ensure that they comply with public health legislation and regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Employee/occupant health complaint at an industrial plant, warehouse, or office building (fumes, dust, headaches, 'bad air'). Specialist interviews the complainant and supervisor, walks the affected area, takes direct-reading measurements (PID, CO/CO2, dust), may place area or personal sampling pumps on workers, checks ventilation and the chemical inventory/SDS, then writes findings and abatement recommendations.

Scheduled compliance inspection of a workplace against occupational/public health rules: chemical labeling and storage, local exhaust ventilation, eyewash and safety showers, sanitation facilities and potable water, spot noise/light readings, hygiene program records, plus worker interviews; issues a written inspection report listing deficiencies and correction deadlines.

Routine periodic hazard-monitoring sweep along a fixed route in a process facility (refinery, chemical plant, food plant): read gauges and surface temperatures, measure ambient gas concentrations against alarm limits, listen for leaks, note spills, leaks and housekeeping issues, and log the readings in a documented report for the safety team.

Public-health inspection of a food establishment or institutional kitchen prompted by an illness or sanitation complaint: probe hot/cold food temperatures, test sanitizer concentration, open coolers and dry storage, observe handwashing and employee hygiene, look for pest evidence, review temperature and illness logs, interview the manager, and issue a scored report or citation.

Complaint at an unstructured site: a private residence or rental unit (mold/moisture, lead paint, sewage backup, rodents) or an active construction/temporary worksite (silica dust, missing sanitation facilities, heat stress). Specialist navigates the space as found, takes moisture/dust readings, collects samples, interviews occupants or workers, applies the housing or safety code, and writes findings.

Technical sampling inspection of an institution: pool/spa water chemistry, hospital water-system Legionella sampling, childcare or long-term-care environmental audit, or lab/cleanroom monitoring. Involves drawing samples with chain-of-custody, taking instrument readings, verifying maintenance and treatment records, and reporting a compliance determination.

Transfers to the fixed-route plant monitoring sweep instance: same objects (process equipment, plant atmosphere), same instrument readings against exposure/alarm limits, same E2 facility.

sources.claim: ANYmal runs regular autonomous inspection missions inside W.R. Grace's Duren chemical plant, executing 120+ thermal, visual and acoustic ... and producing digital reports used by the plant, with no structural changes to the facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: condition-monitoring inspection rounds. Transfers to the routine plant hazard-monitoring sweep: identical route-following in a live human-staffed plant, same class of readings, and delivery of a documented report.

sources.title: Spot at Cargill | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: At Cargill's Amsterdam Multiseed oilseed crush and refinery plant, Spot has run since mid-2024 conducting routine inspections and visual safety checks, walking its route several times a day so leaks of seed and oil are found early; data supports the plant's food and safety quality team.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine plant walkthrough safety/condition checks. Transfers to the fixed-route monitoring sweep instance: same food-plant setting, same visual leak/housekeeping observations, same repeated documented route a safety team accepts.

sources.title: Automated Inspections Key to Industry 4.0 | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot performs scheduled autonomous inspection missions from a docking station, stopping at the same locations to collect thermal, visual, acoustic and gauge data consistently, with results reviewed in Orbit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled asset inspection rounds. Supports the plant monitoring sweep instance by establishing unattended, repeatable route execution and data logging inside working industrial facilities.

tasks.label: Inspect specified areas to ensure the presence of fire prevention equipment, safety equipment, or first-aid supplies.

instances.label: Routine walkthrough of a manufacturing plant or distribution warehouse: verify each marked extinguisher station holds an extinguisher, that it is visible, unobstructed, gauge in the green and tag current; confirm fire hose/sprinkler clearance, eyewash/safety showers and marked egress are present and accessible; log findings on a checklist. Indoor industrial aisles, forklift traffic, noise and dust.

Monthly/quarterly building round in an office, school, lab or healthcare facility: walk multiple floors, corridors and stairwells checking extinguisher cabinets, exit signage, AED cabinet presence, sprinkler head clearance and fire door condition; produce a documented inspection record with photos of deficiencies.

First-aid supply check: open first-aid cabinets, kits, and AED cabinets in break rooms, shops, labs, and vehicles; inventory contents against the required list, check expiration dates on pads, batteries and eyewash bottles, and flag missing/expired items for restock.

Construction or renovation jobsite inspection: confirm extinguishers are present and accessible at hot-work, fueling and generator locations, fire-watch equipment is staged, and a first-aid kit and eyewash are present in the site trailer/gang box; extinguishers often buried by stacked materials. Layout changes daily, rough terrain, mud, active trades.

Outdoor/field operating site round (substation, tank farm, well pad, laydown yard, terminal): verify extinguishers on equipment and at fire stations, safety showers, spill and emergency kits are present, mounted and accessible; weather, gravel and grating underfoot, fenced institution-controlled premises.

tasks.label: Conduct audits at hazardous waste sites or industrial sites or participate in hazardous waste site investigations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Checklist-based EHS compliance audit walkthrough of an operating manufacturing/industrial plant: inspect machine guarding, lockout/tagout, PPE use, chemical storage and labeling, emergency eyewash/extinguishers, egress and housekeeping; open panels and cabinets, test emergency equipment, interview operators and supervisors, review permits and training records, then issue written findings with corrective actions.

RCRA hazardous waste generator compliance audit at an industrial facility: check satellite and 90-day accumulation areas for container closure, labeling and accumulation dates, compatibility, secondary containment and aisle space; verify manifests, land disposal restriction paperwork, contingency plan and training records; interview waste handlers; write audit report.

Routine mandated periodic (weekly/monthly) inspection of a hazardous waste container storage building or drum yard: walk aisles past stacked/rowed drums, look at each container for rust, corrosion, dents, bulging, tilt or leakage, verify inventory identifiers and labels against the site database, and log/report problem containers.

Participation in a hazardous waste site investigation at a contaminated or abandoned site (Superfund RI, Phase II ESA): reconnaissance over uneven, overgrown, debris-strewn ground; instrument screening (PID, FID, radiation, LEL); locating and characterizing unknown drums and stained soil; collecting or overseeing soil/groundwater samples; personal air monitoring of the field crew; documenting conditions.

Audit of a permitted hazardous waste TSDF, transfer/recycling facility or landfill: indoor and outdoor container and tank storage pads, ignitability/compatibility segregation, secondary containment and sump condition, run-on/run-off controls, cell operations and gas monitoring points, plus operating record, inspection log and training file review; findings report.

Health and safety audit at an active remediation or HAZWOPER/construction project: open excavations and shoring, decon line setup, level of PPE in use, real-time air monitoring stations, drum staging areas, heavy equipment traffic; layout changes daily and conditions are weather-dependent; audit findings delivered to the site supervisor.

sources.title: Intelligent Mobile Sensor System (IMSS) for drum inspection and monitoring -- Volume 3. Final report
sources.claim: The IMSS drum-inspection vehicle was evaluated in real operating DOE waste storage facilities, identifying anomalies including rust spots, corrosion, dents and tilted drums with all drums positively identified against the site database.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: the mandated container-condition and inventory inspection of a hazardous/mixed waste storage building, performed in the institution-controlled warehouse where an OHS specialist would perform it.

tasks.label: Collect samples of hazardous materials or arrange for sample collection.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Personal breathing-zone air sampling on production workers in a manufacturing plant, foundry, or construction trade: calibrate sampling pumps, clip pump to belt and cassette/sorbent tube to the worker's lapel, follow the worker through the shift, note task changes, remove and post-calibrate, seal and label media, complete chain-of-custody and ship to the AIHA lab.

Area/grab air sampling at designated points inside a facility: place area pumps, canisters, badges or impaction/settle media at fixed locations (near a degreaser, weld booth, HVAC return), run for a set volume/time, retrieve, label and log; includes indoor-air-quality and gas/vapor grab surveys in occupied buildings.

Bulk sampling of suspect hazardous building materials during an asbestos/lead survey or before renovation/demolition: identify homogeneous areas, wet the material, cut or core pipe lagging, ceiling texture, floor tile or mastic, take paint chips, seal each in a labeled container, patch the spot, log location on the drawing; work off ladders, in crawlspaces, boiler rooms and partially demolished areas.

Surface wipe/swab sampling: lead or beryllium dust wipes over templated 10x10 cm areas on floors, sills and equipment; pesticide or drug-residue wipes; microbial swabs/contact plates and mold tape lifts in a plant, hospital or office, with each medium sealed, labeled and shipped with blanks.

Liquid and waste sampling at a facility or waste site: potable-water first-draw samples at taps for lead, cooling-tower and shower water/swabs for Legionella, metalworking-fluid samples, effluent grab or composite samples at a discharge point, and coliwasa/thief sampling of drummed waste for characterization.

Arranging for sample collection rather than doing it: scoping what must be sampled and by which method, selecting and contracting an accredited lab or industrial-hygiene/hazmat contractor, scheduling site access, issuing the purchase order, specifying chain-of-custody and turnaround, and receiving/forwarding the results.

sources.title: Automated Cleanroom Monitoring with MicronView's Dual-Mode Robot
sources.claim: MicronView's APC/BAS Dual-Mode Robot is a commercially offered autonomous mobile robot that performs cleanroom air sampling rounds, using a 6-axis arm to place and retrieve 90 ... culture-based viable air samples while an onboard particle counter records non-viable counts.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: the robot collects biological-hazard air samples onto media that go to the lab, replacing technicians who gown up, place samplers, and log results.

sources.title: MicronView Dual-mode Robot improves Cleanroom Monitoring
sources.claim: The same robot navigates a working GMP cleanroom by LiDAR/SLAM along validated routes, draws 500 L viable air samples over five minutes at each point, barcodes and timestamps each plate for traceability, and docks itself afterwards; a full day of manual monitoring becomes about two hours unattended.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics (with MFE Inspection Solutions; Chevron deployment)
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs autonomous inspection rounds across an entire 40-acre midstream gas plant carrying gas-detection and other sensor payloads, and detected a combustible-gas plume from a pinhole leak during a round; Chevron runs Spot in a production role performing daily inspections at its Bakersfield cogeneration facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous atmospheric-hazard survey rounds in an industrial plant): shows a legged robot reaching designated sampling points unattended in a cluttered E2 process facility and operating a gas-sensing instrument there, the mobility and instrument half of area air sampling.

sources.title: Siemens Starts up First LiquiRob Robot System on New Posco Slab Caster
sources.claim: Primetals' LiquiRob robot systems, in service since 2007 at POSCO Gwangyang and ordered for voestalpine Linz BOF shops, automatically take samples of molten steel and measure temperature at converters, ladles, tundishes and casters, keeping operators clear of the hazardous area; SMS's X-Pact Sampler performs liquid-steel sampling automatically as well.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (industrial sampling of a hazardous material for laboratory analysis): a fixed robot cell built around the sampling point autonomously captures a physical specimen of a dangerous material into a carrier and routes it to the lab, the E1 form of hazardous-material sample collection.

sources.title: Cross Belt Sampling Systems | McLanahan
sources.claim: Cross-belt mechanical sampling systems automatically sweep a cutter through a moving conveyor stream at timed increments and eject each increment into the sample container for laboratory analysis, following ASTM D7430 mechanical-sampling practice for coal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (representative bulk-solid sampling of a dusty hazardous commodity): when the material is presented to the machine, a machine-controlled cutter takes a defined increment and containerizes it to a recognized standard, which is the E1 counterfactual of bulk material sampling.

sources.title: Automatic Water Samplers | Teledyne ISCO
sources.claim: Teledyne ISCO automatic water samplers are widely deployed programmable machines that draw water or wastewater through a peristaltic pump into arrays of bottles unattended on time- or flow-paced schedules, refrigerated for preservation, for regulatory compliance and effluent monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (unattended compliance liquid sampling): the machine performs the physical act a specialist would - drawing a measured aliquot into a labeled, preserved bottle at a fixed sampling point - at a purpose-built installation.

sources.system: Robotic swabbing system with tactile sensing control
sources.title: Evaluation of Robotic Swabbing and Fluorescent Sensing to Monitor the Hygiene of Food Contact Surfaces
sources.claim: A University of Arkansas robotic swabbing system (UR5e arm, custom sponge-swab gripper, force-sensing feedback) autonomously swabbed food-contact surfaces and was benchmarked against trained and untrained humans on water pickup, coverage and pressure consistency, achieving consistently full surface coverage through closed-loop motion control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (environmental surface swab sampling): same tool, same media and the same defined-area technique as a lead-dust or microbial wipe sample, performed on a surface presented to the arm.

tasks.label: Prepare hazardous, radioactive, or mixed waste samples for transportation or storage by treating, compacting, packaging, and labeling them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: University/hospital EHS specialist consolidating laboratory chemical waste: picking up assorted small containers (solvents, acids, bases, some poorly identified) from satellite accumulation areas in lab buildings, segregating by compatibility, bulking liquids into 55-gal drums or lab-packing bottles with absorbent, adding neutralizer/absorbent as needed, closing, and applying hazardous-waste and DOT labels in a central accumulation area.

Industrial/manufacturing site safety specialist drumming bulk liquid hazardous waste (spent solvent, paint sludge, waste oil, plating rinse) in a plant waste accumulation room: transferring/pumping into DOT-spec drums or totes, sealing bungs, marking and labeling with waste codes and hazard placards, staging on pallets for the TSDF hauler.

Radiation safety/health-physics specialist at a nuclear plant, DOE site, or decommissioning project processing low-level and dry active radioactive waste: sorting and segregating items by radiation level and material, size-reducing and compacting into drums/liners/boxes, surveying, sealing containers, and labeling/recording package data for shipment or interim storage.

Hospital or research-institution safety specialist handling regulated biohazardous and mixed (chem/rad/bio) waste: autoclaving or otherwise treating infectious waste, consolidating sharps and red-bag waste into approved rigid containers, volume-reducing, sealing, and labeling for licensed transporter pickup.

Field/remediation setting: safety specialist packaging waste from a spill cleanup, tank closure, or site remediation outdoors — drumming contaminated soil, absorbents, PPE and debris, lidding and ring-clamping drums, marking and labeling them, and staging in a variable, weather-exposed, site-to-site-different work area.

Hot-lab technician/health physicist preparing small radioactive or mixed-waste samples and residues in a shielded lab or hot cell: stabilizing/absorbing liquids, transferring residues into inner containers, decontaminating and overpacking into shielded shipping containers, and labeling per DOT/NRC requirements.

tasks.label: Perform laboratory analyses or physical inspections of samples to detect disease or to assess purity or cleanliness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial-hygiene analytical lab: batches of workplace air-sampling media arrive by courier (pre-weighed PVC/PTFE filters in cassettes, charcoal/sorbent tubes, impingers). The specialist conditions and weighs filters on a microbalance in a controlled weighing room, desorbs/digests media, runs GC-FID/GC-MS or ICP for solvents, metals and silica, and issues concentration results against OELs with QC.

Environmental/hygiene microbiology bench: potable and cooling-water samples, Legionella samples, and surface/sponge swabs from a plant or hospital are plated or membrane-filtered, incubated, and colonies counted/identified to judge cleanliness or presence of pathogens; results reported against action limits.

Microscopy bench: bulk building-material samples and air-cassette filters analyzed for asbestos (PLM identification of bulk chunks; PCM/SEM fiber counting of cleared filters) and dust/particulate cleanliness checks for abatement clearance.

On-site rapid checks inside a controlled facility (food plant, hospital, water utility): ATP/protein swabs of food-contact or high-touch surfaces, field water test kits (chlorine, coliform presence/absence), quick visual and physical inspection of product or water samples for a pass/fail sanitation verdict during a shift.

On-site sample inspection in unstructured settings: a demolition/renovation site, an older residential building, or a remote field location. The specialist inspects suspect bulk material samples (friability, layering), takes tape lifts/wipes for mold or lead dust, and screens with handheld XRF or field kits amid clutter, dust, variable lighting and unknown layouts.

tasks.label: Evaluate situations or make determinations when a worker has refused to work on the grounds that danger or potential harm exists.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Manufacturing plant: a machine operator refuses to run a press or conveyor claiming a guard is missing, an interlock is bypassed, or lockout/tagout was not performed. The technician interviews the worker and supervisor, observes the equipment and procedures, checks against the machine-guarding standard and the plant's LOTO program, and issues a written determination as to whether an imminent danger exists and what corrective action or return-to-work condition applies.

Construction or industrial contractor site: a worker refuses to climb scaffolding, enter a trench, or work at height citing inadequate fall protection, unshored soil, or unstable access. The technician reviews the competent-person inspection records, evaluates the conditions and applicable standards, consults the site superintendent, and makes and documents a determination on whether the refusal is justified.

Chemical, laboratory, or healthcare setting: a worker refuses a task citing an unfamiliar odor, suspected airborne exposure, respirator fit concerns, or a biological/infectious hazard. The technician reviews the SDS and exposure records, may direct or review air-monitoring or ventilation data, consults an industrial hygienist or safety specialist, and determines whether conditions exceed acceptable exposure limits before authorizing resumption.

Warehouse, transportation, or utility operations: a worker refuses to operate a forklift, truck, or aerial lift over a claimed mechanical defect, or refuses outdoor work citing extreme heat, cold, lightning, or air quality. The technician checks maintenance and inspection records or environmental readings, weighs them against company thresholds and regulatory guidance, and rules on the refusal.

Escalated or formal case: a refusal becomes a union grievance, joint health-and-safety-committee referral, or an OSHA Section 11(c)/whistleblower or state work-refusal complaint. The technician assembles the incident file, interview notes, monitoring data, and prior corrective actions, participates in the committee or investigation meeting, and prepares the written findings and recommended disposition largely from documentation and testimony.

tasks.label: Supply, operate, or maintain personal protective equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Point-of-use issuance of consumable PPE at a plant, hospital, lab or distribution center: worker requests gloves, safety glasses, earplugs, hearing protection, disposable coveralls, N95s or respirator cartridges; the tech verifies entitlement/size, hands the item over from the crib or a floor dispenser, and logs the issue against the employee and cost center.

Running the PPE stockroom: receiving vendor cartons on the dock, unpacking and shelving stock, keeping floor dispensers and lockers replenished, cycle counting, pulling multi-item PPE kits for a new hire or a job, and reordering low stock.

Scheduled servicing of reusable equipment fleets at a fixed service bench in the safety/equipment room: portable gas monitors put through daily bump tests, periodic calibration and charging with records retained; reusable facepieces, SCBA components and chemical suits run through cleaning/disinfection and functional leak/flow testing before being returned to service.

Hands-on respirator upkeep: collecting used half/full-face respirators and PAPRs, taking them apart, inspecting valves, straps, gaskets and headbands for cracks and wear, replacing filters, cartridges and PAPR batteries, reassembling, bagging and shelving each unit with a signed inspection record.

Field operation of PPE: donning respirator, chemical suit, harness and personal gas monitor to accompany a survey or confined-space entry; setting up and tending supplied-air/PAPR systems, ventilation and retrieval gear for the entry crew; inspecting harnesses, lanyards and SCBA in the field at plants, refineries and construction sites in heat, dust and weather.

Fitting PPE to people: quantitative/qualitative respirator fit testing on employees (seating the mask on the face, adjusting straps, running the protocol, coaching donning/doffing and user seal checks), plus sizing harnesses and hearing protection on the worker.

tasks.label: Train workers in safety procedures related to green jobs, such as the use of fall protection devices or maintenance of proper ventilation during wind turbine construction.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift toolbox talk / daily safety briefing delivered verbally to a wind farm construction crew at a site trailer or laydown yard: reviewing the day's fall-protection requirements (100% tie-off, anchor points in the tower and nacelle), rescue-at-height plan, and weather stand-down limits, then answering crew questions and logging attendance.

Formal classroom or training-center session (company office, union hall, or utility training facility) covering green-job hazard topics — fall protection systems, tower confined-space entry and forced-air ventilation during welding/coating, lockout-tagout on turbine drivetrains — using slides, written materials, quizzes, and issuing training records/certifications.

Hands-on instruction at a training tower, mock-up, or on the actual structure: showing workers how to inspect and don a full-body harness, connect self-retracting lifelines and vertical fall-arrest systems on tower ladders, and observing each trainee perform the procedure while correcting technique and confirming competency.

Rooftop or ground-mount solar installation site: instructing installers on roof-edge fall protection (anchors, guardrails, personal fall arrest), ladder safety, and PPE selection, adapting the briefing to that day's roof pitch, access route, and crew mix, including Spanish-language or bilingual delivery.

New-hire orientation and periodic refresher training for green-energy contractors — energy-storage/battery hazards, arc flash, ventilation and respiratory protection during confined-space work — including verifying comprehension, remediating workers who fail, and documenting completion for OSHA/GWO recordkeeping and client audits.

tasks.label: Test workplaces for environmental hazards, such as exposure to radiation, chemical or biological hazards, or excessive noise.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Personal/media-based exposure sampling at a manufacturing or processing plant (also covers biological and water sampling): pre-calibrate pumps with a flow calibrator, clip sampling cassettes/sorbent tubes into workers' breathing zones and fit noise dosimeters at shift start, observe tasks, retrieve and re-calibrate at shift end, seal/label media, take Legionella water or surface-swab samples where required, and ship under chain of custody to the lab.

Routine fixed-route area monitoring round inside an industrial plant, refinery, utility or wastewater facility: walk a set circuit with direct-reading instruments (LEL/H2S/CO/O2, PID for VOCs), thermal camera and sound level/ultrasonic instrument, record readings at defined stations, flag exceedances and note leak locations, and log results into the site's monitoring record.

Pre-entry and task-specific atmospheric testing at an industrial or municipal facility: bump-test/zero the multi-gas meter, lower the sampling probe into a tank, vault, manhole or sewer at multiple depths, verify ventilation/purge, record the results on the confined-space or hot-work permit, and re-test periodically during the job.

Hazard testing on an active construction or field job site taken as found: respirable crystalline silica and welding-fume personal sampling on tradespeople during cutting/grinding/welding, noise and heat-stress readings amid moving equipment, mud, scaffolding and changing layout, with documentation for the contractor's exposure-assessment file.

Radiation protection survey at a nuclear station, accelerator, hospital or industrial radiography facility: dose-rate mapping of accessible areas with a survey meter along a defined route, contamination checks, and logging of readings against a facility map/report for posting and ALARA records.

Indoor environmental quality survey of an office building, school or hospital wing: room-by-room readings of CO2, temperature, relative humidity, CO and particulates against a floor plan, comparing occupied areas with ventilation performance, and compiling the readings into a report.
