tasks.label: Inspect fire suppression systems or portable fire systems to ensure proper working order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Monthly/periodic walk-round of portable fire extinguishers across a manufacturing plant or distribution warehouse: dozens to hundreds of units on wall brackets, posts and columns along aisles. For each unit the technician confirms it is in its designated place and unobstructed, reads the pressure gauge, checks pin/tamper seal, nameplate legibility and physical damage, hefts it for fullness, and logs the result (tag or electronic record).

Extinguisher round in an office, school, hospital or lab building: multi-floor route through occupied corridors, units in recessed glass-front cabinets or on brackets, some behind doors and up stairs/elevators; same presence/access/gauge/seal/condition checks plus documentation.

Riser, valve and fire-pump room check of the water-based suppression system: verify control valves are open, locked/supervised, read system and pump pressure gauges, check for leaks, corrosion and tampered supervisory switches, record readings.

Building-wide sprinkler head survey from floor level: inspect heads 15-30 ft overhead for paint, corrosion, loading, damage, missing escutcheons and correct orientation, and verify 18-inch storage clearance below deflectors throughout racked storage areas.

Special-hazard suppression system checks: commercial kitchen wet-chemical hood systems (nozzle blow-off caps, fusible links, cylinder gauge, manual pull station), clean-agent rooms (cylinder pressure and weight, hoses, detectors), paint-booth dry chemical and mobile-equipment systems; usually requires ladder access and reaching over/behind cooking or process equipment.

Field and mobile assets: extinguishers mounted in fleet truck cabs, on forklifts and heavy equipment, at construction sites, laydown yards and remote well pads; uneven ground, weather, layouts that change weekly, units inside cabs, brackets or weather enclosures.

tasks.label: Verify availability or monitor use of safety equipment, such as hearing protection or respirators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine walk-through of a manufacturing/processing plant floor during production: the technician observes whether workers in posted zones are wearing required hearing protection, respirators, eye and head protection, notes non-compliance by area/crew, coaches workers on the spot, and logs observations for the compliance record. Fixed plant layout, employer-controlled premises, running machinery.

Checking PPE supply points across a facility: earplug and glove dispensers, respirator/cartridge cabinets, spare filter stock in the PPE crib or storeroom, plus stations such as eyewash and extinguishers — confirming each is present, stocked to par level, unexpired, and not blocked; flagging restock needs.

Hands-on inspection of individual respirators in the respiratory protection program: pick up each assigned half-mask/PAPR, check facepiece pliability, straps, inhalation/exhalation valves, correct cartridge type and expiration date, cleanliness and sanitary storage; confirm each enrolled worker has a serviceable unit available.

Field/jobsite walk at a construction site, roadwork zone, abatement job, or client site being surveyed: verify hard hats, hearing protection and task-appropriate respirators are stocked in the gang box/trailer and are actually being used by trades; layout changes daily, weather, uneven ground, multiple employers on site.

Pre-task verification for a high-hazard job inside a plant: before confined-space entry, hot work, or a dusty/chemical task, confirm SCBA or air-purifying respirators, calibrated/bump-tested gas monitors, and harnesses are on hand, serviceable, and correctly donned (including watching a user seal check) before work is authorized.

instances.label: Pre- and post-survey calibration of personal air sampling pumps in the IH office, plant safety office, or field trailer: pump connected by flexible tubing to a representative sampling train (cassette or sorbent tube) and to a primary/secondary flow standard, flow adjusted to the target (e.g., 2.0 L/min) within ±5%, readings documented on a calibration log.

Laboratory bench work in an industrial hygiene / gravimetric lab: verifying and calibrating the analytical microbalance with reference masses, conditioning and pre-/post-weighing filter media used for sampling, preparing calibration standards and setting up analytical instruments for sample analysis, with QC documentation.

instances.label: Baseline hazard survey of newly installed 'green' process equipment inside an industrial or utility facility (biogas/biomass boiler, CO2-capture skid, solvent-recovery or recycling line, electric kiln). Exposure-sampling campaign around a newly introduced green product or process (bio-based solvent, low-VOC adhesive, green cleaning chemical, new coating step): calibrate personal sampling pumps, fit sampling trains to workers' breathing zones, change media during the shift, take bulk and surface wipe samples, record task timing, and package samples with chain-of-custody for the lab. Documentation-and-inventory data gathering on newly procured green equipment/products: request SDSs, manuals and manufacturer test reports from vendors, go to the machine to record nameplate, voltage, refrigerant/battery chemistry and label data, complete the hazard-assessment/JHA form, and interview the operators about how the item is actually used.

Field data collection at an outdoor renewable installation being commissioned or built — new solar array and inverters, battery-storage container, EV charger bank, wind turbine base, or RNG/digester skid. Technician walks as-found terrain taking thermal scans of panels/inverters/battery racks, gas readings near enclosures and digesters, heat-stress/weather readings, and photographs fall, electrical, trip and housekeeping hazards.

Consultant, insurer or municipal technician visiting varied small client premises (school, restaurant, small shop, apartment building, contractor yard) that installed new green equipment — heat pumps, e-bike/battery charging rooms, composting, solar+storage, green cleaning program. Walkthrough with handheld IAQ/CO/CO2/VOC meters and a thermal camera, checklist and photos, occupants present, layout different at every site.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-installation ambient IAQ verification survey in a newly completed or renovated institution-controlled building (office, school, clinic): technician walks a prescribed set of rooms with calibrated multi-parameter meters (CO2, CO, PM, TVOC, temperature, RH), logs breathing-zone readings at set locations and times, compares results to ASHRAE 62.1/OSHA criteria, and writes a compliance report. No mechanical adjustment is made.

Ventilation-rate verification testing of a newly installed system in a finished commercial/institutional building: measuring delivered airflow at supply and return outlets (flow hood or anemometer traverse at ceiling diffusers and grilles, often from a ladder) and outdoor-air intake flow at the air handler, computing cfm/person ventilation rates against design and ASHRAE 62.1, and documenting. Testing only; corrections referred to the mechanical contractor.

Performance verification of newly installed local exhaust ventilation or containment hoods in a plant or laboratory: face/capture velocity traverse grids at hood openings with a thermal anemometer, checking readings against ACGIH/ASHRAE 110 criteria, and documenting pass/fail for each hood. Institution-controlled facility with standard equipment.

Full test-and-balance at commissioning of a newly installed HVAC system in a commercial building still under construction: ladder work with a flow hood at dozens of diffusers amid other trades and debris, adjusting balancing dampers above ceilings and at VAV boxes, changing fan speed/sheaves or VFD settings in the mechanical room, iterating until each zone is within tolerance, and issuing a NEBB-style balance report.

Verification of a newly installed HVAC system in a private home or small tenant space: measuring register airflow and total external static pressure, checking duct runs in attics/crawlspaces, combustion-safety and CO testing, adjusting registers or manual dampers, and advising the homeowner/occupant.

instances.label: Phase II subsurface soil sampling on an abandoned industrial parcel: advancing hand-auger or direct-push borings at grid/targeted locations amid asphalt, fill, rubble and brush; collecting depth-discrete soil into laboratory jars and VOC vials, screening headspace with a PID, writing boring logs, labeling and completing chain-of-custody.

Groundwater sampling from monitoring wells at the site: unlocking/opening well caps, gauging depth to water, deploying pump and tubing, low-flow purging while logging field parameters through a flow-through cell, filling and preserving bottles, decontaminating equipment, and logging the data.

Parcel-scale reconnaissance and documentation of a brownfield: walking/overflying the property to photograph and map conditions, GPS-locate features, record stressed vegetation, staining, fill areas and drum caches, and capture aerial imagery or geophysical (magnetometer) coverage for buried tanks/debris.

Close-in screening and inventory work at site features: handheld PID/FID readings at openings and excavations, XRF surface metals screening, radiation screening, drum and container inventory and label reads, all at scattered, unmapped points among debris and vegetation.

Air, soil-gas and landfill-gas data collection: perimeter and work-zone dust/VOC monitoring during intrusive work, surface methane/landfill gas emission surveys over covered fill areas, and grid-based ambient gas concentration mapping across the site.

Surface water and sediment data for ecological risk: grab water samples and field parameters (pH, DO, conductivity, turbidity) from on-site or adjacent ponds, ditches and streams, plus shallow sediment samples and habitat observations along banks.

Hazardous building materials and waste survey inside derelict on-site structures: bulk asbestos samples from insulation and flooring, lead paint chip/XRF readings, surface wipe samples, and sampling/inventory of abandoned drums and containers in dark, cluttered interiors.

tasks.label: Perform tests to identify any potential hazards related to recycled products used at green building sites.

instances.label: Active green-building jobsite: technician walks the site and screens delivered or installed recycled-content and salvaged materials (reclaimed lumber and trim with old coatings, recycled-content gypsum board, crushed-concrete aggregate, recycled rubber/carpet) with handheld instruments — XRF gun for lead/heavy metals, moisture meter, PID/formaldehyde monitor — taking dozens of readings on varied surfaces and orientations amid other trades, dust, clutter and weather.

Collecting physical samples on the jobsite for laboratory confirmation: chipping coating from salvaged coated wood, cutting pieces of recycled gypsum, recycled rubber flooring or suspect reclaimed pipe/board insulation, bagging and labeling each, recording location and material description, completing chain-of-custody forms and packing the cooler for shipment to an accredited lab.

Personal exposure monitoring of workers who cut, grind or install recycled products: calibrating pumps, fitting pump/cyclone/cassette trains on individual workers in their breathing zone, observing and logging their tasks over the shift, then removing and submitting the media.

Area/task-based characterization of dust and vapor released by a recycled product during installation: siting area sampling trains or direct-reading dust/VOC monitors near the operation, running them through the activity, logging conditions, and producing quantitative concentration data for the material.

Laboratory phase at the accredited testing lab: prepping and analyzing the collected material and air samples — grinding/digesting or pelletizing bulk material, gravimetric filter weighing, XRF/ICP for metals, micro-chamber or chamber VOC/formaldehyde emission testing by TD-GC/MS, microscopy for fibers — with QC checks and reported results.

Testing at the supplier's recycled-materials facility, recycler yard or prefab shop before delivery: sampling incoming lots of recycled aggregate, recycled wood chips or recycled insulation on a fixed-layout industrial site and checking them for contaminants such as treated/painted wood, metals, gypsum or asbestos-containing debris.

tasks.label: Examine practices at green building sites to determine whether adherence to green building standards alters risks to workers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Evaluative walkthrough of an active LEED/green-certified new-construction site: navigate an unfinished multi-story building with debris, ladders, scaffolds and changing layout while trades work; observe how crews apply spray polyurethane foam, install rooftop PV, cut recycled-content materials, apply low-VOC finishes and sort waste; question foremen; compare observed practices to green-standard credit requirements and OSHA rules; write findings on whether the green practices raise or lower worker risk.

Routine documented hazard/condition round on the same active green jobsite: walk the floors on a repeating route, photograph and log observable site conditions and work-practice compliance (openings, drop-offs, housekeeping, PPE use, active equipment, wet/slippery areas), tag items to locations on the floor plan, and hand the documented observations to the safety specialist for analysis.

Instrumented exposure assessment during one specific green practice: carry and set up direct-reading instruments and personal sampling pumps (PID/VOC, respirable dust and silica, noise dosimeter, WBGT heat monitor) on workers spraying foam insulation, cutting recycled masonry, or installing a rooftop array; follow the operation for its duration, record readings, and compare against exposure limits to judge whether the green practice changes exposure risk.

Green retrofit of an occupied existing building (deep energy retrofit, attic/crawlspace insulation, envelope air sealing, HVAC and window replacement): examine crew practices in confined, poorly ventilated and cluttered spaces reached by ladders and hatches, assess whether the tightened envelope and new materials create new hazards for the installers, and report findings.

Post-construction commissioning/occupancy walkthrough of a completed green facility (LEED office, hospital, school or lab): take indoor air quality, ventilation, lighting and thermal readings along a route, inspect maintenance access to rooftop PV, high-bay daylighting and mechanical rooms, and determine whether green design features alter risks to operations and maintenance staff.

sources.system: Spot quadruped with FieldAI Field Foundation Models
sources.title: Case Study: How FieldAI and Boston Dynamics Made Autonomy Practical on Construction Sites
sources.claim: FieldAI's Field Foundation Models on Boston Dynamics Spot are deployed on live commercial construction sites in Asia, Europe and North America, navigating changing sites with no prior maps or preplanned routes and surfacing observable safety-related site conditions in a single job walk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous jobsite inspection and documentation. It transfers to the documentation portion of examining site practices because it occurs in the same unstructured active-construction environment and its outputs are exactly the observable conditions and PPE/work-practice items a technician logs on a hazard round; it does not, however, produce an evaluative determination about green-standard adherence.

sources.claim: Turner Construction runs Spot on DroneDeploy-mapped autonomous routes for daily 360-degree walkthroughs of data-center construction sites, with missions scheduled remotely and typically run overnight when no workers are present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous progress/condition capture on construction sites. It shows robotic capture is routine and reliable in this environment, but the capture is scheduled when crews are absent, so it does not substantiate observing workers' practices in progress.

sources.title: DroneDeploy Revolutionizes Safety Risk Detection in Construction with Launch of Safety AI
sources.claim: DroneDeploy's Safety AI automatically analyzes construction reality-capture imagery (including imagery captured by ground robots) to flag visible OSHA safety risks, rank them by severity and alert the safety team; it is a software analysis layer, not a robot, and is positioned as an add-on that informs human safety staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated OSHA hazard flagging from jobsite imagery. Combined with robotic capture it substantiates producing a documented hazard-observation log at a construction site; it gives no evidence of evaluating green building standard adherence, exposures, or comparative risk.

sources.claim: A midstream oil and gas plant deployed Spot with FLIR MUVE C360 gas detection, thermal camera and the Enhanced Autonomy Payload to run autonomous inspection routes across the whole facility, including combustible-gas monitoring, docking to recharge between routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrument-carrying inspection rounds in an industrial facility. It transfers only to fixed-route ambient measurement inside a controlled facility; it does not substantiate personal breathing-zone sampling on workers or following a mobile crew on a construction site.

sources.claim: ANYbotics offers a commercial gas leak and presence detection ... inspection quadruped, combining modular gas detectors and acoustic imaging to locate leaks and measure ambient gas concentrations during autonomous inspections of industrial plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous atmospheric monitoring rounds in structured industrial facilities. Shows robots can gather gas readings unattended, but the deployments are fixed-asset routes in controlled plants, not exposure assessment of workers performing a specific construction practice.

tasks.label: Assess individuals' degree of drug dependency by collecting and analyzing urine samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine scheduled or random unobserved collection at an outpatient SUD clinic or opioid treatment program: counselor verifies client identity, secures the restroom (water shut off, bluing agent, no bags/coats), hands over a sealed temperature-strip specimen cup, receives the warm specimen within ~4 minutes, checks temperature/volume/color for validity, runs a 10-12 panel instant test cup, reads it at the timed interval, documents results in the EHR, and reviews unexpected positives with the client.

Direct-observed collection at an OTP, drug court or program with prior tampering: a same-gender staff member accompanies the client into the restroom and watches the urine leave the body, then handles, seals and tests the specimen as above; includes managing client resistance, dignity/safety issues, and documentation of the observation.

Residential or inpatient treatment program: random or return-from-pass collection, specimen labeled and initialed in the client's presence, security seal applied, chain-of-custody form completed, specimen bagged and staged for the lab courier; counselor later reviews the confirmatory GC-MS/LC-MS report and quantitative levels (e.g., creatinine-normalized trends) to gauge pattern and degree of use.

Field or community setting: home visit, sober-living house, shelter, jail/mobile outreach van; collection in a bathroom the program does not control, with improvised privacy and security, cooler transport of the specimen, and on-the-spot judgment about specimen integrity.

Problem specimen handling: temperature out of range, dilute/adulterated/substituted sample, or a client with 'shy bladder' who cannot void; counselor re-collects under monitored hydration protocol, may switch to observed collection, documents the irregularity, and escalates to supervisor, court, or prescriber.

instances.label: Loan out standard supportive technology from a disability-services office or AT lending library: pull a stocked laptop, tablet, digital recorder, smartpen or portable charger from the storage cabinet, verify it is charged and working, check it out to the student and hand it over, then take it back and re-stock it at return. Off-the-shelf items held in quantity; indoor office/library setting.

Fit and set up specialized assistive technology with the student present: pair an FM/remote-microphone system with hearing aids and clip the transmitter on an instructor, install and configure screen-reader or magnification software, adjust a CCTV/video magnifier, mount and position an adaptive keyboard, switch, slant board or adapted seating at the student's desk, and test it with the student until it works for them. Classroom, testing room or office.

Escort a student who has low vision or uses a wheelchair/walker but transfers and self-propels independently: walk or roll with them along crowded corridors, take the elevator, badge or hold open heavy doors, unlock the accessible restroom, and get them to the restroom, testing center or classroom and back. Institution-controlled school or campus building.

Hands-on physical assistance with facility access for a student with significant physical or multiple disabilities: push a manual wheelchair, steady a student with unsteady gait, maneuver the chair inside a restroom stall, assist with transfer, clothing or hygiene, or provide close supervision for a student who needs prompting. School restroom and adjacent corridor.

Fetch and deliver equipment or accommodation materials to where the student is: carry a loaner laptop with screen reader, braille or large-print materials, an FM transmitter or a magnifier from the office to a classroom, lab or proctored testing room in another building across campus, hand it to the student, and retrieve it afterwards.

Provide devices and facility-access assistance off-campus: at a work-based-learning or internship site, on a community field trip, or at a student's home — carry and set up the device in an unfamiliar building, guide the student through an entrance, elevator or restroom that no one keeps to a standard, and work around whatever is found there.

instances.label: Unannounced field home visit to a probationer's residence: officer drives to a private address in the caseload area, knocks, is admitted by the client or a household member, verifies who lives there, observes living conditions and looks for contraband, weapons or unapproved persons in plain view, interviews client and family, documents the contact. Neighborhoods, dwelling types, pets, stairs and personal-safety risks vary site to site.

Curfew / home-detention compliance check at the residence, often evening or night: officer travels to the home, makes face-to-face contact to confirm the client is physically present during curfew hours, visually inspects the ankle bracelet strap and charging for tampering, notes who else is present, and logs the check or leaves a notice when no one answers.

Field visit to a workplace or school: officer travels to the employer's premises or the school office, presents credentials at reception, meets a supervisor, HR contact or counselor to verify employment/attendance and behavior, has a brief private contact with the client, records the verification. Premises are institutionally controlled but layouts and gatekeeping differ by site.

Office reporting appointment centered on electronic monitoring equipment: officer fits or removes a GPS/RF ankle device on the seated client's leg, sizes and tightens the strap, checks fiber-optic/tamper integrity, pairs and tests the beacon or base unit, downloads and verifies data, explains conditions and obtains signatures in a probation department interview room.

Drug and alcohol testing as part of a supervision contact: officer administers a handheld breathalyzer or conducts an observed urine collection at the office restroom or during a field visit, reads and records the instant result, seals and labels the specimen for the lab, and confronts or documents a positive result.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 / K7 Autonomous Security Robots
sources.title: Knightscope Unveils the All-New K7 Autonomous Security Robot
sources.claim: Knightscope's autonomous security robots patrol and monitor fixed premises (parking structures, campuses, fence lines, logistics yards) without human driving, relaying video and sensor data to a remote operations center; they observe only and do not knock, enter dwellings, interview occupants, or manipulate objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous patrol and compliance monitoring of premises. It is the closest deployed analogue to a field compliance check, but it covers only institutionally controlled property the client owns and offers no door contact, no identity verification of a person inside a private home, no interviewing and no equipment inspection, so it does not transfer to probation field supervision.

sources.title: Serve Robotics Autonomous Sidewalk Delivery (NVIDIA case study)
sources.claim: Serve Robotics operates a large fleet of autonomous sidewalk delivery robots that navigate public streets and sidewalks in US cities and complete curbside hand-offs of goods; the robots carry items and do not interact with, verify, or assess people at an address.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous travel to a residential address through unstructured public space. This substantiates only the transit leg of a field visit; the robot cannot climb steps, knock, gain admittance, observe a dwelling's interior or hold an interview, so it cannot complete a home or curfew check.

sources.title: NEO humanoid designed for household use, available for preorder - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The leading in-home humanoid intended for US households relies on scheduled remote human teleoperators for tasks it has not learned, so in-home mobile manipulation and interaction of this kind is not autonomous as of 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose work inside private homes. It shows the only commercially offered in-home humanoid depends on remote human control for unfamiliar tasks, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment for home visits or curfew checks.

sources.title: Digit Deployed at GXO in Historic Humanoid RAAS Agreement
sources.claim: The most-deployed commercial humanoid performs repetitive tote handling inside a controlled contract-logistics warehouse under a robotics-as-a-service contract; its demonstrated autonomous manipulation is limited to rigid, standardized containers presented in fixed locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation in a work facility. It marks the frontier of deployed humanoid manipulation — rigid totes in a controlled aisle — far below the compliance and dexterity needed to fit a tamper-proof ankle strap on a person's leg or handle an observed specimen collection, so capability does not transfer.

sources.title: Ava Mobile Telepresence as a Service | Webex App Hub
sources.claim: Enterprise telepresence robots navigate offices and factories autonomously but exist to carry a remote human's video presence; the substantive interaction, judgment and conversation are performed by the remote person, not the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote presence at a work site for a meeting or verification. Navigation is autonomous but the verification, interviewing and judgment come from a continuously connected human operator, which counts as teleoperation, so it cannot complete a workplace or school verification visit.

sources.title: Learning garment manipulation policies toward robot-assisted dressing | Science Robotics
sources.claim: Robotic manipulation of garments and straps directly on a human body remains a research problem studied in laboratory settings; no deployed system fastens or removes a device on a person's limb at working reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: safe robot manipulation of straps and fabric on a human limb, the physical core of fitting an EM ankle device. The evidence is laboratory-stage only, so it cannot substantiate completion even in a purpose-built cell.

tasks.label: Investigate alleged parole violations, using interviews, surveillance, and search and seizure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Unannounced field/home visit to a parolee's residence after an alleged violation (missed curfew, EM alert, new allegation): officer knocks, interviews the parolee and household members, observes living conditions and plain-view contraband, verifies who is living there, and documents observations for a violation report. Private home, unpredictable layout, possibly hostile or intoxicated occupants, pets, children.

Condition-of-supervision search and seizure: officer (usually with police backup) searches the parolee's person, vehicle, or residence — opening drawers, closets, bags, checking under mattresses and in vehicles — locates drugs, paraphernalia, weapons, or unauthorized phones, seizes and bags the items, maintains chain of custody, and may effect a hold/arrest.

Office-based violation interview: parolee is summoned to the probation/parole office after a positive drug test, missed report, or law-enforcement contact; officer confronts them with the evidence, takes a statement, observes demeanor, collects an observed urine sample, and decides on a sanction or violation filing.

Collateral investigation: phone and in-person interviews with employers, treatment providers, family, victims, and arresting officers; verification of employment and residence; review of GPS/electronic-monitoring logs, arrest reports, and lab results; writing the investigative findings into a violation report or affidavit.

Community surveillance: covert or semi-covert observation of a residence, workplace, or known associate's address at odd hours to verify where the parolee actually sleeps, whether curfew is kept, whether prohibited associates or vehicles are present; noting plates, times, and photographs for the file.

sources.title: Autonomous Security Robots | Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 is a commercially deployed autonomous security robot that patrols fixed routes on commercial properties and some public spaces, providing presence, video and sensor streaming to a remote monitoring console; it has no manipulator and does not conduct interviews, searches, or investigative determinations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: security patrol and surveillance. It is the closest fielded analogue to the surveillance element of parole investigation, but it patrols a pre-mapped fixed property route and streams video to human monitors; it cannot conduct targeted observation of a named individual, interview anyone, search property, or produce an investigative finding.

sources.developer: Knightscope / New York City Police Department
sources.title: Police Robots: What They Are & How They're Used | Built In
sources.claim: A K5 robot was trialed by the NYPD to patrol and surveil a subway station, showing the ceiling of fielded police-adjacent robot surveillance: presence and video in an institution-controlled indoor space, with humans doing all interpretation and enforcement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: law-enforcement patrol/surveillance. Shows deployed robotic surveillance is limited to stationary-route video presence in a controlled facility, not covert observation of a specific supervisee or evidence collection.

sources.title: Skydio DFR Command Makes Drone as First Responder Programs a Reality for Jurisdictions of All Sizes
sources.claim: Skydio's Drone-as-First-Responder systems fly dock-launched routes with automated route suggestion and obstacle avoidance for police agencies, but flights are supervised by a remote pilot who directs the camera and interprets the imagery; the aircraft is a camera platform, not an investigator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial police surveillance of an address or incident. Flight autonomy exists, but a remote pilot in command supervises each mission and humans make all identification and violation determinations, so it cannot autonomously complete a parole surveillance assignment end to end.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: The most advanced home-capable humanoid shipping to consumers relies on scheduled remote human operators for complex manipulation in real houses, so no fielded robot can autonomously search a residence's drawers, closets and vehicles for contraband at investigator quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation and object search inside an unmodified private home. Since even household tidying requires teleoperation, the far harder task of a lawful contraband search and seizure in a stranger's home is unsupported.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Random observed urine screen at the probation/parole office: officer pulls a client selected by the random color-code system, verifies ID, hands over a collection cup, directly observes the void (same-gender staff), checks the temperature/validity strip, reads an instant multi-panel cup, records the result, and seals and labels positives for lab confirmation under chain of custody.

Breath alcohol test administered at an office check-in or a scheduled/daily sobriety-program appointment: officer verifies identity, fits a fresh mouthpiece on a handheld or desktop breath tester, instructs the client to blow until a valid sample registers, reads BAC, and logs the result to the case file.

Drug test administered during an unannounced field visit at the offender's home or workplace: officer carries a portable instant urine cup or oral-fluid swab device, verifies identity, collects the specimen on the spot (a home bathroom, a car, a job site), reads or bags the sample, and documents it.

Portable breath alcohol test administered in the field: at the client's residence during a home visit, at a job site, or at a treatment/halfway-house site, often with an uncooperative or intoxicated client and variable conditions.

Testing inside an institution the agency or a partner controls: jail/prison release unit, residential reentry center, day reporting center, or treatment program, where staff conduct observed urine collections in a designated testing room on a fixed schedule and log results.

Specialty specimen collection: cutting a chain-of-custody hair sample from the client's head, applying or removing a sweat patch (skin prep, adhesive patch on arm/back), or fitting and checking a transdermal alcohol ankle monitor.

sources.title: About | Automated Breathalyzer Kiosk

sources.title: Courts and Corrections Agencies Ramp Up Use of AB Kiosk Automated Systems (Business Wire)
sources.claim: AB Kiosk systems are deployed by probation departments and sheriff's offices in nine states (ten South Dakota counties, Marion County IN, San Patricio County TX) and had conducted more than 550,000 probation check-ins and breathalyzer tests as of March 2022; the kiosk verifies identity biometrically, videos the test, and files the result automatically.

sources.title: Automated probation check-ins, alcohol monitoring arrives in South Texas (Corrections1)
sources.claim: Trade press reports continued deployment of the kiosk for probation check-ins and alcohol screening at a Texas community supervision department, at roughly 30 screenings per hour.

sources.system: Thermo Scientific automated drugs-of-abuse testing solution (Indiko/Indiko Plus analyzers with Paracelsus / Drug Court Case Management software)
sources.title: Automated Drug Testing | Thermo Fisher Scientific
sources.claim: Commercial automated drugs-of-abuse testing systems run the laboratory side of a court-ordered drug test on barcoded specimens: chain-of-custody tracking, specimen testing, and electronic result reporting into drug-court case management software.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, laboratory half: once the specimen is presented barcoded in a rack (as a purpose-built setting presents work), the instrument performs the validity and drug-panel testing and reporting that constitute the accepted output of the officer's screen.

sources.title: Drugs of Abuse Testing | Thermo Fisher Scientific
sources.claim: Bench-top clinical chemistry analyzers screen urine for drugs of abuse fully automatically at 120-190 samples per hour, with specimens loadable in any order.
sources.transferJustification: Same task's analytic step: the immunoassay drug panel and specimen-validity chemistry that produce the screen result the officer records.

sources.developer: University of Southern Denmark / Lifeline Robotics collaborators
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous force-controlled swab robot took naso-/oropharyngeal specimens from 52 suspected COVID-19 patients in two clinical studies, with results matching manual sampling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous collection of a biological specimen from a seated cooperative human at a fixed sampling station; it shows machine specimen-taking only with a cooperative subject at a purpose-built station, not observed urine collection from a client with an incentive to defeat the test, nor hair/patch handling.

tasks.label: Demonstrate use and care of equipment for tenant use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Move-in orientation in a supportive/transitional housing apartment: the assistant walks a new tenant through operating and caring for the unit's equipment — stove/oven burners and knobs, refrigerator settings, thermostat, garbage disposal, testing the smoke/CO detector — including wiping the stovetop, cleaning the fridge, and what not to put down the disposal; answers the tenant's questions, has the tenant try each item, and signs off on the orientation checklist.

Shared laundry room in a program-operated residential building: assistant shows a tenant how to load the washer, measure and add detergent, select the cycle, operate the card/coin payment, transfer to the dryer, clean the lint trap, and wipe down the machine; tenant practices under supervision.

Agency-operated group home for residents with intellectual/developmental disabilities: assistant demonstrates kitchen and household equipment (microwave, dishwasher, vacuum, mop/bucket, iron) to one or more residents, using repeated hands-on prompting, safety cautions, and cleaning/maintenance steps, adapting pace and prompts to each resident's ability.

Tenant's own unit (independent living / home-based case management): assistant demonstrates use and care of adaptive or durable medical equipment — wheelchair folding, brakes and cushion cleaning, walker height and tips, shower chair/transfer bench setup, hospital bed controls, nebulizer or oxygen concentrator filter cleaning and charging — then watches tenant and family member practice.

Shelter / SRO / transitional facility unit: assistant demonstrates safety and building equipment — fire extinguisher handling, space heater and window AC safe operation and filter cleaning, radiator valve, intercom/key fob, first-aid kit — with emphasis on hazards and required tenant upkeep, documenting the safety orientation.

sources.title: Introducing Helix 02: Full-Body Autonomy
sources.claim: Figure's Helix 02 humanoid autonomously performs long-horizon appliance manipulation (unloading and reloading a dishwasher) in a full-sized ... with no human intervention, in developer-controlled kitchen environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating a household appliance. It shows a robot can run an appliance sequence autonomously, but the cited system only performs the chore; there is no evidence it instructs a person in the equipment's use and care, which is the output this task requires.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization (π0.5)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 controls a mobile manipulator to perform multi-step household chores (cleaning kitchens/bedrooms, wiping spills, placing dishes) in homes not seen in training.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household object manipulation and cleaning in unseen homes. It substantiates some physical handling of household items but not the demonstration-and-instruction of equipment use and care to a tenant, and reliability is research-demo level.

sources.title: TeachBot — project page
sources.claim: TeachBot is an autonomous robotic ... at a fixed workstation that teaches human workers how to use a robot, combining spoken/graphical lectures with physical demonstration of its own arm movements and learner touch interaction; it is a research prototype evaluated in a user study.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot autonomously instructing a person in equipment use. Transfer is limited: the only 'equipment' TeachBot demonstrates is its own arm at a fixed station; it does not operate external appliances or assistive devices, nor teach cleaning/maintenance, so it does not substantiate completing this task's instances.

sources.claim: Socially assistive robots have autonomously run instructional group sessions (upper-body exercise, Bingo) with residents inside long-term care facilities, guiding participants through repetitions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously delivering an instructional session to residents in a care facility. It covers the social/instructional side only — these robots have no manipulators and cannot operate a stove, washer, or wheelchair or show how to clean and maintain it.

instances.label: Ride-only trip for an independent, ambulatory adult client (e.g., a parent in a family-support program, a client without a car): assistant picks the client up curbside at a home or shelter in a metro area, drives surface streets/freeway to a clinic, benefits office or job interview, drops off, and returns later for the pickup. Client boards, buckles, and walks in unaided; no in-building escort needed.

Client with a mobility impairment (walker, rollator, manual or power wheelchair, oxygen): assistant walks the client from the door of the residence to the agency vehicle, steadies transfer into the seat, folds and stows the walker or operates the lift/ramp and secures the wheelchair with tie-downs, drives, then unloads and escorts the client inside to check-in and back home.

Shopping trip for one or more clients of a group home or developmental-disability/mental-health day program: drive to a grocery or discount store, accompany clients through the aisles, prompt and coach item selection against a list and a budget, push/steer the cart, help at checkout with EBT or program funds, load bags, drive back and carry groceries in.

Transport requiring in-vehicle supervision and support: foster youth to a parental visitation or court date (child restraint, no unaccompanied minors allowed), or a behavioral-health/substance-use client to treatment intake or a probation appointment; the assistant monitors behavior, de-escalates agitation, keeps the client from leaving, and physically walks them in to ensure the appointment is kept.

Rural or small-town county-agency trip: 30-60 miles on two-lane highways, gravel roads and unmarked driveways to a specialty clinic or DSS office, in rain, snow or fog and outside any robotaxi service area; assistant drives the agency vehicle, makes multiple stops, and escorts the client in.

Roaming distribution in public places: standing or walking outside a grocery store, at a bus stop or transit entrance, park, or street festival, approaching passing pedestrians and handing them flyers about an upcoming clinic or benefit program. The leave-behind portion of canvassing: when nobody answers, tucking a flyer or door hanger into the door handle, screen door, or gate, or stuffing flyers into apartment mailbox banks and under doors, across dozens of dwellings.

Circuit of partner sites to drop off and restock printed materials: driving to clinics, WIC offices, food pantries, libraries, laundromats, barbershops and churches, carrying in boxes or stacks of brochures, refilling wall and counter display racks, removing outdated material, and leaving a stack with front-desk staff.

sources.claim: A humanoid service robot was given an autonomous behavior model for approaching non-cooperative pedestrians and handing them flyers, and the model was validated in a field experiment in a real shopping mall (a structured, institution-controlled public facility).

sources.system: Information-providing robot field trial (Satake et al.)
sources.developer: ATR Intelligent Robotics and Communication Laboratories
sources.title: Field trial of an information-providing robot in a shopping mall — IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: A mall service robot moved around handing over flyers to visitors and providing information, working 53.4 hours over 11 days ... major failure and operating autonomously 83.5% of the time (remote help mainly for speech recognition).

sources.title: Relay Robotics Releases New Hotel Delivery Robot That Offers Double the Capacity of Its Predecessor — Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Commercially deployed autonomous delivery robots travel hotel corridors and elevators to bring items from a front desk directly to individual guest-room doors, where the occupant retrieves the item; the fleet has completed over a million deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: door-to-door delivery of small items in an institution-controlled residential building. Carrying printed material to each dwelling door and offering it to the occupant uses the same navigation, door approach, announcement and hand-off, with a lighter payload.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Mobile manipulators are deployed in dozens of US hospitals performing autonomous point-to-point transport of small items (medications, supplies, specimens) between departments and staff, with hundreds of thousands of deliveries completed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior delivery of small items to fixed points and to staff in a health facility. Delivering bundles of brochures to clinic desks, units and racks is the same transport-and-handoff job with a lighter payload.

sources.developer: Academic research group on a commercially available mobile manipulator
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: An integrated mobile-manipulator system autonomously restocked supermarket shelves from stock, achieving 98% success over 724 pick-and-place events during overnight closed-door operation in a store.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing product onto retail shelving inside a structured facility. Refilling a brochure display rack is the same pick-from-stock, place-into-fixture operation with lighter items and comparable placement precision.

sources.title: Robots deployed for re-stocking shelves in convenient stores — GlobalSpec
sources.claim: A commercially deployed store robot autonomously restocks refrigerated beverage shelves in convenience stores, running around the clock in hundreds of stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine restocking of a display fixture in a human retail facility; refilling a brochure rack is the same repetitive place-into-fixture operation on lighter paper items.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels — Restaurant Technology News
sources.claim: Autonomous service robots are widely deployed in restaurants, cafes and hotels to carry items across the floor and present them to seated people at tables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bringing items to seated people in a structured venue. Distributing handout packets to attendees seated at a class is the same navigate-to-people-and-present-item operation.

sources.system: Serve Robotics Gen 3 sidewalk delivery robots
sources.title: Serve Robotics has deployed 2,000+ delivery robots across the U.S. — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Sidewalk delivery robots operate at SAE Level 4 on public sidewalks at fleet scale, but deliveries go to the specific customer who ordered and who comes out to the robot; they do not approach or hand printed material to arbitrary passers-by, nor go to residence doors.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the unstructured (E3) case: it establishes autonomous public-sidewalk navigation and handover to a pre-arranged recipient, not unsolicited distribution of documents to community members.

tasks.label: Perform basic diagnostic procedures, such as blood pressure screening, breast cancer screening, or communicable disease screening.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Blood pressure screening table at a community health fair, church hall, food pantry or senior center pop-up: CHW seats walk-up attendees, selects and applies the correct cuff, takes a reading, logs it on a paper/tablet form, and tells the person whether the value is elevated and whether to seek follow-up. Mixed ambulatory adult population, noisy shared room, no fixed clinical furniture.

Home visit to an enrolled chronic-disease client (hypertension/diabetes): CHW takes blood pressure and pulse (sometimes a finger-stick glucose) at the client's kitchen table or bedside, records the values for the care team, and compares against prior readings. Client may be elderly, frail, or have limited mobility; furniture, lighting and pets vary by household.

Communicable-disease screening during street/shelter/mobile-van outreach: CHW collects the specimen for an HIV/HCV rapid finger-stick or a COVID/flu swab (or draws/arranges a blood specimen for syphilis or hepatitis serology), reads or transmits the result, and links reactive clients to care. Outdoors or in a van, variable clients including unhoused people.

Screening station inside a community health center or FQHC: CHW rooms patients or runs a screening day, measuring blood pressure, pulse, height/weight/BMI and sometimes vision or hearing, and entering values into the EHR for the clinician.

Breast cancer screening activity at a clinic or mobile screening event: CHW teaches and observes breast self-examination, assists with or performs a clinical breast exam per program protocol, and documents findings/refers for mammography.

sources.title: Users — Pursuant Health
sources.claim: Pursuant Health operates over 4,600 self-service health screening kiosks in Walmart and CVS pharmacies; the kiosk is an FDA-cleared Class II medical device that measures blood pressure and weight and stores the data for the user with no staff operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same procedure as the CHW task's core element: an oscillometric cuff is inflated on the subject's upper arm under machine control and a screening blood-pressure value is produced, recorded and flagged for follow-up.

sources.system: Pursuant Health self-service blood pressure kiosk
sources.title: Collaborative study identifies method to make blood pressure monitoring more accessible (Emory News)
sources.claim: A JAMA Cardiology study analyzed ~1.3 million adults screened on Pursuant Health kiosks in Walmart/CVS stores in 49 states, treating the machine-collected readings as valid population blood-pressure screening data; the kiosks deliver over 2.5 million screenings per month.
sources.transferJustification: The cited use is exactly the task's purpose — community blood-pressure screening of walk-up members of the public, including under-resourced groups, with linkage to care.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Shows High Success Rates in Multicenter Trial (Clinical Lab Products)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed diagnostic venous blood draws on 1,633 patients in three outpatient phlebotomy departments in a published multicenter trial, with 94.5% first-stick success, 0.3% hemolysis and only mild adverse events.
sources.transferJustification: Blood-based communicable-disease screening (HIV, HCV, syphilis serology) is physically a diagnostic blood collection from the patient's arm; Aletta performs that exact collection step autonomously on unselected clinic patients.

sources.title: Aletta for Laboratory specialists — Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta operates alongside manual draw stations in phlebotomy departments, the patient starts the procedure, and one trained supervisor is intended to oversee up to three devices — i.e. autonomous operation with only occasional human oversight.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the limited-intervention condition for the blood-collection evidence used for communicable-disease screening.

sources.developer: Haddadin group (Technical University of Munich / Franka Emika collaborators)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: SR-NOCS, an autonomous force-controlled swab robot station, collected naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening specimens from 52 suspected patients in two clinical studies, including one in a public testing location in 2023, with results fully correlating with manual sampling and minimal supervision required.
sources.transferJustification: Respiratory-specimen collection for infectious-disease screening is the same physical procedure a CHW performs when swabbing clients for COVID/flu at an outreach testing site.

sources.title: iSono Health Introduces Wearable, Automated, Portable, FDA-Cleared Breast Ultrasound Platform (Imaging Technology News)
sources.claim: iSono Health's FDA-cleared ATUSA system commercially launched into primary care and OB/GYN offices; a wearable, hands-free accessory automatically acquires a full 3D whole-breast ultrasound volume in about two minutes per breast regardless of operator skill.
sources.transferJustification: Breast cancer screening: once the patient is positioned in the wearable cup the machine performs the whole-breast screening acquisition, substituting for the manual screening examination step, though a person must place the accessory.

sources.title: Your next breast exam could be performed by a robot (New Atlas)
sources.claim: A robotic breast-examination system (IRIS) using tactile sensing to detect lumps with clinician-like forces has been demonstrated only in laboratory/phantom studies presented at a robotics conference, not on screening patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the clinical-breast-exam element of the task; cited as a negative/limiting datapoint since the work is a laboratory demonstration rather than screening of patients.

tasks.label: Conduct home visits for pregnant women, newborn infants, or other high-risk individuals to monitor their progress or assess their needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Prenatal home visit to a pregnant client in her apartment or house: build rapport, review prenatal appointment adherence, administer depression/intimate-partner-violence screening, often take blood pressure or weight, teach warning signs and nutrition, note household conditions (food, utilities, other children, pets, clutter), and arrange referrals (WIC, transport, Medicaid) before leaving.

Postpartum/newborn visit in the family's home: observe the infant (feeding, cord/jaundice, weight if scale carried), physically inspect the sleep surface and crib for safe-sleep hazards, demonstrate techniques (swaddling, latch, bottle prep, car seat), assess maternal mood and bleeding/pain, restock supplies, and document.

Visit to a high-risk adult with chronic disease (hypertension, diabetes, CHF): take blood pressure and/or fingerstick glucose, inspect medication bottles and fill a pill organizer, check the refrigerator/pantry for diet and food security, review symptoms and appointments, assess home hazards, and log findings for the care team.

Visit to a frail elderly or disabled homebound client in an older, often cluttered home: walk through the home for fall and safety hazards, assess activities of daily living and social needs (heat, food, isolation), deliver supplies, coordinate services, and report changes in condition.

Outreach visit to a hard-to-reach client in unstable housing — shelter room, motel, transitional housing, or an unanswered door knock — under uncertain, sometimes unsafe conditions; engage the client, do a brief needs assessment on the spot, and re-schedule or leave information if no contact is made.

sources.developer: Radboud/Dutch hospital research team (IEEE RO-MAN/HRI conference paper)
sources.title: A Social Robot for Autonomous Health Data Acquisition Among Hospitalized Patients: An Exploratory Field Study | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: Pepper, a social robot, autonomously administered five structured health questionnaires to hospitalized patients in an exploratory field study; this is questionnaire data collection only, in a hospital ward, with no physical assessment, clinical judgment, or referral-making.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous structured health-data collection from patients. It is the closest demonstrated analogue to the interview portion of a home visit, but it was a research field study in an institution-controlled hospital ward covering fixed questionnaires only — it does not cover vitals, infant/home inspection, counseling, risk judgment, or referrals, so it cannot substantiate completion of a whole monitoring/assessment visit at any tier.

sources.title: Labrador Systems Announces First Business Customers of its Award-Winning Personal Assistive Robots
sources.claim: Labrador's Retriever is an autonomous mobile robot deployed in private homes and senior-living units, but it fetches and delivers objects; it performs no health assessment, screening, or client interview.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation and item transport inside private homes (E3). It shows in-home mobility is feasible, but the capability is object fetch-and-carry; it provides no evidence of taking vitals, inspecting an infant sleep space, assessing needs, or producing an accepted visit record, so it cannot substantiate this task.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed healthcare mobile manipulator, performs autonomous point-to-point logistics deliveries in hospitals; its deployments are explicitly non-patient-facing logistics, not patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside a structured human health facility (E2). It bounds the state of deployed healthcare robotics — supply logistics rather than patient monitoring or assessment — and therefore does not transfer to conducting a monitoring/assessment visit even in a structured facility.

sources.system: Humanoid sensing robot for cuffless blood pressure (Woo Soo Kim lab)
sources.title: Robots that can check your blood pressure | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: A university lab prototype humanoid measured blood pressure by placing fingertip sensors on a person's chest; this is a research demonstration of one sub-measurement, not a deployed assessment system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic vital-sign measurement, a sub-step of the screening portion of a home visit. Autonomy is not established and the work is a lab prototype covering one measurement, so it cannot support completion of a whole visit at any tier.

sources.title: 1X’s $20K Robot Targets US Homes in 2026, Aims to Reduce the ‘Creepy’ Factor
sources.claim: The only humanoid shipping into private US homes relies on human teleoperation for a substantial share of its behavior, so in-home humanoid capability is not autonomous as of 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose in-home humanoid manipulation and interaction. Because the shipped system is partly teleoperated, it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomously conducting an in-home assessment visit.

sources.title: Autonomous telepresence — Wikipedia
sources.claim: Home-care telepresence robots, the standard way remote clinicians 'visit' patients at home, have little or no autonomy ... depend on a remote human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote clinical home visits mediated by a mobile robot. The assessment is performed by a remote human driving the platform, i.e., continuous teleoperation, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of home monitoring visits.

Assist families to apply for social services, including Medicaid or Women, Infants, and Children (WIC).

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Administer immunizations or other basic preventive treatments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Community mass-vaccination clinic (flu/COVID/Tdap) run by a health department or FQHC in a borrowed indoor venue - church hall, community center, school gym, worksite. Adults and older teens queue, are screened for contraindications and consent, then receive an intramuscular deltoid injection from a prefilled syringe or a dose drawn from a vial; worker swabs, injects, bandages, documents in the immunization registry, and monitors for reactions.

Walk-in immunization at a fixed clinic site - FQHC, public health department clinic, shelter or refugee-resettlement clinic exam room. Adult clients, mixed vaccines (flu, hep B, Tdap, COVID), cold-chain handling, arm exposure varies with clothing and body habitus, charting in the EHR/registry.

Pediatric and adolescent immunization at school-located clinics, WIC offices, daycare or back-to-school events: infants and young children needing positioning, comfort or restraint by a caregiver, thigh or deltoid injections, sometimes two or three injections in one visit, plus parental consent handling.

Outdoor or mobile outreach vaccination - health-fair tent in a park, mobile van at a farmworker camp or encampment, parking-lot pop-up. Variable weather and lighting, no fixed layout, clients standing or seated on folding chairs, crowds and interruptions, supplies carried in coolers.

Home visit to a homebound or frail client (elderly, disabled, post-discharge): vaccinate or give another basic preventive treatment in a living room or bedroom, working around furniture, pets, poor lighting, a recliner or bed, stiff or contracted arms, and clients who need coaxing.

Non-injection basic preventive treatments: applying fluoride varnish to preschoolers' teeth at a Head Start or WIC site, placing and reading a TB skin test, dispensing or administering deworming or vitamin doses, treating head lice, or administering intranasal naloxone during outreach.

sources.developer: Cobionix / University of Waterloo Velocity incubator
sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection | Waterloo News
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform performed what was reported as the first autonomous robotic intramuscular ..., delivering a needle-free vaccine dose into a person's arm at a purpose-built station with no clinician involvement; a one-off demonstration, not a validated clinical product.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: Cobi's demonstrated flow covers the whole injection episode at a fixed station: camera-based patient detection and ID check, arm cleaning, needle-free high-pressure jet injection, disposal of the single-dose capsule, and re-cleaning of the arm.

sources.title: China releases its first autonomous intelligent robot for needle-free vaccine injection - Global Times
sources.claim: A second, independent autonomous needle-free vaccination robot was released by Tongji University, using 3D camera-based recognition to select the injection site on a patient's body; a research release rather than a deployed product.

sources.title: Aletta: An Update About Vitestro's Robotic Blood Draw Device
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta performs the complete venipuncture episode autonomously on seated adults whose arm is positioned in the device - tourniquet, skin prep, ultrasound-guided needle insertion, tube handling and ... - with one staff member supervising several devices; in routine use at European hospital outpatient blood-draw sites since late 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It is the same class of physical act as vaccine administration - locating a site on a seated adult's bare arm, prepping skin, inserting a needle to a controlled depth, bandaging - at tighter precision (a vein lumen) than a deltoid intramuscular injection, on the same objects (adult human arms, sterile single-use consumables) in a healthcare setting. Its clinically validated first-stick performance shows worker-quality needle placement is achievable when the arm is presented to a fixed, purpose-built station.

sources.title: Aletta: An Update About Vitestro's Robotic Blood Draw Device
sources.claim: Aletta's validated scope is limited to routine, straightforward draws on cooperative patients aged 16+ with a normally positionable arm; pediatric patients, patients needing special positioning, stiff or crooked arms, and patients needing emotional support are explicitly outside its capability.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (venipuncture); cited to bound the transfer, showing the demonstrated envelope excludes children and non-standard positioning.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: Aletta is CE-marked and commercially launched in European healthcare settings, i.e. an operating product rather than a prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (venipuncture): establishes the maturity and reliability of autonomous needle placement on human arms, the element that transfers to administering an injection.

sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Landmark Peer-Reviewed Multicenter Clinical Study of Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy in Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: A multicenter clinical trial of the fully autonomous device in routine clinical practice was published in Clinical Chemistry; the company reports about 94.5% first-stick success, comparable to manual phlebotomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (venipuncture): quantifies worker-comparable reliability of autonomous needle insertion into adult arms, the core physical element shared with administering an intramuscular vaccine.

tasks.label: Provide basic health services, such as first aid.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Screening event at a fixed community site (FQHC waiting room, community center, church hall, senior center, worksite health fair): the CHW seats each walk-up resident, selects and wraps a cuff, takes blood pressure (often two readings), records weight/BMI and pulse on a form or tablet, states the result and refers anyone with elevated readings.

Mobile / street outreach screening from a van, pop-up tent, shelter, food pantry line or encampment: blood pressure plus a fingerstick blood-glucose (and sometimes pulse-ox) check on residents who may be unhoused or in poor condition, done standing or on a folding chair, results explained on the spot and logged.

Home visit to an enrolled client (chronic-disease, maternal-child or aging program): take blood pressure, pulse, weight and a fingerstick glucose on a client seated in their own chair or at bedside, record the values and report them to the supervising nurse.

Hands-on basic care during a home or clinic visit beyond simple measurement: checking a diabetic client's feet or a healing wound, helping a client operate their own cuff, inhaler, glucometer or pill organizer, assisting with positioning or hygiene while noting concerns for the nurse.

Minor first aid where an injury occurs (community event, school, shelter, camp, jobsite outreach): assess a cut, scrape, blister, minor burn, insect sting or nosebleed; clean it, apply antiseptic and an appropriately sized dressing or ice pack, and advise on follow-up.

Acute emergency response in the community: recognize a suspected opioid overdose and give intranasal naloxone with rescue positioning, or respond to a faint, seizure or cardiac arrest with CPR/AED while calling EMS and staying with the person until they arrive.

sources.title: Aletta® - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomously performs the complete blood-collection procedure on a seated patient's presented arm, including placing the tourniquet on the upper arm, selecting and puncturing a vein, and applying the bandage afterwards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine venipuncture on a walk-in adult in an outpatient blood-draw room. Transfer to CHW vitals/blood screening: the same objects (a human upper arm, a strap/cuff wrapped on it, a skin puncture, an adhesive dressing), in the same kind of institution-run clinical screening room, at strictly higher precision than inflating a BP cuff or taking a capillary sample.

sources.title: Vitestro launches new website and first public video of Aletta
sources.claim: Aletta is CE marked and available for routine clinical use in European healthcare facilities, i.e. it is a commercial product rather than a laboratory prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity and the setting (European hospitals and blood-draw centres) for the venipuncture-to-screening transfer described above.

sources.title: Vitestro Raises $70M to Advance Robotic Phlebotomy as Labs Confront Workforce Pressures - Dark Daily
sources.claim: Clinical validation of the autonomous device covered more than 4,000 patients in European healthcare facilities with safety and comfort comparable to or better than manual draws, and a reported 95% first-stick success rate.
sources.transferJustification: Quantifies worker-quality performance (first-attempt success, adverse-event rate) for an autonomous body-contact procedure on unselected walk-in patients, which is the reliability bar a CHW screening station would have to meet.

sources.title: Aletta: An Update About Vitestro's Robotic Blood Draw Device
sources.claim: The autonomous phlebotomy workflow needs only supervision, not step-by-step control: patients complete the procedure with the machine while one trained staff member oversees up to three devices at once.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms the 'limited intervention' condition (supervision of several machines, no teleoperation) for the body-contact clinical procedure being transferred to CHW screening.

sources.title: Giant Eagle to deploy higi health stations - Supermarket News
sources.claim: higi operates roughly 11,000 FDA-cleared self-screening health stations in US pharmacies, supermarkets and club stores; a person presents an arm in the station's cuff and the machine measures blood pressure, pulse, weight and BMI and stores the record.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, machine-executed: the blood-pressure/pulse/BMI screening a CHW performs, done by a machine that physically occludes the arm with an inflating cuff. It runs unattended in institution-controlled retail premises, but requires the client to present their own arm into a fixed cradle.

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics / University of Southern Denmark
sources.title: Lifeline Robotics: Home
sources.claim: Lifeline Robotics' automatic swab robot autonomously performs an oropharyngeal sample collection on a person who presents their head at the station, using AI computer vision to locate the target and handling the swab and container itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-of-care specimen collection on a member of the public at a walk-up screening station. It shows autonomous contact with a living person's body in a public health screening workflow, the same interaction pattern as a CHW screening booth.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Robotic wound redressing is still laboratory research at the component level: recent work automates only dressing removal, tape preparation and ..., learned from human teleoperated demonstrations, rather than assessing, cleaning and dressing an injury end to end.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the first-aid instances: shows that even in a laboratory, only sub-steps of dressing a wound are automated, so it cannot support a positive judgment for whole-instance first aid.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: The Cobi platform demonstrated an autonomous needle-free intramuscular injection on a human, scanning the person with LiDAR to choose the injection site without a clinician operating it, as a research demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering a simple clinical procedure to a standing/seated person at a clinic station; corroborates that autonomous body-contact health services can be executed on a presented arm, though only at demonstration maturity.
