tasks.label: Transport or accompany clients to scheduled health appointments or referral sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Curb-to-curb drive: CHW drives an ambulatory, independent client in an agency vehicle or personal car from the client's home to a scheduled clinic appointment across an urban/suburban metro, drops them at the entrance, and returns to pick them up. Public streets, mixed traffic, parking lots.

Door-through-door drive plus escort: CHW knocks at the client's door, walks them to the car, drives to the clinic or referral agency, parks, walks in with the client, gets them to the correct registration desk or department, then drives them home. Client is ambulatory but anxious, limited-English, or unfamiliar with the site.

Accompanying on public transit/on foot: CHW meets the client at home or a bus stop, rides the bus or train with them, manages transfers and fares, walks sidewalks and crosses streets, and delivers them to the appointment or referral site (WIC office, behavioral health clinic), often teaching the route for future trips.

In-facility escort: client arrives at a large hospital or health-center campus; the CHW meets them in the lobby and walks them through corridors, elevators and connecting buildings to the correct department, lab, pharmacy or social-services office, then hands them off to clinic staff.

Frail or mobility-impaired client: CHW helps an elderly or disabled client out of the house and down porch steps, physically supports or transfers them into the vehicle, loads/secures a walker or wheelchair, unloads at the clinic and supports them walking or pushes them inside.

sources.title: Waymo's skyrocketing ridership in one chart | TechCrunch
sources.claim: Waymo operates a fully driverless commercial ride-hailing service at large scale on public urban and suburban streets, carrying passengers door to door in ten US metro areas.

sources.title: Waymo goes driverless in Las Vegas, with Denver, San Diego, Tampa next | Electrek
sources.claim: Waymo activated fully driverless operations (no human at the wheel) in additional US markets in July 2026, confirming continued driver-out commercial operation.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (driving a person to a destination on public roads); establishes the driver-out status of the rides used for the transport instances.

sources.title: Waymo Opens Autonomous Ride-Hailing Service to All in San Francisco | Future Transport-News
sources.claim: Riders already use the driverless service specifically to reach medical appointments, i.e. the exact trip purpose of this task.

sources.title: Waymo and Unlimited Potential Plant Seeds of Collaboration in Phoenix
sources.claim: A Phoenix community health worker organization works with Waymo to give its community members door-to-door rides to appointments and classes, the same client population CHWs transport.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. (with Envoy Air / American Airlines, LAX and MIA)
sources.title: How Autonomous Wheelchairs Work | Aviation Pros
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous power chairs commercially transport passengers with limited mobility to their destination inside airport terminals in the US, navigating crowded concourses and returning themselves afterwards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting a mobility-limited traveler from a check-in area to a gate inside an institutional building. It transfers to escorting a client through a hospital or health-center campus to their appointment: same indoor pedestrian environment, same payload (a seated adult), same requirement to reach a specific room/desk reliably among crowds.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. with Unifi Aviation and Wayne County Airport Authority
sources.title: Unifi Aviation Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport
sources.claim: The same service is deployed at Detroit Metro for Delta customers, but is explicitly limited to passengers who can stand and ...; those needing hands-on boarding help still get human attendants.
sources.transferJustification: Documents the boundary of the capability: autonomous conveyance yes, hands-on transfer of a frail client no.

sources.system: WHILL Autonomous Drive System at Keio University Hospital
sources.developer: WHILL Inc. and Keio University Hospital
sources.title: Demonstration Experiment Begins for In-Hospital Patient Transport Using Personal Mobility with an Autonomous Driving System | Keio University
sources.claim: Autonomous personal-mobility devices have been run inside a hospital to carry patients from the entrance to a destination within the building without staff accompanying them.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the in-facility leg of this task (moving a patient to the right place inside a health facility), in a hospital rather than an airport.

sources.title: 2.3 Accessible Emerging Private Passenger Services | SFMTA
sources.claim: Waymo's wheelchair-accessible service is not autonomous: WAV trips for riders who cannot use the robotaxis are provided in human-driven accessible vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Bounds the driverless capability for the wheelchair-user instance: the accessible rides still require a human driver/attendant.

instances.label: Distributing Holy Communion/Eucharist at a regular worship service in the sanctuary: the minister handles consecrated wafers or bread and a chalice, faces a moving line or kneeling rail of dozens to hundreds of communicants of every age and height, speaks a formula to each, manages intinction, gluten-free hosts and blessings for children, and must not drop or spill the elements.

Baptism or equivalent initiation ordinance in a church: pouring water three times over a squirming infant held over a font, anointing with chrism and tracing a cross on the forehead, or physically supporting an adult and lowering/raising them in a full-immersion baptistry pool without injury.

Wedding ceremony in a church sanctuary or rented venue: leading the couple and party through vows, blessing and handling rings, joining the couple's hands, pronouncing the marriage and signing/filing the marriage license, adapting live to nervous participants, children, photographers and timing changes.

Funeral, committal or memorial rite in a funeral home chapel, church, or graveside at a cemetery: censing or sprinkling the casket with holy water, casting earth on the casket, handing flowers, physically consoling mourners, working outdoors on turf under a tent in variable weather.

Anointing of the sick, last rites, or bedside communion in a hospital, hospice or nursing-home room: anointing the forehead and hands of a frail or unresponsive patient with oil, laying on hands, placing a host in the mouth, working around IV lines, bed rails, monitors and grieving family.

Other occasional rites: imposition of ashes on the foreheads of a long line of worshippers on Ash Wednesday, confirmation with laying on of hands and chrismation, ordinations, blessings of homes, objects, animals and water, plus non-Christian equivalents (temple lamp/aarti offerings, sutra chanting at a memorial).

sources.developer: Evangelical Church in Hesse and Nassau
sources.title: 'BlessU-2' robot priest delivers blessings in five different languages - UPI.com
sources.claim: BlessU-2, a kiosk-style robot installed for a 2017 Reformation-anniversary exhibition in a Wittenberg church, dispensed spoken blessings: a visitor picks a language on its chest touchscreen, the robot recites a Bible verse and blessing, raises glowing arms and prints the text. It handles no ritual elements and touches no one; the church described it as an experiment, not a replacement for church work.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing robot to 'administering a rite': it delivers a blessing autonomously inside a church. It substantiates only speech-plus-arm-gesture rites; it does not pour water, distribute elements, anoint, or contact a person, so it does not transfer to the sacramental instances of this task.

sources.system: Pepper with Nissei Eco Buddhist funeral software
sources.title: SoftBank's Pepper robot programed to perform Buddhist funeral rites in Japan | VentureBeat
sources.claim: A SoftBank Pepper robot programmed by Nissei Eco to chant Buddhist sutras, tap a drum and bow was shown as a low-cost funeral-priest alternative at the Life Ending Industry Expo ...; the routine is pre-scripted audio and arm motion and was a trade-show demonstration rather than a service in regular use.
sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses the funeral-rite instance, but only in the Buddhist form that requires chanting and drum-tapping. It performs none of the physical acts of a Christian committal (censing, sprinkling, casting earth) and its autonomy is not established.

sources.title: Japanese Couple First in the World to Be Wed By a Robot | Communications of the ACM
sources.claim: The first robot-led wedding, conducted by Kokoro's I-Fairy in Tokyo in 2010, was not autonomous: the seated robot was driven through the ceremony by a hidden human operator at a computer.
sources.transferJustification: This is the wedding instance itself, cited as a negative control: the only known robot-officiated wedding was teleoperated and involved no handling of rings or of the marriage licence.

sources.developer: Hiroshi Ishiguro (Osaka University) with Kodai-ji temple
sources.title: Mindar the android priest is revolutionizing Buddhism in Japan | CNN
sources.claim: Mindar, an android modeled on Kannon installed at Kodai-ji temple in Kyoto since 2019, delivers pre-composed sermons with synchronized head, arm and torso motion; it preaches but performs no ritual manipulation of offerings and no contact with worshippers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (preaching / conducting worship) in a temple, an E2 setting. It shows that the deployed state of the art in religious robots is scripted speech and gesture with no object handling or person contact, so it does not transfer to administering rites.

sources.title: Robots are performing Hindu rituals -- some devotees fear they'll replace worshippers | Religion News Service
sources.claim: An industrial robotic arm introduced by an Indian automation firm performs 'aarti', waving an oil lamp before a deity image, shown at a Ganpati festival installation; the arm repeats a fixed lamp-waving trajectory in front of a static idol and performs no other part of a puja.
sources.transferJustification: The closest case of a robot manipulating a ritual object during a rite. It transfers only to a fixed lamp-waving motion toward a stationary object; it is a pre-programmed arm with no demonstrated adaptation and no interaction with worshippers.

sources.title: Japan unveils humanoid robot monk trained in Buddhist scriptures | Interesting Engineering
sources.claim: The most recent religious humanoid, Kyoto University's Buddharoid unveiled in early 2026, attended a temple event where it made hand gestures and answered questions; it is a research demonstrator of spiritual dialogue, not of ritual object handling or physical contact.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the 2026 frontier for robots in religious roles: speech and symbolic gesture at a temple event, with no evidence of administering an ordinance involving elements, water, oil, or bodily contact.

instances.label: Print supplementation in chambers: the clerk works through incoming pocket parts, pamphlet supplements and loose-leaf update packets for state codes, treatises and practice sets — slipping the new pocket part into the sleeve inside the back cover of each bound volume, pulling the superseded one, and inserting/removing individual replacement pages in ring binders per the publisher's filing instructions, on ordinary chambers bookshelves and a work table.

Keeping the chambers/courthouse print collection in order: reshelving reporters, digests and treatises pulled by the judge or co-clerks, integrating newly arrived advance sheets and slip-opinion pamphlets into their runs, shelf-reading for misfiled or missing volumes, and returning borrowed volumes to the courthouse library — all on standard office bookcases in a working chambers.

Assembling a document set for the judge's chambers reference collection: pulling briefs, statutes, key opinions, jury instructions and forms (mostly from electronic sources), printing them, then collating, tabbing, stapling or binding them into a bench book, hearing notebook or chambers case file that is shelved for the judge's use.

Updating the chambers' own reference binders and file drawers: printing newly issued opinions, amended local rules, standing orders and revised forms, three-hole punching them, inserting them at the right tab in an existing binder or folder, and pulling the superseded sheets for recycling.

Receiving and weeding: opening boxed shipments of new bound volumes, replacement volumes and subscription supplements delivered to chambers, checking them in against the subscription list, distributing them to the correct shelf, and boxing withdrawn or superseded volumes for storage, transfer to the court library, or disposal.

sources.system: bookBot (Dematic ASRS), NC State Hunt Library
sources.title: bookBot and Collections | James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
sources.claim: The Hunt Library's bookBot, a Dematic automated storage and retrieval system, stores and retrieves the library's book collection in bins under machine control, delivering requested items to a service point; ~25 North American libraries run such systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: storing and retrieving library volumes. It is the same physical work as shelving/keeping a law collection ordered and retrievable — identical objects (bound books) — executed in a purpose-built storage vault rather than on office bookcases.

sources.system: Lyngsoe Sort Mate 2000 automated materials handling system
sources.title: Library Automation Solutions | Lyngsoe Library Systems
sources.claim: Commercial library automated materials handling systems check in returned items by RFID and convey and sort them without manual handling into bins, trolleys or carts for restocking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting returned volumes back into their proper storage locations. Same objects (books/pamphlets) and same purpose as reshelving a chambers collection, done on a purpose-built conveyor line.

sources.developer: On Demand Books (installed at Cincinnati & Hamilton County Public Library)
sources.title: Espresso Book Machine | Cincinnati & Hamilton County Public Library
sources.claim: A fully integrated machine installed in a public library automatically prints, binds and trims a finished perfect-bound book on demand from a submitted digital file.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing a bound document set from supplied content. This is the physical core of 'assembling appropriate documents' — printing, collating and binding a compilation for the shelf — performed unattended in a purpose-built machine.

sources.system: Duplo 150FR booklet-making and collating system (DFC-100 collator + DBM-150)
sources.title: Duplo 150FR Booklet Maker and Collator System from CLC UK
sources.claim: Commercially sold print-finishing systems automatically collate multi-page sets from feeder stations and stitch, fold and trim them into finished booklets at thousands of sets per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: collating and binding printed document sets. Same objects (loose printed sheets) and same accepted output (an organized, bound set of legal documents) as a clerk assembling a bench notebook, in a purpose-built finishing line.

sources.system: Robotica ABOT-1 automated decant / box-opening system (FANUC robots)
sources.title: Warehouse Replenishment Automation for Fulfillment | FANUC America
sources.claim: Automated decant systems open received cartons robotically and induct the contents into totes for storage in an automated storage system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening incoming cartons and putting the contents away. Same physical steps as unpacking a shipment of law-book volumes and shelving them, performed on a purpose-built receiving line.

sources.title: Amazon tops 1 million robots: Here's what they do | GeekWire
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm picks individual items out of totes using suction and computer vision, running in fulfillment centers among Amazon's fleet of over one million robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: singulating individual flat, rigid items (books are a canonical Amazon SKU) into and out of totes — the item-level handling needed to induct volumes into and out of an automated book store.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch is commercially deployed at DHL for autonomous case unloading of trailers and containers, with ten units running across three countries as of mid-2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling shipping cases at a receiving dock — the box-moving portion of receiving law-book shipments and boxing withdrawn volumes, in a structured facility.

sources.title: The UJI librarian robot | Intelligent Service Robotics
sources.claim: A research mobile manipulator autonomously located and grasped a book from an ordinary library bookshelf, but only as a laboratory-scale demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving a book from a human bookshelf. Cited to show that shelf-level book handling in a human-arranged library exists only as a single-book research demonstration, without the reliability of a worker.

sources.system: π0.5 vision-language-action model on a mobile manipulator
sources.title: π0.5: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: State-of-the-art general-purpose manipulation policies can run multi-step tidying in previously unseen rooms but are explicitly acknowledged to make frequent errors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general pick-and-place tidying of everyday objects in human rooms. Cited to show that open-environment manipulation of the kind chambers work would require is not yet at worker reliability.

instances.label: Semester-start / weekly upkeep of the teaching lab's 20-40 identical desktop workstations: re-imaging or patching the OS, installing course toolchains (compilers, IDEs, VMs, license servers), then walking the room to power each station on, boot from USB/PXE, enter BIOS where needed, log in and confirm each seat works before class.

In-situ peripheral, cable and AV fixes in occupied labs and classrooms: a station with a blank monitor or dead keyboard, a loose HDMI/DisplayPort/USB-C or power lead under a desk, a projector or lectern PC that won't display; professor traces the connection, reseats or replaces the cable/peripheral, and tests it.

Bench-level hardware service on a lab desktop or laptop: open the case, blow out dust, diagnose and swap a failed or upgraded component (RAM, SSD, GPU, PSU, fan), reconnect internal SATA/power leads, reassemble and verify the machine boots and runs the course software.

Upkeep of the department's instructional server/cluster gear in a machine room or lab closet: replacing a failed drive in a rack node, racking or re-cabling a GPU node or switch, dressing network/power cabling, checking fans, filters and thermals on heterogeneous, non-uniform equipment.

Maintaining specialized instructional hardware kits: robotics kits, FPGA/Arduino/Raspberry Pi boards, sensors, breadboards, VR headsets and their controllers — inspecting and testing after each lab session, re-seating jumper wires, resoldering or replacing broken leads, recharging, reassembling kits and restocking bins.

Physical setup, relocation and housekeeping: unboxing and installing new machines or monitors at lab benches, mounting and cable-managing them, rearranging stations for a course, wiping down keyboards/screens, and hauling retired equipment to surplus/e-waste.

sources.system: Gemini Robotics 1.5 (Google DeepMind) and related connector-insertion research, as assessed by Epoch AI
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 — Epoch AI
sources.claim: Independent 2026 capability assessment: inserting cables inside a standard PC case (SATA, PSU, external HDMI/USB) so the machine boots is classified as 'significant limits in lab'; no robot has attempted the ... PC-assembly task, although Gemini Robotics 1.5 autonomously inserted and removed power, USB ... on a computer's front panel.
sources.transferJustification: Cable/connector insertion on computer hardware is the physical core of the peripheral-and-cable maintenance instance; same objects (USB/HDMI/power/LAN), same precision class, but demonstrated on an accessible fixtured panel rather than in a classroom.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 — Epoch AI
sources.claim: Same assessment states no robot has attempted autonomous end-to-end PC assembly, and that industrial-assembly demos depend on controlled setups with limited transfer to new objects and contexts.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence bounding the reassemble-and-verify step of bench hardware repair and new-machine setup.

sources.system: Universal Robots UR7e dual-arm cell with Cambrian AI vision
sources.developer: Teradyne Robotics / Universal Robots with Cambrian Robotics
sources.title: The AI Trainer, the Generalist and the Cable Inserter Walk into a Booth | Machine Design
sources.claim: At Automate 2026, two UR7e cobots guided by ... AI 3D vision system assembled high-density server ..., with the vision system identifying connector orientation and adjusting trajectories in real time.
sources.transferJustification: Server-rack cabling is the same physical operation as re-cabling instructional rack gear (deformable copper cables into dense ports), performed in a purpose-built cobot cell with the rack presented to the robots.

sources.system: Molg robotic microfactory (with ABB robot arms)
sources.title: ABB Robotics and US start-up Molg tackle data center e-waste with robotic microfactories
sources.claim: Molg's robotic microfactory autonomously assembles and disassembles laptop PCs, servers and industrial ...; microfactories have been installed at Sims Lifecycle Services and are rolling out to hyperscaler ITAD facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Automated teardown/rebuild of laptops and servers in a fixtured cell covers the case-opening, fastener removal and module extraction/insertion steps of bench-level component service on the same class of machines.

sources.system: Tianxun (2nd generation) data center O&M robot
sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Enables Five Super Data Centers to Support Double 11 — Alibaba Cloud Community
sources.claim: Alibaba's second-generation Tianxun data-center operations robot performs faulty hard-disk replacement without human intervention — automatic inspection, locating the faulty disk, replacing it and recharging — and Alibaba says the system is in operation at five of its data centers, replacing a disk in about four minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Diagnosing and swapping a failed drive in rack-mounted computing hardware is the same maintenance action as replacing a failed drive in a departmental server; it is done on uniform fleet racks whose bays present drives in known positions.

sources.title: Apple expands global recycling programs — Apple Newsroom
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line autonomously disassembles 15 different iPhone models at 200 units per hour, recovering components for reuse, in a purpose-built recycling line.
sources.transferJustification: Fixtured teardown of consumer computing hardware (fastener removal, module extraction) at production rates demonstrates the E1 form of case-opening and component removal used in bench repair, though on one presented product family.

sources.title: SoftBank develops 'cableless' server rack for data center robots - DCD
sources.claim: SoftBank developed a cableless, 'robot-friendly' server rack in September 2025 specifically so robots can install, replace and inspect servers, because cabling in conventional human-built racks has been a major obstacle to robotic automation in data centers.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that robotic server servicing currently requires the environment to be rebuilt around the machine (E1-style presentation), bounding claims of in-place maintenance in as-found human facilities.
